A device that weighs less than one kilogram is part of a mission that will allow scientists to deliver fourth generation or 4G mobile coverage to the moon in 2019.
If successful, the tiny device will provide the moon with its first ever mobile phone network.
The lunar network will support high-definition streaming of video and data between the moon and Earth.
The network is part of Mission to the Moon.
This is a project with the goal of landing the first privately paid for mission to the moon.
The 4G mission is set to launch from Cape Canaveral in the United States on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket in 2019.
Mission to the Moon intends to establish and test the first elements of a communications network on the moon.
The scientists working on the project opted to build a 4G, rather than a fifth generation or 5G network.
This is because fifth generation networks are still in testing and trial phases.
This means that a 5G network may not yet be stable enough to work on the moon ’s surface.
What are scientists planning to do?
Why did scientists choose to set up a 4G network in their mission?
Firefighters responded to a fire Wednesday night at an abandoned mall in Hayward.
The fire was reported at 9:26 p.m.at an old shopping Centre on Mission Avenue near Saint Mary 's church.
Six fire engines, two trucks and two chiefs responded to the scene.
Crews had the fire under control in about 45 minutes and managed to contain the fire to its point of origin.
There were some people inside the building when the fire broke out, but there were no reports of any injuries.
Fire investigators have responded to the scene but have not yet determined the cause of the fire.
Firefighters will remain on the scene until later this morning to ensure that the fire doesn't start up again.
The shopping mall had not been in use since 2002.
In 2014，City Hall developed plan to knock down the building and replace it with affordable housing.
However，the plan was dropped due to lack of funds.
3.What does the news item say about the fire?
4. What had City Hall planned to do?
Potato chips in Japan are being sold for 6 times their normal price.
This is after the country 's main manufacturer stopped sales due to a potato shortage.
Storms and floods in its main potato-growing region last year caused the worst harvest in more than 3 decades.
Local media reports suggest Calbee and its main rival Koike-Ya are halting almost 50 products.
“We don't know when we ’ll be able to restart，” a company spokesman said.
Snack lovers are panic buying, and many supermarket shelves are bare.
Japanese laws limit the amount of imported potatoes that can be used in Japanese-made products.
Japan says fear of disease is its main reason to block fresh imports.
It still only allows potatoes from selected US states.
This is only at certain times and on condition that they are processed at factories based near Japanese ports.
But global warming has raised the possibility that domestic produce could be seriously affected by rare weather events more often.
5.What problem is Japan facing?
6.Why does Japan limit the import of potatoes?
7.What might affect Japanese domestic produce?
Mr. Brown's lectures are so boring.
Yes, he is not a very exciting speaker.
But the subject is interesting.
During every one of his lectures, I try to listen, I really try, but after about ten minutes, my mind begins to wander and I lose concentration.
But I see that you seem to be OK.
How do you stay focused through the entire hour?
Well, what I do is keep my pen moving.
What do you mean?
It's a method of active concentration I read about.
One of the most effective ways to concentrate is to write things down.
But it has to be done by hand, not typing on a keyboard.
You see, writing by hand forces you to actually engage with what you are learning in a more physical way.
Do you review your notes afterwards then?
Some times, but that not important.
My notes may or may not be useful.
But the point is that by writing down what Mr. Brown says, I can follow his line of thinking more easily.
In fact, sometimes I draw a little too.
You draw in class? And that helps you pay attention?
Yes, honestly, it works for me.
I just draw little lines and nonsense really.
It was also in that article I read.
It can keep the mind active, prevent getting bored and help to concentrate.
Again, the point is to listen hard while keeping the pen moving.
If I'm at home and I need to study, what I do is read out loud.
It has a similar effect to writing by hand.
It helps memorize information in a physical way.
8.What does the man think of Mr. Brown's lectures?
9. What does the woman do during Mr. Brown's lectures?
10.Why does the woman draw in class?
11.What does the woman say about reading out loud?
And where is this?
These photos are from the Taj Mahal in India.
We went there about ten years ago for our honeymoon.
Was it romantic?
Yeah，the Taj Mahal was a very romantic place.
The guide told us there is a famous love story behind this building that all Indians learn in school.
I think it was during the 1600s and the princess at that time died while giving birth to her 14th child.
The emperor loved the princess so much and was so sad when she died that he ordered the palace to be built in her honor.
Wow, that sounds very romantic. It looks amazing.
Yes. It's gorgeous.
It's also larger in real life than it looks in the photos.
The building is very tall and there are gardens and a wall around it all.
It's all built this white stone.
And some walls of the building are decorated with jewels.
It must have been very crowded when you were there.
Yes. It's a very famous tourist destination, so there are thousands of visitors every day.
Was the rest of India crowded?
Yes, very crowded in many cities.
It was sometimes so crowded that it was difficult to walk along the streets, especially through busy markets. And there are so many cars.
Traffic was terrible. But the people are friendly.
The culture is amazing. And we had a great time.
What about the food?
Indian food is great.
There are lots of different dishes to try，and every region has its own special food.

A Pew Research Center survey of more than 1,000 Americans conducted in April, 2016, finds that Americans continue to express largely positive views about the current state of their local public libraries.
For instance, around three quarters say that public libraries provide them with the resources they need.
And 66% say the closing of their local public library would have a major impact on their community although notably, just 33% say this would have a major impact on them personally or on their family.
A majority of Americans feel libraries are doing a good job of proving a safe place for people of hang out or spend time as well as opening up educational opportunities for people of all ages.
And roughly half think their libraries contribute "a lot" to their communities in terms of helping spark creativity among young people and providing a trusted place for people to learn about new technologies.
As in past Pew Research Center surveys of library use，the April 2016 survey also measured Americans ' usage of and engagement with libraries.
Overall, 53% of Americans, aged 16 and older, have had some interaction with a public library in the past year —— either through an in-person visit or using a library website.
Some 48% of adults specifically visited a library in the past 12 months, a modest increase from the 44% who said that in late 2015.
16. What do most Americans say about local public libraries?
17. How can local public libraries benefit young people?
18. What does the 2016 survey show about adult library users?
A Savannah cat is across breed between a domestic cat and a medium-sized wild African cat called the Serval.
The unusual cross became popular among breeders at the end of the 1990s, and in 2001 the International Cat Association accepted it as a new registered breed.
The Savannahs are tall and slim and can weigh up to 9.1 kilograms, making them one of the largest breeds of cats that people can own.
They have a spotted coat similar to that of many types of wild cats and their ears are very large.
They are also commonly compared to dogs in their loyalty, and can be trained to walk on a lead and to fetch.
An often-noted characteristic of the Savannah is its jumping ability.
They are known to jump on top of doors and high cabinets.
Some can leap about 2.5 meters high from a standing position.
Cats are typically known for being very inquisitive and so are the Savannahs.
They often learn how to open doors and cupboards.
Many Savannah cats do not fear water and will play with or even dive into water.
Some owners even shower with their Savannah cats.
Presenting a water bowl to a Savannah may also prove a challengeas, some will promptly begin to bat all the water out of the bowl until it is empty, using their front paws.
19.What do we learn about the Savannah cat?
20. What is characteristic of Savannah cats?
21. What do some people do with their Savannah cats?
When children start school for the very first time, parents often feel a sense of excitement coupled with a touch of sadness at the end of an era.
This is the start of a new adventure for children: playing and interacting with new friends, sharing, taking turns and settling into a new routine.
But of course, this is not the s art of your child 's education which in fact began at birth.
Back then, you would have been your child 's most influential teachers.
During this time at home, your child would have learned more than at any other period in their life.
During your child 's first year in school, much time will be spent in learning to read and they need to know that this is fun and worthwhile.
Your child will naturally copy you, so it is important that you are seen reading and enjoying books, newspapers and magazines rather than just absorbed in screens.
Ultimately, an excellent education should be a close partnership between parents and teachers.
A child 's year splits fairly neatly into thirds: a third at school, a third asleep and a third awake at home or on holiday.
Irrespective of the quality of a school, a child 's home life is of key importance.
It is the determining factor of their academic success.
Your child may have started on a new journey but your work is far from finished.
22.How do parents feel when their children start going to school?
23. What does the passage say about children 's education?
24. What should parents do for the success of their children 's education?
25. What does the passage say is the key factor of children 's academic success?

1 With the development of economy and urbanization, the number of big cities is constantly increasing in China. 2 While big cities are attracting more and more people, they also bring many challenges, such as traffic jams and pollution, just to name a few.
1 The first problem that really bothers me is the traffic congestion in the rush hour. 2 I hate waiting for buses and being late. 3 Therefore, I have to get up very early if I have an appointment in the morning. 4 Next is that the large population in a big city makes it so crowded that you can't find a peaceful place unless staying at home. 5 The supermarkets are always crowded, so are the cinemas and parks. 6 Another consequence of such a large population is that it intensifies the inadequacy of quality medical and educational resources, thus decreasing residents ' sense of happiness.
1 As a result, although I am frequently asked whether I like to live in a big city or not, my answer is always no, definitely not. 2 How about you?

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 Because of the rapid development of communication network, the number of smartphone users in China has increased at an astonishing rate in recent years, which has made major changes to the way many people read. 2 Nowadays they often read news and articles on their smartphones instead of buying traditional newspapers and periodicals. 3 The development of a large number of mobile apps enables people to read novels and other forms of literary works through smartphones. 4 Therefore, the sales of paper books are affected. 5 But surveys show that though the smartphone reading market is growing steadily, over half of the adults still enjoy reading paper books.

questions.answer: 1 Because of the rapid development of communication network, the number of smartphone users in China has increased at an astonishing rate in recent years, which has made major changes to the way many people read. 2 Nowadays they often read news and articles on their smartphones instead of buying traditional newspapers and periodicals. 3 The development of a large number of mobile apps enables people to read novels and other forms of literary works through smartphones. 4 Therefore, the sales of paper books are affected. 5 But surveys show that though the smartphone reading market is growing steadily, over half of the adults still enjoy reading paper books.

questions.explanation:
【考点】名词辨析题。

【语法判断】空格前面是形容词最高级the most serious，后面为现在分词结构occurring in the developing world作后置定语，因此空格处需要填入名词。

【语义判断】本句前半部分提到，就福利成本而言，空气污染每年造成多于5万亿美元的全球经济损失，由此可知，后半部分应指，对于发展中国家而言，空气污染会造成最为严重的影响。因此，空格处需要填入一个表示“不良影响”或“损失”的名词。由此确定名词damage“损害”为本题答案。"

【考点】固定用法题。

【语法判断】空格前面为名词词组a number of costs，后面为介宾结构with air pollution。通过分析句子结构可知，空格处所填词应与后面的介宾结构一起作前面名词词组的后置定语。因此，空格处需要填入形容词或动词的分词形式。

【语义判断】文章首段提到，空气污染每年造成多于5万亿美元的全球经济损失。本句承接首段指出，该数据包含了一些费用。因此，空格处所填词应与后面的with air pollution搭配， 共同表达“与空气污染相关”的意思。备选词中符合以上要求的只有associated。be associated with...意为“与……相关”， 由此确定associated为答案。本句完整形式为“The figures include a number of costs which are associated with air pollution.”， 原文中省略了which are."

【考点】名词辨析题。

【语法判断】空格前面为动词includes，后面有介词like表示列举，因此空格处需要填入名词来作宾语。

【语义判断】文章围绕air pollution展开，本句中提到Indoor pollution，并列举了两种户内空气污染的情况是“家用取暖和家用烹饪”，因此空格处所填名词意思上与家用取暖和家用烹饪有关。根据生活常识可知，取暖与烹饪均会产生一定的空气污染。因此，空格处需要填入一个表示“原因，根源”的名词。由此确定名词sources“根源”为本题答案。"

【考点】形容词辨析题。

【语法判断】空格前为系动词remained，后为介词短语，因此空格处应填入形容词作表语

【语义判断】本句末尾处使用介词despite，表示让步，表达了“虽然家用取暖和家用烹饪这方面有所改善”这一语义。因此，本句前面部分在意思上应该与末尾的介宾结构相反，所以空格处需要填入一个与remained一起表示户内空气污染“依旧存在”的形容词。由此确定形容词constant"持续不断的”为本题答案。

【考点】动词辨析题。    

【语法判断】空格前面为人名Chris Murray，空格后面为代词it，因此判断空格处所填词为动词，且该动词能与宾语it后面的介词as搭配，an“urgent call to action”则为it的宾语补足语。

【语义判断】本句指出，这份报告是一项“呼吁采取行动的紧急号召”。备选动词中，described意为“形容，描述”，可与as搭配，符合句意，故为答案。described...as...意为“将……描述为…...”。    "

【考点】名词辨析题。

【语法判断】空格前有动词have和限定词little，所以空格处需要填入名词。

【语义判断】本句指出，导致人们过早死亡的一个风险因素就是我们吸入的空气。由常识可知，空气是人类生存所必需的客观条件，人们几乎无法操控。因此，空格处应填入一个表示“操控”的名词，故E) control控制”为本题的答案。"

【考点】动词辨析题。

【语法判断】通过分析句子结构可知，空格位于where引导的定语从句中，空格前为名词词组lost-labor income作主语，空格后为副词nearly和名词结构1% of GDP，所以该从句缺少谓语动词，再根据本句前半部分的时态，空格处应填入动词

的第三人称单数形式。

【语义判断】本句前半部分指出，空气污染产生的影响在发展中国家最为严重。空格所在从句进一步说明严重的程度。又因为从句的主语和宾语均为经济学名词结构，因此空格处填入equals“相当于”符合句意：意为“劳动力损失所带来的收入损失相当于几乎1%的国内生产总值”，表明空气污染产生的影响之严重。"

【考点】副词辨析题。

【语法判断】空格前面是代词they，后面为动词experience，因此空格处需要填入副词以修饰其后的动词。

【语义判断】前一句提到，在发展中国家的一些地区，劳动力损失所带来的收人损失相当于几乎1%的国内生产总值。空格所在句进一步解释造成劳动力损失的原因：在中低收入国家，大概有十分之九的人们在居住的地方经受着危险的户外空气污染。因此，空格处需要填人一个表示“长期以来，一直这样”的副词， 修饰experience。由此确定副词regularly“经常”为本题答案。"

【考点】副词辨析题。

【语法判断】空格位于be limited to这个固定用法中，且本句基本结构完整，因此空格处需要填入副词修饰limited。

【语义判断】前一段提到了空气污染给发展中国家带来的影响。空格所在句之后则阐述了空气污染对发达国家的影响，因此，空格处需要填入一个与is not limited to一起表示“不仅仅局限于”的副词，表明这一情况并非只发生在发展中国家。由此确定副词exclusively“仅仅， 唯独”为本题答案。"

【考点】名词辨析题。

【语法判断】空格前为名词diesel，空格后为谓语动词have become more common，所以空格处需要填人名词的复数形式，与名词diesel搭配构成从句的主语。

【语义判断】通过上下文可知，本段的大意是空气污染对发达国家也产生了很大影响：近年来，欧洲国家柴油车辆的日益普遍使得欧洲发达国家也面临着严重的空气污染，导致因相关疾病而过早死去的人的数量达到了几万人。因此可以确定名词vehicles“交通工具，车辆”为本题答案。"

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Several times a month, you can find a doctor in the aisles of Ralph’s market in Huntington Beach, California, wearing a white coat and helping people learn about food. 2 On one recent day, this doctor was Daniel Nadeau, wandering the cereal aisle with Allison Scott, giving her some idea on how to feed kids who persistently avoid anything that is healthy. 3 “ Have you thought about trying fresh juices in the morning?” he asks her. 4 “The frozen oranges and apples are a little cheaper, and fruits are really good for the brain. 5 Juices are quick and easy to prepare, you can take the frozen fruit out the night before and have it ready the next morning.”?
1 Scott is delighted to get food advice from a physician who is program director of the nearby Mary and Dick Allen Diabetes Center, part of the St. Joseph Hoag Health alliance. 2 The center’s ‘Shop with Your Doc’ program sends doctors to the grocery store to meet with any patients who sign up for the service, plus any other shoppers who happen to be around with questions.?
1 Nadeau notices the pre-made macaroni-and-cheese boxes in Scott’s shopping cart and suggests she switch to whole grain macaroni and real cheese. 2 “So I’d have to make it?” she asks, her enthusiasm fading at the thought of how long that might take, just to have her kids reject it. 3 “I’m not sure they’d eat it. 4 They just won’t eat it.”?
1 Nadeau says sugar and processed foods are big contributors to the rising diabetes rates among children. 2 “In America, over 50 percent of our food is processed food,” Nadeau tells her. 3 “And only 5 percent of our food is plant-based food. 4 I think we should try to reverse that.” 5 Scott agrees to try more fruit juices for the kids and to make real macaroni and cheese. 6 Score one point for the doctor, zero for diabetes.?
1 Nadeau is part of a small revolution developing across California. 2 The food-as-medicine movement has been around for decades, but it’s making progress as physicians and medical institutions make food a formal part of treatment, rather than relying solely on medications (药物). 3 By prescribing nutritional changes or launching programs such as ‘Shop with your Doc’, they are trying to prevent, limit or even reverse disease by changing what patients eat. 4 “There’s no question people can take things a long way toward reversing diabetes, reversing high blood pressure, even preventing cancer by food choices,” Nadeau says.?
1 In the big picture, says Dr. Richard Afable, CEO and president of ST. Joseph Hoag Health, medical institutions across the state are starting to make a philosophical switch to becoming a health organization, not just a health care organization. 2 That feeling echoes the beliefs of the Therapeutic Food Pantry program at Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital, which completed its pilot phase and is about to expand on an ongoing basis to five clinic sites throughout the city. 3 The program will offer patients several bags of food prescribed for their condition, along with intensive training in how to cook it. 4 “We really want to link food and medicine, and not just give away food,” says Dr. Rita Nguyen, the hospital’s medical director of Healthy Food Initiatives. 5 “We want people to understand what they’re eating, how to prepare it, the role food plays in their lives.”?
1 In Southern California, Loma Linda University School of Medicine is offering specialized training for its resident physicians in Lifestyle Medicine — that is a formal specialty in using food to treat disease. 2 Research findings increasingly show the power of food to treat or reverse diseases, but that does not mean that diet alone is always the solution, or that every illness can benefit substantially from dietary changes.? 3 Nonetheless, physicians say that they look at the collective data and a clear picture emerges: that the salt, sugar, fat and processed foods in the American diet contribute to the nation’s high rates of obesity, diabetes and heart disease. 4 According to the World Health Organization, 80 percent of deaths from heart disease and stroke are caused by high blood pressure, tobacco use, elevated cholesterol and low consumption of fruits and vegetables.?
1 “It’s a different paradigm (范式) of how to treat disease,” says Dr. Brenda Rea, who helps run the family and preventive medicine residency program at Loma Linda University School of Medicine. 2 The lifestyle medicine specialty is designed to train doctors in how to prevent and treat disease, in part, by changing patients’ nutritional habits. 3 The medical center and school at Loma Linda also has a food cupboard and kitchen for patients. 4 This way, patients not only learn about which foods to buy, but also how to prepare them at home.
1 Many people don’t know how to cook, Rea says, and they only know how to heat things up. 2 That means depending on packaged food with high salt and sugar content. 3 So teaching people about which foods are healthy and how to prepare them, she says, can actually transform a patient’s life. 4 And beyond that, it might transform the health and lives of that patient’s family. 5 “What people eat can be medicine or poison,” Rea says. 6 “As a physician, nutrition is one of the most powerful things you can change to reverse the effects of long-term disease.”?
1 Studies have explored evidence that dietary changes can slow inflammation (炎症), for example, or make the body inhospitable to cancer cells. 2 In general, many lifestyle medicine physicians recommend a plant-based diet — particularly for people with diabetes or other inflammatory conditions.?
1 “As what happened with tobacco, this will require a cultural shift, but that can happen,” says Nguyen. 2 “In the same way physicians used to smoke, and then stopped smoking and were able to talk to patients about it, I think physicians can have a bigger voice in it.”

questions.explanation:
【定位】

由题干中的More than half、Americans和factory-produced定位到文章D) 段第二句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，在美国，超过50%的食物都是加工食品。题干中的More than half of the food对应原文中的over 50 percent of our food，题干中的factory-produced是对原文中processed food的同义转述，故本题正确答案为D) 。

【定位】

由题干中的program、doctors和stores定位到B)段。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位段首句提到，斯科特很高兴能从一位医生那里得到食物方面的建议。接着后一句提到，“和你的医生一起购物”项目把医生派到食品杂货店，与报名申请这项服务的每一位患者以及碰巧在周围且遇到问题的其他每一位购物者会面。题干中的assigns doctors...in food stores是对原文中sends doctors to the grocery store的同义转述，题干中的doctors to give advice to shoppers是对原文中get food advice from a physician以及meet with any patients...any other shoppers的概括归纳，故本题答案为B)。

【定位】

由题干中的growing、research和illnesses定位到文章G)段第二句。


【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句提到，研究结果越来越显示出食物治疗或逆转疾病的力量，题干中的There is growing evidence from research是对原文中Research findings increasingly show的同义转述，题干中的food helps patients recover from various illnesses是对原文中the power of food to treat or reverse diseases的概括归纳，故本题正确答案为G)。

【定位】

由题干中的prepared quickly and easily定位到文章A)段最后一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句意为：准备果汁挺快、挺简单的；你可以在前一天晚上把冷藏的水果拿出来，第二天早上就可以直接用了。题干中的prepared quickly and easily是对原文中quick and easy to prepare的同义转述，故本题正确答案为A)。

【定位】

由题干中的prepare healthy food和change their life定位到文章Ⅰ) 段第三句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句提到，教给人们哪些食物是健��的以及如何准备食物实际上可以改变患者的生活。题干中的Training a patient to prepare healthy food是对原文中teaching people about which foods are healthy and how to prepare them的概括归纳，题干中的change their life是对原文种transform a patient's life的同义转述，故本题答案为I)。

【定位】

由题干中的prescribes food、teaches patients和how to cook it定位到F) 段第三句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，该项目将为忠者提供几袋针对其病情开出的食物，并提供如何烹饪的强化培训。题干中的prescribes food for treatment是对原文中food prescribed for their condition的同义转述，题干中的teaches patients how to cook it是对原文中intensive training in how to cook it的同义转述，故本题正确答案为F)。

【定位】

由题干中的Scott、not keen和a waste of time定位到文章C)段。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位段第二句提到，斯科特问是不是要自己动手做饭，一想到这可能需要很长时间，结果孩子们却拒绝食用，她的热情就消失了，题干中的Scott is not keen是对原文中her enthusiasm fading的同义转述，题干中的simply be a waste of time是对原文中“...at the thought of how long that might take，just to have her kids reject it.”的概括归纳，故本题正确答案为C)。

【定位】

由题干中的Diabetes、advised和plant-based food定位到文章J) 段最后一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题，定位句提到，一般来说，许多生活方式医学专业的医生建议植物性饮食——特别是糖尿病或其他炎症性疾病患者。题干“Diabetes patients are advised to eat more plant-based food.”是对原文中recommend a plant-based diet-particularly for people with diabetes的同义转述，故本题正确答案为J)。

【定位】

由题干中的Using food as medicine和making headway定位到文章E) 段第二句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，食物即药物运动已经存在了几十年，但随着医生和医疗机构不再仅仅依靠药物，而是将食物作为治疗的正式组成部分， 这项运动正在取得进展。题干中的Using food as medicine is no novel idea是对原文中The food-as-medicine movement has been around for decades的同义转述，题干中的making headway是对原文中making progress的同义转述，故本题正确答案为E)。

【定位】

由题干中的Americans’ high rates和the way they eat定位到文章G) 段倒数第二句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句提到，美国人饮食中的盐、糖、肥肉和加工食品导致了该国肥胖症、糖尿病和心脏病的高发病率。题干中的various illnesses是对原文中“...obesity，diabetes and heart disease.”的概括归纳，题干中的result from the way they eat是对原文中“...the salt，sugar，fat and processed foods in the American diet contribute to...”的概括归纳，故答案为G)。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 "California has been facing a drought for many years now, with certain areas even having to pump freshwater hundreds of miles to their distribution system." 2 The problem is growing as the population of the state continues to expand. 3 New research has found deep water reserves under the state which could help solve their drought crisis.? 4 Previous drilling of wells could only reach depths of 1,000 feet, but due to new pumping practices, water deeper than this can now be extracted (抽取). 5 The team at Stanford investigated the aquifers (地下蓄水层)below this depth and found that reserves may be triple what was previously thought.
1 It is profitable to drill to depths more than 1,000 feet for oil and gas extraction, but only recently in California has it become profitable to pump water from this depth. 2 The aquifers range from 1,000 to 3,000 feet below the ground, which means that pumping will be expensive and there are other concerns.? 3 The biggest concern of pumping out water from this deep is the gradual settling down of the land surface. 4 As the water is pumped out, the vacant space left is compacted by the weight of the earth above.?
1 Even though pumping from these depths is expensive, it is still cheaper than desalinating(脱盐)the ocean water in the largely coastal state. 2 Some desalination plants exist where feasible, but they are costly to run and can need constant repairs. 3 Wells are much more reliable sources of freshwater, and California is hoping that these deep wells may be the answer to their severe water shortage.?
1 One problem with these sources is that the deep water also has a higher level of salt than shallower aquifers. 2 This means that some wells may even need to undergo desalination after extraction, thus increasing the cost. 3 Research from the exhaustive study of groundwater from over 950 drilling logs has just been published. 4 New estimates of the water reserves now go up to 2,700 billion cubic meters of freshwater.?

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. By building more reserves of groundwater.

    通过增加地下水储备

B. By drawing water from the depths of the earth.

    通过从地下深处取水

C. By developing more advanced drilling devices.

    通过开发更先进的钻井设备

D. By upgrading its water distribution system.

    通过升级其配水系统”


【定位及答案】

由题干中的California's drought crisis和some researchers定位到首段第三句。定位句指出，新的研究发现，该州地下有深层地下水储备，这可以帮助他们解决干旱危机。由此可见，从地下深处取水是解决加利福尼亚干旱危机的办法，故答案为B)。


【错选分析】

A选项：首段第三句提到，该州的深层地下水储备可以帮助他们解决干旱危机，可见是要开采更多的地下水，而非增加地下水储备，可以排除A)“通过增加地下水储备”；

C选项：首段第四句提到，以前的钻井深度只能达到地下1000英尺，但是由于新的抽水实践的进行，现在能抽取出比这更深的地下水，可见钻井技术是有所提高，但这并不是解决加利福尼亚干旱危机的直接方法，可以排除C)“通过开发更先进的钻井设备”；

D选项：首段第一句提到，加利福尼亚多年来一直面临着干旱问题，一些地方甚至需要从数百英里以外的地方抽运淡水到其配水系统，但配水系统并不能从根本上缓解淡水短缺的问题，可以排除D)“通过升级其配水系统”。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. It was deemed vital to solving the water problem.

    人们认为这对解决水问题至关重要。

B. It was not considered worth the expense.

    这被认为是不值得花钱的。

C. It may not provide quality freshwater.

   它可能无法提供优质淡水。

D. It is bound to gain support from the local people.

    它一定会得到当地人民的支持。


【定位及答案】

由题干中的extracting water from deep aquifers和选项内容定位到第二段第一句。定位句提到，从1，000英尺以下的深度开采石油和天然气是有利可图的，但在加利福尼亚，从1，000英尺以下抽取地下水只是最近才变得有利可图。由定位句中的only recently in California has it become profitable可知，从1，000英尺以下抽取地下水只是最近才变得有利可图，所以可以推断出以前人们认为抽取深层地下水是不值得花钱的，故答案为B)。


【错选分析】

A选项：第三段最后一句提到，加利福尼亚正期望这些深井可以解决他们严重的淡水短缺问题，但A)项用了过去时，意为“过去人们认为它对解决水的问题至关重要”，不符合文意，故排除；

C选项：由最后一段可知，深层地下水比浅一些的地下水的含盐浓度要高，因而会增加淡化成本，但不可将之曲解为抽取的深层地下水质量不好，故排除C)“它可能无法提供高质量的淡水”；

D选项：第二段第二句提到，除了成本高，人们还有其他的一些担忧，因此不能推断出该方法一定会得到当地人们的支持，故可以排除D)“它肯定会得到当地人们的支持”。

【选项概览】

A. The sinking of land surface.

    陆地表面的下陷

B. The harm to the ecosystem.

    损坏生态系统

C. The damage to aquifers.

    损坏地下蓄水层

D. The change of the climate.

    改变气候


【定位及答案】

由题干中的consequence和extractingwater from deep underground定位到第二段第三、四句。定位句指出，从这一深度取水最大的担忧就是陆地表面会逐渐下陷。随着地下水被抽走，地下留出的空余空间会被上面的土壤压实，由此可见，抽取深层地下水的一个结果就是陆地表面的下陷，故答案为A)。



【错选分析】

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 The AlphaGo program’s victory is an example of how smart computers have become.?
1 But can artificial intelligence (AI) machines act ethically, meaning can they be honest and fair?
1 One example of AI is driverless cars. 2 They are already on California roads, so it is not too soon to ask whether we can program a machine to act ethically. 3 As driverless cars improve, they will save lives.? 4 They will make fewer mistakes than human drivers do. 5 Sometimes, however, they will face a choice between lives. 6 Should the cars be programmed to avoid hitting a child running across the road, even if that will put their passengers at risk? 7 What about making a sudden turn to avoid a dog? 8 What if the only risk is damage to the car itself, not to the passengers?
1 Perhaps there will be lessons to learn from driverless cars, but they are not super-intelligent beings. 2 Teaching ethics to a machine even more intelligent than we are will be the bigger challenge.?
1 About the same time as AlphaGo’s triumph, Microsoft’s ‘chatbot’ took a bad turn. 2 The software, named Taylor, was designed to answer messages from people aged 18-24. 3 Taylor was supposed to be able to learn from the messages she received. 4 She was designed to slowly improve her ability to handle conversations, but some people were teaching Taylor racist ideas. 5 When she started saying nice things about Hitler, Microsoft turned her off and deleted her ugliest messages.?
1 AlphaGo’s victory and Taylor’s defeat happened at about the same time. 2 This should be a warning to us. 3 It is one thing to use AI within a game with clear rules and clear goals. 4 It is something very different to use AI in the real world. 5 The unpredictability of the real world may bring to the surface a troubling software problem.
1 Eric Schmidt is one of the bosses of Google, which own AlphaGo. 2 He thinks AI will be positive for humans. 3 He said people will be the winner, whatever the outcome. 4 Advances in AI will make human beings smarter, more able and “just better human beings.”?

【定位及答案】

由题干中的the example of AlphaGo's victory定位到第一段。定位段指出，阿尔法围棋程序的胜利例证了计算机已经变得有多聪明，即计算机可以变得非常智能，故答案为D)。且该例子位于文章首段，有引出文章主题的功能，故该例子也是为了呼应文章主题，应结合文章整体主旨考虑。


【错误选项分析】

A 选项【过度推理】：虽然文章一开始就提到阿尔法围棋程序的胜利例证了计算机已经变得有多聪明，但不可将其夸大为计算机将会在各方面战胜人类，可以排除A)“计算机将会战胜人类”；

B选项【反向干扰】：文章最后一段表明人类才是最终的胜利者，用unmatched来形容计算机的潜力太绝对，计算机终将不可能超越人类，故可以排除B)“计算机有难以匹敌的潜力”；

C选项【反向干扰】：文章最后一段指出人工智能对人类将是有利的存在，由此可见计算机并非人类的潜在对手，而是可以为人类服务的工具，可以排除C)“计算机是人类潜在的对手”。

Rescue crews pulled a man to safety after a collapse at a construction site in Brooklyn on Tuesday.
The incident happened on the 400 block of Rutland Road just after 12：30 p.m.
The Fire Department of New York says the vacant 100-year-old building being pulled down partially collapsed.
A man described as a "non-worker civilian" was buried up to his waist in the basement.
The man was collecting building materials when the first floor collapsed underneath him.
He was trapped under a beam about 10 feet below the surface for nearly an hour and a half.
The man was then taken to hospital.
Officials said he is in stable condition with non-life threatening injuries.
The building was reportedly purchased by a neighboring church in 2011.
It was the site of a 2006 fire and has remained vacant ever since.

Being bad at maths should no longer be seen as a badge of honor or down to genetics, according to National Numeracy, a new organization which aims to challenge the nation 's negative view of the subject.
Chris Humphries, chairman of the group, said that poor maths skills can affect an individual 's life, leaving them at a higher risk of being excluded from school, or out of work.

I can 't do math 's attitude that is prevalent in the UK, " adding that it was vital that all primary school teachers understand key maths concepts, as young children who fail to learn the basics will suffer later on.

My grandparents started the company in 1955.

All parents know it is difficult to get children to eat their vegetables.

But researchers have discovered that youngsters who are not praised for trying vegetables are more likely to eat them eventually.
The study found that the best way to get children to eat food they do not like is simply to give them repeated exposure to it.
Psychologists from Ghent University in Belgium studied 98 children.
They gave them five kinds of vegetables to eat —— mushrooms, peas, eggplants, carrots and cabbages.
The taste tests revealed that carrots were the least-liked vegetable among youngsters.

The other two groups were given rewards of a toy or verbal praise.

The other rubbish comes from missions that did not have human crews.

In my line of work, I receive a lot of emails.
I also send a lot of emails.
Though social media and messaging apps have taken over some of the roles from email as a form of communication, email is likely to retain an important role for business communication in the future.
Surprisingly, though, a lot of companies and organizations lack formal guidelines for emailing.
As most of you will soon be entering the workforce, I would like to share with you my own rules for emailing.
If someone sends you an email, reply to them acknowledging the email.
A simple "thank you" let the sender know that their email has arrived safely, that it has not been lost among what could be 50 other emails that have arrived in your email inbox that day.
It's not necessary to reply to a mass email sent to numerous recipients.
These emails are often informative rather than personalized correspondence requiring a response or action.
But it's common politeness to respond to a personal message, preferably within 24 hours of receiving it.
It's also important to use proper English.
Just because emails are a quick form of communication, doesn't mean emails, especially business emails, should be written using informal shortened forms of words.
Think of an email as a letter.
Spelling, grammar and punctuation should not be overlooked.
And never use capitals to emphasize a word or words in an email.
It's the same as yelling.

questions.answer: 1 It is a fact that more and more Chinese can hardly do without their mobile phones nowadays. 2 Many of them, including senior citizens, use mobile apps to keep in touch and expand their circle of friends. 3 They also use mobile phones to shop online and search for information because they are portable. 4 What's more, communication through mobile apps costs less than traditional phones. 5 However, this new trend results in the over dependency on mobile phones in social contact. 6 As a matter of fact, some young people have become so addicted to mobile phones that they have neglected the face-to-face communication with their family and friends.

questions.explanation:
【考点】

名词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格位于不定冠词a之后，空格后面为介词to，因此空格处需要填一个名词。

【答案解析】

本句指出，通过语音信箱消息向下属传递，结合备选名词，warning“告诫”一词能体现上级与下属之间的关系，故为正确选项。通读文章可以发现，本文是在说明如何传递棘手消息，reward意为“报酬，奖赏”，是好消息，不符合文章主旨，故排除。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格后面为并列连词and，故空格处所填词与and后面的名词productivity为并列关系。因此，空格处需要填入名词。

【答案解析】

本句提到，我们手头上的各种通信方式带来了效率等好处。再根据and表示的并列关系，空格处所填名词应为褒义而且可以和productivity并列， 由此确定convenience“方便，便利”为答案。

【考点】

副词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格所在部分句子结构完整，因此空格处应填人一个副词， 修饰when引导的从句。

【答案解析】

本句指出，当要传递的消息对接收者来说是坏消息或是不希望听到的消息时，管��者该怎样作出最佳选择。备选副词中，particularly意为“特别，尤其”，强调一种特殊的情况，符合句意，故为答案。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格位于We've之后，名词短语之前，由此判断空格处应填人动词的过去分词构成完成时。

【答案解析】

空格所在部分指出，我们务沟通顾问和礼仪专家。备选动词中，surveyed为过去分词形式，意为“调查”，符合句意，且与下文内容相呼应，故为正确答案。

【考点】

副词辨析题。

【词性分析】

分析句子结构可知，本句句子结构完整，因此空格处应填入副词。

【答案解析】

空格所在句指出，我们调查了商务沟通顾问和礼仪专家，为使用不同的方式传递棘手信息提供了以下指导。备选副词中，effectively“有效地”符合句意， 故为答案。

【考��】

形容词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格位于is the most之后，故空格处应填入形容词。

【答案解析】

通过上下文可知，本句论述的是面对面交流的特点，下一句则指出私人化程度逐级降低的交流方式。备选形容词中，intimate“亲密的”符合句意，表示面对面交流是最亲密的沟通方式，因此为正确答案。

【考点】

形容词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格位于the most之后，is email之前，所以空格处应填入形容词使结构完整，而且该词应该可以用于形容电子邮件的特点。

【答案解析】

本句承接前一句的面对面交流的方式，对其他几种交流方式进行了私人化程度降序排列，由此可知，越往后的交流方式越不私人化。结合备选形容词可知，电子邮件应该是最“不友好的”， 故unfriendly“不友好的”为正确答案。

【考点】

形容词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格位于定冠词the之后，名词situation之前，因此空格处需要填入形容词， 用于修饰其后的名词situation。

【答案解析】

上一句说明儿种沟通方式通常情况下排序。本句指出，其中一些可能会根据情况或个人的偏好改变顺序。备选形容词中，只有specific“具体的，特有的”满足语义要求， 与situation构成搭配，表示“具体情况”，故为答案。

【考点】

形容词辨析题，

【词性分析】

空格前面为My，后面为名词concern，所以空格处需要填入形容词， 作concern 的定语。

【答案解析】

本句中说明了礼仪专家达纳·卡斯帕森的观点：我_____关心的是，我怎样才能温和或文明地传达这条信息呢?备选形容词中，primary意为“主要的”，代入句中表示“如何温和或文明地传达这条信息是礼仪专家最关心的”，符合句意，故为正确答案。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

分析句子结构可知，空格位于修饰something的定语从句中，从句缺少谓语动词，因此空格处应填人动词使结构完整。结合时态来看，空格处应填入动词原形。

【答案解析】

前一句说明达纳对道歉方式的选择；优先选择当面道歉，然后依次是打电话和手写便条。结合上文所述的使用电子邮件是最不友好的的可知，本句应指达纳不会选择使用电子邮件道歉。备选动词原形中， avoid意为“避免”， 代入句中表示“完全避免使用电子邮件道歉”，符合句意，故为正确选项。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 The busy streets in Paris were uneven and caked in thick mud, but there was always a breathtaking sight to see in the shop windows of Patisserie de la Rue de la Paix. 2 By 1814, people crowded outside the bakery, straining for a glimpse of the latest sweet food created by the young chef who worked inside.?
1 His name was Marie-Antoine Carême, and he had appeared, one day, almost out of nowhere. 2 But in his short lifetime, which ended exactly 184 years ago today, he would forever revolutionize French gourmet food （美食）, write best-selling cook books and think up magical dishes for royals and other important people.?
1 Carême's childhood was one part tragedy, equal part mystery. 2 Born the 16th child to poor parents in Paris in either 1783 or 1784, a young Carême was suddenly abandoned at the height of the French Revolution. 3 At 8 years old, he worked as a kitchen boy for a restaurant in Paris in exchange for room and board. 4 By age 15, he had become an apprentice （学徒） to Sylvain Bailly, a well-known dessert chef with a successful bakery in one of Paris 's most fashionable neighborhoods.?
1 Carême was quick at learning in the kitchen. 2 Bailly encouraged his young apprentice to learn to read and write. 3 Carême would often spend his free afternoons at the nearby National Library reading books on art and architecture.? 4 In the back room of the little bakery, his interest in design and his baking talent combined to work wonders — he shaped delicious masterpieces out of flour, butter and sugar.
1 In his teenage years, Carême fashioned eatable copies of the late 18th century's most famous buildings — cookies in the shape of ruins of ancient Athens and pies in the shape of ancient Chinese palaces and temples. 2 Sylvain Bailly, his master, displayed these luxuriant creations — often as large as 4 feet tall — in his bakery windows.?
1 Carême's creations soon captured the discriminating eye of a French diplomat, Charles Maurice de Talleyrand-Périgord. 2 Around 1804, Talleyrand challenged Carême to produce a full menu for his personal castle, instructing the young baker to use local, seasonal fruits and vegetables and to avoid repeating main dishes over the course of an entire year. 3 The experiment was a grand success and Talleyrand's association with French nobility would prove a profitable connection for Carême.?
1 French Emperor Napoleon Bonaparte was known to be unimpressed by the declining taste of early 18th century cooking, but under pressure to entertain Paris's high society, he too called Carême to his kitchen at Tuileries Palace. 2 In 1810, Carême designed the extraordinary cake for the wedding of Napoleon and his second bride, Marie-Louise of Austria. 3 He became one of the first modern chefs to focus on the appearance of his table, not just the flavor of his dishes. 4 “I want order and taste. 5 A well-displayed meal is enhanced one hundred percent in my eyes,” he later wrote in one of his cook books.?
1 In 1816, Carême began a culinary (烹饪的) journey which would forever mark his place as history's first top chef. 2 He voyaged to England to cook in the modern Great Kitchen of the prince regent (摄政王), George Ⅳ, and crossed continents to prepare grand banquets for the tables of Tsar Alexander Ⅰ of Russia. 3 Never afraid to talk up his own accomplishments, a boastful Carême made a fortune as wealthy families with social ambitions invited him to their kitchens.? 4 Later, in his cook books, he would often include a sketch of himself, so that people on the street would be able to recognize — and admire — him.
1 Carême's cooking displays became the symbol of fine French dining; they were plentiful, beautiful and imposing. 2 Guests would fall silent in wonder as servants carried Carême's fancy creations into the dining hall. 3 For a banquet celebrating the Grand Duke Nicholas of Russia's visit to George Ⅳ's Brighton Pavillion on Jan. 18, 1817, the menu featured 120 different dishes, highlighting eight different soups, 40 main courses, and 32 desserts.
1 As he traveled through the homes of early 19th century nobility, Carême forged the new art of French gourmet food. 2 Locked in hot kitchens, Carême created his four “mother sauces.” 3 These sauces — béchamel, velouté, espagnole and allemande — formed the central building blocks for many French main courses. 4 He also perfected the soufflé — a baked egg dish, and introduced the standard chef's uniform — the same double-breasted white coat and tall white hat still worn by many chefs today. 5 The white clothing conveyed an image of cleanliness, according to Carême — and in his realm, appearance was everything.
1 Between meals, Carême wrote cook books that would be used in European kitchens for the next century. 2 His manuals including The Royal Parisian Baker and the massive five-volume Art of French Cooking Series (1833-1847, completed after his death) first systematized many basic principles of cooking, complete with drawings and step-by-step directions.? 3 Long before television cooking shows, Carême walked readers through common kitchen tasks, instructing them to “try this for yourself, at home” as famous American Chef Julia Child might do, many years later.
1 In the end, however， it was the kitchen that did Carême in. 2 Decades of working over coal fires in tight, closed spaces with little fresh air (to ensure his dishes would not get cold) had fatally damaged his lungs. 3 On Jan. 12, 1833, Carême died just before he turned 50.
1 But in his lifetime, Carême, ever confident, could see beyond his short domination in the kitchen. 2 He wanted to “set the standard for beauty in classical and modern cooking, and prove to the distant future that the French chefs of the 19th century were the most famous in the world,” as he wrote in his papers.?
1 Decades later, chef Auguste Escoffier would build upon Carême's concept of French cuisine （烹饪）. 2 But in the very beginning, there was just Carême, the top chef who elevated dining into art.

questions.explanation:
【定位】

由题干中的appearance和flavor定位到文章G)段第三句。

【答案解析】

同义转述题、定位句提到，他成为第一批不只关注菜肴味道而且关注菜品外观的现代大厨之一。定位句中���He指的就是Careme。题干中的stressed both the appearance and flavor of dishes对应原文中的“...focus on the appearance of his table，not just the flavor of his dishes...”，故答案为G)。

【定位】

由题干中的French chefs和most outstanding定位到文章M)段最后一句。

【答案解析】

同义转述题，定位句指出��卡雷姆想要为经典和现代烹饪设立美学标准，并向子孙后代证明，19世纪的法国厨师是世界上最有名的。题干中的later generations和most outstanding分别对应定位句中的the distant future和most famous：而题干中的of his time指的就是定位句中的of the 19th century，故答案为Ｍ)。

【定位】

由题干中的a French diplomat和connections定位到文章F)段，

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位段前几句指出，卡雷姆为一位法国外交官査尔斯·莫里斯·德·塔利朗-佩里戈尔德服务，为他的个人城堡制作一份完整的束单。最后一句作出总结，卡雷姆取得了巨大的成功，同时塔利朗与法国贵族的交往关系也证明对卡雷姆有利。由此可知，卡雷姆为一名法国外交官和他的人脉脚服务，从中获益颇丰。题干是对这段细节的归纳和总结，故答案为F)。

【定位】

由题干中的dessert chef定位到文章C) 段最后一句。

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，到了15岁的时侯，卡雷姆已经成为西尔万·贝利的学徒。西尔万·贝利是一位著名的甜品师，在巴黎最时尚的街区之一拥有一家成功的面包店。题干中的learned his trade from是对定位句中become an apprentice to的同义转述，而题干中的a famous dessert chef in Paris指的就是Sylvain Bailly，故答案为C)。

【定位】

由题干中的the shop windows和his master定位到文章E)段最后一句

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，他的师傅西尔万·贝利把这些华丽的作品—通常有4英尺高—展示在他的面包店的橱窗里。题干中的creative works对应定位句中的creations，指代该段首句提到的18世纪后期最著名建筑的可食版作品，题干中的exhibited对应定位句中的displayed，故答案为E)。

【定位】

由题干中的art and architecture定位到文章D)段第三句。

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句提到，卡雷姆经常在下午有空的时候泡在附近的国家图书馆里读一些有关艺术和建筑的书籍。按下来的一句介绍，他用面粉，黄油和糖塑造出了美味的杰作。题干是对本段第三、四句的总结。题干中的create extraordinary desserts和ordinary ingredients分别对应原文中的shaped delicious  master piceces和“...flour，butter and sugar。”， 故答案为D)

【定位】

由题干中的the latest sweet food定位到文章A)段最后一句。

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，到1814年时，人们会挤在店门外，争着瞧一眼在里面工作的年轻厨师创制的最新甜食。题干中的were eager to和have a look at分别对应定位句中的straining for和a glimpse of，题干中的Careme就是定位句中的the young chef，故答案为A)。

【定位】

由题干中的socially ambitious families定位到文章H)段倒数第二句。

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，从不畏惧大肆赞扬他自己的成就，自负的卡雷姆发了一大笔财，因为一些有社会野心的富裕家庭会邀请他去他们的厨房。题干中的became extremely wealthy和rich and socially ambitious families分别对应定位句中的made a fortune和wealthy families with social ambitions，故答案为H) 。

【定位】

由题干中的cooking principles和in a systematic way定位到文章K) 段第二句。

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，卡雷姆所撰写的烹饪指南首次将很多烹饪的基本原理系统化，并且书中还配有插图和一步步的操作指南。题干中的fundamental cooking principles和systematic way分别是对定位句中basic principles of cooking和systematized的同义转述，故答案为K)。

【定位】

由题干中的revolutionary定位到文章B) 段第二句。

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，在卡雷姆短暂的一生中，他彻底地改变了法国美食。题干中的French cooking和revolutionary分别对应定位句中的French gourmet food和revolutionize，故答案为B)。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 Roughly the size of a soda can, sitting on a bookshelf, a relatively harmless gadget may be turning friends away from your home.? 2 The elephant in your living room is your Internet-connected security camera, a device people are increasingly using for peace of mind in their homes. 3 But few stop to think about the effect these devices may have on house guests. 4 Should you tell your friends, for instance, that they're being recorded while you all watch the big game together?
1 “It's certainly new territory, especially as home security cameras become easier to install,” says Lizzie Post, president of the Emily Post Institute, America's foremost manners advisors.? 2 “I think it will be very interesting to see what etiquette (礼仪) emerges in terms of whether you tell people you have a camera or not, and whether guests have a right to ask that it be turned off, if it's not a security issue.”
1 Post wants to make clear that she's not talking about legal rights, but rather personal preference.? 2 She also wants to explain that there are no right or wrong answers regarding manners on this front yet, because the technology is just now becoming mainstream. 3 Besides, the Emily Post Institute doesn't dictate manners.
1 When it comes to security cameras, Post says it's a host's responsibility to make sure guests feel comfortable within their home.? 2 “I'm always a fan of being open and honest.” 3 For instance, if the host casually acknowledges that there is a camera in the room by telling a story about it, that may be enough to provide an opening for a guest to say if they are uncomfortable.
1 However, if a contractor is working in your home, you don't need to tell them that there are cameras watching. 2 Then again, the air of accountability that the camera generates can also work in contractors' favor.? 3 “If anything does go wrong while they're in the house, they don't want to be blamed for it,” she says. 4 “In fact, the camera could be the thing that proves that they didn't steal the $20, or knock the vase off the table.”

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

For what reason may your friends feel reluctant to visit your home?

为什么你的朋友不愿意来你家？

A) The security camera installed may intrude into their privacy.

家中安装的摄像头可能会侵犯到他们的隐私

B) They don’t want their photos to be circulated on the Internet.

他们不希望自己的照片在网上传播

C) The security camera may turn out to be harmful to their health.

安全摄像头可能会对他们的健康有害

D) They may not be willing to interact with your family members.

他们可能不愿意和你的家人交流

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的feel reluctant to visit your home和题文同序原则定位到1段①句。文章开篇第一句指出，一个相对没什么危险的小玩意儿，大致只有苏打水易拉罐那么大，可能会让朋友对你家敬而远之。作者在本段最后提出一个问题：朋友在你家一起观看大型比赛时，你会告诉他们，他们都被录下来了吗?由这两句可知，朋友不愿到家中做客可能是因为在家中安装摄像头会侵犯朋友的隐私，故答案为A)。

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【无中生有&过度推理】：原文未提及朋友的照片问题，B)“他们不希望自己的照片在网上传播”为过度推断，可以排除。

C选项【过度推理】：本段倒数第二句指出“But few stop to think about the effect these devices may have on house guests.”，选项C) 错误地将句中的effect过度推断为对身体健康的影响，原文未提及有关健康的信息，因此可以排除C)“安全摄像头可能会对他们的健康有害”

D选项【无中生有】：原文并未提及D)“他们可能不愿意和你的家人交流”，可以排除。

choices.label: B

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What does Lizzie Post say is new territory?

利齐·波斯特说什么是新领域？

A) The effect of manners advice on the public.

礼仪方面的建议对公众的影响

B) Cost of applying new technologies at home.

在家里应用新技术的成本

C) The increasing use of home security devices.

家庭安全设备日益广泛的应用

D) Etiquette around home security cameras.

家庭安全摄像头周围的礼仪

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Lizzie Post和new territory定位到2段①句。定位句提到了美国首席礼仪顾问、艾米丽·波斯特学院院长利兹·波斯特的话：这当然是一个新领域，尤其是当家庭安全摄像头变得更容易安装的时候。下文指出，波斯特认为看看主人和客人在处理家庭安全摄像头问题时会出现什么样的礼仪是非常有趣的。由此可知，定位句中的new territory“新领域”是指家庭安全摄像头涉及的礼仪，故答案为D)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【无中生有】：原文未提及“礼仪方面的建议对公众的影响”，可以排除A)。

B选项【无中生有】：本段第一句指出家庭安全摄像头变得更容易安装了，但并未提及有关安装成本的信息，可以排除B)“在家里应用新技术的成本”。

C选项【答非所问】：C)的干扰性较大。第一段第二句指出，越来越多的人在他们的家中使用家庭安全摄像头以求心安，但波斯特所谈论的话题并不是安全摄像头的应用范围的问题，而是其中涉及的礼仪问题。考生应注意波斯特是美国首席礼仪顾问，是礼仪方面的专家，文中引用她的观点一定是为了论证和礼仪相关的问题，同时要注意正确选项一定与本文主旨相关，因此排除C)“家庭安全设备日益广泛的应用”。

【题目及选项概览】

What is Lizzie Post mainly discussing with regard to the use of home security cameras?

关于家庭安全摄像头的使用，Lizzie Post主要讨论什么？

A) Legal rights.   

法律权利

B) Moral issues   

道德问题

C) Likes and dislikes of individuals.

个人喜好

D) The possible impact on manners.

可能对礼仪造成的影响

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Lizzie Post、the use of home security cameras和选项内容定位到3段①句。定位句指出，波斯特想澄清的是，她讨论的不是法律权利问题，而是个人偏好问题。由此可知，波斯特想讨论的是个人偏好问题.选项C) Likes and dislikes of individuals对应定位句中的personal preferences，故答案为C).

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【反向干扰】：A)“法律权利”与定位句的表述矛盾，可以排除。

B选项【无中生有】：本文未提及道德问题，可以排除B)“道德问题”。根据定位段可知，D选项【答非所问】：D)“可能对礼仪造成的影响”并非波斯特主要讨论的问题，可以排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: Making their guests feel at ease.

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What is a host’s responsibility regarding security cameras, according to Lizzie Post?

利齐·波斯特说，主持人对安全摄像头的责任是什么？

A) Making their guests feel at ease.

确保客人在做客时感到舒适

B) Indicating where they are.

指出它们在哪里

C) Turning them off in time.

及时关闭它们

D) Ensuring their guests’ privacy.

确保客人的隐私

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的a host's responsibility定位到4段①句。定位句提到，当说到安全摄像头，波斯特认为，主人有责任确保客人在做客时感到舒适。选项A) Making their guests feel at ease对应定位句中的make sure guests feel comfortable，故答案为A)。

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【过度推理】：4段指出，如果主人通过讲述一件有关摄像头的事儿来漫不经心地承认房间里有摄像头，这也许就足够为客人提供一个机会来表达他们是否觉得不舒服。文章未提及B)“指出它们在哪里”，可以排除。

C选项【过度推理】：本段并未指出波斯特认为主人的责任是要关闭摄像头，C)“及时关闭它们”为过度推断，可以排除。

D选项【无中生有】：文章未提及D)“确保客人的隐私”，可以排除。

choices.label: C
choices.text: It can help them learn new technology.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It can make their visit more enjoyable.

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

In what way can the home security camera benefit visitors to your home?

家庭安全摄像头能以什么方式让到家的访客受益？

A) It can satisfy their curiosity.

它能满足他们的好奇心

B) It can prove their innocence.

它可以证明访客的清白

C) It can help them learn new technology.

它可以帮助他们学习新技术

D) It can make their visit more enjoyable.

它可以使他们的访问更愉快

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的benefit visitors定位5段②句。定位句指出，摄像头所产生的负责任的氛围也对承包商有利。在后面的两句中，波斯特举例说明益处所在：他们施工期间，如果家里确实出了问题，他们不想因此受到指责；摄像头会成为证明他们没偷那20美元或者没碰掉桌上花瓶的东西。由此可知，家庭安全摄像头可证明访客的清白，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A/C/D选项【无中生有】：文中没有提及A)“它能满足他们的好奇心”、C)“它可以帮助他们学习新技术”和D)“它可以使他们的访问更愉快”，均可以排除。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 PepsiCo is to spend billions of dollars to develop drinks and snacks and reformulate existing ones with lower sugar, salt and fat, as consumers demand healthier options and regulatory pressure intensifies amid an obesity epidemic （流行病）.?
1 The maker of Mountain Dew and Gatorade has been one of the earlier movers in the industry to offer products with reduced levels of unhealthy ingredients — PepsiCo claims a packet of its chips now contains less salt than a slice of white bread. 2 However, its new 10-year plan makes clear it believes it still has a long way to go.?
1 Shifting eating habits, including a sharp drop in consumption of sparkling drinks, have forced radical change on the industry. 2 But those shifts have yet to be reflected in record obesity levels, which stand at 36.5% overall in the US.
1 Indra Nooyi, PepsiCo chairman, said the plan to make its products healthier was important for the company's growth.? 2 But on the subject of obesity, she pointed out that consumers’ lifestyles have changed significantly, with many people being more sedentary (久坐不动的) not least because more time is spent in front of computers.? 3 She said PepsiCo's contribution was to produce healthier snacks that still tasted good.
1 “Society has to change its habits,” she added. 2 “We can't do much to alter sedentary lifestyles, but we can provide consumers with great-tasting products, low in salt, sugar and fat. 3 In the past we had to have a taste trade-off. But we're breaking that trade-off.”
1 PepsiCo's plan for its foods and drinks is based on guidelines from the World Health Organisation, which last week backed using taxes on sparkling drinks to reduce sugar consumption.? 2 Initiatives also include efforts to reduce its environmental impact, water consumption and materials used in packaging by 2025.
1 PepsiCo did not say exactly how much it planned to invest to reach its goals. 2 However, Dr Mehmood Khan, chief scientific officer, said the company had doubled research and development spending in the past five years and was “committed to sustaining investment”, adding that companies cannot cost-cut their way to increasing sales. 3 PepsiCo's research and development budget in 2015 was $754 million.

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

Why is PepsiCo making a policy change?

百事为什么要改变政策？

A) To win support from the federal government.

为了赢得联邦政府的支持

B) To be more competitive in the global market.

在全球市场上更具竞争力

C) To satisfy the growing needs for healthy foods.

去满足消费者对健康食品的需求

D) To invest more wisely in the soft drink industry.

更明智地投资软饮料行业

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的PepsiCo和change定位到1段。定位段指出，在肥胖流行病的肆虐之下，消费者要求更健康的食品，监管压力也与日俱增，因此百亭公司计划斥资数十亿美元开发饮料和零食，同时现���的产品也改用低糖、低盐和低脂的配方。由此可知，百事公司故变策略是为了满足消费者对健康食品的需求，故答案为C).

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【过度推理】：定位段提到了监管的压力与日俱增，但并不能由此推出百事公司改变策略是为了赢得联邦政府的支持，可以排除A)。

B/D选项【无中生有】：原文没有提到B)“在全球市场上更具竞争力”和D)“更明智地投资软饮料行业”，可以排除。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What does PepsiCo think it will have to do in the future?

百事公司认为未来该怎么办？

A) Invest more to develop new snacks.

多投资来开发新零食

B) Reduce levels of obesity in the US.

降低美���的肥胖水平

C) Change consumers’ eating habits.

改变消费者的饮食习惯

D) Keep on improving its products.

继续改善产品

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的PepsiCo和in the future定位到2段。定位段第一句后半部分及②句提到，百事公司声称，现在一包百事薯条的盐含量比一片白面包还少。然而，该公司新发布的十年计划表明，公司认为仍然还有一段漫长的路要走。由此可知，这条路指的是改进产品使其变得更健康，即百事公司在未来十年会继续改进产品，故答案为D)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【答非所问】：文章在1段虽然提到了百事公司计划开发饮料和零食，但这并非该公司的宏观计划，不是最优选项，可以排除A)“多投资来开发新零食”。

B选项【无中生有】：3段指出，饮料零食业发生了根本性的变化，但这些变化并不足以影响美国创纪录的肥胖率。文章并未提及百事公司的计划是要降低美国的肥胖水平，可以排除B)“降低美国的肥胖水平”。

C选项【过度推理】：3段①句指出，人们饮食习惯的改变，包括气泡饮料消费量的大幅下降，已迫使该行业发生了根本性的变化，但并不能由此推出百事公司的计划是要改变人们的饮食习惯，可以排除C)“改变消费者的饮食习惯”。

【题目及选项概览】

Why does PepsiCo plan to alter its products, according to Indra Nooyi?

英德拉•诺伊称，百事公司为何计划改变产品？

A) To ensure the company’s future development.

确保公司的未来发展

B) To adapt to its customers’ changed taste.

去适应消费者变化的口味

C) To help improve its consumers’ lifestyles.

去帮助提升消费者的生活方式

D) To break the trade-off in its product design.

去打破其在产品设计方面的妥协局面

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Indra Nooyi定位到4段①句。定位句指出，百事公司董事长英德拉·努伊表示，这项旨在为消费者提供更健康产品的计划对公司的发展很重要。由此可知，百事公司改变产品对于公司的未来发展非常重要，选项A) 中的ensure the company's future development对应定位句中的was important for the company's growth，故答案为A)。

 

【错误选项分析】

B/C选项【无中生有】：百事公司董事长英德拉·努伊并没有提到百事公司改变产品是为了适应客户口味的变化和帮助改善消费者的生活方式，可以排除B)和C)。

D选项【偷换概念】：5段最后一句指出，百事公司之前不得不牺牲口味才能做到平衡，但现在该公司正在打破这种妥协局面。选项D)“打破其在产品设计方面的妥协局面”是对原文意思的曲解，可以排除。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What does Indra Nooyi say about the obesity epidemic?

关于肥胖的流行，英德拉·努伊怎么说？

A) It is mainly caused by overconsumption of snacks.

这主要是由对零食的过度食用造成的

B) It results from high sugar and salt consumption.

它是摄人高糖、高盐的结果

C) It is attributable to people’s changed lifestyles.

它主要归结于人们的生活方式的变化

D) It has a lot to do with longer working hours.

这与较长的工作时间有很大关系

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Indra Nooyi和obesity epidemic定位到4段②句。定位句提到，在肥胖这个问题上，英德拉·努伊指出消费者的生活方式发生了很大的变化，许多人久坐不动的时间更长了，这不仅仅是因为人们要花更多的时间在电脑前办公。由此可知，英德拉·努伊认为美国的肥胖问题主要是因为人们的生活方式发生了改变，故答案为C)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A/B选项【无中生有】：英德拉·努伊并没有提及A)“这主要是由对零食的过度食用造成的”和B)“它是摄人高糖、高盐的结果”，可以排除。

D选项【偷换概念】：定位句指出，是人们久坐的习惯等生活方式的改变造成了美国的肥胖问题，而非人们工作时间很长造成了美国的肥胖问题，D)“这与较长的工作时间有很大关系”与原文表述不一致，可以排除。

【题目及选项概览】

What has PepsiCo been doing to achieve its objective?

百事公司为实现目标做了什么？

A) Studying WHO’s guidelines.  

研究世界卫生组织的指导方针

B) Increasing its research funding.

致力于保持投资

C) Expanding its market overseas.

拓展其海外市场 

D) Cutting its production costs.

降低其生产成本

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的achieve its objective定位到6段①句。定位句指出，百事公司没有具体说明计划投入多少资金以实现这一目标。接下来一句指出，该公司首席科学官穆罕默德·可汗博士表示，在过去五年中，百事公司的研发支出增加了一倍，并称该公司“致力于保持投资”。由此可知，为了实现自己的目标，百事公司一直在增加研发经费，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【过度推理】：文章6段指出，百事公司的食品和饮料计划是根据世界卫生组织的指导方针制订的，并不能由此推出该公司为了实现自己的目标一直在研究世界卫生组织的指导方针，可以排除A)“研究世界卫生组织的指导方针”。

C选项【无中生有】：本文并未提及C)“拓展其海外市场”，可以排除。

D选项【反向干扰】：定位句指出，企业无法通过削减成本来增加销售量，选项D)“降低其生产成本”的表述与文章意思矛盾，可以排除。

1 The recent years have witnessed a sharp rise in the number of college students who successfully start their careers after graduation.
1 However, many others fail to do so because the transition from a student to an employee is actually full of challenges. 2 First of all, you might not be popular with every colleague, which is frustrating for a newcomer in the work place. 3 So you'd better try to make a good impression on all of your workmates, especially your boss. 4 Furthermore, there probably is a gap between what you learned at school and what you are required to do at work. 5 You have to learn quickly and avoid making too many stupid mistakes. 6 Finally, you may find you are always on a tight budget because of the low salary for a new graduate and all kinds of living expenses, which make it difficult to make ends meet.
1 As the old proverb goes, “ Well begun is half done.” 2 If you can handle these challenges skillfully after graduation, you will clear the path for further career development, either job promotion or starting your own business. 3 So hang on in there and never give up!

sections.title: Section A 选词填空
sections.passage: 1 A few months ago, I was down with a terrible cold which ended in a persistent bad cough. 2 No matter how many different 1 I tried, I still couldn’t get rid of the cough.? 3 Not only did it 2 my teaching but also my life as a whole.? 4 Then one day after class, a student came up to me and 3 traditional Chinese medicine.? 5 From her description, Chinese medicine sounded as if it had magic power that worked wonders. 6 I was 4 because I knew so little about it and have never done it before.? 7 Eventually, my cough got so much 5 that I couldn’t sleep at night, so I decided to give it a try.? 8 The Chinese doctor took my pulse and asked to see my tongue, both of which were new 6 to me because they are both non-existent in Western medicine.? 9 Then the doctor gave me a scraping (刮) treatment known as “ Gua Sha “. 10 I was a little 7 at first because he used a smooth edged tool to scrape the skin on my neck and shoulders.? 11 A few minutes later, the 8 strokes started to produce a relieving effect and my body and mind began to 9 deeper into relaxation.? 12 I didn’t feel any improvement in my condition in the first couple of days, but after a few more regular visits to the doctor, my cough started to 10.? 13 Then, within a matter of weeks, it was completely gone!

questions.explanation:
【考点】

名词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前面是how many different，故空格处应为名词，且为复数形式。

【答案解析】

文章首句指出，作者因感冒而引发严重的咳嗽。由此可知，作者尝试的事情应与疾病相关。名词选项中，remedies意为“药物”，且为复数形式，从语义和结构上均符合本题要求，故为答案。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前为主语it，指代the cough，后面为宾语my teaching和my life，故推断空格处应为动词，且该句为倒装句，Not only did it后面应为动词原形。

【答案解析】

根据上一句内容，作者的咳嗽一直无法痊愈，那么它带来的结果一定是不好的。备选动词原形中，in convenience有“给……带来不便，添麻烦”的意思，符合句意，且与空格后面的宾语teaching和life相搭配，故为答案。其他备选动词原形中，E) lessen意为“减少，降低”，后面常跟与数量相关的名词，teaching和life无法量化，故排除。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前为came up to me和并列连词and，后面为名词词组traditional Chinese medicine，故推断空格处应为动词过去式。

【答案解析】

上文指出，作者的咳嗽不见好转，给其工作和生活带来了不便。由此推断，本句是指作者的学生提供了解决办法，“推荐”了中医疗法。recommended意为“推荐”，且为过去式，故为答案。

【考点】

语义推断题。

【词性分析】

空格前为was，空格后为because引导的原因状语从句，故推测空格处应为形容词或分词结构。

【答案解析】

由because引导的原因状语从句可知，作者对中医知之甚少，且以前从未尝试过。由此推断，作者必然对此疗法心存疑虑，hesitant意为“犹豫的”，符合语境，故为答案，其他备选词中，G) pressured意为“有压力的”，根据后文，作者一开始并未尝试中医疗法，因此也不存在压力，故排除。J) scared意为“害怕……的， 对……感到惊慌的”，作者仅仅提到对中医知之甚少，以前也从未尝试过，且一开始未打算尝试，因此不会有“害怕”的心理，故排除。

【考点】

形容词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前为my cough got so much，空格后为that引导的从句，故推断空格处应为形容词。

【答案解析】

根据上下文可知，作者起初并未尝试刮痧，而后来却尝试了这种疗法，可见一定是疾病加重引起了这一变化。worse为bad的比较级，意为“病情更重的”，可被much修饰，故为答案。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前为new，故推测空格处应为名词，且根据be动词were可知，名词应为复数形式。

【答案解析】

本句前半部分指出，中医为作者把脉、看舌头；后半部分又说明西医中没有这些方法。因此，new后应为experiences，表示“经历，体验”。其他备选名词中，I) remedies意为“补救法；药物”，把脉和看舌头均为问诊的方法，而非补救法或药物，所以排除。

【考点】

形容词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前为I was a little，空格后为at first和because引导的原因状语从句，故推断空格处应为形容词。

【答案解析】

because引导的原因状语从句指出，医生用一种边缘光滑的工具刮作者颈部和肩膀的皮肤。由此推断，作者可能会有点儿害怕，scared意为“害怕……的，对……感到惊慌的”，故为答案。其他备选形容词中，C) hesitant意为“犹豫的”，常用于描述作选择时的感受， 不符合句意。G) pressured意为“有压力的”，在接受治疗时，“害怕……的”比“有压力的”更适合用来描述病人的心理感受，故排除。

【考点】

语义推断题。

【词性分析】

空格前为the，空格后为名词stroke故推测空格处应为形容词或分词结构。

【答案解析】

本句描述作者接受刮痧治疗后的感受。根据上一句对刮痧的描述，医生用边缘光滑的工具刮作者的皮肤，那么这种刮压应该非常有力，pressured意为“有压力的”，除了表示心理感受，也可以表示身体感受，故为答案。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前为不定式符号to，空格后为deeper into relaxation，故推断空格处应为不及物动词的原形，且和into相搭配。

【答案解析】

本句前半部分指出，这种刮压开始产生一种让人放松的效果。故推断后半部分是说明作者的身心都开始深深沉人一种放松状态。sink意为“下沉， 沉没”， 可以和into搭配，意为“沉浸在，沉入”，故为答案。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前为不定式符号to，空格后无宾语，故推断空格处应为不及物动词的原形。

【答案解析】

本句前半部分指出，在(治疗后的)最初几天，作者没有感到情况有任何好转：后半部分用but进行转折，下一句则明确指出几周后咳嗽完全消失了。由此推断，本句后半部分表示病情有所好转， 咳嗽情况有所减轻。lessen意为“减少，降低”，符合句意，故为答案。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 When you drop a piece of food on the floor, is it really OK to eat if you pick it up within five seconds? 2 An urban food myth contends that if food spends just a few seconds on the floor, dirt and germs won’t have much of a chance to contaminate it. 3 Research in my lab has focused on how food becomes contaminated, and we’ve done some work on this particular piece of wisdom.?
1 While the “five-second rule” might not seem like the most pressing issue for food scientists to get to the bottom of, it’s still worth investigating food myths like this one because they shape our beliefs about when food is safe to eat.
1 So is five seconds on the floor the critical threshold （门槛） that separates a piece of eatable food from a case of food poisoning? 2 It’s a bit more complicated than that. 3 It depends on just how many bacteria can make it from floor to food in a few seconds and just how dirty the floor is.?
1 Wondering if food is still OK to eat after it’s dropped on the floor is a pretty common experience. 2 And it’s probably not a new one either. 3 A well-known, but inaccurate, story about Julia Child may have contributed to this food myth. 4 Some viewers of her cooking show, The French Chef, insist they saw Child drop lamb on the floor and pick it up, with the advice that if they were alone in the kitchen, their guests would never know.?
1 In fact it was a potato pancake, and it fell on the stovetop, not on the floor. 2 Child put it back in the pan, saying, “But you can always pick it up and if you’re alone in the kitchen, who’s going to see it?” 3 But the misremembered story persists. 4 It’s harder to pin down the origins of the oft-quoted five-second rule, but a 2003 study reported that 70% of women and 56% of men surveyed were familiar with the five-second rule and that women were more likely than men to eat food that had dropped on the floor.?
1 So what does science tell us about what a few moments on the floor means for the safety of your food? 2 The earliest research report on the five-second rule is attributed to Jillian Clarke, a high school student participating in a research project at the University of Illinois. 3 Clarke and her colleagues introduced bacteria to floor tiles （瓷砖） and then placed cookies on the tiles for varying times. 4 They reported bacteria were transferred from the tiles to the cookies within five seconds, but didn’t report the specific amount of bacteria that made it from the tiles to the food.?
1 But how many bacteria actually transfer in five seconds? 2 In 2007, my lab at Clemson University published a study in the Journal of Applied Microbiology. 3 We wanted to know if the length of time is in contact with a contaminated surface affected the rate of transfer of bacteria to the food. 4 To find out, we introduced bacteria to squares of tile, carpet or wood. 5 Five minutes after that, we placed either bacon or bread on the surface for 5,30 or 60 seconds, and then measured the number of bacteria transferred to the food. 6 We repeated this exact procedure after the bacteria had been on the surface for 2,4,8 and 24 hours.
1 We found that the number of bacteria transferred to either kind of food didn’t depend much on how long the food was in contact with the contaminated surface — whether for a few seconds or for a whole minute. 2 The overall number of bacteria on the surface mattered more, and this decreased over time after the initial introduction. 3 It looks like what’s at issue is less how long your food stays on the floor and much more how contaminated with bacteria that patch of floor happens to be.?
1 We also found that the kind of surface made a difference as well. 2 Carpets, for instance, seem to be slightly better places to drop your food than wood or tile. 3 When a carpet was contaminated, less than 1% of the bacteria were transferred. 4 But when the food was in contact with tile or wood, 45-70% of bacteria were.
1 Last year, a study from Aston University in the UK used nearly identical parameters （参数） to our study and found similar results. 2 They also reported that 87% of people asked either would eat or had eaten food fallen on the floor.
1 Should you eat food fallen on the floor then? 2 From a food safety standpoint, if you have millions or more bacteria on a surface, 0.1% is still enough to make you sick. 3 Also, certain types of bacteria are extremely harmful, and it takes only a small number to make you sick. 4 For example, 10 bacteria or less of an especially deadly strain of bacteria can cause severe illness and death in people with compromised immune systems. 5 But the chance of these bacteria being on most surfaces is very low.?
1 And it’s not just dropping food on the floor that can lead to bacterial contamination. 2 Bacteria are carried by various “media”, which can include raw food, moist surfaces where bacteria have been left, our hands or skin and from coughing or sneezing （打喷嚏）. 3 Hands, foods and utensils （器皿） can carry individual bacteria living in communities contained within a protective film. 4 These microscopic layers of deposits containing bacteria are known as biofilms and they are found on most surfaces and objects. 5 Biofilm communities can harbor bacteria longer and are very difficult to clean. 6 Bacteria in these communities also have an enhanced resistance to sanitizers （清洁剂） and antibiotics compared to bacteria living on their own.?
1 So the next time you consider eating fallen food, the odds are in your favor that you can eat it without getting sick. 2 But in the rare chance that there is a micro-organism that there is a micro-organism that can make you sick on the exact spot where the food dropped, you can be fairly sure that the bug is on the food you are about to put in your mouth.?
1 Research or common sense tells us that the best thing to do is keep your hands, utensils and other surfaces clean.?

questions.explanation:
【定位】

由题干中的A research project、bacteria和in five seconds定位到文章F) 段第二句和第四句。

 

【答案解析】

细节辨认题。定位句提到了最早的对5秒法则的研究报告。报告指出，细菌在5秒之内从地砖转移到了饼干上，这和题干中指出的细菌在5秒内由地面转移到食物上意思相同，故答案为F)。

【定位】

由题干中的depends much on和the number of bacteria定位到文章C) 段第三句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，这(食物是否被污染)取决于到底有多少细菌会在几秒内从地上进到食物中，以及地面到底有多脏。题干中的the number of bacteria that get on to it与定位句中的how many bacteria can make it from floor to food属于同义转述， 故答案为C) 。很多考生由于H)段中也出现了题干中的关键词，如contaminated、depend much on和number of bacteria等而误选H)，但该段主要讲食物上面的细菌数量是由接触时长和地面的干净程度决定的，而不是讨论食物受污染的判断标准，因此可排除。

【定位】

由题干中的contamination和dropping on the floor定位到文章L) 段前两句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句指出，也不是仅仅把食物掉在地上就会引起细菌污染。细菌可由多种“媒介”携带，包括生的食物、细菌曾经停留的潮湿表面、我们的双手和皮肤，以及咳嗽或打喷嚏。题干指出，食物污染也许由不同的因素导致，这是对定位句的归纳概括，故答案为L)。

【定位】

由题干中的Males和females定位到文章E)段最后一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句最后指出，一项2003年的研究报告指出，女性比男性更有可能吃掉在地上的食物 题干中的food that may have been contaminated对应定位句中的food that had dropped on the floor，题干中的Males are less likely是对定位句中women were more likely的同义转述，故答案为E)。

【定位】

由题干中的The author's research和how food gets contaminated定位到文章A) 段最后一句。

 

【答案解析】

细节辨认题。定位句指出，“我”的实验室的调查主要关注食物是如何被污染的。题干中的centers around和定位句中的focused on表达的意思相同，且后面宾语内容基本一致，故答案为A)。

【定位】

由题干中的Keeping everything clean和the best way定位到文章N) 段。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，研究或常识告诉我们，最好的方法是保持你的双手、器皿和其他表面的清洁。题干中的the best way是对定位句中the best thing的同义转述，题干中的Keeping everything clean是对定位句中“...keep your hands, utensils and other surfaces clean.”的同义转述，故答案为N)。

【定位】

由题干中的Chances和not fall sick定位到文章M)段第一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，所以下次当你考虑吃掉在地上的食物时，对你有利的可能性是吃掉它后你也不会生病。题干中的Chances是对定位句中odds的同义转述，题干中的will not fall sick是对定位句中without getting sick的同义转述，故答案为M)。

【定位】

由题干中的experience和whether or not to eat food picked up from the floor定位到文章D)段第一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，想知道食物在掉落在地上之后是否还可以食用是一个很常见的经历。第二句接着指出，这可能也不是什么新鲜事了。题干中的For along time people have had the experience是对这两句中a pretty common experience和not a new one的总结，故答案为D)。

【定位】

由题干中的Some strains of bacteria和deadly consequences定位到文章K) 段第三、四句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题，定位句指出，某些类型的细菌是非常有害的，只需要一点点就可致病。并举例说明一种特别致命的菌种中的10个或更少的量就能导致免疫系统受揭的人患严重疾病或死亡题干正是表述了这种致命菌种的危害性， 答案为K)。

【定位】

由题干中的bacteria got onto the food利how long the food stayed on a contaminated floor定位到文章H)段第一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，我们发现转移到任何一种食物上的细菌数量并不太取决于食物接触被污染表面的时间长短。题干中的stayed on 是对定位句中was in contact with的同义转述，故答案为H)。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 The latest in cat research reveals that the lovely animal seems to have a basic grasp on both the laws of physics and the ins and outs of cause and effect. 2 What you may not realize, however, is that the learning process actually continues — in your dreams.
1 According to a newly published study, cats seem to be able to predict the location of hiding prey (猎物) using both their ears and an inborn (天生的) understanding of how the physical world works.?
1 In a recent experiment, Japanese researchers taped 30 domestic cats reacting to a container that a team member shook. 2 Some containers rattled (发出响声) ；others did not. 3 When the container was tipped over, sometimes an object fell out and sometimes it didn’t.
1 It turns out that the cats were remarkably smart about what would happen when a container was tipped over. 2 When an object did not drop out of the bottom of a rattling container, they looked at it for a longer time than they did when the container behaved as expected.
1 “Cats use a causal-logical understanding of noise or sounds to predict the appearance of invisible objects,” lead researcher Saho Takagi says in a press release.? 2 The researchers conclude that cats’ hunting style may have developed based on their common-sense abilities to infer where prey is, using their hearing.?
1 Scientists have explored this idea with other endearing creatures: babies. 2 Like cats, babies appear to engage in what’s called “preferential looking”— looking longer at things that are interesting or unusual than things they perceive as normal.?
1 When babies’ expectations are violated in experiments like the ones performed with the cats, they react much like their animal friends. 2 Psychologists have shown that babies apparently expect their world to comply with the laws of physics and cause and effect as early as two months of age.
1 Does the study mean that cats will soon grasp the ins and outs of cause and effect? 2 Maybe. 3 Okay, so cats may not be the next physics faculty members at America’s most important research universities. 4 But by demonstrating their common sense, they’ve shown that the divide between cats and humans may not be that great after all.?

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What do we learn from a newly published study about cats?

我们从一项新发表的关于猫的研究中学到了什么？

A) They can be trained to understand the physical world.

它们可以被训练去理解周围的世界

B) They know what kind of prey might be easier to hunt.

它们知道何种猎物会更容易捕捉

C) They have a natural ability to locate animals they hunt.

它们有一种天生的能力来定位他们猎杀的动物

D) They are capable of telling which way their prey flees.

它们能够辨别猎物逃走的方向

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的a newly published study about cats定位到2段。文章2段指出，根据一项最新发表的研究，猫似乎能够通过自己的耳朵以及一种天生的对于外界如何运转的理解力来预测出隐藏的猎物的位置。定位段中的prey即选项C) 中的animals they hunt，而定位段中的in born和选项C) 中的natural表达的意思也相同，故答案为C)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【反向干扰】：A) 中的be trained和文中的in born相矛盾，可以排除A)“它们可以被训练去理解周围的世界”；

B选项【无中生有】：文中虽然提及猎物，但并未对哪种猎物更容易捕捉进行区分，可以排除B)“它们知道何种猎物会更容易捕捉”；

D选项【偷换概念】：文中predict the location是指预测猎物所在的地点，而非逃走的方向，可以排除D)“它们能够辨别猎物逃走的方向”。

choices.label: D
choices.text: Their mastery of cause and effect.

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What may account for the cats’ response to the noise from the containers?

什么可以解释猫对集装箱噪音的反应？

A) Their inborn sensitivity to noise.

它们天生对噪音的敏感性

B) Their unusual sense of direction.

它们不同寻常的方向感

C) Their special ability to perceive.

它们特殊的察觉能力

D) Their mastery of cause and effect.

它们对因果关系的掌握

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的cats' response to the noise定位到5段①句。文章第五段主要围绕验结论阐述原因，定位句指出，带头的研究高木佐保在一次媒体发布会上说：“猫利用丈噪音或声音的一种因果逻辑理解来预测看见的物体的出现。”定位句中的causal logic a和选项D) 中的cause and effect意思相同，故答案为D)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：文中强调了猫对因果推理的能力，没有提到对噪音的敏感性，可以排除A)“它们天生对噪音的敏感性”；

B选项【无中生有】：文中未提及猫对方向的辨别能力，可以排除B)“它们不同寻常的方向感”；

C选项【范围过大&偷换概念】：C)“它们特殊的察觉能力”这一选项内容过于宽泛，并未指出察觉什么,文中只提到了猫的听觉，未提到视觉，且定位句中的动词predict和题干中的perceive并非同义词，可以排除。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What is characteristic of the way cats hunt, according to the Japanese researchers?

日本研究人员称，猫的捕猎方式有什么特点？

A) They depend on their instincts.

它们依赖本能

B) They rely mainly on their hearing.

它们主要依赖于听觉

C) They wait some time before attack.

它们在攻击前等待一会儿

D) They use both their ears and eyes.

它们用耳朵和眼睛

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的characteristic of the way cats hunt和the Japanese researchers定位到5段最后一句。定位句指出，研究者们总结道，猫的这种捕猎方式也许是基于一种依靠听力来推断猎物位置的常识性能力发展而来。也就是说，猫的捕猜方式的特点是它们主要依赖听力，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：文中提到依靠听力推断猎物位置的常识性能力，未提到本能，可以排除A)“它们依赖本能”；

C选项【无中生有】：文中未提及C)“它们在攻击前等待一会儿”，可以排除；

D选项【范围过大】：文中提到了听力，未提及视力，可以排除D) “它们用耳朵和眼睛”.

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

In what way do babies behave like cats?         

婴儿在什么方面表现得像猫？

A) They focus on what appears odd.

他们专注于那些看起来很奇怪的事情。

B) They view the world as normal.

他们认为世界是常态的

C) They do what they prefer to do.

他们做自己更喜欢的事情

D) They are curious about everything.

他们对所有事物都感到好奇

 

【定位及答案】

出题干中的babies behave like cats定位到6段②句。定位句指出了婴儿和猫的相似之处：和猫一样，小婴儿们也会进行所谓的“选择性观看”一比起那些他们认为寻常的事物，他们对于有趣的事物或是不同寻常的事物会注视更久.定位句中的looking longer和选项A) 中的focus on表达的意思相同， 选项A) 中的odd是对定位句中interesting or unusual的同义转述，故答案为A)。    

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【偷换概念】：虽然文中提及婴儿会对不同寻常的情况更关注，但这并不意味着他们认为世界应该是一成不变的，可以排除B)“他们认为世界是常态的；

C选项【无中生有】：文中来提及C)“他们做自己更喜欢的事情”，可排除；

D选项【偷换概念】：文中只是提到婴儿对不同寻常的事物会格外关注，未指出他们对所有事物都好奇，可以排D)“他们对所有事物都感到好奇”。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What can we conclude about cats from the passage?

从这篇文章中我们能得出什么关于猫的结论？

A) They have higher intelligence than many other animals.

它们比很多其他动物有更高的智力

B) They interact with the physical world much like humans.

它们与物质世界的互动很像人类

C) They display extraordinarily high intelligence in hunting.

它们在捕猎方面展现出了超强的智力

D) They can aid physics professors in their research work.

它们能够在研究方面辅助物理学教授

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的conclude about cats定位到末段最后一句。定位句指出，猫通过展示它们的常识，证明了它们和人类之间的区别也许并没有那么大。这里的“区别也许并没有那么大"需要联系全文的主要内容进行理解，文章主线是在讨论猫和人类在对物理学的规律以及因果关系的来龙去脉的理解上区别也许并没有那么大，也就是选项B) 提到的interact with the physical word much like humans，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A/C选项【无中生有】：文中未提及intelligence，可以排除A) “它们比很多其他动物有更高的智力”和C)“它们在捕猎方面展现出了超强的智力”；

D选项【反向干扰】：文中最后一段指出，猫无法成为物理学教员，可以排除D)“它们能够在研究方面辅助物理学教授”。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 Imagine you enter a car with no steering wheel, no brake or accelerator pedals (踏板). 2 Under a voice-activated command, you say an address. 3 “The fastest route will take us 15.3 minutes. 4 Should I take it?” 5 You say “yes” and you are on your way. 6 The car responds and starts moving all by itself. 7 All you have to do is sit back and relax.
1 How weird would it be if, one day in the future, everyone had such a car? 2 No crazy driving, no insults, no cutting in; traffic laws would be respected and driving much safer. 3 On the other hand, imagine the cost savings for local police enforcement and town budgets without all those speeding and parking tickets.?
1 A new technology has the potential to change modern society in radical ways. 2 There’s no question that self-driving vehicles could be an enormous benefit. 3 The potential for safer cars means accident statistics would drop: some 94% of road accidents in the U.S. involve human error. 4 Older drivers and visually-or physically-impaired people would gain a new level of freedom.? 5 Maintaining safe speeds and being electric, self-driving cars would drastically reduce pollution levels and dependency on non-renewable fuels. 6 Roads would be quieter, people safer.
1 But we must also consider the impact of the new technology on those who now depend on driving for their livelihoods. 2 According to the U.S. 3 Department of Labor, in May 2015 there were 505,560 registered school bus drivers. 4 The American Trucking Association lists approximately 3.5 million professional truck drivers in the U.S.
1 The companies developing self-driving vehicles should be partnering with state and federal authorities to offer retraining for this massive workforce, many of whom will be displaced by the new technology. 2 This is similar to what’s happening in the coal and oil industries, a situation that fuels much of the current political discontent in this country.?
1 New technologies will, and should, be developed. 2 This is how society moves forward. 3 However, progress can’t be one-sided. 4 It is necessary for the companies and state agencies involved to consider the ethical consequences of these potential changes to build a better future for all.?

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What would be the impact of the extensive use of driverless cars?

大量使用无人驾驶汽车会带来什么影响？

A) People would be driving in a more civilized way.

人们会以更文明的方式驾驶汽车

B) It would save local governments a lot of money.

这将为地方政府节省大量资金

C) More policemen would be patrolling the streets.

更多的警察会在街上巡逻

D) Traffic regulations would be a thing of the past.

交通法规将会成为历史

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的impact、the extensive use of driverless cars和题文同序原则定位到2段。定位段指出了广泛使用无人驾驶汽车的影响。末句提到，完全没有超速和停车罚单的情况会为当地警察执法和城市预算节省大量成本。由此可知，这会给当地政府省下很多钱，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【反向干扰】：根据常识可知，无人驾驶汽车并不需要人驾驶，A)“人们会以更文明的方式驾驶汽车”表明开车的还是人，偏离了文章主旨，故可以排除。

C选项【反向干扰】：C)“更多的警察会在街上巡逻”和文中所述的节省警力相矛盾，故可以排除。

D选项【过度推理】：虽然文中描绘了一番和谐交通的前景，但并不能由此推出交通法规会被取缔，故可以排除D)“交通法规将会成为历史”。
