1 That’s the conclusion of a recently 5 study, which analysed 259 bottles from 11 brands sold in nine countries, 6 an average of 325 plastic particles per litre of water.? 2 These microplastics included a 7 commonly known as PET and widely used in the manufacture of clothing and food and 8 containers.? 3 The study was conducted at the State University of New York on behalf of Orb Media, a journalism organisation. 4 About a million bottles are bought every minute, not only by thirsty tourists but also by many of the 2. 1 billion worldwide who live with unsafe drinking water.
1 Confronted with this 9, several bottled-water manufacturers including Nestle and Coca-Cola undertook their own studies using the same methodology.? 2 These studies showed that their water did contain microplastics, but far less than the Orb study suggested. 3 Regardless, the World Health Organisation has launched a review into the 10 health risks of drinking water from plastic bottles.?

questions.explanation:
【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前面有or，说明空格所在部分_____the ruins of Angkor与wandering about on a Thai island构成并列结构。并列结构前后成分要一致， 因此本空应填人动词的-ing形式。

【答案解析】

本句是在设想出国旅游的情形。空格前面提到，想象你正在泰国的一个小岛上漫步，空格后面应该表示你在“欣赏”或者“游览”吴哥遗址。因此， 本题答案为B) admiring。

【考点】

语义推断题。

【词性分析】

空格前面是系动词is，因此可填入形容词或名词作句子的表语，也可填入动词分词形式构成被动句或现在进行时。

【答案解析】

本句中的The bottle指上文提到的随手从当地小贩那里买的a bottle of water，由此可以推断，瓶子是密封的、未打开的，故本题答案为M) sealed。

【考点】

语义推断题。

【词性分析】

空格前面有系动词is和副词so，因此应填入形容词作句子的表语。

【答案解析】

本句中的But表示该句语义与上一句构成转折关系，上一句提到，瓶了的标签上写着“纯净水”，由转折关系可知，本句是在说明瓶子里面的水不一定是纯净的，因此应填入含有“纯净，天然”意义的形容词， 故本题答案为I) natural。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

分析句子结构可知， 空格位于that引导的宾语从句中，这个从句缺少谓语动词，又因为从句主语是more than 90 percent of all bottled water，因此空格处应填人动词的第三人称单数形式。

【答案解析】

本句承接上一句，说明瓶装水并不纯净。空格所在宾语从句指出，全世界出售的90%以上的瓶装水中塑料微粒。因此,空格处应填人含有“包含，含有”意义的动词，故本题答案为C) contains。备选项中， 另外一个动词的第三人称单数形式是N) solves， 填入空格不符合上下文语义，故排除。

【考点】

语义推断题。

【词性分析】

空格位于介词短语of a recently ____study中， 前有副词recently， 后有名词study，因此应填入形容词或动词的分词形式。

【答案解析】

根据常识可知，只有公开了研究结果， 人们才能知道研究的结论，因此可推断本空应填入含有“公开，公布”意义的词，故答案为K) released。备选项中， L) revealing有“揭示， 揭露” 的含义， 但是study应该是被公开，应用过去分词，故排除L)。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

第二段首句的主干是That's the conclusion，其后的which引导非限制性定语从句，修饰study，其后空格所在部分应该是结果状语，表明这项研究的结果，由此推测空格处应填入动词的分词形式。

【答案解析】

空格后内容表明，每升水中平均有325个塑料微粒，这应该是该研究的结果，故空格处应填入含有“发现”意义的动词。所以，本题答案为L) revealing“揭示，揭露”。

【考点】

名词辨析题。  

【词性分析】

空格前面有冠词a，后面是过去分词短语作后置定语，因此推测空格处应填人可数名词的单数形式。

【答案解析】

空格所在部分指出，这些塑料微粒包括一种俗称PET的____。PET应该是一种化学物质，因此木空应填入含有“物质，材料""意义的名词，故答案为O) substance。

【考点】

语义推断题。

【词性分析】

clothing、food和______containers由and连接，是并列关系，因此空格处应填入形容词或名词，修饰containers。

【答案解析】

空格所在部分指出， PET这种物质广泛用于制造服装、食品和_______ 容器。由上文可知，PET是在瓶装水里发现的，由此可推断PET也可用于生产盛液体的容器， 故本题答案为G) liquid。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前有限定词this，因此应填入名词单数形式或不可数名词。

【答案解析】

本句指出，包括雀巢、可口可乐在内的几家瓶装水生产商利用同样的方法进行了他们自己的研究。由此可知，this______指的就是第二段研究的结果，所以空格处应填人含有“发现，结论，结果”意义的名词。备选项中只有E) evidence符合文义， 填入空格表示“面对这一证据”。

【考点】

形容词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前有定冠词the， 后面有名词， 因此应填入形容词，

【答案解析】

空格所在句前一句提到，瓶装水生产商自己的研究发现，他们的水中含有的塑料微粒比奥博媒体的研究发现的要少得多。但是无论多少，水中的塑料微粒对人体健康都是有害的，因此世界卫生组织发起这项审查，不过目前风险还不明确，因此本空应填人含有“潜在的，隐藏的”意义的形容词，故本题答案为J) potential。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 On Wednesday, a polar wind brought bitter cold to the Midwest. 2 Overnight, Chicago reached a low of 21 degrees Fahrenheit below zero, making it slightly colder than Antarctica （南极洲）, Alaska, and the North Pole. 3 Wind chills were 64 degrees below zero in Park Rapids, Minnesota and 45 degrees below zero in Buffalo, North Dakota, according to the National Weather Service. 4 Schools, restaurants, and businesses closed, and more than 1,000 flights were canceled.
1 Even the United States Postal Service (USPS) suspended mail delivery. 2 “Due to this arctic outbreak and concerns for the safety of USPS employees,” USPS announced Wednesday morning, “the Postal Service is suspending delivery Jan. 30 in some 3-digit ZIP Code locations.” 3 Twelve regions were listed as unsafe on Wednesday, on Thursday, eight remained.?
1 As global surface temperatures increase, so does the likelihood of extreme weather. 2 In 2018 alone, wildfires, volcanic eruptions, hurricanes, mudslides, and other natural disasters cost at least $49 billion in the United States. 3 As my colleague Vann Newkirk reported, Puerto Rico is still confronting economic and structural destruction and resource scarcity from 2017’s Hurricane Maria. 4 Natural disasters can wreck a community’s infrastructure, disrupting systems for months or years. 5 Some services, however, remind us that life will eventually return, in some form, to normal.?
1 Days after the deadly 2017 wildfires in Santa Rosa, California, a drone （无人机） caught footage （连续镜头） of a USPS worker, Trevor Smith, driving through burned homes in that familiar white van, collecting mail in an affected area. 2 The video is striking: The operation is familiar, but the scene looks like the end of the world. 3 According to Rae Ann Haight, the program manager for the national-preparedness office at USPS, Smith was fulfilling a request made by some of the home owners to pick up any mail that was left untouched. 4 For Smith, this was just another day on the job. 5 “I followed my route like I normally do,” Smith told a reporter. 6 “As I came across a box that was up but with no house, I checked, and there was mail — outgoing mail — in it. 7 And so we picked those up and carried on.”?
1 USPS has sophisticated emergency plans for natural disasters. 2 Across the country, 285 emergency-management teams are devoted to crisis control. 3 These teams are trained annually using a framework known as the three Ps: people, property, product. 4 After mail service stops due to weather, the agency’s top priority is ensuring that employees are safe. 5 Then it evaluates the health of infrastructure, such as the roads that mail carriers drive on. 6 Finally, it decides when and how to re-open operations. 7 If the destruction is extreme, mail addressed to the area will get sent elsewhere. 8 In response to Hurricane Katrina in 2005, USPS redirected incoming New Orleans mail to existing mail facilities in Houston. 9 Mail that was already processed in New Orleans facilities was moved to an upper floor so it would be protected from water damage.?
1 As soon as it’s safe enough to be outside, couriers （邮递员） start distributing accumulated mail on the still-accessible routes. 2 USPS urges those without standing addresses to file change-of-address forms with their new location. 3 After Hurricane Katrina hit in 2005, mail facilities were set up in dozens of locations across the country in the two weeks that USPS was unable to provide street delivery.?
1 Every day, USPS processes, on average, 493.4 million pieces of mail — anything from postcards to Social Security checks to medicine. 2 Spokespeople from both USPS and UPS told me all mail is important. 3 But some mail can be extremely sensitive and timely. 4 According to data released in January 2017, 56 percent of bills are paid online, which means that just under half of payments still rely on delivery services to be completed.?
1 It can be hard to identify which parcels are carrying crucial items such as Social Security checks, but USPS and UPS try their best to prioritize sensitive material. 2 They will coordinate with the Social Security Administration to make sure that Social Security checks reach the right people in a timely fashion. 3 After Hurricane Florence and Hurricane Michael last fall, USPS worked with state and local election boards to make sure that absentee ballots were available and received on time.?
1 Mail companies are logistics （物流） companies, which puts them in a special position to help when disaster strikes. 2 In a 2011 USPS case study, the agency emphasized its massive infrastructure as a “unique federal asset” to be called upon in a disaster or terrorist attack. 3 “I think we’re unique as a federal agency,” USPS official Mike Swigart told me, “because we’re in literally every community in this country... 4 We’re obligated to deliver to that point on a daily basis.”?
1 Private courier companies, which have more dollars to spend, use their expertise in logistics to help revitalize damaged areas after a disaster. 2 For more than a decade, FedEx has supported the American Red Cross in its effort to get emergency supplies to areas affected by disasters, both domestically and internationally. 3 In 2012, the company distributed more than 1,200 MedPacks to Medical Reserve Corps groups in California. 4 They also donated space for 3.1 million pounds of charitable shipping globally. 5 Last October, the company pledged $l million in cash and transportation support for Hurricanes Florence and Michael. 6 UPS’s charitable arm, the UPS Foundation, uses the company’s logistics to help disaster-struck areas rebuild. 7 “We realize that as a company with people, trucks, warehouses, we needed to play a larger role,” said Eduardo Martinez, the president of the UPS Foundation. 8 The company employs its trucks and planes to deliver food, medicine, and water. 9 The day before I spoke to Martinez in November, he had been touring the damage from Hurricane Michael in Florida with the American Red Cross. 10 “We have an obligation to make sure our communities are thriving,” he said.?
1 Rebuilding can take a long time, and even then, impressions of the disaster may still remain. 2 Returning to a normal life can be difficult, but some small routines — mail delivery being one of them — may help residents remember that their communities are still their communities. 3 “When they see that carrier back out on the street,” Swigart said, “that’s the first sign to them that life is starting to return to normal.”?

questions.explanation:
【定位】

由题干中的employees' safety定位到文章E)段第四句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，由于天气原因导致的邮寄服务停止后，该机构的首要任务是确保员工的安全：原文中的the agency指的就是The United States Postal Service，题干中的ensure its employees' safety对应定位句中的ensuring that employees are safe， 故答案为E)。

【定位】

由题干中的unique、communities和federal agencies定位到文章①段倒数第二句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，美国邮政署官员迈克·斯威格特认为美国邮政署作为一个联邦机构是独一无二的，因为它几乎存在于这个国家的每个社区。题干中的One official指的是原文中的USPS official Mike Swigart， 题干中的more direct reach to communities是对定位句中we're in literally every community in this country的同义转述，故答案为D。

【定位】

由题干中的Natural disasters和 community life定位到文章C) 段倒数第二句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，自然灾害能够破坏一个社区的基础设施，扰乱系统达几个月或几年之久。由此可知，自然灾害对于社区生活有着持久的影响。题干中的have along-lasting impact on community life是对定位句中wreck a community's infrastructure，disrupting systems for months or years的同义转述， 故答案为C)。

【定位】

由题干中的Mail delivery service和payments定位到文章G) 段最后一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，根据2017年1月份公布的数据，56%的账单是通过线上支付的，这意味着只有不到一半的账单仍然依靠邮政服务来完成，由此可知，邮递服务仍要负责几乎一半的账单递送工作。题干中的is...responsible for对应定位句中的rely on，题干中的almost half of payments对应定位句中的under half of payments，故答案为G) 。

【定位】

由题干中的a mailman on the street、sign和life becoming normal定位到文章K) 段最后一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，斯威格特说，当人们看到邮递员再次出现在街上，那对于他们来说就是生活开始恢复正常的第一个信号。题干中的a mailman on the street对应定位句中的carrier back out on the street，题干中的sign of life becoming normal again对应定位句中的sign to them that life is starting to return to normal，故答案为K)。

【定位】

由题干中的Hurricane Katrina和mail service points定位到文章F) 段最后一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，2005年飓风“卡特里娜”来袭后，在美国邮政无法提供街道投递服务的地方，全国各地两周内新建了几十个邮政设施。题干中的interrupted routine delivery和temporary mail service points分别对应定位句中的USPS was unable to provide street delivery和mail facilities， 故答案为F) 。

【定位】

由题干中的suspended和extreme cold weather定位到文章B) 段第一、二句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句指出，甚至美国邮政署也暂停了邮件投递业务。美国邮政署周三早上宣布：“由于这次极寒天气爆发，出于对公司员工的安全考虑，美国邮政署将暂停1月30日在一些三位数邮编地区的邮递服务。”题干提到的美国一些地区的邮递服务由于极寒天气而暂停是对定位句的归纳概括，故答案为B)。

【定位】

由题干中的Private postal companies，disaster relief efforts和urgent supplies定位到文章J)段第一句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句指出，私人快递公司有更多的钱可以花，他们利用自己在物流领域的专长，帮助灾后受损地区恢复生机。接下来的第二至四句通过举例说明了一些私人快递公司在灾后所做的工作。题干是对J)段内容的归纳概括，故答案为J)，

【定位】

由题干中的A dedicated USPS employee 和extreme conditions定位到文章D) 段第一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，2017年，加利福尼亚州圣罗莎那场致命的火灾过后几天，一架无人机捕捉到了一位美国邮政署员工特雷弗·史密斯的连续镜头。他正开着那辆熟悉的白色货车穿梭在焚毁的房子中间，揽收受灾区内的郎件，题干中的A dedicated USPS employee和on the job分别对应定位句中的a USPS worker和collecting mail in an affected area，故答案为D)。

【定位】

由题干中的work hard、identify和priority treatment定位到文章H) 段第一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，虽然很难识别出哪些包裹装着社保账单等关键物品，但是美国邮政署和美国联合包裹运送服务公司都会尽他们的最大努力来优先处理敏感材料。题干中的work hard对应定位句中的try their best，题干中的priority treatment对应定位句中的prioritize sensitive material，故答案为H) 。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 Professor Ashok Goel of Georgia Tech developed an artificially intelligent teaching assistant to help handle the enormous number of student questions in the online class, Knowledge-Based Artificial Intelligence. 2 This online course is a core requirement of Georgia Tech’s online Master of Science in Computer Science program.? 3 Professor Goel already had eight teaching assistants, but that wasn’t enough to deal with the overwhelming number of daily questions from students.
1 Many students drop out of online courses because of the lack of teaching support. 2 When students feel isolated or confused and reach out with questions that go unanswered, their motivation to continue begins to fade. 3 Professor Goel decided to do something to remedy this situation and his solution was to create a virtual assistant named Jill Watson, which is based on the IBM Watson platform.?
1 Goel and his team developed several versions of Jill Watson before releasing her to the online forums. 2 At first, the virtual assistant wasn’t too great. 3 But Goel and his team sourced the online discussion forum to find all 40,000 questions that had ever been asked since the class was launched. 4 Then they began to feed Jill with the questions and answers. 5 After some adjustments, and sufficient time, Jill was able to answer the students’ questions correctly 97% of the time. 6 The virtual assistant became so advanced and realistic that the students didn’t know she was a computer.? 7 The students, who were studying artificial intelligence, were interacting with the virtual assistant and couldn’t tell it apart from a real human being. 8 Goel didn’t inform them about Jill’s true identity until April 26. 9 The students were actually very positive about the experience.?
1 The goal of Professor Goel’s virtual assistant next year is to take over answering 40% of all the questions posed by students on the online forum. 2 The name Jill Watson will, of course, change to something else next semester. 3 Professor Goel has a much rosier outlook on the future of artificial intelligence than, say, Elon Musk, Stephen Hawking, Bill Gates or Steve Wozniak.?

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What do we learn about Knowledge-Based Artificial Intelligence？

关于“基于知识的人工智能”，我们了解到什么信息？

A）It is a robot that can answer students’ questions.

它是一个可以回答学生问题的机器人

B）It is a course designed for students to learn online.

它是一门为学生在线学习而设计的课程

C）It is a high-tech device that revolutionizes teaching.

��是一种彻底变革教学的高科技设备

D）It is a computer program that aids student learning.

它是一个帮助学生学习的计算机程序

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Knowledge-Based Artificial Intelligence定位到1段①②句。定位句指出，戈埃尔教授开发了一个人工智能助教来帮助处理在线课程中大量的学生问题，这门在线课程名叫“基于知识的人工智能”， 是佐治亚理工学院计算机科学在线硕士课程的核心要求。由此可见，“基于知识的人工智能”是一门为学生在线学习而设计的课程，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A/C/D选项【偷换概念&过度推理】：三个错误选项均根据an artificially intelligent teaching assistant to help handle. .. student questions(处理学生问题的A1助教) 推断而来,而且C还将“回答问题”夸大为“革新教学”,三项均偷换了题干中概念所指代的内容。

 

【解题思路】

根据各选项结构(A is B结构着重指向事物属性)可知,本题实际考查特殊概念的具体所指。文章首句引出两个首次出现的概念"A1助教”和“在线课程”,但前者使用了不定冠词an,而后者则使用定冠词the加以限定,由the的特指功能可推测其后逗号引出的专有名词是对the online class的特指说明,专指“基于知识的人工智能”这门在线课程,而非别的在线课程。另外本题也可巧用分析排除法:A、C、D的表语“机器人”“高科技设备”"计算机程序”实质均指向“人工智能”,只有B指向“课程",可排除雷同选项,确定B正确。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What problem did Professor Goel meet with？

戈埃尔教授遇到了什么难题？

A）His students were unsatisfied with the assistants.

他的学生对助教不满意

B）His course was too difficult for the students.

他的课程对学生来说太难

C）Students’ questions were too many to handle.

学生问题太多，处理不过来

D）Too many students dropped out of his course.

有太多学��退出了他的课程

 

【定位及答案】

本题考查“戈埃尔教授所遇困难”。可根据problem. . Professor Goel定位至首段末句(that wasn't enough to deal with...)及第二段③句(remedy this situation)。首段末句针对该段①句事件“戈埃尔教授开发了一个AI助教”解释背景原因“教授虽然已有8名助教,但仍不足以应付学生每天提出的大量问题”;第二段③句针对该段①②句所述在线课程窘境“教学支持不足导致学生的问题得不到答复,学生选择退课”提出戈埃尔的解决方案“推出AI助教”。综合可知,戈埃尔教授所遇到的难题是“教学支持不足,学生问题太多,处理不过来",故C正确。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：该选项将首段末句"8名助教不足以应付学生的大量问题”的实际内涵“学生问题太多,助教忙不过来”曲解为“助教水平差,令学生不满”,

B选项【过度推理&无中生有】：该选项由首段“学生每天提出大量问题”臆断出“课程太难”,而原文未提及这一信息。

D选项【偷换概念】：该选项将第二段①句所述各类在线课程(online courses为泛指)所遇问题“许多学生因问题得不到解答而选择退课”缩窄为戈埃尔教授的在线课程(“基于知识的人工智能”)遇到的问题,且将退课人数“许多”夸大为“太多”。

 

【解题思路】

本题考查戈埃尔教授开发“AI助教”的背景原因。前两段均论及背景原因,可相互印证理解:首段末句以wasn't enough和overwhelming number的对比凸显问题焦点“助教人数不足,学生问题太多”;第二段①②句传递具体的因果逻辑“教学支持不足一学生问题得不到答复学生的学习动力减弱→学生退课”;综合可知开发"AI助教”要解决的难题是“学生的问题太多,人工助教处理不过来”。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What do we learn about Jill Watson？

关于吉尔·沃森，我们了解到什么信息？

A）She turned out to be a great success.

她最终大获成功

B）She got along pretty well with students.

她和学生相处的很好

C）She was unwelcome to students at first.

她一开始不受学生欢迎

D）She was released online as an experiment.

她被当做一项实验发布到网上

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Jill Watson定位到3段第⑤⑥句。定位句指出，经过一些调整和足够的时间后，吉尔回答学生问题的正确率能够达到97%。虚拟助理变得非常先进而且逼真，以至于学生们都不知道她是一台计算机。由此可知，吉尔最后取得了巨大的成功，故答案为A)。

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【过度推理】：定位句只提到吉尔的成功，未提及与学生们的相处，B)项为过度推理，故排除。

C选项【过度推理】：3段②句指出，一开始，这个虚拟助理做得并不太好。但人并没有说明学生不喜欢吉尔，故排除C)项。

D选项【无中生有】：文中未提及D) “她被作为实验发布到网上”，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

How did the students feel about Jill Watson?

学生对吉尔·沃森有何感想？

A) They thought she was a bit too artificial.

他们认为她有点不太自然

B) They found her not as capable as expected.

他们发现她的能力不及预期

C) They could not but admire her knowledge.

他们禁不住钦佩她的学识

D) They could not tell her from a real person.

他们没能把她与真人区分开来

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的students feel about Jill Watson定位到3段⑦-⑨句。定位句指出，学习人工智能的学生与虚拟助理进行互动，而且无法将其与真人区分开来，故答案为Ｄ)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【反向干扰】：该选项源自文中高频词artificially intelligent artificial intelligence, 但artificial单独使用时才指“人造的,虚假的,不自然的”,显然与第三段信息"Jill Watson非常先进逼真,学生并不知道她不是真人”相悖。

B选项【反向干扰】：该选项将第三段⑦句couldn't tell it apart from a real human being的含义“未察觉出它其实不是真人(暗示其能力非常出色,堪比真人),反向曲解为“其能力比不上真人"。

C选项【过度推理】：该选项由3段细节信息“给Jill灌输40000个问题和答案"Jill 能在97%的时间里正确回答学生的问题”臆断出"Jill备了大量知识”,进而捏造出“其渊博学识令学生无比饮佩"。

 

【解题思路】

本题实际从学生感受角度考查Jill Watson的应用效果。第三段①至⑤句(句群1)介绍Jill Watson经过多次升级迭代后的答题成效(尚未论及学生反应) ,随后0至D句(句群2)借复现主题词the students…The students... The students...紧密串联,从学生感受角度侧面说明Jill Watson的应用效果,故可将本题解题范围大体圈定为句群2,将各项与句群2的信息点逐一比对,即可确定正确项。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What does Professor Goel plan to do next with Jill Watson?

戈埃尔教授下一步打算让吉尔·沃森做什么？

A) Launch different versions of her online.

在网上发布她的不同版本

B) Feed her with new questions and answers.

给她灌输新的问题和答案

C) Assign her to answer more of students’ questions.

指派她回答更多学生问题

D) Encourage students to interact with her more freely.

鼓励学生更自由的与她互动

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Professor Goel和plan to do定位到4段③句。定位句指出，戈埃尔教授的虚拟助教明年的目标是回答网上论坛里学生提出的40%的问题，由此可见，戈埃尔教授会让虚拟助教回答更多的学生问题，故答案为C)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：该选项将第三段①句信息“在网上发布之前开发了好几个版本”曲解为“将在网上发布多个版本”。

B选项【无中生有】：该选项源自第三段③句所述开发过程中的细节“给Jill Watson灌输40000个问题和答案",但文中未提及“她会被灌输新的问题和答案"。

D选项【无中生有】：该选项由第三段①句所述过去事实“学生与Jill Watson的互动经历"捏造出未来打算“鼓励学生与Jill Watson更加自由地互动”。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 Thinking small, being engaging, and having a sense of humor don’t hurt. 2 Those are a few of the traits of successful science crowdfunding efforts that emerge from a recent study that examined nearly 400 campaigns. 3 But having a large network and some promotional skills may be more crucial.
1 Crowdfunding, raising money for a project through online appeals, has taken off in recent years for everything from making movies to producing water-saving gadgets. 2 Scientists have tried to tap Internet donors, too, with mixed success. 3 Some raised more than twice their goals, but others have fallen short of reaching even modest targets.?
1 To determine what separates science crowdfunding triumphs from failures, a team led by science communications scholar Mike Schafer of the University of Zurich examined the content of the webpages for 371 recent campaigns.?
1 Four traits stood out for those that achieved their goals, the researchers report in Public Understanding of Science. 2 For one, they use a crowdfunding platform that specializes in raising money for science, and not just any kind of project. 3 Although sites like Kickstarter take all comers, platforms such as Experiment. com and Petridish. org only present scientific projects. 4 For another, they present the project with a funny video because good visuals and a sense of humor improved success. 5 Most of them engage with potential donors, since projects that answered questions from interested donors fared better.? 6 And they target a small amount of money. 7 The projects included in the study raised $4000 on average, with 30% receiving less than $1000. 8 The more money a project sought, the lower the chance it reached its goal, the researchers found.?
1 Other factors may also significantly influence a project’s success, most notably, the size of a scientist’s personal and professional networks, and how much a researcher promotes a project on their own. 2 Those two factors are by far more critical than the content on the page. 3 Crowdfunding can be part of researchers ’ efforts to reach the public, and people give because “they feel a connection to the person” who is doing the fundraising — not necessarily to the science.?

【题目及选项概览】

What do we learn about the scientists trying to raise money online for their projects?

关于试图在晚上为自身项目筹集资金的科学家，我们了解到什么？

A) They did not raise much due to modest targets.

由于目标不高，他们没有筹集到多少资金

B) They made use of mixed fundraising strategies.

他们采用了五花八门的筹集策略

C) Not all of them achieved their anticipated goals.

他们并非都达到了自己的预期目标

D) Most of them put movies online for the purpose.

他们大多数为达目的而将影片放到网上

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的the scientists和raise money online定位到2段②③句。定位句指出，科学家们也曾尝试利用互联网捐助者，但成败参半，有些筹到的资金比目标多了一倍多，但有些却连小的目标都没达到，由此可见，并非所有的科学家都成功地筹集到了资金，故答案为C)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【反向干扰】：2段③句提到，有些筹到的资金比目标多了一倍多，但有些却连小的目标都没达到。故排除A)“由于目标不高，他们没有筹集到多少资金”。

B选项【无中生有】：2段只是指出科学家众筹成败参半 (with mixed success) ， 并未提及筹集资金的具体方法，故排除B)“他们采用了混合融资策略”，

D选项【偷换概念】：2段①句提到，近年来，众筹风靡于各个领域，从制作电影到生产节水设备等，而非大多数科学家把电影放到网上就是为了众筹，故排除D)。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What is the purpose of Mike Schafer’s research of recent crowdfunding campaigns?

迈克·费舍尔研究近期众筹活动的目的是什么？

A) To create attractive content for science websites.

为了给科学网站创建有吸引力的内容

B) To identify reasons for their different outcomes.

为了找出导致不同结果的原因

C) To help scientists to launch innovative projects.

为了帮助科学家开展创新项目

D) To separate science projects from general ones.

为了区分科学项目与普通项目

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Mike Schafer's research定位到3段。定位段提到，为了确定科学众筹成功与失败的原因，苏黎世大学的科学传播学学者迈克·沙费尔领导的一个团队调查了最近371个活动的网页内容。由此可知，迈克·沙费尔该项研究是为了找出造成不同结果的原因，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【词汇干扰&答非所问】：该选项利用3段the content of the webpages" (371个近期众筹活动的)网页内容”以及4段④句present the project with a funny video“利用有趣视频来展示(科研)项目"两个碎片信息捏造而来,但前者指向研究对象,后者指向研究启示,均与研究目的无关。

C选项【词汇干扰】：该选项利用文中高频词scientists, projects以及常规思维“科学项目应该具有新意(才可能获得更多捐助)”扭曲而来,但文章关注的是“科研众筹活动的成功因素”而非“众筹的科研项目的新颖性".

D选项【偷换概念】：利用第三段中separates... from…、第四段②③句中any kind of project, scientific projects的这两个碎片信息杂糅捏造而来, 将研究目的中所涉及的“分离”的对象“成(的因素)vs败(的因素)”愉换为“科研项目vs普通项目"

 

【解题思路】

本题考查“目的(purpose)",与之相关的表达词通常有to, in order to, in order that, so that, so as to, for the purpose of等。解答时只要找到目标表达词即可准确定位。第三段段首明确以动词不定式结构To...传递了研究目标之意,该部分中核心动词为determine,与之契合的唯有B项中identify,故锁定B,然后可借助文意加以佐证“搞清楚导致成或败的因素 找到导致不同结果的原因"。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What trait contributes to the success of a crowdfunding campaign?

什么特质有助筹集活动取得成功？

A) The potential benefit to future generations.

对子孙后代的潜在益处

B) Its interaction with prospective donors.

与其潜在捐赠者互动

C) Its originality in addressing financial issues.

其解决财务问题的创意

D) The value of the proposed project.

拟议项目所具备的价值

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的trait和contributes to定位到4段⑤句。定位句指出，大多数成功的科学众筹项目都与潜在的捐助者有密切联系，因为回答那些感兴趣的捐助者问题的项目会进展得更顺利。由此可知，与可能的捐助者互动有助于众筹活动的成功，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A、D选项【常识干扰】：该选项利用惯常思维“对后代有益、本身有价值的项目更可能获得公众捐款”设障,但并非文中内容。

C选项【偷换概念】：将特征四“以少量资金作为目标”曲解为“有创意地解决(资金不足等)财务问题"。

 

【解题思路】

本题着重点在透过现象“人物观点题”看本质“事实细节题"。纵观各项均为They should be.. 提出建议,使某事物具备良好条件/使其向好发展,其中They指代the financial targets of crowd funding projects)可推断题目实际考查“成功众筹项目的目标资金应具备什么特征/条件”,即针对研究人员发现的第四个特征进行提问,就此很容易将答案锁定为A项。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What did the researchers think of the financial targets of crowdfunding projects?

研究人员如何看待众筹项目的财务目标？

A) They should be small to be successful.

它们应该小一些以取得成功

B) They should be based on actual needs.

它们应该基于实际需要

C) They should be assessed with great care.

它们应该被仔细评估

D) They should be ambitious to gain notice.

它们应该宏大些以获得关注

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的financial targets of crowdfunding projects定位到4段⑥-⑧句。定位句提到，成功众筹项目的目标是一小笔钱。研究中涉及的项目平均筹集金额为4，000美元，其中30%的项目获得的资金不足1，000美元。研究人员发现，项目需要的资金越多，它实现目标的机会就越小。由此可知，研究人员认为科学众筹要想成功，应设立较小的目标资金，故答��为A)。

 

【错误选项分析】

B/C选项【常识干扰】：利用惯常思维“众筹目标金额应基于实际需要,应仔细评估”设障,但并非文中研究人员发现的结果。

D选项【反向干扰&偷换概念】：首先与“以小量金额为目标”相悖,同时将目标“获得成功”偷换为“获得关注”。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What motivates people to donate in a crowdfunding campaign？

什么促使人们在众筹活动中捐款？

A）The ease of access to the content of the webpage.

访问网页内容的便利性

B）Their desire to contribute to the cause of science.

它们为科学事业做出贡献的愿望

C）The significance and influence of the project itself.

项目本身的意义和影响

D）Their feeling of connection to the scientists themselves.

它们与科学家本身的关联感

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的motivates和donate定位到5段③句。位句指出，众筹可以成为研究人员努力接触公众的一部分，人们捐款是因为“他们感觉与筹款人有联系”——而不是与科学有联系。由此可见，人们捐款是因为他们感觉与科学家有联系，故答案为D)，

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【无中生有】：该选项利用末段②句the content on the page捏造干扰,但该句意在说明“人际关系网及宣传投入比网页内容更重要”,且文中并未探讨“网页内容访问的便利性”。

B选项【反向干扰】：该选项与文末句“未必与科学有关”的言外之意“并不太关注自己对科学的贡献”相悖。

C选项【偷换概念】：该选项从significantly influence“望文生义”出significance and influence,但文意实际指向“(其他因素对众筹项目的)重大影响”,而非“(众筹项目的)意义和影响"。

 

【解题思路】

由题干motivates(成为…的动机;是 …的原因)可知,本题为因果细节题(解题思路为寻找因果表达词进行定位,再根据定位内容比对选项)。文中末句出现因果表达词because,进而将答案区锁定至"they feel a connection to the person" who is doing the fundraising-not necessarily to the science(其中包含to A not to B取舍结构),最后敲定形、神皆相似的选项D.

sections.title: 听力
sections.passage:
A 9-year-old Central California boy braved strong currents and cold water to swim from San Francisco to Alcatraz Island and back.
A California television station in Fresno reported Tuesday that James Savage set a record as the youngest swimmer to make the journey to the former prison.
The TV station reported that by completing the swim, the fourth-grade student from Los Banos broke a record previously held by a 10-year-old boy.

His father said he had offered his son $100 as a reward; to encourage his struggling son, he doubled it to $200.

Scientists have identified thousands of known ant species around the world—and only a few of them bug humans.
Most ants live in the woods or out in nature.
There, they keep other creatures in check, distribute seeds, and clean dead and decaying materials from the ground.
A very small percentage of ants do harm to humans.
But those are incredibly challenging to control.
They are small enough to easily slip inside your house, live in colonics that number in the tens of thousands to the hundreds of thousands, and reproduce quickly.
That makes them good at getting in, and hard to kick out.
Once they settle in, these insects start affecting your home.
In addition to biting ants, other species can cause different kinds of damage.
Some, like carpenter ants, can undermine a home ‘s structure, while others interfere with electrical units.
Unfortunately, our homes are very attractive to ants, because they provide everything the colony needs to survive, such as food, water, and shelter .
So how can we prevent ants from getting into our homes?
Most important of all, avoid giving ants any access to food, particularly sugary food, because ants have a sweet tooth.
We also need to clean up spills as soon as they occur and store food in airtight containers.
Even garbage attracts ants, so empty your trash as often as possible, and store your outside garbage in a lidded can, well away from doors and windows.

上文提到，美国汽车创新中心已经从底特律迁到硅谷。空格所在句指出，让无人驾驶汽车的生产重返底特律，密歌根州的立法者采取了行动，即作出了努力。结合备选项可知,A) bid""(为争取某物作的)努力”符合题意,a bid to do sth.意为“为争取某物而作的努力”。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前是谓语动词introduced,空格后是that引导的从句,空格处所填词在主句中作introduced的宾语，同时是that引导的从句的先行词,因此应填入名词。

【答案解析】

根据空格前的关键词lawmakers可推断，密歇根州的立法者通过立法使密歇根州在美国发展无人驾驶汽车方面处于最有利的地位，因此G) legislation""法律，法规”符合题意。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

 

【词性分析】

空格前为所有格,空格后为介词in,因此空格处应填入名词，Michigan's_____作句子的主语。

 

【答案解析】

空格所在句句意为:密歇根州在汽车研发领域的受到了几个州和国家的威胁。结合本句中our leadership in transportation可知，空格处也应是指密歇根州在汽车研发方面的领导地位。对比备选项中的名词，dominance“优势，显要，突出”与leadership 意思接近，符合句意,故D)为答案。此处表示密歇根州在汽车研发上的主导地位受到了威胁。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

分析句子结构可知，空格前是动词短语desire to，其中to是不定式符号，空格后是名词短语our leadership，因此空格处应填入动词原形。

【答案解析】

空格位于which引导的定语从句中，which指代several states and countries。结合上文可知，密歇根州在汽车研发方面的主导地位受到了威胁，这些威胁来自几个州和国家，它们想要______密歇根州在交通运输领域的领导地位。结合备选项可知，[I] replace“接替，取代”符合句意。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【词性分析】

分析句子结构可知，the lead of four bills recently introduced在句中作Senator Mike Ko wall的同位语。空格前是the lead，作定语修饰空格处所填词，空格后是介词of，因此空格处应填人表示某种身份的名词，进一步解释说明Senator Mike Ko wall。

【答案解析】

根据four bills recently introduced以及上文的Michigan lawmakers have introduced...可知，Senator Mike Ko wall应是最近提出的四项法案的提案人。结合备选项可知，N) sponsor“提案人，发起人，倡议者”为正确答案。

【考点】

动词辨析题，

 

【词性分析】

空格位于情态动词would和名词短语a substantial update之间， 应填人动词原形，作主句的谓语。

 

【答案解析】

分析句意可知，如果这四项法案都以书面形式通过了，那么它们是对密歇根州一项法律的重大更新。空格处应填人表示“是，等同于”之意的动词，结合备选项，J) represent“等于，相当于，意味着”符合句意。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前是复合形容词on-demand，格后是介词of，因此空格处应填人不可数名词或复数名词，作setup的宾语。

【答案解析】

分析句子结构可知，and连接send groups of self-driving cars on cross-state road trips与setup on-demand of self-driving cars两个并列成分。根据groups of self-driving cars可知， 空格处应填人与groups同义的名词，再结合备选项可知，E) fleets“车队”符合句意。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【词性分析】

通过分析句子结构可知，该句主谓宾齐全，成分完整，In在句中作状语，空格处应填入名词，作In的宾语。

【答案解析】

空格前一句介绍密歇根州的做法，空格所在句提及加利福尼亚州的做法，前后形成对比。再结合备选项，B) contrast“差异，差别”符合句意。in contrast为固定搭配，意为“相比之下”。

【考点】

形容词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前有比较级标志词far more，空格后有名词rules，空格处应填入形容词作定语修饰rules.

【答案解析】

上文提到，密歇根州出台法律鼓励发展无人驾驶技术。空格所在句则指出，加利福尼亚州提出了各种规定，禁止无人驾驶技术用于商业用途。与密歇根州相比，加利福尼亚州对无人驾驶技术的态度更严格，故空格处应填人表示“严格的”之意的形容词。结合备选项，K) restrictive“限制(性)的，约束(性)的”符合句意。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Today in the United States there are 72,000 centenarians（百岁老人）. 2 Worldwide, Probably 450,000. 3 If current trends continue, then by 2050 there will be more than a million in the US alone. 4 According to the work of Professor James Vaupel and his co-researchers, 50% of babies born in the US in 2007 have a life expectancy of 104 or more. 5 Broadly the same holds for the UK, Germany, France, Italy and Canada, and for Japan 50% of 2007 babies can expect to live to 107.?
1 Understandably, there are concerns about what this means for public finances given the associated health and pension challenges. 2 These challenges are real, and society urgently needs to address them. 3 But it is also important to look at the wider picture of what happens when so many people live for 100 years. 4 It is a mistake to simply equate longevity (长寿) with issues of old age. 5 Longer lives have implications for all of life, not just the end of it.
1 Our view is that if many people are living for longer, and are healthier for longer, then this will result in an inevitable redesign of work and life. 2 When people live longer, they are not only older for longer, but also younger for longer. 3 There is some truth in the saying that “70 is the new 60” or “40 the new 30.” 4 If you age more slowly over a longer time period, then you are in some sense younger for longer.?
1 But the changes go further than that. 2 Take, for instance, the age at which people make commitments such as buying a house, getting married, having children, or starting a career. 3 These are all fundamental commitments that are now occurring later in life. 4 In 1962, 50% of Americans were married by age 21. 5 By 2014, that milestone (里程碑) had shifted to age 29.?
1 While there are numerous factors behind these shifts, one factor is surely a growing realization for the young that they are going to live longer. 2 Options are more valuable the longer they can be held. 3 So if you believe you will live longer, then options become more valuable, and early commitment becomes less attractive. 4 The result is that the commitments that previously characterized the beginning of adulthood are now being delayed, and new patterns of behavior and a new stage of life are emerging for those in their twenties.
1 Longevity also pushes back the age of retirement, and not only for financial reasons. 2 Yes, unless people are prepared to save a lot more, our calculations suggest that if you are now in your mid-40s, then you are likely to work until your early 70s; and if you are in your early 20s, there is a real chance you will need to work until your late 70s or possibly even into your 80s. 3 But even if people are able to economically support a retirement at 65, over thirty years of potential inactivity is harmful to cognitive (认知的) and emotional vitality. 4 Many people may simply not want to do it.?
1 And yet that does not mean that simply extending our careers is appealing. 2 Just lengthening that second stage of full-time work may secure the financial assets needed for a 100-year life, but such persistent work will inevitably exhaust precious intangible assets such as productive skills, vitality, happiness, and friendship.?
1 The same is true for education. 2 It is impossible that a single shot of education, administered in childhood and early adulthood, will be able to support a sustained, 60-year career. 3 If you factor in the projected rates of technological change, either your skills will become unnecessary, or your industry outdated. 4 That means that everyone will, at some point in their life, have to make a number of major reinvestments in their skills.?
1 It seems likely, then, that the traditional three-stage life will evolve into multiple stages containing two, three, or oven more different careers. 2 Each of these stages could potentially be different. 3 In one the focus could be on building financial success and personal achievement, in another on creating a better work/life balance, still another on exploring and understanding options more fully, or becoming an independent producer, yet another on making a social contribution. 4 These stages will span sectors, take people to different cities, and provide foundation for building a wide variety of skills.?
1 Transitions between stages could be marked with sabbaticals (休假) as people find time to rest and recharge their health, re-invest in their relationships, or improve their skills. 2 At times, these breaks and transitions will be self-determined, at others they will be forced as existing roles, firms, or industries cease to exist.
1 A multi-stage life will have profound changes not just in how you manage your career, but also in your approach to life. 2 An increasingly important skill will be your ability to deal with change and even welcome it. 3 A three-stage life has few transitions, while a multi-stage life has many. 4 That is why being self-aware, investing in broader networks of friends, and being open to new ideas will become even more crucial skills.?
1 These multi-stage lives will create extraordinary variety across groups of people simply because there are so many ways of sequencing the stages. 2 More stages mean more possible sequences.
1 With this variety will come the end of the close association of age and stage. 2 In a three-stage life, people leave university at the same time and the same age, they tend to start their careers and family at the same age, they proceed through middle management all roughly the same time, and then move into retirement within a few years of each other. 3 In a multi-stage life, you could be an undergraduate at 20, 40, or 60; a manager at 30, 50, or 70; and become an independent producer at any age.?
1 Current life structures, career paths, educational choices, and social norms are out of tune with the emerging reality of longer lifespans. 2 The three-stage life of full-time education, followed by continuous work, and then complete retirement may have worked for our parents or even grandparents, but it is not relevant today. 3 We believe that to focus on longevity as primarily an issue of aging is to miss its full implications. 4 Longevity is not necessarily about being older for longer. 5 It is about living longer, being older later, and being younger longer.?

questions.explanation:
【定位】

由题干中的have more careers定位到文章I)段第一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，传统的三阶段人生似乎将演变为包含两个、三个甚至更多不同职业的多阶段人生。题干中的now对应定位句中的the traditional three-stage life, 题干中的have more careers 对应定位句中的multiple stages containing two, three, or even more different careers。题干是对定位句的同义转述，故答案为I)。

【定位】

由题干中的extending one's career、positive和negative effects定位到文章G)段。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位段指出，简单地延长我们的职业生涯并不意味着有吸引力。延长职业生涯可以为我们活到100岁的生活提供经济保障，但同时也会损害我们的友谊、幸福等无形资产。换句话说，延长职业生涯既有积极影响，也有消极影响。题干中的have both positive and negative effects是对定位段内容的归纳概括，故答案为G)。

【定位】

由题干中的Americans和marriage定位到文章D)段最后两句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句提到，1962年，50%的美国人在21岁之前结婚。到2014年,这一里程碑已经转移到了29岁。经过简单计算可知，美国人的结婚时间平均推迟了八年。题干是对定位句的归纳概括，故本题正确答案为D)。

【定位】

由题干中的today和parents or grandparents定位到文章N段第二句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到,全日制教育、然后连续工作直到完全退休，这样三阶段的人生可能适用于我们的父母甚至祖父母，但已经不适用于现在了。由此可知,我们���父母或祖父母可能会遵循传统的三阶段的人生模式，但这并不适用于现在的年轻人，即年轻人不再遵循父母或祖父母的人生模式:题干中的the pattern of life of their parents or grandparents 是对定位句中The three-stage life of fulltime education, followed by continuous work, and then complete retirement的同义转述，题干中的no longer follow对应定位句中的not relevant, 故本题正确答案为N)。

【定位】

由题干中的live over 100和by the mid-21st century 定位到文章A)段。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位段提到，如今，美国有72,000名百岁老人。全世界大概有45万。如果目前的趋势继续下去，那么到2050年，仅在美国就有超过100万的百岁老人。英国、德国、法国、意大利和加拿大与美国情况类似。即到21世纪中叶，预计会有更多人活到100多岁。题干是对定位段内容的归纳概括故本题正确答案为A).

【定位】

由题干中的changes和approach to life定位到文章K)段第一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，多阶段的人生将不仅导致你管理自己的事业的方式产生深刻变化，而且还会导致你的生活方式产生深刻变化。题干中的radical changes是对定位句中profound changes的同义转述题干中的people's approach to life是对定位句中your approach to life 的同义转述，故本题正确答案为K)。

【定位】

由题干中的technological change, necessary和skill定位到文章H)段最后两句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，如果将预计的技术变革速度考虑在内，要么你的技能变得没有必要,要么你的行业已经过时了。这意味着，在生命中的某个阶段，每个人都不得不对自己的技能进行一些大的再投资。换句话说，为了适应快速的技术变革,人们必须不断提升自己的技能。题干中的Fast technological change 是对定位句中the projected rates of technological change 的同义转述,题干中的constantly upgrade their skill是对定位句中make a number of major reinvestments in their skills的同义转述，故本题正确答案为H)。

【定位】

由题干中的retire early. do harm to和mental and emotional well-being 定位到文章F)段最后两句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，即使人们能够在经济上支持自己65岁退休,30多年不工作也会对认知和情感活力造成伤害。许多人可能根本不想这样做。由此可知,提前退休，长时间不工作可能会对人们的精神和情感健康造成伤害。题干中的Many people may not want to retire early是对定位句中Many people may simply not want to do it的同义转述，题干中的do harm to their mental and emotional well-being 是对定位句中is harmful to cognitive and emotional vitality 的同义转述，故本题正确答案为F)。

【定位】

由题干中的close link和age and stage定位到文章M)段第-句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，伴随这种多样性,年龄和人生阶段的紧密联系即将结束。结合上文可知，定位句中的this variety 指的是多阶段人生的多样性。题干中的The close link between age and stage是对定位句中the close association of age and stage的同义转述，cease to exist是对定位句中will come the end of.的同义转述，故本题正确答案为M)。

【定位】

由越干中的living a longer and healthier life和rearrange their work and life定位到文章C)段第一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，如果许多人活得更长、健康的时间更长,那么这将不可避免地导致重新规划工作和生活。题干中的People living a longer and healthier life是对定位句中many people are living for longer, and are healthier for longer的同义转述，题干中的will have to rearrange their work and life是对定位句中will result in an inevitable redesign of work and life的同义转述，故本题正确答案为C。

1 In the classic marriage vow （誓约）, couples promise to stay together in sickness and in health.? 2 But a new study finds that the risk of divorce among older couples rises when the wife — not the husband — becomes seriously ill.
1 “Married women diagnosed with a serious health condition may find themselves struggling with the impact of their disease while also experiencing the stress of divorce,” said researcher Amelia Karraker.
1 Karraker and co-author Kenzie Latham analyzed 20 years of data on 2,717 marriages from a study conducted by Indiana University since 1992. 2 At the time of the first interview, at least one of the partners was over the age of 50.
1 The researchers examined how the onset （发生） of four serious physical illnesses affected marriages.? 2 They found that, overall, 31% of marriages ended in divorce over the period studied. 3 The incidence of new chronic （慢性的） illness onset increased over time as will, with more husbands than wives developing serious health problems.
1 “We found that women are doubly vulnerable to marital break-up in the face of illness,” Karraker said. 2 “They’re more likely to be widowed, and if they’re the noes who become ill, they’re more likely to get divorced.”?
1 While the study didn’t assess why divorce in more likely when wives but not husbands become seriously ill, Karraker offers a few possible reasons. 2 “Gender norms and social expectations about caregiving many make it more difficult for men to provide care to sick spouses,” Karraker said.? 3 “And because of the imbalance in marriage markets, especially in older ages, divorced men have more choices among prospective partners than divorced women.”
1 Given the increasing concern about health care costs for the aging population, Karraker believes policymakers should be aware of the relationship between disease and risk of divorce.
1 “Offering support services to spouses caring for their other halves may reduce marital stress and prevent divorce at older ages,” she said. 2 “But it’s also important to recognize that the pressure to divorce may be health-related and that sick ex-wives may need additional care and services to prevent worsening health and increased health costs.”?

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What can we learn about marriage vows from the passage?

关于婚姻誓约，我们可以从文中了解到什么信息？

A) They may not guarantee a lasting marriage.

它们可能无法保障婚姻长久

B) They are as binding as they used to be.

它们和过去一样有约束力

C) They are not taken seriously any more.

它们不再受到重视

D) They may help couples tide over hard times.

它们可以帮助夫妻度过难关

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的marriage vows定位到1段①句。定位句指出，在经典的结婚誓约中，夫妻双方承诺无论生病还是健康都要在一起。接下来一句继而指出，一项新的研究发现，当上了年纪的夫妻中的妻子而不是丈夫得了严重的疾病时，离婚的风险会上升。由此可推断出结婚誓约并不能保证持续长久的婚姻，故答案为A).

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【反向干扰】：1段②句提到，当妻子而不是丈夫得了严重的疾病时，离婚的风险会上升,可见现在的婚姻状况已经发生了变化，婚姻暂约也失去了其约束作用，故排除B)“它们像过去样具有约束作用”

C选项【无中生有】：文中并未提及C“它们再也不被重视" .故排除;

D选项【反向干扰】：根据1段②句可知，当妻子得了严重的疾病时，离婚的风险会上升.即婚姻督约并不能帮助伴倡们共渡难关，故排除D)"它们会帮助伴侣们共渡难关”。

questions.explanation:

What did Karraker and co-author Kenzie Latham find about elderly husbands?

卡拉克和合著者肯齐·莱瑟姆关于老年丈夫的研究发现是什么？

他们通常不善于照顾自己

B选项【过度推理】：定位段提到，丈夫比妻子更容易出现严重的健康问题，但并没有提到丈夫随着年龄增加而增加患重病的概率,B)“他们会越来越容易患上严重的疾病”属于过度推断，故排除

C选项【偷换概念】：4段③句提到，在这一时期，新的慢性疾病的发生率也会随之增加，其中丈夫比妻子更容易出现严重的健康问题。由此可见,男性在老年时期更容易患病，但并不能由此推出C)“他们会像他们的妻子一样患上各种疾病”，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What does Karraker say about women who fall ill?

关于患病女性，卡拉克说了什么？

A) They are more likely to be widowed.

她们更有可能丧偶

B) They are more likely to get divorced.

她们更有可能离婚

C) They are less likely to receive good care.

她们不太可能受到悉心照顾

D) They are less likely to bother their spouses.

她们烦扰配偶的可能性更小

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Karraker和women who fall ill定位到5段。定位段指出，在面对疾病时，女性更容易遭遇婚姻的破裂，她们有可能丧偶，如果她们是生病的一方,更有可能被离婚。由此可见，老年女性患病时更容易被离婚，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：5段②句指出，女性更容易遭遇婚姻的破裂，如果她们是生病的一方，更有可能被离婚。由此可见，生病的女性面临的主要压力是被离婚，而不是丧偶，故排除A)“她们更有可能丧偶";

C选项【过度推理】：文章6段②句提到，男性更难为重病的配偶提供照顾，但是并不能由此推出患病女性不太可能得到好的照顾,C)“她们不太可能得到良好的照顾”属于过度推断，故排除:

D选项【无中生有】：文中未提及D) “她们麻烦配偶的可能性比较小”故排除。

【题目及选项概览】

Why is it more difficult for men to take care of their sick spouses according to Karraker?

卡拉克认为男性更难照顾患病配偶的原因是什么？

A) They are more accustomed to receiving care.

他们更习惯于获得照顾

B) They find it more important to make money for the family.

他们觉得挣钱养家更为重要

C) They think it more urgent to fulfill their social obligations.

他们认为旅行社会义务更为紧迫

D) They expect society to do more of the job.

他们希望社会承担更多照护工作

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的more difficult for men to take care of their sick spouses定位到6段②句。定位句提到.性别准则以及社会对付出关怀的预期可能使得男性更难为重病的配偶提供照顾。由此可见,男性之所以更难照料患病的伴侣是由性别准则以及社会对付出关怀的预期决定的，即不同性别所承担的社会分工不同,而男性更习惯于接受照料,故答案为A).

 

【错误选项分析】

B/C选项【过度推理】：该选项过度推断定位句信息:“丈夫更看重在外面挣钱、履行社会义务”带有“为丈夫疏于照顾妻子正名”之意,脱离全文“客观介绍研究发现”的大前提。

D选项【偷换概念】：该选项将末段卡拉克的建议“(社会)应该为照顾患病配偶的丈夫提供支持服务、为患病妻子提供额外照顾和服务”偷换为“男性的主观看法”。

【题目及选项概览】

What does Karraker think is also important?

卡拉克认为哪一点也很重要？

A) Reducing marital stress on wives.

减轻妻子的婚姻压力

B) Stabilizing old couples’ relations.

稳定老年夫妻的关系

C) Providing extra care for divorced women.

为离异女性提供额外照顾

D) Making men pay for their wives’ health costs.

让男性支付妻子的医疗费用

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Karraker和also important定位到8段②句。定位句指出，重病的前妻们也许需要额外的照顾和服务以防止健康状况日益恶化和健康成本不断增加。由此可见,人们需要给离婚的女性提供更多的关怀与括助，定位句中的ex-wives, additional care分别对应C)中的divorced women, extra care,故答案为C).

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念&过度推理】：8段②句指出。离婚的压力也许与健康有关，但并不能由此推出要减轻妻子所面临的婚姻压力，故排除A)“减轻妻子们所承受的婚姻压力"

B选项【无中生有】：文中未提及B)“稳定老年伴侣的关系"，故排除

D选项【答非所问&无关干扰】：由定位句可知，同样重要的是人们要认识到重病的前妻需要更多额外的照顾和服务。这与男性是否支付医药费无关，故排除D)“让男性支付他们妻子的医疗账单”。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 If you were like most children, you probably got upset when your mother called you by a sibling’s (兄弟姐妹的) name.? 2 How could she not know you? Did it mean she loved you less?
1 Probably not. 2 According to the first research to tackle this topic head-on, misnaming the most familiar people in our life is a common cognitive (认知的) error that has to do with how our memories classify and store familiar names.?
1 The study, published online in April in the journal Memory and Cognition, found that the “wrong” name is not random but is invariably fished out from the same relationship pond: children, siblings, friends. 2 The study did not examine the possibility of deep psychological significance to the mistake, says psychologist David Rubin, “but it does tell us who’s in and who’s out of the group.”
1 The study also found that within that group, misnamings occurred where the names shared initial or internal sounds, like Jimmy and Joanie or John and Bob. 2 Physical resemblance between people was not a factor. 3 Nor was gender.?
1 The researchers conducted five separate surveys of more than 1,700 people. 2 Some of the surveys included only college students; others were done with a mixed-age population. 3 Some asked subjects about incidents where someone close to them — family or friend — had called them by another person’s name. 4 The other surveys asked about times when subjects had themselves called someone close to them by the wrong name. 5 All the surveys found that people mixed up names within relationship groups such as grandchildren, friends and siblings but hardly ever crossed these boundaries.?
1 In general, the study found that undergraduates were almost as likely as old people to make this mistake and men as likely as women. 2 Older people and this mistake and men as likely as women. 3 Older people and women made the mistake slightly more often, but that may be because grandparents have more grandchildren to mix up than parents have children.? 4 Also, mothers may call on their children more often than fathers, given traditional gender norms. 5 There was no evidence that errors occurred more when the misnamer was frustrated, tired or angry.

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

How might people often feel when they were misnamed?

被叫错名字时，人们通常会有什么感受？

A)Unwanted.

不被需要

B)Unhappy.

不高兴

C)Confused.

困惑

D)Indifferent.

不在乎

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的feel和when they were misnamed定位到1段①句。定位句指出，如果你和大多数孩子一样，当你的母亲叫你的时候误叫成了你兄弟姐妹的名字，你很有可能感到难过。由此可见，当被人叫错名字的时候，人们通常会感到不高兴,故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：该选项将②句疑问之意“是否爱得更少”偷换为肯定之意“爱得更少”,然后再将“爱得更少”程度加深为“不爱”,从而捏造出“不被需要,多余”.

C选项【过度推理】：该选项由②句连续发问臆断出被叫错名字者“困惑:不知道到底是因为不认识还是因为爱得更少而被叫错",而②句How could. .. not,Did it mean...less实质均暗含被叫错名字者“失落、沮丧”的态度。

D选项【反向干扰】：该选项与被叫错名字者内心感受upset、心中疑惑How could... Did it mean...所传递的“(对名字被叫错之事)极为在乎”态度相悖。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What did David Rubin’s research find about misnaming?

关于“叫错名字”，戴维·鲁宾的研究发现了什么？

A)It is related to the way our memories work.

这与我们记忆的运作方式相关

B)It is a possible indicator of a faulty memory.

这可能是错误记忆的信号

C)It occurs mostly between kids and their friends.

这大多发生在孩子与其朋友之间

D)It often causes misunderstandings among people.

这经常引起人们之间的误解

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的research和misnaming定位到2段②句。定位句提到，根据首个积极解决这一话题的研究可知，叫错生活中最熟悉的人的名字是一种常见的认知错误,这种错误与我们的记忆如何归类和储存熟悉的名字有关。由此可知，叫错他人姓名的情况与我们记忆的工作模式有关,故答案为A).

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【偷换概念】：定位句提到，叫错名字是一种常见的认知错误，而不是错误记忆的提示，故排除B)"它可能是记忆有问题的迹象”;

C选项【偷换概念】：文章3段①句指出，叫错的名字并不是随机的，而是来自相同的关系群:孩子、兄弟姐妹和朋友。由此可见，被叫错名字的对象往往是同一个群体成员，而不是“叫错名字现象的易发人群：孩子和朋友之间“，故排除C)“它主要发生在孩子和他们的朋友之间"

D选项【答非所问&无关干扰】：该选项利用首段最后两句隐藏文意“被叫错名字的人通常会感觉不被爱，不被认可“捏造而来，但这并非是研究发现，故排除。

【题目及选项概览】

What is most likely the cause of misnaming?

什么很可能是叫错名字的原因？

A) Similar personality traits.

个性特征相似

B) Similar spellings of names.

名字拼写相似

C) Similar physical appearance.

外貌相似

D) Similar pronunciation of names.

名字发音相似

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的the cause of misnaming和题文同序原则定位到4段。定位段指出，该研究还发现在那个群体中，叫错名字的情况会发生在名字开头或中间的发音相同的人身上。由此可见，名字中相似的发音会导致叫错姓名的情况发生,故答案为D)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：该选项由3段①句“被叫错者通常属于同一个关系池:朋友、兄弟姐妹、子女”捏造而来,认为“属同一个关系池的人大多个性特征相似”,但“同属关系池”≠“个性特征相似".

B选项【偷换概念】：文章4段①句明确指出，叫错名字的情况会发生在名字开头或中间的发音相同的人身上，因此这个原因与名字的发音有关，与拼写无关,故排除B)“相似的名字拼写";

C选项【反向干扰】：文章4段②句指出,外表的相似并不是叫错名字的原因，故排除C)“相似的外貌特征”。

【题目及选项概览】

What did the surveys of more than 1,700 subjects find about misnaming?

关于叫错名字，针对1700多名调查对象的调查发现了什么？

A) It more often than not hurts relationships.

它通常会损害关系

B) It hardly occurs across gender boundaries.

它很少跨越性别界限

C) It is most frequently found in extended families.

它最常见于大家庭中

D) It most often occurs within a relationship groups.

它最长发生在一个关系群内容部

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的the surveys of more than 1 700 subjects定位到5段。定位段⑤句提到，所有的调查都发现，人们对于名字的混淆往往存在于某种关系群体中，如孙子辈的孩子们、朋友和兄弟姐妹,但是很少跨越这些界限。由此可见，混酒名字的事情往往发生在某种关系群体中故答案为D)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【词汇干扰&无中生有】：该选项由首段现象“叫错名字让被叫错者不高兴”及全文复现词relationship杂糅���造而来,但文中无据可依。

B选项【偷换概念】：将5段⑤句中these boundaries具体所指boundaries of relationship groups偷换为gender boundaries,而第四段末句明确指出“叫错名字与性别无关(即会跨越性别界限)"。

C选项【偷换概念】：该选项由grandchildren衍生出extended families(与核心家庭相对,指几代同堂的大家庭),将文中个例“子孙辈名字(以及朋友名字、兄弟姊妹名字等其他属于同一关系池内部的名字)容易搞混”窄化曲解为“叫错名字常见于大家庭中”。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

Why do mothers misname their children more often than fathers?

为什么母亲比父亲更常叫错孩子的名字?

A) They suffer more frustrations.

她们遭受更多沮丧

B) They become worn out more often.

她们更常感到精疲力竭

C) They communicate more with their children.

她们和孩子的交流更多

D) They generally take on more work at home.

她们在家通常承担更多工作

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的mothers misname their children more often than fathers 定位到6段③句。定位句指出。鉴于传统的性别准则，母亲叫孩子名字的次数或许多于父亲。传统的性别准则即母亲在家里承担照顾子女的职责，而父亲在外挣钱养家。由此可见,母亲之所以会出现较多的叫错孩子姓名的情况，是因为与孩子们接触的时间较多，故答案为C.

 

【错误选项分析】

A/B选项【反向干扰】：文章6段④句指出，目前还没有证据可以表明当人们在沮丧、疲劳或生气时会更容易犯这一错误。由此可见，沮丧的情绪并不会增加人们犯这一错误的概率,疲倦也同样不会,故排除A)"她们遭受更多的挫折”和B)“她们更容易变得疲倦";

D选项【无中生有】：文中并未提及D)“总的来说，她们在家里承担更多的工作"，故排除。

Mount Etna is one of the most active volcanoes on Earth.
The mountain has been in a state of near continuous eruption for half a million years.
Exploring the Etna geographical area reveals a history written in fire.
Before the eruptions, it was covered by forests of pine trees.
Located in southern Italy, Etna is the highest active volcano in Europe.
However, its height often changes when volcanic material accumulates during eruptions and subsequently collapses.
Few volcanoes in the world have an eruption history so thoroughly documented by historical records—Etna 's eruption history dates back as far as 1500 BC.
Some two hundred eruptions have been recorded down through the centuries, but compared with other volcanoes, most of its eruptions have so far been fairly light in terms of death and destruction.
Only about one hundred deaths have been attributed to the volcano.
The mountain hasn't been entirely harmless, however； in 1928 it destroyed the town of Mascali.
Over the centuries, Etna 's lower slopes have been shaped by human hands to take advantage of rich soils for growing grapes, apples and nuts.
Local people have also carved out over two hundred caves in the soft rock, and used them for everything from sacred burial places to food storage.
Large mammals once wandered the volcano 's slopes, but today foxes, wild cats, rabbits, and mice are more common.
Some of those small mammals help to sustain such big birds as golden eagles.

My name is Brandon Leonard, and I 'm an author, magazine writer, filmmaker and public speaker.
I 'm self-employed, which means I work for myself and I do what I love.
We have a popular saying in America which goes, “Do what you love, and you'll never work a day in your life.
But I 'm here to tell you that instead of focusing on doing what we love, I think we should focus on loving what we do.
In my line of work, you 'll hear a lot about talent, which is an idea we mostly invented to give ourselves an excuse to be lazy.
Here 's why: if you see someone doing something really well, you would say it 's because they are talented.
You think they are somehow special.
You discount the tremendous amount of work they 've done to get to where they are.
Research has shown that talent is nothing without hard work.
I choose to believe in hard work, but not so much in talent.
There are no special people, just people who put in enough hard work until something special happens.
I can promise you one thing: whatever you choose to do for a career, if you work hard at it, eventually special things will happen.
They may not happen as quickly as you 'd like them to, and they may turn out to be completely different from the special things you imagined at the beginning, but they will happen.

A question we often ask others and are also frequently asked by others is "what do you normally do after school or work?"
Some commonplace answers are, “Well, I go to the gym." "Um, I just go home and watch TV. ” "I meet my friends for dinner." or "I just go to bed because it 's so late and I 'm tired.
Unlike any of these typical responses, I 'm proud to say that I love to dance salsa after a long and tiring day of work.
Salsa is a kind of dancing that evolved in the mid-1970s in New York.
My dancing life began not because I wanted to do it, but because my mother was sick and tired of seeing me running around after school doing nothing.
So she enrolled me into a ballet course when I was six.
I fell in love with it instantly and continued with ballet dancing for about ten years.
Then, I left my native country of New Zealand to start my career as an English teacher, which eventually brought my dancing life to a halt.
It wasn 't until I rediscovered salsa in a lovely studio while working in Asia that I renewed my passion for dancing.
Since then, I have been trying to attend dancing classes twice a week after work.
It 's a great way for me to relieve stress and pressure, and dance my way towards feeling energetic and happy again.

sections.passage: 1 Lanterns originated in the Eastern Han Dynasty, and were at first used primarily for lighting. 2 In the Tang Dynasty, people used red lanterns to celebrate a stable life. 3 Since then, lanterns have become popular in many parts of China. 4 Lanterns are usually made of brightly-colored tissue paper in a variety of shapes and sizes. 5 In traditional Chinese culture, red lanterns symbolize a happy life and flourishing business, usually hung during festivals like the Spring Festival, the Lantern Festival and the National Day. 6 Today, red lanterns can also be seen in many other parts of the world.

形容词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前面是最高级标志词the most,后面是名词predators,因此本空应填入形容词作定语。

【答案解析】

空格所在句指出，作为最______食肉动物之一，虎鲸也许不符....本句的主语是killer whales, 空格处表示它们是最_____食肉动物之一。由名字killer whales可以推断这种动物很凶残，下一句提到these beasts of the sea,由beasts 也可以得出同样的判断。因此,本空应填人含有“凶猛的，凶残的”意义的形容词,故C)brutal野蛮的，凶残的”为本题答案。

空格前面是副词highly,后面是名词behaviors,因此本空应填入形容词作定语。

【答案解析】

空格所在句指出，但是，这些海中猛兽确实展现出许多非常行为，这些行为似乎正在推动着它们基因的发展。前一句提到，虎鲸也许不符合有教养的生物的形象。本句与前一句构成转折关系，说明虎鲸的许多行为可以体现出它们是有教养的，因此本空填人的形容词应该是褒义的，而且与“有教养”相关。备选形容词中，只有K) refined"" 优雅的,有教养的”符合要求。

空格前面是关系代词which,后面是动词means,且which引导的定语从句成分完整，因此应填入副词修饰动词。

空格所在句指出，“文化”一词来源汗拉丁语“colerc”,_____“意思就是“培养”。 本句解释“文化”一词的词源，which引导的非限制性定语从句又是对拉丁语“colere”的一种解释. 结合备选副词可知,literally“根据字面意思，按照原义”符合句意，故为答案。

动词辨析题。

空格前面是be动词is,且空格处所填词和空格后的过去分词learnt是由or 连接的并列成分，因此本空应填入动词的过去分词形式。

空格所在句指出，格陵兰岛的爱斯基摩人数代都以猎杀北极高脂肪的海洋哺乳动物为生，他们产生了某些基因适应性来帮助他们消化和利用这种富含脂肪的食物，因此他们能在寒冷的气候中_____。由此可推断，爱斯基摩人能消化和利用富含脂肪的食物，这使得他们能在寒冷的气候中生活。因此，本空应填人含有“生活，生存”意义的动词原形。结合备选项可知,本题答案为O) thrive""茁壮成长，兴旺”

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前面是词组a range of和形容词different,因此应填入复数名词。

【答案解析】

空格所在句指出,同人类-样 ，虎鲸聚居在全球许多不同的。本句说明虎鲸在地球上分布很广泛，由此可推断空格处应填人含有“居住地，栖息地”意义的复数名词，故本题答案为G) habitats 栖息地，生活环境”。另外一个备选复数名词B) adaptations"" 适应;改编版”不符合句意,因此排除。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

分析句子结构可知，空格位于由that引导的定语从句中，从句中缺少谓语，因此应填入动词。本文通篇用的是现在时，而且此定语从句的先行词是an empire,因此应填入动词的第三人称单数形式。

【答案解析】

空格所在句指出,同人类一样 ,虎鲸聚居在全球许多不同的栖息地，占据着地球上的每一处海洋盆地，拥有一个从南极_____至北极的帝国。由句意可知，从南极到北极都分布着虎鲸的栖息地。因此,本空应填人含有“扩展,延伸”意义的动词。结合备选项可知,本题答案为F)extends""延伸”。另外一个动词的第三人称单数L) revolves"" (使)旋转”不符合句意，因此排除。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格位于lead sb. to do sth.的结构中,因此应填入动词原形。

【答案解析】

空格所在句前一句提到，不同种群的虎鲸必须学习不同的捕猎技巧,才能在追捕当地猎物时占据上风。空格所在句指出,这反过来又对它们的饮食习惯产生重大影响，这使科学家，学习特定种群的捕猎方法的能力也许正在推动着虎鲸的基因发展。文中并未说明“学习某一种群特有的捕猎方法的能力也许正在驱动着虎鲸的基因发展”这一论断是否得到证实，因此空格处应填入含有“猜测，猜想，推测""意义的动词原形,故本题答案为M) speculate“猜测,推测”。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Broad demographic (人口的) shifts is marital status, educational attainment and employment have transformed the way young adults in the U.S. are living, and a new Pew Research Center analysis highlights the implications of these changes for the most basic element of their lives — where they call home. 2 In 2014, for the first time in more than 130 years, adults ages 18 to 34 were slightly more likely to be living in their parents’ home than they were to be living with a spouse or partner in their own household.
1 This turn of events is fueled primarily by the dramatic drop in the share of young Americans who are choosing to settle down romantically before age 35. 2 Dating back to 1880, the most common living arrangement among young adults has been living with a romantic partner, whether a spouse or a significant other.? 3 This type of arrangement peaked around 1960, when 62% of the nation’s 18-to 34-year-olds were living with a spouse or partner in their own household, and only one-in-five were living with their parents.
1 By 2014, 31.6% of young adults were living with a spouse or partner in their own household, below the share living in the home of their parents (32.1%). 2 Some 14% of young adults lived alone, were a single parent or lived with one or more roommates. 3 The remaining 22% lived in the home of another family member (such as a grandparent, in-law or sibling (兄弟姐妹), a non-relative, or in group quarters like college dormitories.
1 It’s worth noting that the overall share of young adults living with their parents was not at a record high in 2014. 2 This arrangement peaked around 1940, when about 35% of the nation’s 18-to 34-year-olds lived with mom and/or dad (compared with 32% in 2014). 3 What has changed, instead, is the relative share adopting different ways of living in early adulthood, with the decline of romantic coupling pushing living at home to the top of a much less uniform list of living arrangements.
1 Among young adults, living arrangements differ significantly by gender. 2 For men ages 18 to 34, living at home with mom and/or dad has been the dominant living arrangement since 2009. 3 In 2014,28% of young men were living with a spouse of partner in their own home, while 35% were living in the home of their parent(s). 4 Young women, however, are still more likely to be living with a spouse of romantic partner(35%) than they are to be living with their parent(s)(29%).?
1 In 2014, more young women (16%) than young men (13%) were heading up a household without a spouse or partner. 2 This is mainly because women are more likely than men to be single parents living with their children. 3 For their part, young men (25%) are more likely than young women (19%) to be living in the home of another family member, a non-relative or in some type of group quarters.?
1 A variety of factors contribute to the long-run increase in the share of young. 2 Adults living with the parents.? 3 The first in the postponement of, if not retreat from, marriage. 4 The average age of first marriage has risen steadily for decades. 5 In addition, a growing share of young adult may be avoiding marriage altogether. 6 A previous Pew Research Center analysis projected that as many as one-in-four of today’s young adults may never marry.? 7 While cohabitation（同居）has been on the rise, the overall share of young adults either married or living with an unmarried partner has substantially fallen since 1990.
1 In addition, trends in both employment status and wages have likely contributed to the growing share of young adults who are living in the home of their parent(s), and this is especially true of young men. 2 Employed young men are much less likely to live at home than young men without a job, and employment among young men has fallen significantly in recent decades. 3 The share of young men with jobs peaked around 1960 at 84%. 4 In 2014, only 71% of 18-to-34-year-old men were employed. 5 Similarly with earnings, young men’s wages (after adjusting for inflation) have been on a downward trajectory (轨迹) since 1970 and fell significantly form 2000 to 2010. 6 As wages have fallen, the share of young men living in the home of their parent(s) has risen.?
1 Economic factors seem to explain less of why young adult women are increasingly likely to live at home. 2 Generally, young women have had growing success in the paid labor market since 1960 and hence might increasingly be expected to be able to afford to afford to live independently of their parents. 3 For women, delayed marriage — which is related, in part, to labor market outcomes for men — may explain more of the increase in their living in the family home.?
1 The Great Recession (and modest recovery) has also been associated with an increase in young adults living at home. 2 Initially in the wake of the recession, college enrollments expanded, boosting the ranks of young adults living at home. 3 And given the weak job opportunities facing young adults, living at home was part of the private safety net help young adults to weather the economic storm.?
1 Beyond gender, young adult’s living arrangements differ considerably by education — which is tied to financial means. 2 For young adults without a bachelor’s degree, as of 2008 living at home with their parents was more prevalent than living with a romantic partner. 3 By 2014, 36% of 18-to 34-year-olds who had not completed a bachelor’s degree were living with their parent(s) while 27% were living with a spouse or partner. 4 Among college graduates, in 2014 46% were married or living with a partner, and only 19% were living with their parent(s). 5 Young adults with a college degree have fared much better in the labor market than their less-educated counterparts, which has in turn made it easier to establish their own households.?

【答案解析】

【定位】

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，对女性而言，推迟结婚一 这在某种程度上与劳动力市场上男性就业不景气相关——或许能更好地解释为什么越来越多的女性选择在父母家居

住。题干中的due to对应定位句中的explain,故答案为I).

【定位】

由题干中的grown和decreased pay定位到文章H)段最后一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出,随着工资的下降,住在父母或其中一方的家中的年轻男性的比例开始上升。题干中的their decreased pay对应定位句中的wages have fallen,故答案为H)。

【定位】

【答案解析】

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 According to the majority of Americans, women are every bit as capable of being good political leaders as men. 2 The same can be said of their ability to dominate the corporate boardroom. 3 And according to a new Pew Research Center survey on women and leadership, most Americans find women indistinguishable from men on key leadership traits such as intelligence and capacity for innovation, with many saying they’re stronger than men in terms of being passionate and organized leaders.?
1 So why, then, are women in short supply at the top of government and business in the United States? 2 According to the public, at least, it’s not that they lack toughness, management talent or proper skill sets.
1 It’s also not all about work-life balance. 2 Although economic research and previous survey findings have shown that career interruptions related to motherhood may make it harder for women to advance in their careers and compete for top executive jobs, relatively few adults in the recent survey point to this as a key barrier for women seeking leadership roles.? 3 Only about one-in-five say women’s family responsibilities are a major reason why there aren’t more females in top leadership positions in business and politics.
1 Instead, topping the list of reasons, about four-in-ten Americans point to a double standard for women seeking to climb to the highest levels of either politics or business, where they have to do more than their male counterparts to prove themselves.? 2 Similar shares say the electorate (选民) and corporate America are just not ready to put more women in top leadership positions.
1 As a result, the public is divided about whether the imbalance in corporate America will change in the foreseeable future, even though women have made major advances in the workplace. 2 While 53% believe men will continue to hold more top executive positions in business in the future, 44% say it’s only a matter of time before as many women are in top executive positions as men.? 3 Americans are less doubtful when it comes to politics: 73% expect to see a female president in their lifetime.?

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What do most Americans think of women leaders according to a new Pew Research Center survey?

根据皮尤研究中心一份最新调查，大多数美国人对女性领袖有什么看法？

A)They have to do more to distinguish themselves.

她们必须做得更多才能脱颖而出

B)They have to strive harder to win their positions.

她们必须更加努力才能赢得自己的职位

C)They are stronger than men in terms of willpower.

她们比男性拥有更强大的意志力

D)They are just as intelligent and innovative as men.

她们就像男性一样聪明且富有创造力

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的a new Pew Research Center survey 定位到1段③句。定位句指出，皮尤研究中心一项有关女性和领导力的新的调查显示，大多数美国人认为，在智力和创新能力等关键的领导力特质上，女性与男性没有什么区别。故答案为D)“她们和男性样聪明,样有创新能力”。

 

【错误选项分析】

A/B选项【答非所问】：选项A)和B)是根据4段①句设置的干扰项。4段①句提到，那些想要跻身政界或商界高层的女性需要面对双重标准，她们需要比男性做得更多来证明自己。但是这是约40%的美国人的观点，并不是皮尤研究中心新的调查中显示的大多数美国人的观点，故排除A)“她们必须做得更多才能脱颖而出”和B)“她们必须更加努力才能贏得她们的职位”。

C选项【无中生有】：文章并未提及有关女性的意志力的问题，故排除C)“她们的意志力比男性强”。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What do we learn from previous survey findings about women seeking leadership roles?

关于寻求领导地位的女性，我们从此前的调查发现中知道了什么？

A)They have unconquerable difficulties on their way to success.

她们在通往成功的道路上有着克服不了的困难

B)They are lacking in confidence when competing with men.

她们在同男性竞争时缺乏自信心

C)Their failures may have something to do with family duties.

她们的失败有可能与家庭责任相关

D)Relatively few are hindered in their career advancement.

在职业发展中遇阻的女性相对较少

 

【��位及答案】

由题干中的previous survey findings和seeking leadership roles定位到3段②句。定位句提到，虽然经济研究和之前的调查结果表明，女性因为生育造成的职业中断可能会使她们更难在职业生涯中取得进步，更难竞争高管职位，但在最近的调查中，相对来说只有很少的人认为这是构成女性寻求领导角色的主要障碍。由此可知,之前的调查认为，女性的家庭责任会令其更难推进职业生涯，也很难在工作中去竞争高管职位，故答案为C)“她们的失败可能与家庭责任有关"。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【过度推理】该选项将定位句中“生/养育致事业中断，可能更难发展晋升（may make it harder）”夸大为“困难克服不了”（unconquerable）。

B选项【过度推理&无中生有】：B选项利用文中所述“女性生理方面有劣势（为家庭不得不牺牲事业）”臆断出“女性在职场上因性别而自卑”，文中并未提及女性的心理。

D选项【反向干扰】：定位句指出,之前的调查结果表明，女性因为生育造成的职业中断可能会使她们更难在职业生涯中取得进步，更难竞争高管职位,D)“相对较少的人在她们的职业发展中受到阻碍”与定位句的意思刚好相反，故排除。

【题目及选项概览】

What is the primary factor keeping women from taking top leadership positions according to the recent survey?

根据最新的调查，阻碍女性获得顶层领导职位的主要原因是什么？

A)Personality traits.

性格特点

B)Family responsibilities.

家庭责任

C)Gender bias.

性别偏见

D)Lack of vacancies.

职位空缺不足

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的the primary factor 和taking top leadership positions 定位到4段①句。定位句指出,约40%的美国人认为,最主要的原因是那些想要跻身政界或商界高层的女性需要面对双重标准，她们需要比男性做得更多来证明自己。由此可见，根据最近的调查，阻碍女性担任高层领导职位的主要因素是女性需要面对双重标准，即人们对女性有性别歧视,故答案为C)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【反向干扰】：该选项与首段③句“根据最新调查,女性和男性在关键性领导力品质方面不相上下,甚至比男性更有激情、更有条理"相悖。

B选项【断章取义】：该选项对第三段③句family responsibilities are a major reason断章取义,忽略only about one-in-five(仅两成人这么认为)所暗含的“家庭责任并非主要原因".

D选项【偷换概念】：该选项将第四段②句“选民及企业没有做好准备让女性担任高位”臆断为“职位空缺太少”。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What does the passage say about corporate America in the near future?

关于近期未来的美国企业界，文中说了什么？

A)More and more women will sit in the boardroom.

越来越多的女性将会坐进董事会会议室

B)Gender imbalance in leadership is likely to change.

领导层的性别失衡问题可能会改变

C)The public is undecided about whether women will make good leaders.

公众对女性是否能成为优秀的领导者犹疑不定

D)People have opposing opinions as to whether it will have more women leaders.

人们对企业界是否会有更多的女性领导者有分歧

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的corporate America和in the near future定位到5段①②句。定位句提到，尽管女性在职场上取得了重大进步,但在不久的未来,公众对美国公司内部的不平衡状况是否会发生改变意见不一。53%的人认为，未来男性将继续担任更多的高层管理职位;44%的人表示,女性担任高层管理职位的人数与男性一样多只是时间问题。由此可知，关于是否会有更多的女性领导人，人们有不同的意见,故答案为D)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A/B选项【答非所问】：A、B项利用②③句“女性与男性高管数量齐平只是时间问题”“希望能有一位女性总统”干扰,但它们仅为(存在分歧的)公众当中一部分人的看法(44%、73%) ,并非题干所问“作者/文中所说”。

What do most Americans expect to see soon on America’s political stage?

大多数美国人预计很快能在本国政治舞台上看到什么情况？

A)A woman in the highest position of government.

越来越多的女性积极参与政治

大部分女性投票选举一位女总统

sections.passage:
1 People have grown taller over the last century, with South Korean women shooting up by more than 20cm on average, and Iranian men gaining 16.5cm. 2 A global study looked at the average height of 18-year-olds in 200 countries 1914 and 2014.?
1 The results reveal that while Swedes were the tallest people in the world in 1914, Dutch men have risen from 12th place to claim top spot with an average height of 182.5cm. 2 Latvian women. Meanwhile, rose from 28th place in 1914 to become the tallest in the world a century later, with an average height of 169.8cm.
1 James Bentham, a co-author of the research from Imperial College, London, says the global trend is likely to be due primarily to improvements in nutrition and healthcare. 2 “An individual’s genetics has a big influence on their height, but once you average over whole populations, genetics plays a less key role,” he added.?
1 A little extra height brings a number of advantages, says Elio Riboli of Imperial College. 2 “Being taller is associated with longer life expectancy,” he said. 3 “This is largely due to a lower risk of dying of cardiovascular （心血管的） disease among taller people.”?
1 But while height has increased around the world, the trend in many countries of north and sub-Saharan Africa causes concern, says Riboli. 2 While height increased in Uganda and Niger during the early 20th century, the trend has reversed in recent years, with height decreasing among 18-year-olds.?
1 “One reason for these decreases in height is the economic situation in the 1980s,” said Alexander Moradi of the University of Sussex. 2 The nutritional and health crises that followed the policy of structural adjustment, he says, led to many children and teenagers failing to reach their full potential in terms of height.
1 Bentham believes the global trend of increasing height has important implications. 2 “How tall we are now is strongly influenced by the environment we grew up in,” he said. 3 “If we give children the best possible start in life now, they will be healthier and more productive for decades to come.”?

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What does the global study tell us about people’s height in the last hundred years?

关于过去百年里人们的身高，这项全球性研究告诉了我们什么？

A）There is a remarkable difference across continents.

各大洲间存在显著差异

B）There has been a marked increase in most countries.

在大多数国家有显著增长

C）The increase in people’s height has been quickening.

人们身高增长不断加快

D）The increase in women’s height is bigger than in men’s.

女性身高增幅大于男性

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的global study和people's height in the last hundred years定位到1段。定位段指出，在过去的一个世纪里，人们的身高不断增长，其中韩国女性的平均身高增加了20多厘米，伊朗男性的平均身高增加了16.5厘米。-项全球研究调查了1914 年至2014年间200个国家18岁人群的平均身高。第二段接着指出调查结果，列举的几个国家身高均有显著增长。由此可推断，全球大多数国家身高都有明显的增长故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念&词汇干扰】：该选项由1段South Korean, Iranian(属亚洲)增高, 2段Dutch,、Latvian(属欧洲)增高,5段Africa(非洲)先增后降的具体叙述中望文生义出“各大洲存在显著差异”,而文中研究针对的是“国家(countries)"而非“洲(continents)"。

C选项【偷换概念】：该选项将全文关键词increasing height, height has increased“身高增长"偷换为increase (in height) has been quickening“身高增速一直在加快".

D选项【词汇干扰&无中生有】：该选项由1、2段“韩国女性身高增幅大于伊朗男性”及“拉脱维亚女性身高排名跃升位次多于荷兰男性”捏造而来,但该研究只对男性、女性身高变化分别进行纵向研究,并未横向比较男女性身高增幅。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What does James Bentham say about genetics in the increase of people’s height?

关于遗传基因对身高增长的作用，詹姆斯·本瑟姆说了什么？

A）It counts less than generally thought.

它没有普遍认为的那么重要

B）It outweighs nutrition and healthcare.

它比营养和医疗保健更重要

C）It impacts more on an individual than on population.

它对个人的影响大于对群体的影响

D）It plays a more significant role in females than in males.

它对女性的作用比对男性的作用更加显著

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的James Bentham和genetics定位到3段，3段②句提到，伦敦帝国理工学院的詹姆斯认为一个人的基因对其身高有很大的影响，但是一且把他们的身高平均到整个人口基数中,基因的作用就不那么重要了。由此可以推断，基因对于个体的影响大于对整个人群的影响，故答案为C)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【词汇干扰】：该选项根据碎片信息“没那么重要(plays a less key role)"断章取义,而忽视其前述条件:当涉及人口整体的平均身高时。】

B选项【反向干扰】：定位段指出，全球身高增长趋势可能主要是由于营养和医疗保健的改善。一个人的基因对其身高有很大的影响，但是一旦把他们的身高平均到整个人口基数中，基因的作用就不那么重要了。由此可见，对于整个群体来说，营养和医疗保健改善的作用要大于基因，故排除B)。

D选项【偷换概念】：将“对个体影响大于对群体影响”偷换为“对女性影响大于对男性影响”,而本瑟姆并未谈及遗传基因对男女身高的影响。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What does Elio Riboli say about taller people?

关于高个人群，诶里奥·里博利说了什么？

A）They tend to live longer.

他们的寿命往往更长

B）They enjoy an easier life.

他们的生活环境更加安逸

C）They generally risk fewer fatal diseases.

他们患致命疾病的风险通常较低

D）They have greater expectations in life.

他们对生活有更高的期望

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Elio Riboli定位到4段。定位段指出,埃利奥·诺里博利认为稍微高一点儿会带来很多好处。个子越高,预期寿命越长。由此可见，个子越高,活得越久,故答案为A)。

【错误选项分析】

B选项【无中生有】：定位段并未提及高个子的人活得更轻松,故排除B)。

C选项【偷换概念】：定位段指出,埃利奧.诺里博利认为,个子越高，预期寿命越长。这主要是由于高个子人群死于心血管疾病的风险较低。但由此无法得出高个子的人通常患有致命疾病的风险要少,故排除C)。

D选项【词汇干扰】：定位段指出,个子越高,活得越久。但由此并不能得出高个子的人对生活有更高的期望,D)选项的干扰来自life expectancy"预期寿命”和expectations in life“对生活的期望”之间的区别,故排除)。

【题目及选项概览】

What do we learn about 18-year-olds in Uganda and Niger?

关于乌干达和尼日尔的18岁人���，我们了解到什么？

A) They grow up slower than their peers in other countries.

他们比其他国家的同龄人长得慢

B) They are actually shorter than their earlier generations.

他们实际上比前几代人更矮

C) They find it hard to bring their potential into full play.

他们发觉很难充分发挥其潜能

D) They have experienced many changes of government

他们经历了多次政权更迭

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的18-year-olds 和in Uganda and Niger定位到5段②句。定位句提到，尽管乌干达人和尼日尔人的身高在20世纪初呈增长趋势,但近年来这一趋势发生了逆转，18岁人群的身高呈下降趋势。由此可知，乌干达和尼日尔的18岁人群实际上比他们的前几代人更矮,故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：定位句是说近年来乌干达和尼日尔的18岁人群比他们前几代人要矮，而并不是比其他国家的同龄人成长得慢,A)与定位句表述相矛盾,故排除。

C选项【偷换概念&过度推理】：6段②句指出,结构调整政策带来了营养和健康危机，从而导致许多儿童和青少年未能充分发挥身高方面的潜力。但由此并不能得出乌干达和尼日尔的18岁人群很难充分发挥自己其他方面的潜力,C)与文章表述不一致,故排除。

D选项【无中生有&常识干扰】：6段①句指出,苏塞克斯大学的亚历山大·莫拉迪认为,身高下降的原因之一是20世纪80年代的经济形势。但根据本句无法推出乌干达和尼日尔的18岁人群经历了政府的许多变化,故排除D)。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What does James Bentham suggest we do?

詹姆斯·本瑟姆建议我们做什么？

A) Watch closely the global trend in children’s development.

密切关注儿童发展的全球趋势

B) Make sure that our children grow up to their full height.

确保我们的孩子充分长高

C) Try every means possible to improve our environment.

尽一切可能改善我们的环境

D) Ensure our children grow up in an ideal environment.

确保我们的孩子在理想的环境中成长

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的James Bentham suggest定位到7段②③句。定位句指出，边沁认为我们现在的身高很大程度上受到成长环境的影响。如果我们现在就给孩子们最好的人生开端,那么他们在未来几十年里会更健康、会成为更有价值的人。由此可知，边沁认为我们应确保我们的孩子在一个理想的环境中成长,故答案为D)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【词汇干扰】：该选项利用7段碎片信息the global trend, children和grew up杂糅干扰,但文中未提及"儿童发展的全球趋势”

B选项【过度推理&偷换概念】：该选项由7段③句“儿童和青少年无法充分发挥其身高潜能”主观推断Bentham建议“确保孩子充分发挥身高潜能”,但Bentham的关注点在于“孩子的成长环境(饮食营养及医疗设施等)对身高的影响,进而对个人健康、发展成就的影响".

C选项【偷换概念（范围过大）】：该选项将第7段②句the environment we grew up in“成长环境”过度泛化为our environment"人类环境"。

1 A group of student volunteers, recruited by the Student Union, went to visit a Hope Elementary School in a neighboring county on the 5th of the June with the intention of celebrating the upcoming Dragon Boat Festival with the children there.
1 Upon arrival, our volunteers were surrounded by a crowd of lively children. 2 Their innocent smiles refreshed everyone exhausted from the long journey. 3 After being guided to a classroom, the volunteers unpacked a suitcase filled with precooked sticky rice dumplings. 4 While the dumplings were heated up, a volunteer explained the origin and customs of the Dragon Boat Festival to the children, who could hardly hide their growing excitement. 5 After the meal finished, a tug of war was held as a substitute for a dragon boat race, in which all the kids seemed deeply involved either by pulling at the rope with all their strength or cheering competitors on wildly.
1 It was a day of real joy. 2 But more than that, our volunteers gave the pupils a rewarding experience of the glamour of traditional Chinese culture and teamwork.

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 Paper cutting is a unique form of Chinese folk art and has a history of more than 2,000 years. 2 Paper cutting probably originates in the Han Dynasty, following the invention of paper. 3 Since then, it has gained popularity in many places of China. 4 The materials and tools used for paper cutting are simple: paper and scissors. 5 Paper-cuts are usually made of red paper, because red is associated with happiness in traditional Chinese culture. 6 Therefore, on festive occasions such as weddings and the Chinese New Year, red paper-cuts are the first choice for decorating doors and windows.

questions.stem: ①剪纸是中国民间艺术的一种独特形式，已有2,000多年的历史。②剪纸很可能源于汉代，继纸张发明之后。③从此，它在中国的许多地方得到了普及。④剪纸用的材料和工具很简单：纸和剪刀。⑤剪纸作品通常是用红纸做成的，因为红色在中国传统文化中与幸福相联。⑥ 因此，在婚礼、春节等喜庆场合，红颜色的剪纸是门窗装饰的首选。
