【考点】

形容词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前是定冠词the,后面是名词词组ups and downs,因此空格处应填入形容词。

【答案解析】

空格所在句介绍第一种财务压力，即投资市场的起伏带来的财务压力。投资市场总是有涨有跌的，这是正常现象，因此空格处应填入含有“正常的，通常的”意义的形容词，由此确定I) normal“正常的"为本题答案。

【考点】

副词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格所在部分与not so much the ups构成并列结构，the ups 前面有副词词组not so much,因此空格处应填入副词。

【答案解析】

空格所在结构与破折号前面的内容密不可分，是对ups and downs of investment markets做进一步解释。由常识可知，人们并不那么担心投资的上涨,但一定会担心下跌，因此空格处应填入含有“一定,确定”意义的副词,故答案为E) definitely“确切地，肯定地”。

【考点】

形容词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前是不定冠词a,后面是名词percentage,因此空格处应填入形容词。

【答案解析】

本段介绍第二种财务压力，即债务带来的压力，其中信用卡债务和贷款是核心要素。本段最后一句提到，虽然有汽车贷款或抵押贷款带来的债务,但是对很多人来说，信用卡是导致财务困难的源头。由此可知，在债务导致的财务压力中,很多情况下，信用卡和贷款是主要原因，因此空格处应填入含有“多的，大的”意义的形容词，故D)considerable“相当大的""为本题答案。

【考点】

副词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格后面是形容词最高级the least known,并且句子成分完整，因此空格处应填入副词。

【答案解析】

第三段介绍了第三种财务压力——继承性财务压力。文章在介绍前两种压力时，用到了apparent“明显的 ” 和common“普遍的”，而在介绍第三种压力时用到的形容词the least known“最不为人知的”。由此可知，相对于前两种压力而言，第三种可能是鲜为人知的，因此应填入含有“也许，可能”意义的副词,故本题答案为J) possibly“可能,或许”。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格处与后面的fought构成并列谓语，因此空格处应填入动词的过去式。

【答案解析】

本句说明了什么样的人会经历继承性压力。空格所在从句提到，他们的父母经常为了钱___和打架。 因此,空格处应填入与fought“打架”意义相近的动词，故本题答案为B) argued“争论，争吵”。动词过去式形式的备选词还有L) rebelled,但 是填入空格不符合句意，因此排除。

【考点】

词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前是冠词an和形容词unattractive,因此空格处应填入可数名词单数形式。

【答案解析】

由本段可知，由于父母因钱而争吵不休，他们的子女便认为金钱是一个充满压力的话 题,因此规划财务的意见也变得没有吸引力。空格处所填词与the thought形成照应，因此应填入含有“意见，建议”意义的名词，由此确定K) proposition“提议，建议”是本题答案。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空���前的现在分词短语suffering inherited financial anxiety 作后置定语，修饰Those,空格所在句缺少谓语动词，因此空格处应填入动词，且能与to do连用。

【答案解析】

本句介绍了经历继承性财务压力的人所呈现的两种模式，但是这种划分并不是完全绝对的，因此应填入含有“通常，倾向于”意义的动词，故本题答案为N) tend“倾向于，往往会”。 tend to do意为“往往会发生,通常会发生”。在备选动词中,其余三个动词都不能与to do连用，因此排除。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前是情态动词would,因此空格处应填入动词原形。

【答案解析】

本句介绍了经历继承性财务压力的人所呈现的第一种模式。 空格前的put their head in the sand是一个习语，意为“逃避现实”,来源于鸵鸟遇到危险时把头埋进沙子里的典故。空格所在部分对此进行进一步的解释，空格后的内容与处理财务问题有关，因此部分应表达他们会避免做这些事情。由此可以确定本题答案为C)avoid“避免”。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前是限定词other,因此空格处应填入名词。

【答案解析】

本句介绍了经历继承性财务压力的人所呈现的第二种模式。这些人会对所有事情进行细致入微的分析，与第一种避免处理财务问题的人相比,这是另一种极端，因此应填入含有“极端”极端意义的名词，故本题答案为F) extreme“极端”。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前是形容词complete, 因此空格处应填入名词。

【答案解析】

由后句可知，第二种人确信，他们所做的任何决定都是错误的。所以，他们虽然细致入��地分析了所有事情，却什么也不做，由此确定本题答案为G) inaction “不作为，无行动”。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Imagine a drug that could enhance a child’s creativity and critical thinking. Imagine that this drug were simple to make, safe to take, and could be had for free. 2 The nation’s leading pediatricians（ 儿科医生） say this miracle compound exists. 3 In a new clinical report, they are urging doctors to prescribe it liberally to the children in their care.
1 “This may seem old-fashioned, but there are skills to be learned when kids aren’t told what to do,” said Dr. Michael Yogman, a Harvard Medical School pediatrician who led the drafting of the call to arms. 2 Whether its rough physical play, outdoor play or pretend play, kids derive important lessons from the chance to make things up as they go, he said.?
1 The advice, issued Monday by the American Academy of Pediatrics, may come as a shock to some parents. 2 After spending years fretting （ 烦恼 ） over which toys to buy, which apps to download and which skill-building programs to send their kids to after school, letting them simply play — or better yet, playing with them — could seem like a step backward. 3 The pediatricians insist that it’s not. 4 The academy’s guidance does not include specific recommendations for the dosing of play. 5 Instead, it asks doctors to advise parents before their babies turn two that play is essential to healthy development.?
1 “Play is not silly behavior,” the academy’s report declares. 2 It fosters children’s creativity, cooperation and problem-solving skills — all of which are critical for a 21st⁃century workforce. 3 When parents engage in play with their children, it builds a wall against the harmful effects of all kinds of stress, including poverty, the academy says. 4 In the pediatricians’ view, essentially every life skill that’s valued in adults can be built up with play. 5 “Collaboration, negotiation, decision-making, creativity, leadership, and increased physical activity are just some of the skills and benefits children gain through play,” they wrote. 6 The pediatricians appeal comes as kids are being squeezed by increasing academic demands at school and the constant invasion of digital media.?
1 The trends have been a long time coming. 2 Between 1981 and 1997, detailed time-use studies showed that the time children spent at play declined by 25 percent. 3 Since the adoption of sweeping education reforms in 2001, public schools have steadily increased the amount of time devoted to preparing for standardized tests. 4 The focus on academic “ skills and drills” has cut deeply into recess （课间休息） and other time for free play.?
1 By 2009, a study of Los Angeles kindergarten classrooms found that five-year-olds were so burdened with academic requirements that they were down to an average of just 19 minutes per day of “choice time,” when they were permitted to play freely with blocks, toys or other children. 2 One in four Los Angeles teachers reported there was no time at all for “free play.” 3 Increased academic pressures have left 30 percent of U. S. kindergarten classes without any recess. 4 Such findings prompted the American Academy of Pediatrics to issue a policy statement in 2013 on the “crucial role of recess in school.”?
1 Pediatricians aren’t the only ones who have noticed. 2 In a report titled “Crisis in the Kindergarten,” a group of educators, health professionals and child advocates called the loss of play in early childhood “a tragedy, both for the children themselves and for our nation and the world.” 3 Kids in play-based kindergartens “end up equally good or better at reading and other intellectual skills, and they are more likely to become well-adjusted healthy people,” the Alliance for Childhood said in 2009. 4 Indeed, new research demonstrates why playing with blocks might have been time better spent, Yogman said. 5 The trial assessed the effectiveness of an early mathematics intervention （干预 ） aimed at preschoolers. 6 The results showed almost no gains in math achievement.?
1 Another playtime thief: the growing proportion of kids’ time spent in front of screens and digital devices, even among preschoolers. 2 Last year, Common Sense Media reported that children up through age eight spent an average of two hours and 19 minutes in front of screens each day, including an average of 42 minutes a day for those under two. 3 This increase of digital use comes with rising risks of obesity, sleep deprivation and cognitive （认知的）, language and social-emotional delays, the American Academy of Pediatrics warned in 2016.?
1 “ I respect that parents have busy lives and its easy to hand a child an iPhone,” Yogman said. 2 “ But there’s a cost to that.? 3 For young children, its much too passive. 4 And kids really learn better when they’re actively engaged and have to really discover things.”
1 The decline of play is a special hazard for the roughly 1 in 5 children in the United States who live in poverty. 2 These 14 million children most urgently need to develop the resilience （韧劲） that is cultivated with play. 3 Instead, Yogman said, they are disproportionately affected by some of the trends that are making play scarce: academic pressures at schools that need to improve test scores, outside play areas that are limited or unsafe, and parents who lack the time or energy to share in playtime.
1 Yogman also worries about the pressures that squeeze playtime for more affluent kids. 2 “The notion that as parents we need to schedule every minute of their time is not doing them a great service,” he said. 3 Even well-meaning parents may be “robbing them of the opportunity to have that joy of discovery and curiosity — the opportunity to find things out on their own.”?
1 Play may not be a hard sell to kids. 2 But UCLA pediatrician Carlos Lerner acknowledged that the pediatricians new prescription may meet with skepticism （怀疑） from parents, who are anxious for advice on how to give their kids a leg up in the world. 3 They should welcome the simplicity of the message, Lerner said. 4 “ It’s liberating to be able to offer them this advice: that you spending time with your child and letting him play is one of the most valuable things you can do,” he said. 5 “ It doesn’t have to involve spending a lot of money or time, or joining a parenting group. 6 It’s something we can offer that’s achievable. 7 They just don’t recognize it right now as particularly valuable.”?

questions.explanation:
【定位】

由题干中的digital devices、steals和playtime定位到文章H)段第一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到另一个盗走游戏时间的小偷，即孩子花在屏幕和数字设备前的时间越来越多。题干中的Increased use of digital devices对应定位句中的the growing proportion of kids' time spent in front of screens and digital  devices,故答案为H)。

【定位】

由题干中的an increasing amount of time 、public schools、recess和academic activities定位到文章E)段第三、四句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句指出,自2001年全面推行教育改革以来，公立学校一直在稳步增加准备标准化考试的时间，对学术“技能和训练”的关注已经大大减少了课间休息和其他自由活动的时间。题干中的Since the beginning of this century对应定位句中的Since the adoption of sweeping education reforms in 2001，题干中的an increasing amount of time has been shifted in public schools from recess to academic activities academic “skills and drills"" has cut deeply into recess and other time for free play的概括归纳, 故答案为E)。

【定位】

由题干中的acknowledged pediatricians、parents 和doubt定位到文章L)段第二句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句指出，让孩子们接受玩游戏这一建议不难，但可能会遭到家长们的质疑，他们急切地希望得到如何助孩子一臂之力的建议。题干中的kids may welcome pediatricians' recommendation对应定位句中的Play may not be a hard sell to kids,题干中的their parents may doubt its feasibility是对定位句中the pediatricians' new prescription may meet with skepticism from parents的概括归纳，故答案为L)

【定位】

由题干中的professionals、young children's playtime和the world定位到文章G)段第二句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句指出,在一份题为《幼儿园危机》的报告中，一群教育工作者、卫生专业人士和儿童(权利)倡导者称,无论是对儿童本身，还是对我们的国家和世界来说，幼儿时期的游戏缺失都是“一场悲剧”。题干中的some professionals 是对定位句中a group of educators, health professionals and child advocates的��括归纳,题干中的deprivation of young children's playtime wild o harm not only to children themselves but to the country and the world是对定位句中called the loss of play in early childhood “a tragedy， both for the children themselves and for our nation and the world""的同义转述，故答案为G)

【定位】

由题干中的playing with children、harmed和stress定位到文章D) 段第三句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题，定位句指出，当父母和孩子们一起玩耍时，这就为孩子筑起了一堵墙，以抵御包括贫困在内的各种压力带来的有害影响。题干中的By playing with children是对定位句中When parents engage in play with their children 的同义转述， 题干中的prevent them from being harmed by stress是对定位句中build saw all against the harmful effects of all kinds of stress，including poverty的概括归纳， 故答案为D) 。

【定位】

由题干中的discovery和Yogman定位到文章D段。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题，定位段指出，尤格曼认为，父母因为忙碌而让孩子玩手机是有代价的，对小孩子来说，玩手机太被动了，当孩子们积极参与并真正发现事物时，他们可以学得更好。换言之，儿科医生尤格曼认为玩手机或数字设备会阻碍孩子主动发现事物。题干是对定位段的概括归纳，故答案为I)。

【定位】

由题干中的letting children simply play、backwards和skills定位到文章C) 段第二句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题，定位句指出，多年来，家长们一直在为买什么玩具、下载哪些应用程序、让孩子放学后去参加哪些技能培养项目而烦恼，仅仅是让他们玩耍——或者说，与他们一起更好地玩要——似乎像是后退了一步， 题干中的The suggestion of letting children simply play和sound like going backwards分别是对定位句中letting them simply play-or better yet， playing with them和could seem like a step backward的同义转述,题干中的parents who want to help，build their children's skills是对定位句spending years fretting over which toys to buy，which apps to download and which skill-building programs to send their kids to afterschool的概括归纳，故答案为C)。

【定位】

由题干中的the idea， schedule children’s time和may not be helpful定位到文章K) 段第二句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，尤格曼认为，父母需要为孩子安排他们每一分钟的时间这样一种观念其实并不是在帮孩子。题干中的the idea that parents should carefully schedule children's time和may not be helpful分别是对定位句中The notion that as parents we need to schedule every minute of their time和could seem like a step backward的同义转述， 题干中的may not be helpful是对定位句中not doing them a great service的同义转述， 故答案为K) 。

【定位】

由题干中的One quarter of teachers、no time和playing freely定位到文章下) 段第二句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题，定位句指出，洛杉矶四分之一的教师表示根本没有时间“自由地玩耍”。题干中的One quarter of teachers in an American city 和had no time for playing freely分别是对定位句中One in four Los Angeles teachers和there was no time at all for “free play.”的同义转述， 故答案为F)。

【定位】

由题干中的a pediatrician、learning和create things定位到文章B) 段第二句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题，定位句指出，尤格曼认为，无论是剧烈的身体运动、户外游戏，还是扮演游戏，孩子们都能在边玩耍边创作东西的过程中学到重要的一课。题干中的no matter what kind of play 是对定位句中Whether it's rough physical play，outdoor play or pretend play的概括,题干中的learning how to create things是对定位句中derive important lessons from the chance to make things up as they go的归纳，故答案为B) 。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 Americans spend billions of dollars each year trying to change our weight with diets, gym memberships and plastic surgery.
1 Trying to live up to the images of "perfect" models and movie heroes has a dark side: anxiety, depression, as well as unhealthy strategies for weight loss or muscle gain. 2 It also has a financial cost.? 3 Having an eating disorder boosts annual health care costs by nearly US $ 2,000 per person.
1 Why is there both external and internal pressure to look "perfect"? 2 One reason is that society rewards people who are thin and healthy-looking. 3 Researchers have shown that body mass index is related to wages and income.? 4 Especially for women, there is a clear penalty at work for being overweight or obese. 5 Some studies have also found an impact for men, though a less noticeable one.
1 While the research literature is clear that labor market success is partly based on how employers and customers perceive your body image, no one had explored the other side of the question. 2 Does a persons own perception of body image matter to earnings and other indicators of success in the workplace?
1 Our recently published study answered this question by tracking a large national random sample of Americans over a critical time period when bodies change from teenage shape into adult form and when people build their identities.?
1 As in other research, women in our sample tend to over⁃perceive weight — they think they’re heavier than they are — while men tend to under⁃perceive theirs.
1 We found no relationship between the average persons self-perception of weight and labor market outcomes, although self⁃perceived weight can influence self-esteem （ 自尊心）, mental health and health behaviors.
1 While the continued gender penalty in the labor market is frustrating, our finding that misperceived weight does not harm workers is more heartening?
1 Since employers’ perception of weight is what matters in the labor market, changing discrimination laws to include body type as a category would help. 2 Michigan is the only state that prohibits discrimination on the basis of weight and height. 3 We believe expanding such protections would make the labor market more fair and efficient.?

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What does the author say may have an adverse impact on people?

作者说什么可能对人们有不良影响？

A) Undergoing plastic surgeries in pursuit of beauty.

为追求美而接受整形手术

B) Imitating the lifestyles of heroes and role models.

模仿主角和榜样的生活方式

C) Striving to achieve perfection regardless of financial cost.

不顾经济成本力争达到完美

D) Attempting to meet society’s expectation of appearance.

试图满足社会对外貌的期望

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的adverse impact定位到2段①句。定位句指出，试图达到“完美”模特和电影英雄的形象有不良影响，这会导致一系列问题。由此可见，试图满足社会对外表的期望会产生负面影响，故答案为D) “试图满足社会对外表的期望”。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【以偏概全】：A)提到的整形手术只是追求完美体型的一种方式，不够全面，故排除。

B选项【无中生有&过度推理】：第二段第一句只是提到力求“完美"模特和电影英雄那样的形象，并未提及模仿他们的生活方式，故排除B)。

C选项【范围过大】：定位句提到追求完美形象的问题，且全文都围绕体型进行探讨，C)中的 achieve perfection意义太宽泛，与文章内容不符，故排除。

【题目及选项概览】

What have researchers found out about people’s earnings?

关于人们的收入，研究人员发现了什么？

A) They are closely related to people’s social status.

它们与人们的社会地位紧密相关

B) They have to do with people’s body weight and shape.

它们与人们的体重和体型相关

C) They seem to matter much less to men than to women.

较之女性，它们似乎对男性而言远没有那么重要

D) They may not be equal to people’s contributions.

它们可能与人们的贡献不相当

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的people's  earning 定位到3段③句。定位句提到，研究人员发现，体重指数与工资和收人有关，由此可知人们的收人和体重、体型有关，故答案为B).

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【无中生有】：文中没有提到社会地位和收人的关系，故排除A).

D选项【无中生有】：文中没有提到D)中提及的贡献问题,故排除。

老板对雇员身体形象的看法如何影响其晋升

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的recent study和focus on定位到5段。定位段指出作者的团队近期公布的研究回答了这个问题，因此可从上一段找出这个问题是什么。4段最后一句就是作者的研究重点，即一个人对自己身体形象的看法是否会影响他的收人和其他职场中成功的指标，故答案为C)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：4段①句指出，虽然研究文献资料清楚地表明，劳动力市场的成功在一定程度 上取决于雇主和顾客对你身体形象的看法，但没有人探究过这个问题的另一面，而这才是作者研究的重点，故排除A)。

B选项【无中生有】：文中未提及B)"在劳动力市场上追求成功时最重要的品质”，故排除。

D选项【答非所问&反向干扰】：由4段①句可以看出D)"老板对身体形象的认知如何影响员工的进步”是前人已经研究过的内容,而非作者的研究重点，故排除。

sections.passage:
1 The work-life balance is dead. 2 By this, I’m not advocating that you should give up your pursuit of having a fulfilling career and a thriving personal life, and I am definitely not saying that you have to give up one to have the other. 3 I also acknowledge that we have a work⁃life problem, but I’m arguing that the concept of balance has never been helpful, because it’s too limiting.? 4 You see, our language makes a difference, and how we refer to things matters because it affects our thinking and therefore our actions.?
1 At the minimum, most of us work because we want to be able to support ourselves, our families, and the people around us. 2 In the ideal world, we' re all doing work that we' re proud of and that provides meaning and purpose to us. 3 But even if your job doesn’t give you shivers of joy with each new day, working is a part of what each of us does and the contribution we make to society.? 4 When you separate work and life, it's a little bit harder to make that connection. 5 But when you think of work as part of a full life and a complete experience, it becomes easier to see that success in one aspect often supports another.
1 Losing your balance and falling isn’t pleasant. 2 A goal to balance suggests that things could quickly get off balance, and that causes terrible outcomes. 3 It's more constructive to think of solutions that continue to evolve over shifts in life and work. 4 Rather than falling or failing, you may have good days or better days or not-so-good days. 5 These variations are normal, and it's more useful to think of life as something that is ever evolving and changing, rather than a high-risk enterprise where things could go wrong with one misstep.?
1 How we talk to ourselves matters, and how we talk about issues makes a difference. 2 Let’s bury “work-life balance” and think bigger and better about work-life fulfillment to do a little less balancing and a lot more living.?

1 In brief, teachers are supposed to take both the teaching efficiency and students ' learning outcome into consideration, and make a good balance between them. 2 After all, all the use of PPT should respect the educational principles and students ' real needs.

questions.explanation:
【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

分析空格所在句子可知，空格前后均为名词词组，句中缺少谓语动词，因此本空应填入动词。

【答案解析】

本句指出，世界上大大小小的航空公司的飞机座椅都会用到蓝色。因此，本空应填入含有“使用，利用""意义的动词，由此可知本题答案为H) integrate“使融入”。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前是限定词no，因此本空应填入名词。

【答案解析】

由下一句可知，所有航空公司的飞机座椅都会融入蓝色是有其心理学原因的，所以这不是巧合：由此可知，本空应填入含有“巧合”意义的名词， 故本题答案为B) coincidence“巧合”。

【考点】

形容词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前是is， 空格后是with， 因此本空应填入形容词或动词的分词形式。

【答案解析】

空格前一句提到，航空公司的飞机座椅都会用到蓝色，其背后有心理学原因。本句揭示原因：蓝色能让人联想到信任、效率、安静、凉爽、沉思和平静这些积极的品质。因此，本空应填入含有“联系到，联想到“意义的形容词或动词的分词形式，故本题答案为A) associated“(与……)相关联的”。在备选的形容词或动词的分词形式中，其他选项都不能与with搭配，因此排除。

【考点】

形容词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前是more，而且空格处所填词作it的宾语补足语，因此本空应填入形容词。

【答案解析】

空格前的it指代the airline's brand。由句意可知，奈杰尔·古德认为，设计师的工作是强化航空公司的品牌，从而使更多的人认识该品牌。因此，本空应填入含有“可识别的，可辨认的”意义的形容词，由此确定本题答案为L)recognizable“可辨认的， 可认出的”。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

分析句子结构可知，空格所在部分是定语从句， that指代先行词an inter作从句的主语，而该从句中没有谓语动词。又因为主语是第三人称单数，因此本空应填入动词的第三人称单数形式。

【答案解析】

由空格后面的to create a pleasant environment(以创造令人愉悦的环境) 可知,飞机的内饰应该让人感到十分舒适，因此，本空应填入含有“产生，制造”意义的动词，结合所给选项，I) maximizes“使增加到最大限度”最符合句意，故为正确答案。在备选的动词第三人称单数形式中，O) symbolizes不符合句意，因此排除。

【考点】

形容词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前是less，而且空格处所填词作the traveling experience的宾语补足语， 因此本空应填入形容词。

【答案解析】

本段解释飞机座椅采用蓝色的原因。and后面的句子指出，据说蓝色能产生冷静的感觉，也就是说，为了让飞行体验不那么紧张而使用蓝色。因此，本空应填入含有“紧张的，有压力”意义的形容词，由此确定本题答案为N)stressful“充满压力的， 紧张的”。

【考点】

形容词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前是定冠词The，后面是名词aim，因此本空应填入形容词。

【答案解析】

本句指出，目的是营造像在家一样的令人放松的感觉。本段第一句也提到，所有工作都是为了让飞行体验不那么紧张。由此可推断，营造令人放松的感觉是主要的目的，因此本空应填入含有“主要的”意义的形容词，故本题答案为K) principal最重要的，主要的”。

【考点】

形容词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格前的feel作系动词，而且空格处所填词与domestic、earthy是并列关系， 因此本空应填入形容词。

【答案解析】

由句意可知，航空公司的主要目的是营造轻松的感觉，因此倾向于使用柔和的颜色，给人一种像家的、朴实的感觉。因此，本空应填入含有""轻松， 放松""意义的形容词，J) natural“自然的，不做作的”的词义最接近，由此确定为本题答案。

【考点】

副词辨析题。

【词性分析】

空格位于谓语动词has stuck之间，因此应填入副词。

【答案解析】

本句说明飞机座椅采用蓝色的趋势在数十年前就出现了，一直沿用到现在。stuck(原形是stick) 本义有“卡住”的意思， 说明选用蓝色的传统就像被卡住一样，被保留至今。因此，本空应填入含有“只是，只不过""意义的副词，故本题答案为M) simply“只是，仅仅”， 备选副词中， D)drastically“激烈地， 急剧地”一般用于说明改变的程度，与句意不符，因此排除。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【词性分析】

分析句子结构可知，空格所在部分是定语从句， that指代先行词shade，作从句的主语，而该从句中没有谓语动词。又因为主语是第三人称单数，因此本空应填入动词的第三人称单数形式。

【答案解析】

第一段最后一句提到，蓝色与信任、效率、安静、凉爽，沉思和平静这些积极的品质有关，而本句又提到，蓝色是一种令人愉悦的能代表公司的传统颜色，_______可信和安全。所以，本句也是在解释蓝色的象征意义。因此，本空应填入含有“象征，代表""意义的动词第三人称单数形式，故本题答案为O) symbolizes“象征”。在备选的动词第三人称单数形式中，I)maximizes不符合句意，因此排除。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 I still remember my fourth-grade social studies project. 2 Our class was studying the Gold Rush, something all California fourth-graders learned. 3 I was excited because I had asked to research Chinese immigrants during that era. 4 Growing up in the San Francisco Bay Area, I had always known that "San Francisco" translated to " Gold Mountain" in Chinese. 5 The name had stuck ever since Chinese immigrants arrived on the shores of Northern California in the 1850s, eager to try their luck in the gold mines. 6 Now I'd have the chance to learn about them.
1 My excitement was short-lived. 2 I remember heading to the library with my class and asking for help. 3 I remember the librarian's hesitation. 4 She finally led me past row after row of books, to a corner of the library where she pulled an oversized book off the shelf. 5 She checked the index and turned over to a page about early Chinese immigrants in California. 6 That was all there was in my entire school library in San Francisco, home of the nation's first Chinatown. 7 That was it.?
1 I finally had the opportunity to learn about Asian Americans like myself, and how we became part of the fabric of the United States when I took an introductory class on Asian-American history in college. 2 The class was a revelation. 3 I realized how much had been missing in my textbooks as I grew up. 4 My identity had been shaped by years of never reading, seeing, hearing, or learning about people who had a similar background as me. 5 Why, I wondered, weren't the stories, histories, and contributions of Asian Americans taught in K-12 schools, especially in the elementary schools? 6 Why are they still not taught??
1 Our students-Asian, Latino, African American, Native American, and, yes, white-stand to gain from a multicultural curriculum. 2 Students of color are more engaged and earn better grades when they see themselves in their studies. 3 Research has also found that white students benefit by being challenged and exposed to new perspectives.?
1 For decades, activists have called for schools to offer anti-racism or multicultural curricula. 2 Yet a traditional American K-12 curriculum continues to be taught from a Eurocentric point of view. 3 Being multicultural often falls back on weaving children of color into photographs, or creating a few supporting characters that happen to be ethnic - an improvement, but superficial nonetheless. 4 Elementary school classrooms celebrate cultural holidays — Lunar New Year! 5 Red envelopes! Lion dancers! 6 ——but they're quick to gloss over（掩饰）the challenges and injustices that Asian Americans have faced. 7 Most students don't, for example, learn about the laws that for years excluded Asians from immigrating to the U. S. 8 They don't hear the narratives of how and why Southeast Asian refugees (难民） had to rebuild their lives here.?
1 Research into what students learn in school has found just how much is missing in their studies. 2 In an analysis, Christine Sleeter, a professor in the College of Professional Studies at California State University, Monterey Bay, reviewed California's history and social studies framework, the curriculum determined by state educators that influences what is taught in K-12 classrooms. 3 Of the nearly 100 Americans recommended to be studied, 77% were white, 18% African American, 4% Native American, and 1% Latino. 4 None were Asian American.?
1 Worse, when Asian Americans do make an appearance in lesson books, it is often laced with problems. 2 " There hasn't been much progress, " says Nicholas Hartlep, an assistant professor at Metropolitan State University. 3 His 2016 study of K-12 social studies textbooks and teacher manuals found that Asian Americans were poorly represented at best, and subjected to racist caricatures (拙劣的模仿） at worst. 4 The wide diversity of Asian Americans was overlooked; there was very little mention of South Asians or Pacific Islanders, for example. 5 And chances were, in the images, Asian Americans appeared in stereotypical (模式化的）roles, such as engineers.?
1 Teachers with a multicultural background or training could perhaps overcome such curriculum challenges, but they're few and far between. 2 In California, 66% of K-12 teachers are white, compared with a student population that is 76% students of color. 3 Nationwide, the gap is even greater. 4 It isn't a requirement that teachers share the same racial or ethnic background as their students! 5 But the imbalance poses challenges, from the potential for unconscious bias to a lack of knowledge or comfort in discussing race and culture.?
1 How race and ethnicity is taught is crucial, says Allyson Tintiangco-Cubales, an Asian-American studies professor at San Francisco State University. 2 She added that it's not so much about the teacher's background, but about training. 3 "You can have a great curriculum but if you don't have teachers dedicated (专注于）to teaching it well, " she says, "it won't work as well as you want it to. "?
1 Some teachers are finding ways to expose students to Asian-American issues - if not during school hours, then outside of them. 2 This summer, Wilson Wong will lead a class of rising fifth-graders at a day camp dedicated to Chinese culture and the Chinese-American community in Oakland, California. 3 His student，for instance, will learn about how Chinese immigrant built the railroads in California, and even have a chance to " experience" it themselves: They will race each other to build a railroad model on the playground, with some student being forced to " work" longer and faster and at cheaper wages. 4 Wong, a middle school teacher during the school year, hopes he's exposing the student to how Chinese Americans contributed to the U.S., something that he didn't get as a student growing up in the San Francisco Bay Area. 5 "I planted the seeds early," he says. 6 "That's what I'm hoping for. "?
1 And, despite setbacks, the tide may finally be turning. 2 California legislators passed a bill last year that will bring ethnic studies to all its public high schools. 3 Some school districts, including San Francisco and Los Angeles, already offer ethnic studies at its high schools. 4 High schools in Portland, Chicago, and elsewhere have either implemented or will soon introduce ethnic studies classes. 5 And, as more high schools begin teaching it, the door could crack open for middle schools, and, perhaps inevitably, elementary schools, to incorporate a truly more multicultural curriculum. 6 Doing so will send an important message to the nation's youngest citizens: Whatever your race or ethnicity, you matter. 7 Your history matters. 8 Your story matters.?

questions.explanation:
【定位】

由题干中的cultural holidays、injustices和elementary school classrooms定位到E) 段第四句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，小学课堂庆祝一些文化节日—-农历新年!发红包!舞狮子!——但是他们很快地掩饰了亚裔美国人面对的挑战和不公平。题干中的the injustices experienced by Asian Americans是对定位句中injustices that Asian Americans have faced的同义转述，故答案为E)。

【定位】

由题干巾的Chinese immigrants和the author's school library定位到B) 段第二至七句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句提到，作者和同班同学一起去图书馆寻求帮助，图书管理员带着他来到图书馆的一个角落，从架子上拿下一本硕大的图书，她查阅索引，翻到了关于早期来到加利福尼亚州的中国移民的一页，这就是在旧金山作者的校图书馆里能找到的所有。根据这段的描述可以看出，作者学校的图书馆里关于中国移民的信息少之又少，故答案为B)。

【定位】

由题干中的A middle schoolteacher、contributions和Chinese immigrants to American定位到J)段倒数第三句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，身为一名中学教师的王老师希望他能让学生们了解华裔美国人是如何为美国做出贡献的，这是他曾经还是旧金山港湾区的学生的时候并未得到的。题干中的help students learn about对应定位句中的he's exposing the students to，题干中的Chinese immigrants to America对应定位句中的Chinese Americans，故答案为J) 。

【定位】

由题干中的No Asian Americans和recommended for study定位到F) 段最后两句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句提到，在受到推荐接受研究的近100名美国人中，77%是白人，18%是非裔美国人，4%是印第安人，1%是拉丁美洲人。没有一个是亚裔美国人。出此可知，用于K-12课堂研究、受到推荐的历史人物名单中，不包含亚裔美国人，故答案为F)。

【定位】

由题干中的lack of teachers、a multicultural perspective和curriculum challenges定位到H)段第一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题.定位句提到，有着多文化背景或是经过这种培训的老师或许能够克服这种课程挑战，但是他们的数量非常稀少。题干中的teachers with a multicultural perspective对应定位句中的Teachers with a multicultural background or training，题干中的meet the curriculum challenges对应定位句中的overcome such curriculum challenges，故答案为H) 。

【定位】

由题干中的ethnic backgrounds，learn better和a multicultural curriculum定位到D) 段第一、二句。


【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句提到，我们的学生——亚裔美国人、拉丁美洲人、非裔美国人、印第安人，还有白人——会从跨文化课程中有所收获。当有色人种的学生们在学习过程中看到了关于自己的内容，他们会更加专注而且取得更好的成绩。也就是说，在这种多文化融合的课程中，有色人种的学生们收获更大， 题干中的learn better是对定位句中are more engaged and earn better grades的归纳概括，故答案为D)。

【定位】

由题干中的high schools in America、ethnic studies和curriculums定位到K) 段第二至四句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句提到，去年，加利福尼亚州的立法者通过了一项法案，将把种族研究纳人所有公立高中。包括旧金山和洛杉矶在内的一些学区已经在其高中开设了种族研究课程。波特兰市、芝加哥和其他地方的高中已经实施或即将引人种族研究课程。归纳该部分大意，可以概括为：越来越多的美国高中正在将种族研究纳人课程体系中，故答案为K)。

【定位】

由题干中的some K-12 textbooks and teacher manuals和inadequately and improperly represented定位到G) 段第三句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，他在2016年对K-12社会研究课本和教师手册的研究中发现，最好的情况是亚裔美国人被描述的非常恶劣，最坏的情况是他们受到了种族主义者拙劣的模仿，由此可知，K-12教科书和教师手册中对亚裔美国人的描述是不恰当的，题干中的inadequately and improperly represented对应定位句中的poorly represented，故答案为G) 。

【定位】

由题干中的taking a class in college、information about Asian Americans和left out of the textbooks定位到C) 段第一至三句。


【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，当作者在大学学习一门关于亚裔美国人历史的人门课程时，他最终有机会了解像他一样的亚裔美国人，以及他们是如何成为美国社会结构的一部分。这门课程揭露了真相。伴随着作者的成长，他意识到教科书中缺失了多少信息。综合来看这三句，作者在学习了大学课程后了解了更多关于亚裔美国人的信息，同时也发现K-12教育阶段缺失很多信息。题干中的was left out是对定位句中had been missing的同义转述，故答案为C) 。

【定位】

出题干中的An Asian-American studies professor、teacher training和teachers’ background定位到Ⅰ)段第一、二句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，旧金山州立大学的亚裔美国人研究教授阿里森·廷天科-库贝尔斯说：如何教授种族和民族问题至关重要。她补充说，这与老师的背景没多大关系，但是与培训有关，题干中的placed greater emphasis on teacher training than on teachers’ background对应定位句中的not so much about the teacher's background，but about training， 故答案为I)。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 When is cleaning walls a crime? 2 When you're doing it to create art, obviously. 3 A number of street artists around the world have started expressing themselves through a practice known as reverse graffiti （涂鸦）. 4 They find dirty surfaces and paint them with images or messages using cleaning brushes or pressure hoses (高压水管）. 5 Either way, it's the same principle: the image is made by cleaning away the dirt.? 6 Each artist has their own individual style but all artists share a common aim: to draw attention to the pollution in our cities. 7 The UK's Paul Curtis, better known as Moose, operates around Leeds and London and has been commissioned by a number of companies to make reverse graffiti advertisements.?
1 Brazilian artist, Alexandre Orion, turned one of Sao Paulo's transport tunnels into an amazing wall painting in 2006 by getting rid of the dirt. 2 Made up of a series of white skulls (颅骨）, the painting reminds drivers of the effect their pollution is having on the planet. 3 "Every motorist sits in the comfort of their car, but they don't give any consideration to the price their comfort has for the environment and consequently for themselves, " says Orion.?
1 The anti-pollution message of the reverse graffiti artists confuses city authorities since the main argument against graffiti is that it spoils the appearance of both types of property: public and private. 2 This was what Leeds City Council said about Moose's work: "Leeds residents want to live in clean and attractive neighbourhoods. 3 We view this kind of advertising as environmental damage and will take strong action against it." 4 Moose was ordered to "clean up his act. " 5 How was he supposed to do this: by making all property he had cleaned dirty again??
1 As for the Brazilian artist's work, the authorities were annoyed but could find nothing to charge him with. 2 They had no other option but to clean the tunnel — but only the parts Alexandre had already cleaned. 3 The artist merely continued his campaign on the other side. 4 The city officials then decided to take drastic action. 5 They not only cleaned the whole tunnel but every tunnel in Sao Paulo.?

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What do we learn from the passage about reverse graffiti?

关于反向涂鸦艺术，我们从文中得知什么？

A) It uses paint to create anti-pollution images.

它用涂料创作反污染的图画

B) It creates a lot of trouble for local residents.

它给当地居民带来了许多麻烦

C) It causes lots of distraction to drivers.

它很容易让司机分心

D) It turns dirty walls into artistic works.

它把污秽的墙壁变成了艺术作品

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的reverse graffiti定位到1段③句。定位句后的两句指出，他们找到一些有污垢的墙面，然后用清洁刷或高压水管在上面画上图像或文字。不管用哪种方式，原则是一样的：通过擦去污垢画上图像。由此可知，反向涂鸦使肮脏的墙面变成了艺术作品，故答案为D)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：首段第四句提到，街头艺术家找到一些有污垢的墙面，然后用清洁刷或高压水管在上面画上图像或文字，而不是使用颜料，故排除A)，

B选项【反向干扰】：首段倒数第二句提到，所有的艺术家都有一个共同的目的，即提醒人们注意我们城市里的污染，而非给当地市民造成困扰，故排除B)。

C选项【偷换概念】：第二段提及一条交通隧道里的反向涂鸦壁画旨在提醒司机他们造成的污染对地球的影响，但并未说反向涂鸦会分散司机的注意力，故排除C)。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What do reverse graffiti artists try to do?

反向涂鸦艺术家试图做什么？

A) Publicise their artistic pursuit.

宣扬他们的艺术追求

B) Beautify the city environment.

美化城市环境

C) Raise public awareness of environmental pollution.

提高公众对环境污染的认识

D) Express their dissatisfaction with local governments.

表达对地方政府的不满

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的reverse graffiti artists定位到1段⑥句。定位句指出，所有的艺术家都有一个共同的目的：提醒人们注意我们城市里的污染。由此可知，反向涂鸦艺术家想提高公众对于环境污染的意识，故答案为C)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【无中生有】：文中没有提及反向涂鸦艺术家想要宣传他们的艺术追求，故排除A)，

B选项【答非所问】：反向涂鸦虽然产生了美化城市的效果，但这并不是反向涂鸦艺术家的目的，故排除B)。

D选项【无中生有】：文中没有提及反向涂鸦艺术家想要表达他们对当地政府的不满，故排除Ｄ)。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What do we learn about Brazilian artist Alexandre Orion?

关于巴西艺术家Alexandre Orion，我们了解到什么？

A) He was good at painting white skulls.

他擅长画白色的颅骨

B) He chose tunnels to do his graffiti art.

他选择隧道来做涂鸦艺术

C) He suggested banning all polluting cars.

他建议取缔所有污染环境的车辆

D) He was fond of doing creative artworks.

他喜欢创作富有创新性的艺术作品

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Brazilian artist Alexandre Orion定位到2段①句。定位句指出，巴西艺术家历山大·奥利恩在2006年通过清除灰尘把圣保罗的一条交通隧道变成了一幅令人惊叹的壁画。由此可见，亚历山大·奥利恩选择了在隧道里创作他的涂鸦艺术，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念&过度推理】：2段②句指出，亚历山大·奥利恩创作的反向涂鸦壁画是由一系列的白色颅骨构成的，但由此并不能推断出亚历山大·奥利恩擅长画白色的颅骨，故排除A)。

C选项【过度推理】：2段③句指出：奥利恩认为，每一位汽车驾驶员舒服地坐在他们的车里，但是他们丝毫没有考虑到他们的舒适给环境进而给他们自己带来的代价，奥利恩确实提醒司机要注意环境污染问题，但由此无法推出奥利恩建议禁止所有污染环境的汽车，C)为过度推断，故排除。

D选项【偷换概念&过度推理】：第二段只是指出亚历山大·奥利恩创作了一幅令人惊叹的反向涂鸦壁画，由此无法推断他喜欢创作艺术作品，D)为过度推断，故排除。

【题目及选项概览】

What does the author imply about Leeds City Council's decision?

关于利兹市议会的决议，作者暗示了什么？

A) It is simply absurd.

它简直荒唐

B) It is well-informed.

它有充分依据

C) It is rather unexpected.

它相当的出乎意料

D) It is quite sensible.

它非常合理

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Leeds City Council’s decision定位到3段②-⑤句。定位句提到，利兹市议会对穆斯的作品作出这样的评价：“利兹市民想要生活在干净和有魅力的社区里。我们认为这种广告是对环境的破坏，我们会采取强硬措施来抵制它。” 穆斯被要求“清理自己做过的事”。他应该怎么做呢?要把他已经清洁的所有墙面再弄脏吗?作者以反讽的语气说明无法清除已经创作好的反向涂鸦作品。由此可见，作者暗示利兹市议会的决定很荒谬，故答案为A)。

 

【错误选项分析】

B/C/D选项【反向干扰】：根据定位句，作者并不认为利兹市议会的决定非常有见地、很出人意料或非常明智，故排除B)、C)和D)。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

How did Sao Paulo city officials handle Alexandre Orion's reverse graffiti?

圣保罗市政府官员是如何处理亚历山大·奥利安的反向涂鸦的？

A) They made him clean all the tunnels in Sao Paulo.

他们让他清洁圣保罗的所有隧道

B) They took drastic action to ban all reverse graffiti.

他们采取严厉措施禁止一切反向涂鸦行为

C) They charged him with polluting tunnels in the city.

他们控告他污染城市隧道

D) They made it impossible for him to practice his art.

他们使他再不可能实践他的艺术

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Sao Paulo city officials定位到4段④⑤句。定位句指出，圣保罗市官员决定采取严厉措施。他们不仅清理了整个隧道，而且把圣保罗的每一条隧道都清理了。由此可知，所有隧道被清理干净了，亚历山大就无法在隧道里进行反向涂鸦创作了，故答案为D)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：4段②句指出，当局没有别的选择，只能把隧道清理了——但只是清理了亚历山大已经清理的那部分，而不是让亚历山大亲自去清理，故排除A).

B选项【偷换概念】：4段④句指出，圣保罗市官员决定采取严厉措施，即清理了该市所有的隧道，而非禁止所有反向涂鸦创作，故排除B)。

C选项【反向干扰】：4段①句指出，对于那位巴西艺术家的作品，当局非常恼怒，但是找不到任何理由指控他，C)与本句说法相矛盾，故排除。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 The practice of paying children an allowance became popular in America about 100 years ago. 2 Nowadays, American kids on average receive about $ 800 per year in allowance. 3 But the vast majority of American parents who pay allowance tie it to the completion of housework. 4 Although many parents believe that paying an allowance for completing chores benefits their children, a range of experts expressed concern that tying allowance very closely to chores may not be ideal.? 5 In fact, the way chores work in many households worldwide points to another way.
1 Suniya Luthar, a psychologist, is against paying kids for chores. 2 Luthar is not opposed to giving allowances, but she thinks it's important to establish that chores are done not because they will lead to payment, but because they keep the household running.? 3 Luthar's suggested approach to allowance is compatible with that of writer Ron Lieber, who advises that allowances be used as a means of showing children how to save, give, and spend on things they care about. 4 Kids should do chores, he writes, "for the same reason adult do, because the chores need to be done, and not with the expectation of compensation.?
1 This argument has its critics, but considering the way chores are undertaken around the world may change people's thinking. 2 Professor David Laney of Utah State University has studied how families around the world handle chores. 3 At about 18 months of age, Laney says, most children become eager to help their parents, and in many cultures, they begin helping with housework at that age.? 4 They begin with very simple tasks, but their responsibilities gradually increase. 5 And they do these tasks without payment. 6 Laney contrasts this with what happens in America. 7 "We deny our children's bids to help until they are 6 or 7 years old," Lancy says, "when many have lost the desire to help and then try to motivate them with payment. 8 The solution to this problem is not to try to use money as an incentive to do housework, but to get children involved in housework much earlier; when they actually want to do it. " 【355 words】?

【题目及选项概览】

What do some experts think about paying children for doing chores?

一些专家对付钱让孩子做家务有什么看法？

A) It may benefit children in more ways than one.

它对孩子的好处可能不止一个

B) It may help children learn the worth of labor.

它或许有助于孩子了解劳动的价值

C) It may not turn out to be the best thing to do.

它可能不会是最佳解决办法

D) It may not be accepted by low-income parents.

它或许无法被低收入父母接受

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的some experts， paying children和chores定位到1段④句。定位句指出，尽管很多父母认为因为完成家务活而给孩子零用钱对他们的孩子来说是有益的，但很多专家担心把零用钱和做家务联系得太紧密了可能并不理想。由此可知，专家认为给孩子钱让他们做家务可能不是最好的办法， 故答案为C) 。选项C) 中的the best thing对应定位句中的ideal。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【答非所问】：1段④句提到，很多父母认为因为完成家务活而给孩子零用钱对他们的孩子是有益的，这是很多美国父母的想法，非专家的看法，故排除A)。

B选项【无中生有】：1段②句提到大多数美国父母把给孩子零用钱和完成家务活联系在一起，但并未指出专家认为这会让孩子懂得劳动的价值，故排除B)。

D选项【无中生有】：原文并未提及低收入���庭，故排除D)。

【题目及选项概览】

According to Suniya Luthar, doing chores will help children learn to _____ .

根据Suniya Luthar，做家务有助于孩子学会______。

A) share family responsibilities

分担家庭责任

B) appreciate the value of work

体会劳动的价值

C) cultivate the spirit of independence

培养独立精神

D) manage domestic affairs themselves

自己操持家庭事务

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Suniya Luthar定位到2段第①②句。定位句提到，心理学家苏妮娅·卢瑟反对因为做家务而给孩子钱。卢瑟不反对给孩子零用钱，但是她认为重要的是应该明确不是因为做家务能得到钱而做家务，而是因为做家务能让一个家庭正常运转。由此可知，苏妮娅·卢瑟认为做家务能帮孩子学会分担家庭责任，故答案为A)。

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【无中生有】：文中没有提及欣赏工作的价值，故排除B)。

C选项【无中生有&过度推理】：2段③④句指出，卢瑟建议的获取零用钱的方法与作家罗恩·利伯建议的方法一致。罗恩·利伯建议零用钱被用作一种向孩子展示如何节省、给予和花在他们在乎的东西上的方法，由此无法推出做家务可培养孩子的独立精神，故排除C)，

D选项【过度推理】：2段②句指出，卢瑟认为应该明确不是因为能得到钱而做家务，而是因为做家务能让一个家庭正常运转，由此不能推出让孩子们自己操持家庭事务，D)为过度推理，故排除。

【题目及选项概览】

What does Ron Lieber think should be the goal of giving children allowances?

Ron Lieber认为，给孩子零用钱的目的应该是什么？

A) To help to strengthen family ties.

帮助加强家庭联系

B) To teach them how to manage money.

教他们如何管理金钱

C) To motivate them to do more housework.

鼓励他们做更多家务

D) To show parent appreciation of their help.

表达父母对他们帮忙的感谢

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Ron Lieber定位到2段③句。定位句指出，罗恩·利伯建议零用钱被用作一种向孩子展示如何节省、给予和花在他们在乎的东西上的方法。由此可见，罗恩·利伯认为零花钱教会孩子如何管理金钱，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【无中生有】：罗恩·利伯并未提及零花钱可增强家庭纽带关系，故排除A)，

C选项【偷换概念&过度推理】：本段③句指出，罗恩·利伯认为孩子们应该做家务，但并未指出零花钱可激励孩子做更多的家务，C)为过度推理，故排除。

D选项【无中生有】：原文并未提及父母赏识孩子所提供的帮助，故排除D)。

【题目及选项概览】

What does David Laney say about 18-month-olds?

关于18个月大的孩子，David Laney说了什么？

A) They have a natural instinct to help around the house.

他们有一种帮忙做家务的本能

B) They are too young to request money for what they do.

他们年纪太小，无法为自己所做的家务所求报酬

C) They should learn to understand family responsibilities.

他们应该学会理解家庭责任

D) They need a little incentive to get involved in housework.

他们需要一点激励才会参与家庭劳动

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的David Lancy和18-month-olds定位到3段③句。定位句提到，兰西认为大多数孩子在大约18个月的时候会渴望帮助他们的父母。由此可见，18个月的孩子本能地想在家里帮忙，故答案为A)。

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【无中生有】：兰西并未提及18个月的孩子因为太小而没法要求付钱，故排除B)，

C选项【过度推理】：本段④句指出，他们从很简单的任务开始，但是他们的责任会逐渐增长，原文中兰西并未提及18个月的孩子应该学会理解家庭责任，故排除C)。

D选项【答非所问】：本段⑦句指出，在美国，直到孩子六七岁失去了帮忙的意愿时，父母才以报酬的方法来激励他们。这并非针对18个月孩子的做���，故排除D)。

【题目及选项概览】

What does David Laney advise American parents to do?

David Laney建议美国父母怎么做？

A) Set a good example for children in doing housework.

在做家务上给孩子树立一个好榜样

B) Make children do housework without compensation.

让孩子无偿做家务

C) Teach children how to do housework.

教孩子如何做家务

D)Accept children's early bids to help.
接受孩子们早期想要帮忙的意图

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的David Lancy和advise定位到3段⑧句。定位句指出兰西的观点：解决这个问题的办法不是试图用金钱来激励孩子做家务，而足当他们真正想做的时候，让他们更早地参与到家务中。由此可知，兰西认为美国父母应接受孩子早期想帮忙的尝试，故答案为D)，

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【无中生有】：原文并未提及美国父母在做家务方面给孩子树立好榜样，故排除A).

B选项【词汇干扰&偷换概念】：该选项是针对②段④句中的not with the expectation of compensation设置的干扰，此处是表达孩子们应该做家务，而不是为了期望得到补偿而做家务，并不是表达让孩子们无偿做家务，故排除B)。

C选项【无中生有】：原文并未提及教孩子们如何做家务，故排除C)。

1 Firstly, you can save a great deal of time and energy to search information by using the online library. 2 You can even get the information you need without stepping out of your dorm room. 3 Secondly, he abundant digital information might beyond your imagination compared with the real libraries. 4 For example, online libraries make it possible for you to read a rare book stored in only a few large libraries. 5 Finally, you needn't linger over book shelves or take notes in libraries. 6 All the information could be downloaded into your computer and you can decide when and how to read them.
1 To sum up, we get a much easier access to knowledge by using online libraries, which are a powerful tool for modern people to read, study and research. 2 Thus, everyone is expected to learn how to use them.

United Airlines has apologized for mistakenly shipping an American family's pet dog thousands of miles in the wrong direction to Japan.
The dog owner ’s beloved 10-year-old dog named Buddy took an unexpected 16-hour flight to Tokyo following a mix-up by the airline.
The dog owner ’s family are currently in the process of moving.
They were meant to be reunited with the pet in their new home city in Texas.
But when they arrived at the United Airlines cargo facility in the southern U. S. state, they found a stranger 's dog waiting in Buddy’s place.
Both of the dogs had been sent to the wrong destinations on connecting flights from Denver, with Buddy mistakenly being sent to Japan instead.
Buddy was given a physical checkup when he arrived at Tokyo ���s International Airport.
The dog was then sent back to the U. S. on a private charter jet.
“ I'm so glad he 's alive and coming home soon !" said the relieved dog owner.
“ And an error occurred during the connections in Denver. We have notified our customers that their pets arrived safely.
We will arrange to return the pets to them as soon as possible,” a spokesperson of United Airlines said.

The baby hasn't been given a name yet.

Zoo officials said during this pregnancy, she was closely monitored through physical exams and blood tests.
Dr. Sue Tygielski is the zoo 's director of zoological operations.
She said the elephant ’s birth went smoothly and that there were no complications.
The new baby expands the zoo 's elephant herd to six.

I can’t believe that duck hunting is still legal in so many parts of the world.
The scientific evidence from countries like Australia, Canada and the USA clearly indicates a decline in the birds ’ numbers.
But can anyone be sure if the decline is really caused by the hunting or by climate change?
It’s caused by both in fact.
We see more droughts in countries like Australia.
Ducks are birds that feed and breed in areas where there is a lot of water, but their habitats have been shrinking in recent decades because of the droughts.
And I guess with fewer places to inhabit, they concentrate in greater numbers in few areas, which surely makes them easier targets for the hunters.
It does. My grandfather was a duck hunter.
He told me hunting ducks and geese began in the 19th century.
They were easily found and plentifully available food source in farming areas, especially for poor immigrants.
What do they use for hunting during that period?
They use new types of guns, and birds could easily be shot down in flight.
And in such great numbers, their commercial hunting of ducks and geese became an industry.
Yet, there’s no commercial farming of these birds nowadays.
Their meat is hardly eaten in Western countries.
No, duck hunting seemingly exists as the continuation of a tradition.
Well, ducks have never been popular with farmers like my grandfather anyway because they sometimes destroy crops.
In fact, farmers used to poison them in large numbers.
That somehow doesn't surprise me.
Nobody places much value on the lives of these poor birds or on their meat.

Homework is an important part of schooling, but the purposes of giving children homework will change as they grow older.
At the primary level, the main aim is to cultivate good habits, like learning to plan and exercising self-discipline.
During the secondary school years, extending what is learned at school is positively related to academic achievement, so the content of homework becomes more important.
So how can you help your child do their best?
Creating an ideal working environment will make it easier for them to get down to their assignments quickly.
Make sure it’s free of distractions, and for primary school children at least -- somewhere near you, so you can answer questions and offer encouragement.
You probably have to help younger children plan their session, but it’s important that by the end of primary school it’s second nature.
Get them to tell you everything they have to do.
Then encourage them to establish an order in which they do work.
When there are several different assignments, make sure they begin with one they enjoy, so it seems easy to get started.
It’s best to take on the most difficult task second -- once they're settled, but before they get tired.
If older children have more than an hour of homework, encourage them to schedule a short break to stretch.
If you encourage them to tell you what they’ve learned, they’ll absorb the information more deeply and remember it more readily.
16. What is the main aim of homework for primary school kids?
17. What does the passage suggest parents do to help their children?

Workers at Mexican oil company will receive a healthy incentive of almost $ 300 a year if they meet certain body weight standards.
To qualify for the bonus, they must maintain a healthy weight.
For those who are overweight or obese, they could receive the bonus if they reduce their weight by 10% during the year.
Some applaud the policy as fair, because it rewards both the individuals who maintain a healthy weight and those who are working towards achieving it.
But critics say the policy contradicts recommendations by many health experts, who warn that a person’s weight is influenced by genetic and environmental factors.
That means weight can be hard for individuals to control, which makes the bonus unfair.
Some experts say the policy is inconsistent with the science of what we know about body weight regulation.
These experts argue that focusing on wage is the wrong approach.
A more productive method of encouraging health among employees is to promote healthy behaviors.
For example, companies can give workers gym memberships, or encourage participation in lectures on healthy eating and living.
They can also reduce sweets and provide healthier snacks in the office and healthier meals at the company canteen.
Or they can give employees more time during their lunch break to exercise.
These are much better and much more productive ways for companies to move forward on their employees ’ well-being.
19.Who will qualify for the bonus in Mexican oil company?
20. What do critics think of Mexican oil company ’s bonus policy?
21. What do experts propose companies do about workers ’ well-being?
Campaigners have warned that the British government is not doing enough to prevent left-handed pupils from falling behind their peers.
They claim that thousands of children are still being “ penalized ” for being left-handed.
This is due to a lack of action from ministers, who’ve failed to take any meaningful action for years.
It is feared that a failure to address early-year challenges, such as poor handwriting, leads to much more serious problems down the line — with these pupils facing reduced career prospects.
Studies in recent years show that left-handed children are more likely to suffer with learning difficulties and their scores are lower on IQ tests.
Campaigners feel it’s strange that children in British schools are penalized because they happen to be left-handed.
They don’t understand why successive governments have failed to act on this.
They want the department of education to record which children are left-handed and what their educational attainments are, since they make up some 10% of the population.
In early-year education, left-handed children are struggling and making a mess of their handwriting.
Educators don’t know how to deal with this.
In many cases, there is no active help and a lack of teacher training.
Campaigners point out that a high percentage of the prison population is left-handed.
They say that these prison numbers are unusually high and ask why it is the case.
22. Why are some people criticizing the British government?
23. What do studies in recent years show about left-handed children?
24. What do the campaigners demand the department of education do?
25. What do the campaigners want to know about left-handed prisoners?

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 Karez is a water conservancy system founded in the dry region of Xinjiang, in which underground channels join wells together. 2 The system collects a large amount of rainwater and melted snow water that seep underground, and drains the water to the ground by the natural mountain slope for the irrigation of fields and the daily use. 3 Karez reduces the evaporation on the ground and does little harm to the surface, thus protecting natural resources and the ecological environment effectively. 4 The system embodies the Chinese wisdom that people and nature co-exist in harmony, and is well recognized as a major contribution to the human civilization.

questions.stem: ①坎儿井(Karez)是新疆干旱地区的一种水利系统，由地下渠道将水井连接而成。②该系统将春夏季节渗入(seep into)地下的大量雨水及积雪融水收集起来，通过山体的自然坡度引到地面，用于灌溉农田和满足人们的日常用水需求。③坎儿井减少了水在地面的蒸发(evaporation)，对地表破坏很小，因而有效地保护了自然资源与生态环境。④坎儿井体现了我国人民与自然和谐共存的智慧，是对人类文明的一大贡献。
questions.answer: 1 Karez is a water conservancy system founded in the dry region of Xinjiang, in which underground channels join wells together. 2 The system collects a large amount of rainwater and melted snow water that seep underground, and drains the water to the ground by the natural mountain slope for the irrigation of fields and the daily use. 3 Karez reduces the evaporation on the ground and does little harm to the surface, thus protecting natural resources and the ecological environment effectively. 4 The system embodies the Chinese wisdom that people and nature co-exist in harmony, and is well recognized as a major contribution to the human civilization.

questions.explanation:
【考点】

形容词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格前是数词two,空格后是名词individuals,因此本空应填入形容词。【答案解析】

空格所在句意为：但一段关系是由两个___个体组成的。 而下一句是关于这些个体的个性特征,由此可知,本句表达的是一段关系由两个不同的个体组成，因此本空应填入含有“不同的，独特的”意义的形容词，由此确定本题答案为O。

【考点】

动词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格后是并列连词or和动词lack,因此空格处也应填入一个动词原形。

【答案解析】

or意为“或者”,表示选择关系,且后面出现了moreorless这组意义相反的词，所以此处的动词应该与lack“缺乏”意思相反，故本空应填入含有“拥有”意义的动词,由此确定本题答案为I。

【考点】

动词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格前是likely to,因此本空应填入动词原形。

【答案解析】

空格所在句意为：这些个体拥有或缺乏的个性特征通常可以让一段关系更可能或更不可能综合前一句可知，一段关系包括两个不同的个体，他们各自的个性特征会影响他们的关系，结合备选动词可知，本空填人含有“持续，持久”意义的动词更合适，由此确定答案为D。

【考点】

形容词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格前有情态动词can和be动词原形，因此本空应填入形容词或动词的过去分词形式。【答案解析】

空格所在句的意思是：谦逊有时会被缺乏自信。由常识可知，如果一个人太谦虚，可能会被误认为是缺乏自信。因此本空应填入含有“混淆，误认为”意义的词,由此确定答案为C。K项与C项意思相近，但不能与with搭配使用，因此排除。

【考点】

名词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格前有定冠词the,后面是介词of，因此本空应填入名词。

【答案解析】

空格所在句意为：研究人员已经意识到，谦虚通常标志着非常令人钦佩的个人品质的     。将备选项中的三个名词分别代入空格，只有J“存在"符合句意，因此为正确答案。

【考点】

动词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格所在结构是have the ability to do sth.，因此本空应填人动词原形。

【答案解析】

空格所在句意为：谦逊意味着你有能力准确地     自己的不足，同时也不否认自己的技能和优势。此处应选择一个能与副词accurately以及后面宾语deficiencies搭配的动词。综合备选项可知，B项与deficiencies搭配,意为“评估不足”,符合句意，为本题答案。

【考点】

名词辨析题

名词辨析题

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读

1 "I used to work very hard. 2 I love to create things, grow them and solve problems," said Meng Li, a successful app developer in San Francisco. 3 "I didn't really care about my mind and my body until they decided to go on strike. "
1 Ms. Li said her stress led to sleeplessness. 2 When she did sleep, she experienced "problem-solving dreams," which left her feeling unrested when she woke up. 3 After I became a first-time mother, I quickly realized I was so busy caring for other people and work that I felt like I'd lost myself, she said.?
1 It's a common story - one we frequently ridicule and readily dismiss, for example, by claiming that women tend to complain more than men, despite the growing sum of research that underlines the problem. 2 Women are twice as likely to suffer from severe stress and anxiety as men, according to a 2016 study published in The Journal of Brain & Behavior. 3 The American Psychological Association reports a gender gap year after year showing that women consistently report higher stress levels.? 4 Clearly, a stress gap exists.
1 "The difference is not really news to me, as a clinical psychologist," said Erin Joyce, a women and couples therapist in Los Angeles. 2 "It's been well documented in extensive research over the years that prevalence rates for the majority of the anxiety disorders are higher in women than men." 3 Some people may argue that this is merely reported data, and they say many men feel the same pressures as women in terms of fulfilling responsibilities at work and home.? 4 In other words, we're all really, really stressed.
1 "The difference, however, is in the nature and scope of these responsibilities in the home environment in particular, " Dr. Joyce said. 2 For example, the United Nations reported that women do nearly three times as much unpaid domestic work as men.? 3 The problem is, housework is often overlooked as work, even though it is often as laborious (or in some cases, more so) as any paid job. 4 As the scholar Silvia Federici put it in 1975, the unpaid nature of domestic work reinforces the assumption that "housework is not work, thus preventing women from struggling against it."
1 It's not just inside the home, though. 2 Research from Nova Southeastern University found that female managers were more likely than male managers to display "surface acting," or forcing emotions that are not wholly felt. 3 "They expressed optimism, calmness and sympathy even when these were not the emotions that they were actually feeling," the study said.?
1 Surface acting is a prime example of “emotional labor," a concept that the writer Jess Zimmerman made familiar in a 2015 essay. 2 The essay sparked a massive thread on the internet community blog MetaFilter. 3 Hundreds of women spoke up about their own experience with emotional labor: the duties that are expected of them, but go unnoticed. 4 These invisible duties become apparent only when you don't do them.? 5 Like domestic labor, emotional labor is generally dismissed and not labeled work. 6 But research shows it can be just as exhausting as paid work. 7 Emotional labor can lead to difficulty in sleeping and family conflict. 8 Sure, circumstantial stress, like losing a job, may lead to these same issues. 9 But emotional labor is not circumstantial. 10 It's an enduring responsibility based on the socialized gender role of women.
1 Like Ms. Li, many women try to manage the added stress to reach what Dr. Joyce said was an unattainable ideal. 2 "Some professional women aim to do it all. 3 They want to reach the top of the corporate ladder and fly like supermom," she said. 4 When women don't reach this ideal, they feel guilty; and even more stressed.? 5 After her own struggle with this, Ms. Li took a step back and used her experience to build Sanity & Self, a self-care app and platform for overworked women. 6 "The realizations I had in that process helped me gain insights and ultimately got me ready to integrate self- care into my daily life," she said.
1 The stress problem extends beyond mental health when you consider the link between stress, anxiety and heart health. 2 Worse, most of what we know about heart disease comes from studies involving men. 3 However, "there are many reasons to think that it's different in women," Harvard Medical School reported. 4 For example, women are more likely to experience disturbed sleep, anxiety and unusual fatigue before a heart attack. 5 Stress is so normalized that it is easy for women to shrug off those symptoms as simply the consequences of stress.? 6 Many women also do not experience chest pain before a heart attack the way men do, which leads to fewer women discovering problematic heart issues. 7 Harvard reports that women are "much more likely than men to die within a year of having a heart attack" and "many women say their physicians sometimes don't even recognize the symptoms."
1 The good news is, women are more likely than men to take charge of their stress and manage it, the American Psychological Association reports. 2 The concept of self-care, at its core, is quite simple. 3 "The basics of adequate sleep, healthy diet and exercise are a good place to start," Dr. Joyce said. 4 "Support from trusted relationships is vital. 5 This includes professional support from various health and wellness providers if stress is becoming increasingly overwhelming."?
1 Disconnecting from work and home responsibilities is also obviously important. 2 But it's much easier said than done. 3 It is important to understand what causes your stress in the first place. 4 "Get really specific with what's stressing you out," Ms. Li said.? 5 "We often chalk up our stress to broad experiences like work. 6 But work stress can take many different forms. 7 Is a colleague being disrespectful of your time? 8 Is a boss undermining your day-to-day control over decision making? 9 These are different causes of stress and can benefit from different kinds of self-care."
1 Ideally, your spouse or partner will be supportive, rather than dismissive, of your stress. 2 It is important to talk through these issues before they come to a head. 3 "Women working outside of the home should make an effort to have a conscious conversation with their partners about more equitable sharing of household and family responsibilities," Dr. Joyce said.

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 As many office workers adapt to remote work, cities may undergo fundamental change if offices remain under-utilized.? 2 Who will benefit if working from home becomes the norm?
1 Employers argue they make considerable savings on real estate when workers shift from office to home work. 2 However, these savings result from passing costs on to workers.
1 Unless employees are fully compensated, this could become a variant of parasitic (寄生的) capitalism, whereby corporate profits increasingly rely on extracting value from the public — and now personal — realm, rather than on generating new value.
1 Though employers are backed by a chorus of remote work advocates, others note the loneliness, reduced productivity and inefficiencies of extended remote work.?
1 If working from home becomes permanent, employees will have to dedicate part of their private space to work. 2 This requires purchasing desks, chairs and office equipment.
1 It also means having private space dedicated to work: the space must be heated, cleaned, maintained and paid for. 2 That depends on many things, but for purposes of illustration, I have run some estimates for Montreal. 3 The exercise is simple but important, since it brings these costs out of the realm of speculation into the realm of meaningful discussion.?
1 Rough calculations show that the savings made by employers when their staff works from home are of similar value to the compensation workers should receive for setting offices at home.?
1 What does this mean for offices in cities? 2 One of two things may happen: Employers pass these costs onto employees. 3 This would be a form of expropriation (侵占), with employees absorbing production costs that have traditionally been paid by the employer. 4 This represents a considerable transfer of value from employees to employers.
1 When employees are properly compensated, employers' real estate savings will be modest.? 2 If savings are modest, then the many advantages of working in offices — such as lively atmosphere, rapidity of communication, team-building and acclimatization (适应环境) of new employees — will encourage employers to shelve the idea of remote work and, like Yahoo in 2013, encourage employees to work most of the time from corporate office space.

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 The human thirst for knowledge is the driving force behind our successful development as a species.? 2 But curiosity can also be dangerous, leading to setbacks or even downfalls. 3 Given curiosity's complexity, scientists have found it hard to define.
1 While pinning down a definition has proven tricky, the general consensus is it's some means of information gathering.? 2 Psychologists also agree curiosity is intrinsically (内在地) motivated.
1 Curiosity covers such a large set of behaviors that there probably isn't any single "curiosity gene" that makes humans wonder about and explore their environment. 2 That said, curiosity does have a genetic component. 3 Genes and the environment interact in many complex ways to shape individuals and guide their behavior, including their curiosity.?
1 Regardless of their genetic makeup, infants have to learn an incredible amount of information in a short time, and curiosity is one of the tools humans have found to accomplish that gigantic task.
1 Hundreds of studies show that infants prefer novelty.? 2 It's what motivates non-human animals, human infants and probably human adults to explore and seek out new things before growing less interested in them after continued exposure.
1 But curiosity often comes with a cost.
1 In some situations, the stakes are low and failure is a healthy part of growth. 2 For instance, many babies are perfectly proficient crawlers, but they decide to try walking because there's more to see and do when they stand upright. 3 But this milestone comes at a small cost. 4 A study of 12- to 19-month-olds learning how to walk documented that these children fell down a lot. 5 Seventeen times per hour, to be exact. 6 But walking is faster than crawling, so this motivates expert crawlers to transition to walking.
1 Sometimes, however, testing out a new idea can lead to disaster. 2 For instance, the Inuit people of the Arctic regions have created incredible modes to deal with the challenges of living in northern climates, but what we forget about are the tens of thousands of people that tried and failed to make it in those challenging landscapes.?

A new study carried out by the university of Lincoln has found a link between the personalities of cat owners and the behavior and well-being of their cats.
The findings suggest that just as apparent personality can affect the personality of a child, the same is true for a cat and its owner.
Owners defined as individuals with high levels of anxiety, fear, anger, depression and loneliness were more likely to have cats with behavioral issues.
Such cats display more aggressive and anxious behavioral styles as well as more stress related sickness.
They were also more likely to have an ongoing medical condition and be overweight.
The research also found that mentally well-adjusted owners had come from happier and healthier cats.
The researchers explained that many owners regard their pets as a family member and form close social bonds with them.
The majority of owners want to provide the best care for their pets and is therefore possible that pets could be affected by the way their owners interact with and manage them.
The study highlights an important relationship between our personalities and the well-being of our pets.
Further research is needed to investigate the cause of nature of this relationship and look at how owners ' personalities are directly influencing their pet 's behavior and well-being.
It is possible that the well-being of pets is driven by the underlying nature of the owner not simply by their conscious decisions and behaviors.

One 50-minute run can add seven hours to your life.
This was a claim made by The Times last week.
The claim was based on a new review of studies about the effects of running.
The review concluded that an average runners live three years longer than non-runners and that running does more to extend life than any other form of exercise.
But there's more to running than its health benefits.
Research published in recent years have shown that running changes your brain and mind in some fascinating ways from increasing your brain function to regulating your emotions.
However, the precise effects vary according to whether you engage in short fast running or long distance running.
For example, in one study, researchers compared participants ' ability to learn new words after several minutes of intense running, and after 40 minutes of gentle running.
Participants were able to learn 20 percent faster after the intense running and they showed a superior memory when tested again a week later.
In another study, researchers asked volunteers to jog for 30 minutes and then showed them clips from a sad movie.
Participants who usually struggled to handle negative emotions were more intensely affected by the sad clips just as you'd expect.
But crucially, this was less so if they had completed the 30 minutes jog.
The researchers said moderate exercise appears to have helped those participants to be less vulnerable to the impact of the sad movie.

Welcome to the tour of the Hill House.
This house built in 1904 is one of the most well-known works of Charles Hill, the famous architect.
It was designed and built for local entrepreneur and his family.
Before starting the tour, let me give you a brief introduction about the design of this amazing building.
Prior to beginning his design, the architect spends sometime in the client 's old home, observing their life and studying their habits.
This meant that he could design the house according to the needs of the family.
The client 's main desire was to have a home with unique design, so the architect was given complete freedom.
The building style is radically different from what was the fashion of the period.
At the time, most large homes were constructed of timber and brick.
This one, however, is made of concrete, a novel construction material in those days.
The interior of the house, including the fittings and furniture, was also designed by the same person.
Most of the furniture you will see is original and in good condition.
However, both pieces in the children 's bedrooms are copies built to the designs of the architect.
Fortunately, all the blueprints for both the building and its contents have been preserved, so we've been able to replace badly damaged furniture.
Let's begin our tour, starting from the rooms.

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 Dujiangyan, whose construction was started in the 3rd century BC, is located across the Minjiang River in west Chengdu Plain, about 50 kilometers away from Chengdu. 2 What presses people most is the damless water control. 3 For over 2, 000 years, it has been playing an effective role in flood prevention and irrigation, turning the Chengdu Plain into a fertile land guaranteed for harvest against drought or flood and one of the most significant grain production areas in China. 4 Dujiangyan serves as the oldest water conservancy project in the world, which is still used to control water without the help of dam, embodying the Chinese wisdom that people and nature co-exist in harmony.

questions.stem: ①都江堰(Dujiangyan)坐落在成都平原西部的岷江上，距成都市约50公里，始建于公元前三世纪。②它的独特之处在于无需用坝调控水流。③两千多年来，都江堰一直有效地发挥着防洪与溉作用，使成都平原成为旱涝保收的沃土和中国最重要的粮产地之一。④都江堰工程体现了我国人民与自然和谐共存的智慧，是全世界年代最久、仍在使用、无坝控水的水利工程。
questions.answer: 1 Dujiangyan, whose construction was started in the 3rd century BC, is located across the Minjiang River in west Chengdu Plain, about 50 kilometers away from Chengdu. 2 What presses people most is the damless water control. 3 For over 2, 000 years, it has been playing an effective role in flood prevention and irrigation, turning the Chengdu Plain into a fertile land guaranteed for harvest against drought or flood and one of the most significant grain production areas in China. 4 Dujiangyan serves as the oldest water conservancy project in the world, which is still used to control water without the help of dam, embodying the Chinese wisdom that people and nature co-exist in harmony.

1 It is commonly believed that the great English dramatist and poet William Shakespeare was born in Stratford-on-Avon on April 23, 1564. 2 But it is impossible to know the 1 day on which he was born.?
1 Church records show he was baptized (施洗礼) on April 26, and three days was a customary amount of time to wait before baptizing a newly born baby. 2 Shakespeare's date of death is 2 known, however: it was April 23, 1616.? 3 He was 52 and had retired to Stratford three years before.
1 Although few plays have been performed or analyzed as extensively as the 38 plays Shakespeare wrote, there are few surviving details about his life. 2 This 3 of biographical information is due primarily to his social 4; he was not a noble, but the son of a leather trader.?
1 Shakespeare 5 attended the grammar school in Stratford, where he would have studied Latin and read 6 literature.? 2 He did not go to university and at age 18 married Anne Hathaway, who was eight years his 7.? 3 They had four children, including the twins, Hamnet and Judith. 4 Nothing is known of the period between the birth of the twins and Shakespeare's 8 as a dramatist in London in the early 1590s.?
1 In a million words written over 20 years, he 9 the full range of human emotions and conflicts with a 10 that remains sharp today.? 2 As his great contemporary the poet and dramatist Ben Jonson said, " He was not of an age, but for all time. "

questions.explanation:
【考点】

形容词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格前有定冠词the,空格后是名词day，因此空格处应填人形容词。

【答案解析】

本句意为：但是不可能知道他出生的日期。根据下一句可知,教会记录显示，莎士比亚于4月26日受洗，在为新生婴儿施洗之前,通常需要等待三天。因此莎士比亚生于4月23日是人们根据教会受洗记录的推测，而他的确切出生日期无从得知，因此空格处应填人含有“确切的，精确的”意义的形容词，由此确定答案为E。

【考点】

副词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格后是形容词known，因此空格处应填入副词。

【答案解析】

本句意为：然而，莎士比亚的死亡日期是知道的：1616年4月23日。however表示转折关系，本句与前面提到的莎士比亚的具体出生日期不明形成对比。也就是说，莎士比亚的死亡日期是准确的，因此空格处应填人含有“确信地，确凿地”意义的副词，由此确定答案为C。

【考点】

名词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格前有This，后面是“of+名词”的结构，因此空格处应填入名词。

【答案解析】

本句意为：传记信息的     主要是由于他的社会     。由前一句可知，关于莎士比亚生活的细节很少留存下来，因此空格处应填入含有“缺少”意义的名词，由此确定答案为L。

【考点】

名词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格前有形容词social，因此空格处应填入名词。

【答案解析】

本句意为：传记信息的缺少主要是由于他的社会     ；他不是贵族，而是一个皮革商人的儿子。由分号后面的noble和the son of a leather trader可知，这是两种高低不同的社会地位，因此空格处应填入含有“地位”意义的名词，由此确定答案为H。

【考点】

副词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格后有动词attended,因此空格处应填入副词。

【答案解析】

本句意为：莎士比亚     就读于斯特拉特福的文法学校。由第二段可知，由于社会地位低下，关于莎士比亚生活的细节很少留存下来，因此莎士比亚曾就读于斯特拉特福的文法学校也是人们的推测，并非确凿的信息，因此空格处应填入含有“可能,大概”意义的副词，由此确定答案为J。

【考点】

形容词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格后有名词literature,因此空格处应填入形容词。

【答案解析】

本句意为：在那里他学习拉丁语并阅读___文学。 备选项中能和文学搭配的只有B项 classical，意为“古典文学”，由此确定答案为B。

【考点】

名词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格前有形容词性物主代词his, 因此空格处应填入名词。

【答案解析】

本句意为:他没有上大学,18岁时娶了比他____八岁的安妮 · 海瑟薇。由句意可知，此处表示安妮 · 海瑟薇比莎士比亚年长或年轻八岁。而莎士比亚此时才18岁，所以安妮 · 海瑟薇应该比莎士比亚年长八岁,由此确定答案为M。

【考点】

名词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格前有名词属格Shakespeare's， 因此空格处应填入名词。

【答案解析】

本句意为：从双胞胎出生到16世纪90年代初莎士比亚在伦敦作为戏剧家      之间的这个阶段人们一无所知。根据文章大意，人们对莎士比亚在伦敦成名之后的生活细节了解得比较多，而对在此之前的知之甚少，所以这一时期指的是莎士比亚成名之前，因此空格处应填入含有“出现"意义的名词，由此确定答案为D。

【考点】

动词辨析题

【词性分析】

分析句子结构可知,空格所在的句子缺少谓语动词，因此空格处应填人动词。

【答案解析】

本句意为：在20多年的时间里，他用一百万字的篇幅，____人类全部的情感和冲突。也就是说,莎士比亚的文字记录或描述了人类的情感和冲突，因此空格处应填入含有“记录，描述”意义的动词，由此确定答案为A。

【考点】

名词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格前有不定冠词a,因此空格处应填入名词。

【答案解析】

本句意为：在20多年的时间里，他用一百万字的篇幅，以今天仍然敏锐的     描述了人类全部的情感和冲突。本句是对莎士比亚作品的评价。that remains sharp today是修饰莎士比亚描述人类的各种情感与冲突的方式,说明他的方式是十分准确的，因此空格处应填人含有“准确”意义的名词，由此确定答案为I。备选的其他名词不能用sharp修饰，因此排除。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Humans are creatures of habit. 2 We love to establish a routine and stick with it. 3 Then we often put ourselves on auto-pilot. 4 Routines can be incredibly useful in helping you get things done. 5 However, too much of a routine can also make you incredibly boring.? 6 Nevertheless, many people live lives that are boringly predictable, or live a life where everything is outlined or planned.
1 To tell the truth, interesting people are more popular among their friends. 2 If you don't arouse someone's curiosity or brighten someone's day, you probably come across as being a little bit dull.? 3 But that doesn't mean your life has ended and you can't do anything to change it. 4 If you find yourself searching for something to say beyond small talk, try these tactics to find more interesting approaches to conversation.
1 Recently, I was at a gathering of colleagues when someone turned to me and asked, "So, what's new with you?" 2 Ordinarily, I think I'm a good conversationalist.? 3 After all, it's literally my job to talk to people and tell their stories or share their advice. 4 And that's not exactly an unexpected question. 5 Still, the only “new-to-me" topics that came to mind were my daughter's basketball tournament (锦标赛) and my feelings about that morning's political headlines- neither amusing nor appropriate topics at that moment.
1 Oh, no, I thought. Have I become boring? 2 But sharing our experiences in an authentic way to connect with other people is what makes us interesting, says associate professor Michael Pirson. 3 The hesitation I felt in not sharing the ordinary things that were happening in my life, and the wild mental search for something more interesting, may have backfired and made me seem less interesting.
1 "If someone is making up some conversation that might be interesting, it's probably not going to land well," says Pirson, whose expertise includes trust and well-being, mindfulness, and humanistic management.? 2 It's going to feel like a made-up conversation that people don't necessarily want to tune in to.
1 The most interesting people aren't those who've gone on some Eat, Pray, Love journey to find themselves. 2 Instead, Pirson says, they 're those who examine the ordinary. 3 "Often, the 'boring things' may not be boring at all. 4 Maybe they are actually little miracles," he says.? 5 Share your observations about the world around you - interesting stories you heard or things you noticed and you may be surprised by the universal connection they inspire.
1 This is essentially how Jessica Hagy starts her day. 2 The author of How to Be Interesting: An Instruction Manual, Hagy spends a lot of time thinking about what's interesting to her. 3 People who are interesting are persistently curious, she says.?
1 Think about the everyday things around you and ask questions about them. 2 What is that roadside monument I see on my way to work every day? 3 Who built that interesting building in my city? 4 What nearby attractions haven't I visited? 5 Why do people do things that way? 6 Use what you find to ask more questions and learn more about the world around you. 7 Having that sort of curiosity is almost like a protective gear from getting into boredom, she says. 8 And when you find things that are truly interesting to you, share them.
1 Television veteran Audrey Morrissey, executive producer of NBC's The Voice, is always looking for what will make a person or story interesting to viewers: 2 It's usually a matter of individuality.? 3 "Having a strong point of view, signature style, or being a super-enthusiast in a particular field makes someone interesting," she says. 4 That means embracing what is truly interesting or unique about yourself. 5 "Many people are 'not boring' in the way that they can carry a conversation or can be good at a social gathering, etc. 6 To be interesting means that you have lived life, taken risks, traveled, sought out experience to learn for yourself and share with others, " she says.
1 Of course, it's possible to be a fountain of knowledge and a boring person, says public relations consultant Andrea Pass. 2 Paying attention to the listener is an important part of having a conversation that's interesting to both parties.? 3 Talking on and on about what's interesting to you isn't going to make you an interesting person, she says.
1 "If the listener is not paying attention, it's your sign to shorten the story or change direction. 2 Make sure to bring the audience into the conversation so that it is not one-sided," Pass says. 3 Be a better listener yourself, and give others opportunities to participate in the conversation by inviting them with questions or requests to share their own experiences or thoughts. 4 (e. g., "Now, tell me about your favorite book," or "Have you ever been to that attraction?") 5 Questions are a powerful tool, especially when they encourage others to disclose information about themselves. 6 A 2012 study from the University of California, Santa Barbara, found that roughly 40% of the time we are talking, we're disclosing subjective information about our experience. 7 And when we're doing so, our brains are more engaged. 8 So one strategy to leave others with the impression that you're a sparkling conversation partner is to get others to talk about themselves.?
1 Being relatable is also essential, Morrissey says. 2 The best entertainment and storytelling comes from people who are relatable - those who don't shy away from opening up but freely share who they are and what they care about. 3 These are the people viewers most relate to and find interesting. 4 Being authentic, honest, and vulnerable is always interesting."
1 I have now come to realize that being boring, in actuality, is not only about who you are as a person, but also how you present yourself. 2 No matter what, make sure you are having fun in life. 3 Because when you are enjoying, people around you will begin to enjoy as well. 4 Show some interest in them and they will definitely show some in you.? 5 If you are a very reserved person, this could be a little difficult at first. 6 But with a little effort, you can definitely improve.
