questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What does Liebman say about industry-funded research?

利伯曼对行业资助的研究怎么说？

A. It simply focuses on nutrition and health.

它只关注营养和健康。

B. It causes confusion among consumers.

它在消费者中引起混乱。

C. It rarely results in objective findings.

它很少产生客观的结果。

D. It runs counter to the public interest.

这与公众利益背道而驰。


【定位及答案】

由题干中的Liebman和industry-funded research定位到第五段。

第五段第二、三句提到，利伯曼认为“食品工业为研究提供资金时，通常会得到相应的回报。"他们所支付的往往是一个利于推动该行业的发展的发现。由此可见，由食品工业资助的研究，其结果并不客观，故答案为C）。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【无中生有】：文中并没有提及这些研究只关注营养和健康，A）为无中生有，故排除。

B选项【B过度推断】：定位段指出，这些研究的结果大多有利于推动该行业的发展，而非这些结果会对大众造成混乱，B）为过度推断，故排除。

D选项【无中生有】：文章并未提及利伯曼认为这些研究结果会损害公众利益，故排除D）。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What is the author's advice to consumers?

作者对消费者的建议是什么？

A. Follow their intuition in deciding what to eat.

根据他们的直觉决定吃什么。

B. Be doubtful of diet experts' recommendations.

对饮食专家的建议持怀疑态度。

C. Ignore irrelevant information on their news feed.

忽略新闻提要上的无关信息。

D. Think twice about new nutrition research findings.

对新的营养研究结果三思而后行。


【定位及答案】

由题干中的 author's advice to consumers 定位到第六段第一句。

定位句指出，鉴于这种环境， 消费者在阅读营养科学的最新发现时应持怀疑态度，并且忽略新闻推送上弹出的最新研究。由此可见，作者的建议是对新的营养研究成果三思而后行，D）中的Think twice对应原文中的skeptical，故答案为 D）。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【过度推断】：文章末段最后两句提到，我们知道什么是健康饮食——多吃蔬菜，少吃垃圾食品，平衡热量。其他一切都很难通过实验来完成。这句话的意思是其他应该怎么做其实很难通过实验的方式验证，而非建议读者要靠直觉，A）为过度推断，故排除。

B选项【偷换概念】：定位句指出，要对新的研究结果持怀疑的态度，而非对饮食专家的建议持怀疑态度，故排除 B）。

C选项【曲解文意】：定位句指出，消费者应忽略新闻推送的最新研究，而非忽略无关信息，故排除C）。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 Success was once defined as being able to stay at a company for a long time and move up the corporate ladder. 2 The goal was to reach the top, accumulate wealth and retire to a life of ease. 3 My father is a successful senior executive. 4 In 35 years, he worked for only three companies.?
1 When I started my career, things were already different. 2 If you weren't changing companies every three or four years, you simply weren't getting ahead in your career.? 3 But back then, if you were a consultant or freelancer (自由职业者），people would wonder what was wrong with you. 4 They would assume you had problems getting a job.
1 Today, consulting or freelancing for five businesses at the same time is a badge of honor.? 2 It shows how valuable an individual is. 3 Many companies now look to these "ultimate professionals" to solve problems their full-time teams can't. 4 Or they save money by hiring" top-tier (顶尖的） experts" only for particular projects.
1 Working at home or in cafes, starting businesses of their own, and even launching business ventures that eventually may fail, all indicate "initiative," "creativity," and "adaptability," which are desirable qualities in today's workplace. 2 Most important, there is a growing recognition that people who balance work and play, and who work at what they are passionate about, are more focused and productive, delivering greater value to their clients'?
1 Who are these people? 2 They are artists, writers, programmers, providers of office services and career advice. 3 What's needed now is a marketplace platform specifically designed to bring freelancers and clients together. 4 Such platforms then become a place to feature the most experienced, professional, and creative talent. 5 This is where they conduct business, where a sense of community reinforces the culture and values of the gig economy (零工经济），and where success is rewarded with good reviews that encourage more business.
1 Slowly but surely, these platforms create a bridge between traditional enterprises and this emerging economy. 2 Perhaps more important, as the global economy continues to be disrupted by technology and other massive change, the gig economy will itself become an engine of economic and social transformation.?

【题干及选项概览】

What does the author use the example of his father to illustrate?

作者用他父亲的例子来说明什么？

A. How long people took to reach the top of their career.

人们花了多长时间才达到事业的巅峰。

B. How people accumulated wealth in his father's time.

在他父辈的年代，人们是如何积累财富的。

C. How people viewed success in his father's time.

人们如何看待他父辈的年代的成功。

D. How long people usually stayed in a company.

人们通常在一家公司呆多久。

由题干中的the example of his father定位到第一段。

定位段指出，成功曾经被定义为能在一家公司任职很长时间并获得晋升。目的是到达高位，积累财富，退休后安度晚年。第 三、四句提到了作者父亲的亲身经历，用以说明该段前两句的内容，即在其父辈的年代，人们对于成功的定义是怎样的，故答案为C）。


【错误选项分析】

A/B选项【过度推断】：文章首段虽然提及了在作者父辈的年代, 人们会在一家公司中努力晋升并积累财富，但并未提及晋升的年限问题以及积累财富的方式，故排除A）和B）。

D选项【以偏概全】：该段虽然提到了作者父亲任职的时间，但是并不能代表所有人的情况，故排除D）。

Why did people often change jobs when the author started his career?

为什么当作者开始他的职业生涯时人们经常换工作？

A. It was considered a fashion at that time.

这在当时被认为是一种时尚。

B. It was a way to advance in their career.

这是他们职业发展的一种方式。

C. It was a response to the changing job market.

这是对不断变化的就业市场的回应。

D. It was difficult to keep a job for long.

长时间保持一份工作是很困难的。

由题干中的often change jobs和the author started his career定位到第二段第一、二句。

定位句提到，当作者开始他的职业生涯时，事情已经不同了。如果你不是每三四年就换一家公司，那么就说明你并未在职业生涯中前进。由此可知，人们频繁换工作是为了促进职业发展，故答案为B）。


【错误选项分析】

A/C/D选项【无中生有】：A）项提及的时尚问题，在定位段中并无体 现，故排除。C）项提及不断变化的就业市场，同样在第二段中没有涉及，故排除。D）项指出长久地坚持一份工作很难，文中无此类表述，故排除。

What does the author say about people now working for several businesses at the same time?

作者对现在同时为数家企业工作的人怎么说？

A. They are often regarded as most treasured talents.

他们通常被认为是最宝贵的人才。

What have businesses come to recognize now?

为什么有些人对工作更有激情。

What does the author say about the gig economy?

作者是如何看待零工经济的？

A. It may force companies to reform their business practice.

它可能会迫使公司改革其商业惯例。

B. It may soon replace the traditional economic model.

它可能很快取代传统的经济模式。

定位句指出，或许更重要的是，随着全球经济持续受到科技和其他重大改变的干扰，零工经济本身将会成为经济和社会转型的引擎，故答案为D）。

A选项【无中生有】：文中没有提及它可能迫使公司改变运营方式，故排除A）。

B选项【过度推断】：结合文章大意，零工经济仍在发展阶段，并不会很快替代传统经济，故排除B）。

questions.stem: ①普洱(Pu' er)茶深受中国人喜爱，最好的普洱茶产自云南的西双版纳(xishuangbanna)，那里的气候和环境为普洱茶树的生长提供了最佳条件。②普洱茶颜色较深，味道与其他的茶截然不同。③普洱茶泡(brew)的时间越长越有味道。④许多爱喝的人尤其喜欢其独特的香味和口感。⑤普洱茶含有多种有益健康的元素，常饮普洱茶有助于保护心脏和血管，还有减肥、消除疲劳和促进消化的功效。

questions.explanation:
【考点】

名词辨析题

【词性判断】

空格位于形容词性物主代词my之后，因此空格处需要填入名词。

【答案解析】

本句意为：在付款之前，我被要求在 EFTPOS终端上对"店铺_____"进行评分。由第一段可知，每次购买东西以后，都需要对该公司 的表现进行评分,也就是顾客对店铺体验评分，因此空格处应填入含有“体验，经历"意义的名词，故本题答案为E) experience。

【考点】

形容词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格位于the most之后、名词 activities之前，因此空格处需要填入形容词。

【答案解析】

本句意为：即使是最_____的活动， 比如打电话给澳洲电信或从澳大利亚邮政领取包裹，也会收到短信或电子邮件调査，询问“我们做得怎么样?”。由列举的例子可知，这些都是很常见的事情，因此空格处应填入含有“常见的，普通的”意义的形容词，故本题答案为B) commonplace

【考点】

副词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格位于本句的谓语are followed up 之间,因此空格处需要填入副词。

【答案解析】

本句意为：网上购物之后_____会有客户满意度调査。第一段提到，购买任何东西都需要评分，那么网购也不例外。因此空格处应填入含有“通常”意义的副词，备选副词中J) routinely“例行地，惯常地”最符合句意，故为本题答案。

【考点】

形容词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格位于副词so之后,因此空格处需 要填入形容词。

【答案解析】

本句意为：很多公司都_____需要星评，所以如果你删除了调査，公司就会再给你发一个。由句意可知，很多公司会锲而不舍地追着顾客让他们点评，因为他们非常需要顾客的评价, 因此空格处应填入含有“迫切的,急需的"意义的形容词，故本题答案为D) desperate。

【考点】

语义理解题

【词性分析】

空格位于be动词are之后，空格处应 填入形容词或动词的分词形式。

【答案解析】

本句意为：当我们才刚刚有机会使用 一些应用软件时，我们就会_____给它们打分。 由下一句可知，一个在线课程提供商在顾客刚刚使用不久时，就催促顾客为其打分,因此空格处应填入含有“催促，促使”意义的词，故本题答案为 H) prompted。

【考点】

副词辨析题

【词性分析】

分析句子结构可知，空格所在部分结构完整，不缺成分，因此空格处需要填入副词。

【答案解析】

本句意为：我使用过的一家在线课程提供商在你只完成了_____2%的课程后，就询问你对这门课程的看法。由句意可知，2%未必是确切的数字，是强调刚刚使用不久，因此空格处应填入含有“大约”意义的词，故本题答案为 I) roughly。另外一个备选副词J) routinely不符合句意，因此排除。

【考点】

形容词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格位于不定冠词a之后，名词 display之前，因此空格处需要填入形容词。

【答案解析】

空格所在部分意为：因为一个_____星星反馈已经成为现代经济的核心影响力来源。根据前文可知，商家评分用的是星星，而星星通常给人闪闪发光的联想，因此空格处应填入含有“闪亮的“意义的形容词，故本题答案为K) shining。

【考点】

动词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格位于can't help but结构中，根据固定搭配，空格处应填入动词原形。

【答案解析】

本句意为：然而，你不禁_____这些公司的业务是否以捏造的东西为基础。由句意可知，if在此处意为“是否"，因此空格处应填入含有“想知道,想了解"意义的动词，故本题答案为 O) wonder。

【考点】

动词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格位于主语I之后,空格所在部分 缺少谓语,因此空格处需要填入动词。

【答案解析】

本句意为：我_____，在做网上调査时，我只是点击离我鼠标光标最近的_____，以便把这讨厌的东西从屏幕上弄掉。上一句提到，公司的业务也许是基于编造的东西，而本句作者以自身为例进行说明。因此空格处应填入含有 “承认"意义的动词，故本题答案为C) confess。

【考点】

名词辨析题

【词性分析】

空格位于动词click和定冠词the之后，因此空格处需要填入名词。

【答案解析】

本句意为：在做网上调查时，我只是点击离我鼠标光标最近的_____，以便把这讨厌的东西从屏幕上弄掉。根据常识可知，做问卷调査就是根据实际情况选择不同的回答。因此空格处应填入含有“答案，选项"意义的名词,故本题答案为 G) option。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 How do early career setbacks affect our long-term success? 2 Failures can help us learn and overcome our fears. 3 But disasters can still wound us. 4 They can screw us up and set us back. 5 Wouldn't it be nice if there was genuine, scientifically documented truth to the expression "what doesn't kill you makes you stronger''?
1 One way social scientists have probed the effects of career setbacks is to look at scientists of very similar qualifications. 2 These scientists, for reasons that are mostly arbitrary, either just missed getting a research grant or just barely made it. 3 In social sciences, this is known as examining "near misses" and "narrow wins" in areas where merit is subjective. 4 That allows researchers to measure only the effects of being chosen or not. 5 Studies in this area have found conflicting results. 6 In the competitive game of biomedical science, research has been done on scientists who narrowly lost or won grant money. 7 It suggests that narrow winners become even bigger winners down the line. 8 In other words, the rich get richer.?
1 A 2018 study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, for example, followed researchers in the Netherlands. 2 Researchers concluded that those who just barely qualified for a grant were able to get twice as much money within the next eight years as those who just missed out. 3 And the narrow winners were 50 percent more likely to be given a professorship.?
1 Others in the US have found similar effects with National Institutes of Health early-career fellowships launching narrow winners far ahead of close losers. 2 The phenomenon is often referred to as the Matthew effect, inspired by the Bible's wisdom that to those who have, more will be given. 3 There's a good explanation for the phenomenon in the book The Formula: The Universal Laws of Success by Albert Laszlo Barabasi. 4 According to Barabasi, it's easier and less risky for those in positions of power to choose to hand awards and funding to those who've already been so recognized.?
1 This is bad news for the losers. 2 Small early career setbacks seem to have a disproportionate effect down the line. 3 What didn't kill them made them weaker. 4 But other studies using the same technique have shown there's sometimes no penalty to a near miss. 5 Students who just miss getting into top high schools or universities do just as well later in life as those who just manage to get accepted. 6 In this case, what didn't kill them simply didn't matter. 7 So is there any evidence that setbacks might actually improve our career prospects? 8 There is now.?
1 In a study published in Nature Communications, Northwestern University sociologist Dashun Wang tracked more than 1,100 scientists who were on the border between getting a grant and missing out between 1990 and 2005. 2 He followed various measures of performance over the next decade. 3 These included how many papers they authored and how influential those papers were, as measured by the number of subsequent citations. 4 As expected, there was a much higher rate of attrition (减员) among scientists who didn't get grants. 5 But among those who stayed on, the close losers performed even better than the narrow winners. 6 To make sure this wasn't by chance, Wang conducted additional tests using different performance measures. 7 He examined how many times people were first authors on influential studies, and the like.?
1 One straightforward reason close losers might outperform narrow winners is that the two groups have comparable ability. 2 In Wang's study, he selected the most determined, passionate scientists from the loser group and culled (剔除) what he deemed the weakest members of the winner group. 3 Yet the persevering losers still came out on top. 4 He thinks that being a close loser might give people a psychological boost, or the proverbial kick in the pants.?
1 Utrecht University sociologist Arnout van de Rijt was the lead author on the 2018 paper showing the rich get richer. 2 He said the new finding is apparently reasonable and worth some attention. 3 His own work showed that although the narrow winners did get much more money in the near future, the actual performance of the close losers was just as good.
1 He said the people who should be paying regard to the Wang paper are the funding agents who distribute government grant money. 2 After all, by continuing to pile riches on the narrow winners, the taxpayers are not getting the maximum bang for their buck if the close losers are performing just as well or even better. 3 There's a huge amount of time and effort that goes into the process of selecting who gets grants, he said, and the latest research shows that the scientific establishment is not very good at distributing money. 4 "Maybe we should spend less money trying to figure out who is better than who," he said, suggesting that some more equal dividing up of money might be more productive and more efficient. 5 Van de Rijt said he's not convinced that losing out gives people a psychological boost. 6 It may yet be a selection effect. 7 Even though Wang tried to account for this by culling the weakest winners, it's impossible to know which of the winners would have quit had they found themselves on the losing side.?
1 For his part, Wang said that in his own experience, losing did light a motivating fire. 2 He recalled a recent paper he submitted to a journal, which accepted it only to request extensive editing, and then reversed course and rejected it. 3 He submitted the unedited version to a more respected journal and got accepted.?
1 In sports and many areas of life, we think of failures as evidence of something we could have done better. 2 We regard these disappointments as a fate we could have avoided with more careful preparation, different training, a better strategy, or more focus. 3 And there it makes sense that failures show us the road to success. 4 These papers deal with a kind of failure people have little control over-rejection. 5 Others determine who wins and who loses. 6 But at the very least, the research is starting to show that early setbacks don't have to be fatal. 7 They might even make us better at our jobs. 8 Getting paid like a winner, though? 9 That’s a different matter.?

questions.explanation:
【定位】

由题干中的a close loser和persevere in their research定位到文章G）段倒数第一、二句。


【答案解析】

细节辨认题。倒数第一句提到，作为一个略输者可能会给人们带来心理上的激励，或俗话所说的一种有激励效果的意外挫折。题干中的 motivate 对应原文中的 give people a psychological boos，题干中的 persevere in their research对应原文中的persevering losers，故答案为G）。

【定位】

由题干中的researchers already recognized定位到文章D）段最后一句。


【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句指出，巴拉巴西认为, 对于那些掌权者来说，选择把奖项和资金交给那些已经得到认可的人更容易，风险也更小。题干中的 Grant awarders 和 researchers already recognized分别对应定位句中的those in positions of power 和 those who've already been so recognized,而题干中的favor表明颁奖者的倾向,与定位句中的easier and less risky相对应，故答案为D）。

【定位】

由题干中的early setbacks和job performance定位到文章K）段倒数第三、四句。


【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，但至少，研究开始表明，早期的挫折不一定是致命的。它们甚至可以让我们在工作上做得更好。题干中的help people improve their job performance 对应原文中的 make us better at our jobs，故答案为 K）。

【定位】

由题干中的contradictory findings定位到文章B）段倒数第四句。


【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，这一领域的研究发现了相互矛盾的结果。题干中的Research by social scientists on the effects of career setbacks指的就是定位句中的Studies in this area，而题干中的contradictory findings对应定位句中的 conflicting results，故答案为 B）。

【定位】

由题干中的 the best interest of taxpayers 和narrow winners定位到文章I）段第二句。


【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，如果略输者表现同样好甚至更好，通过继续把财富积累在少数赢家身上，纳税人并没有得到最大的回报。定位句中的riches指的就是money。题干中的the best interest of taxpayers 和 keep giving money to narrow winners 对应原文中的 getting the maximum bang for their buck 和 continuing to pile riches on the narrow winners，故答案为 I）。

【定位】

由题干中的Scientists who persisted in research without receiving a grant 和 made greater achievements定位到文章F）段倒数第三句。


【答案解析】

细节辨认题。定位句指出，在那些留下来的人中，略输者甚至比险胜者表现得更好。题干中的 Scientists who persisted in research without receiving a grant 和 made greater achievements 分别对应定位句中的the close losers和 performed even better，而题干中的 those who got one with luck指的就是定位句中的the narrow winners，题干中的 persisted in research 是对定位句中的stayed on的同义转述，故答案为F）。

【定位】

由题干中的rejected、one journal和get accepted定位到文章J）段第二、三句。


【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句提到，他回忆起最近他提交给某杂志的一篇论文，该杂志接受了这篇论文，却要求进行大量的编辑，然后又改口拒绝了这篇论文。他将未经编辑的版本提交给了一家更受尊敬的杂志，并被接受了。题干中的A research paper 对应原文中的 a recent paper，题干是对定位句的归纳概括，故答案为J）。

【定位】

由题干中的narrow winners of research grants、better chances 和 be promoted to professors定位到文章C）段最后一句。


【答案解析】

细节辨认题。定位句指出，险胜的人获得教授职位的可能性高出50%。题干中的narrow winners of research grants 和 professors 分别对应定位句中的 the narrow winners 和 professorship，而题干中的had better chances就是对定位句中的were 50 percent more likely的同义转述，故答案为C）。

【定位】

由题干中的more fruitful、distribute grants 和 on a relatively equal basis 定位到文章 I）段倒数第四句。


【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，也许我们应该花更少的钱来弄清楚谁比谁更优秀，这暗示一些更平等的资金分配可能会更有成效，更有效率。 题干中的 more fruitful 和 on a relatively equal basis分别对应定位句中的more productive and more efficient 和 more equal，而题干中的 distribute grants 是对定位句中的dividing up of money的同义转述，故答案为I）。

【定位】

由题干中的 Minor setbacks in their early career 和 a strong negative effect 定位到文章 E）段第二、三句。


【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，职业生涯早期的小挫折似乎会对未来产生不成比例的影响。那些没有杀死他们的东西让他们变得更弱了。题干中的 Minor setbacks in their early career 和 a strong negative effect 分别对应原文中的 Small early career setbacks 和 have a disproportionate effect，故答案为E）。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 Boredom has become trendy. 2 Studies point to how boredom is good for creativity and innovation, as well as mental health. 3 It is found that people are more creative following the completion of a tedious task.? 4 When people are bored, they have an increase in "associative thought" 一 the process of making new connections between ideas, which is linked to innovative thinking. 5 These studies are impressive, but in reality, the benefits of boredom may be related to having time to clear your mind, be quiet, or daydream.
1 In our stimulation-rich world, it seems unrealistic that boredom could occur at all. 2 Yet, there are valid reasons boredom may feel so painful. 3 As it turns out, boredom might signal the fact that you have a need that isn't being met.?
1 Our always-on world of social media may result in more connections, but they are superficial and can get in the way of building a real sense of belonging. 2 Feeling bored may signal the desire for a greater sense of community and the feeling that you fit in with others around you.? 3 So take the step of joining an organization to build face-to-face relationships.? 4 You'll find depth that you won't get from your screen no matter how many likes you get on your post.
1 Similar to the need for belonging, bored people often report that they feel a limited sense of meaning.? 2 It's a fundamental human need to have a larger purpose and to feel like we're part of something bigger than ourselves. 3 When people are bored, they're more likely to feel less meaning in their lives. 4 If you want to reduce boredom and increase your sense of meaning, seek work where you can make a unique contribution, or find a cause you can support with your time and talent.
1 If your definition of boredom is being quiet, mindful, and reflective, keep it up. 2 But if you're struggling with real boredom and the emptiness it provokes, consider whether you might seek new connections and more significant challenges. 3 These are the things that will genuinely relieve boredom and make you more effective in the process.

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What have studies found about boredom?

关于无聊的研究发现了什么？

A) It facilitates innovative thinking.

它促进创新思维。

B) It is a result of doing boring tasks.

这是做无聊工作的结果。

C) It helps people connect with others.

它帮助人们与他人联系。

D) It does harm to one's mental health.

它对人的精神健康有害。


【定位及答案】

由题干中的studies和boredom定位到第 一段第二、三句。

文章第一段第二句提到，研究指出，无聊是如何有利于创造力的。第三句提 到，研究发现，人们在完成一项枯燥乏味的任务后 更有创造力。第四句进一步指出，当人们感到无聊时，他们会增加“联想思维"，这与创新思维有关。由此可见，科学家对无聊所做的研究表明，无聊可以激发人们的创造性思维，故答案为A）。


【错误选项分析】

B选项【曲解文意】：文章第一段第三句提到，人们在完成一项枯燥乏味的任务后更有创造力，从事无聊工作的结果是有创造力，而不是更加无聊，故排除B）。

C选项【曲解文意】：C）项是根据第四句中new connections设置的干扰项，文中是指“联想思维”是在思想之间建立新联系的过程，而非无聊帮人们与他人建立联系，故排除。

D选项【反向干扰】：文章第一段第二句提到，无聊如何有利于创造力和创新，以及心理健康。由此可见，无聊对心理健康是有益的，而非有害的，故排除D）。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What does the author say boredom might indicate?

作者说无聊可能意味着什么？

A) A need to be left alone.

需要一个人独处。

B) A desire to be fulfilled.

渴望得到满足。

C) A conflict to be resolved.

需要解决的冲突。

D) A feeling to be validated.

需要被认同的感觉。


【定位及答案】

由题干中的boredom might indicate定位 到第二段最后一句。

定位句提到，事实证明，无聊可能表明你的需求没有得到满足。由此可知，当人们感到无聊时，这表明人们的某种需求未得到满足，故答案为B）。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【理解片面】：文章第五段第一句提到，如果你对无聊的定义是安静、专注和反省，那就坚持下去。但并未提到无聊意味着需要独处，由此可知，该选项过于片面，故排除A）。

C选项【无中生有】：文中并未提及无聊意味着需要解决的冲突，故排除C）。

D选项【曲解文意】：文章第三段第二句提到，感到无聊可能表明更强烈的群体意识渴望，并且想要融入你周围的人之中，这与想法或情感被认同有所不同，故排除D）。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What do we learn about social media from the passage?

我们从这篇文章中学到了什么？

A) It may be an obstacle to expanding one's connections.

这可能是扩大人际关系的障碍。

B) It may get in the way of enhancing one's social status.

它可能会妨碍提高一个人的社会地位。

C) It may prevent people from developing a genuine sense of community.

这可能会妨碍人们形成真正的群体意识。

D) It may make people feel that they ought to fit in with the outside world.

它可能会让人们觉得他们应该融入外部世界。


【定位及答案】

由题干中的social media定位到第三段第一、二句。

定位句指出，我们一直在线的社交媒体世界可能会产生更多的联系，但这些联系是肤浅的，可能会妨碍建立真正的归属感。感到无聊可能表明更强烈的群体意识的欲望，并且想要融入你周围的人之中。由此可见,过多的社交媒体会妨碍我们建立真正的归属感，造成群体意识的缺失，故答案为C）。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【曲解文意】：文章第三段第一句指出，我们一直在线的社交媒体世界可能会产生更多的联系，由此可见， 社交媒体是可以扩大人际关系的，故排除A）。

B选项【无中生有】：文中并未提及社交媒体会妨碍人们提高社会地位, 故排除B）。

D选项【反向干扰】：文章第三段第二句指出，感到无聊可 能表明更强烈的群体意识欲望，并且想要融入你周围的人之中，由此可见，社交媒体并不能帮助人们融入周围的人群中，而是妨碍了人们现实生活的粘合度，故排除D）。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What does the author suggest people do to get rid of boredom?

作者建议人们做些什么来摆脱无聊？

A) Count the likes they get on their posts.

数一数他们在帖子上得到的喜欢。

B) Reflect on how they relate to others.

反思他们与他人的关系。

C) Engage in real-life interactions.

参与现实生活中的互动。

D) Participate in online discussions.

参与在线讨论。


【定位及答案】

由题干中的get rid of boredom定位到第三段第三句和最后一段第二、三句。

第三段第三句提到采取措施加入一个组织，建立面对面的关系。最后一段第二句提到，如果你正与真正的无聊和它所引发的空虚作斗争，考虑一下你是否可能寻求新的联系 和更重大的挑战。这些事情将真正缓解无聊，让你在这个过程中更有效率。综合两部分内容可知，答案为C）。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【曲解文意】：文章第三段最后一句明确提到，你会拥有深度的人际交往，这是你无论在你的帖子上得到多少点赞都获得不了的。由此可见，社交媒体上获得的关注，并不能满足人们现实生活中的情感需要，故排除A）。

B选项【无中生有】：文章并未提及人们可以通过反思如何与他人相处来摆脱无聊，故排除B）。

D选项【曲解文意】：文章第三段最后一句只提到了发表帖子这种网络社交方式，并未提及在线讨论，D）不符合文义，故排除。

choices.label: C
choices.text: Define boredom in their unique way.

choices.text: Devote themselves to a worthy cause.

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What should people do to enhance their sense of meaning?

人们应该做些什么来增强他们的意义感？

A) Try to do something original.

尝试做一些原创的东西。

B) Confront significant challenges.

面对重大挑战。

C) Define boredom in their unique way.

 用他们独特的方式定义无聊。

D) Devote themselves to a worthy cause.

 献身于有价值的事业。


【定位及答案】

由题干中的enhance their sense of meaning定位到第四段最后一句。

定位句指出,如果你想减少无聊感，增加你的意义感，找一份你能做出独特贡献的工作，或者找一个你能用时间和才能支持的事业。由此可见，作者认为，人们想要增加意义感的两种方法为:一、找一份可以做出独特贡献的工 作；二、找一份能有时间和才能支持的事业。故答 案为D）。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【曲解文意】：文章第四段最后一句指出，要增加意义感， 找一份你能做出独特贡献的工作，但原创的事情并不一定能做出独特的贡献，故排除A）。

sections.passage:
1 Can you remember what you ate yesterday? 2 If asked, most people will be able to give a vague description of their main meals: breakfast, lunch, dinner. 3 But can you be sure you've noted every snack bar in your car, or every handful of nuts at your desk? 4 Most people will have a feeling that they've missed something out.
1 We originally had this suspicion back in 2016, puzzled by the fact that national statistics showed calorie consumption falling dramatically over past decades. 2 We found reliable evidence that people were drastically under-reporting what they ate.?
1 Now the Office for National Statistics has confirmed that we are consuming 50% more calories than our national statistics claim.?
1 Why is this happening? 2 We can point to at least three potential causes. 3 One is the rise in obesity levels itself. 4 Under-reporting rates are much higher for obese people, because they simply consume more food, and thus have more to remember.?
1 Another cause is that the proportion of people who are trying to lose weight has been increasing over time. 2 People who want to lose weight are more likely to under-report their eating — regardless of whether they are overweight or not. 3 This may be driven partly by self-deception or "wishful thinking".
1 The final potential cause is an increase in snacking and eating out over recent decades — both in terms of how often they happen and how much they contribute to our overall energy intake. 2 Again, there is evidence that food consumed out of the home is one of the most poorly recorded categories in surveys.?
1 So, what's the message conveyed? 2 For statistics, we should invest in more accurate measurement options. 3 For policy, we need to focus on options that make it easy for people to eat fewer calories. 4 If people do not know how much they are eating, it can be really hard for them to stick to a diet. 5 Also, we should be looking for new ways to ensure what people eat wouldn't have much impact on their waistlines.? 6 If this works, it won't matter if they can't remember what they ate yesterday.

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What did the author suspect back in 2016?

在2016年的时候作者怀疑什么？

A) Calorie consumption had fallen drastically over the decades.

在过去的几十年里，卡路里的消耗量急剧下降。

B) Most people surveyed were reluctant to reveal what they ate.

大多数被调查者不愿透露他们吃了什么。

C) The national statistics did not reflect the actual calorie consumption.

国家统计数据没有反映实际的卡路里消耗量。

D) Most people did not include snacks when reporting their calorie intake.

大多数人在报告卡路里摄入量时不包括零食。


【定位及答案】

由题干中的suspect和back in 2016定位到第二段。

定位段指出，早在2016年他们就有了这种怀疑，因为国家统计数据显示，在过去几十年，卡路里消耗量大幅下降，这让他们感到困惑。有可靠的证据证明人们严重地漏报了他们吃的东西。由此可见，有证据显示人们漏报了自己摄入的食物，因此作者怀疑国家统计局数据的真实性，故答案为C)。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：文章第二段指出，国家统计数据显示，过去 几十年，卡路里消耗量大幅下降，这让他们感到困 惑。由此可见，卡路里消耗量的下降数据令人困惑，这是引起怀疑的原因，并非怀疑的内容，故排除A)。

B选项【曲解文意】：下文中提到人们漏报数据的原因，并非不想透露，而是因为某些原因无法准确汇报，故排除B)。

D选项【曲解文意】：文章第一段倒数第二句提到，你能确定你注意到了你在车里吃的小吃，或者你桌子上的每一把坚果吗，这是一个反问的句子，并不是作者的怀疑，而是一个事实，故排除D)。

1 Nowadays, the topic of physical exercise has attracted unprecedented public attention. 【引出话题：人们对体育锻炼的关注】 2 However, a great number of college students still neglect the important role it plays in achieving success. 【转折：大学生没有充分意识到体育锻炼重要性】
1 To list just a few of the benefits of taking physical exercise. 【引出体育锻炼的若干好处】 2 First of all, exercise on a regular basis, such as jogging and swimming, enhances our physical health, which, in turn, keeps us energetic and vigorous in academic learning and future working. 【论点1：增强体魄，保证活力】 3 In addition, sports such as football and basketball, can cultivate our team spirit, communicative competence and leadership, and these vital skills will carry us further in career and social life. 【论点2：培养团队精神、沟通能力和领导力】 4 Last but not least, the sweat from exercise takes away our daily stress and anxiety, and participation in sports brings us the spirit of grit — the perseverance for a long-term goal, even if in adversity. 【论点3：释放压力焦虑，培养坚毅精神】
1 In conclusion, we should never ignore the significance of physical activities. 【总结：不应忽略体育活动的重要性】 2 It makes sense when you read the inspiring story of Zhong Nanshan, who keeps the habit of doing exercise from his 20s until now, 80s. 【举例：以钟南山为例】 3 So, why don't we start now? 【反问收尾：呼吁现在开始锻炼】

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 In the Chinese lunar calendar, Start of Autumn means the end of summer and the beginning of autumn. 2 The first thing brought about by the beginning of autumn is the change of weather, with the temperature gradually dropping. 3 When people see the leaves begin to turn yellow and fall, they know that autumn has come, which is called " a falling leaf heralds autumn ". 4 But at this time, the hot weather is not completely over. 5 The high temperature usually lasts for a period of time and it is called, " the autumn tiger ". 6 The beginning of autumn is of great significance to farmers. 7 At this time, various autumn crops grow rapidly and begin to mature, and the harvest season is coming.

questions.stem: ①在中国农历中，立秋(Start of Autumn)意味着夏天的结束和秋天的开始。②立秋带来的首先是天气的变化，气温逐渐下降。③人们看到树叶开始变黄飘落时，知道秋天已经来临，这就是所谓的“一叶知秋”。④但此时酷热的天气并未完全结束。⑤高温通常还会持续一段时间，被称为“秋老虎。⑥立秋对农民意义重大。⑦这时各种秋季作物迅速生长、开始成熟，收获的季节即将到来。
questions.answer: 1 In the Chinese lunar calendar, Start of Autumn means the end of summer and the beginning of autumn. 2 The first thing brought about by the beginning of autumn is the change of weather, with the temperature gradually dropping. 3 When people see the leaves begin to turn yellow and fall, they know that autumn has come, which is called " a falling leaf heralds autumn ". 4 But at this time, the hot weather is not completely over. 5 The high temperature usually lasts for a period of time and it is called, " the autumn tiger ". 6 The beginning of autumn is of great significance to farmers. 7 At this time, various autumn crops grow rapidly and begin to mature, and the harvest season is coming.

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 This fall, thousands of college students from across the country will begin their undergraduate studies at colleges around the nation. 
 2 They will inevitably pack too much to fit in their tiny dorm rooms. 
 3 They will also carry with them a huge student loan debt, in addition to countless "hidden" out-of-pocket costs paid for by their bank accounts and the bank accounts of their families.?
1 At my well-respected, private, four-year university in Washington, D.C., which boasts a yearly tuition of $44,046 not including room and board, I receive over $57,000 yearly in financial aid. 2 As a student from a family that is struggling to make ends meet, my financial aid package is a combination of federal grants and federal work study, university merit scholarships and financial aid awards, and about $8,000 yearly in federally subsidized （有补贴的） and unsubsidized loans. 
 3 On paper, my expenses and my financial aid just about even out. 
 4 Off paper, they don't.?
1 Universities today are in the business of making money, and mine is no exception. 
 2 They hit me right out of gate with a $160 fee to attend my freshman orientation, a price which does not include the cost of travel to and from the District. 
 3 Almost every class has an associated fee not included in the cost of tuition, most between $40 and $100. 
 4 Fees for lab science classes are the highest, and all students at my university are required to take at least one lab before they graduate.
 5 Buying a laptop proved a necessity and, thankfully, a relative bought me one as a gift. 
 6 Renting a mini-fridge for my dorm room costs my roommates and me about $140 a year.?
1 Schools will charge you whatever they can. 
 2 The costs of any damage to the dorm, including elevators, bathrooms, and common areas, are billed to every person on a dorm floor, or even the entire building if they do not know who caused the damage. 
 3 After I fell out of my bed twice during my freshman year, the university installed a railing — for $20, billed to my student account.
 4 My financial aid did not anticipate any of these costs, and so it did not cover them.?
1 An Internet search of "hidden costs" of college turns up a host of articles on parent-centered websites on the college application process. 
 2 These articles are almost always geared towards upper and middle-class families. 3 For students already struggling to pay tuition, these costs may be the least of their worries.
1 So what hidden costs should low-income students really be paying attention to? 
 2 My college experience offers a few examples.
1 If you are a low-income student who will be attending school out-of-state, make sure you know if you can use your state benefits, such as the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP. 
 2 It wasn’t until after I had accepted admission to an out-of-state school that I learned that I could not use my Ohio Medicaid on campus for anything other than emergency care. 
 3 My benefits became invalid the second I moved out of Ohio. 4 After my freshman year, I had to opt for the school 's insurance plan, which costs around $2,000 a year.
 5 Even if your school offers a flat-rate fee for a doctor 's appointment at the student health center (mine is $20 a visit), these fees often do not include extra fees for lab tests or prescription medications （药物）.?
1 If you plan on paying off bills in your student account with a credit card, be aware of any additional costs. 
 2 My school charges an additional fee for the use of a credit card to settle outstanding charges, which can add upwards of 3% of the balance to your bill.?
1 Colleges often offer the most generous packages during freshman year as a way to attract new students. 
 2 My family was careful to ask about the chances of financial aid being taken away after my freshman year. 
 3 We were assured that, except for low grades or a raise in family income, no money would be taken away.? 4 We did not know to ask — and the school did not readily point out — that even if tuition rises, my financial aid package will stay the same. 
 5 So when my university voted to raise tuition costs 3% at the end of my freshman year, my financial aid package remained the same and I was suddenly responsible for an additional $1,200 for the next year. 
 6 The university administration will likely vote to raise costs at least once more before my graduation.?
1 Yes, I chose to attend an expensive university far from my hometown.
 2 Yes, there were cheaper options. 
 3 But there are promising students from struggling families across the nation who should not rule out their dream schools entirely. 
 4 All things considered, I am paying significantly less than the ticket price of my university, and having an educational experience in Washington, D.C., that I would not have had anywhere else. 
 5 As a low-income student from a down-and-out Rust Belt community, these educational experiences have enormous potential to brighten my future —— and my family's future.?
1 The key is to make sure that students and their families understand that hidden costs exist, and that they may prove problematic.
 2 Fill out a more comprehensive checklist, and be wary of listed prices that seem too low. 
 3 Understand just how complicated the financial aid process is.
1 Students and families must also understand their ability to self-advocate. 
 2 They should not pay student bills or excess fees blindly.
 3 If something does not look right, ask about it. 
 4 If it still doesn't look right, negotiate it. 
 5 In cases where parents are working multiple jobs, are less knowledgeable about college bureaucracies, have limited English language skills, or are not contributing financially to their child's education, the burden of self-advocacy will fall on the student.? 6 I understand the difficulty, and the embarrassment. 
 7 But it is necessary.
1 In the grand scheme of things, however, colleges also must come to understand that the hidden fees they ask for may prove unmanageable for the very kinds of low-income or first-generation students they are trying desperately to attract.

questions.explanation:
【定位及答案】

由题干中的financial aid、remains unchanged 和tuition rises定位到I段④句。

④句提到，我们并不知道要去询问———学校也没有打算指出——即使学费上涨，我的补助计划依旧保持原样。

⑤句接着用事实证明，来年学费增长了3%，但经济补助还是和原来的一样。

题干中的financial aid和tuition rises 在④句中直接出现，题干中的remains unchanged对应定位句中的stay the same 和⑤句���的remained the same，故答案为I）。

【定位及答案】

由题干中的state benefits和go to college out of the state定位到G）段②③句。

定位句指出，直到我被一所州外的学校录取以后，我才知道除了急救护理，我不能在校园里使用我在俄亥俄州的医疗补助。我的福利在我离开俄亥俄州的那一刻就失效了。题干是对定位句的概括总结，故答案为G）。

【定位及答案】

由题干中的The financial aid the author receives和cover all her college expenses定位到B）段③④句。

定位句指出，从理论上来看，我的支出和财政补助基本持平。实际而言，并非如此。题干中的cover是对定位句中even out的同义转述。

题干中的is supposed to 意为“应该是"，用于表示某事本应发生而没有发生，这与定位句中的On paper和Off paper表达含义一致，故答案为B）。

【定位及答案】

由题干中的damages dorm facilities、not identified和students are required to share the cost定位到D）段②句。

②句指出，宿舍的任何损坏，包括电梯、浴室和公共区域，都会向该楼层的所有学生征收费用，如果他们不知道是谁导致的损坏，甚至会向整栋楼收费。

题干中的 damages dorm facilities对应定位句中的any damage to the dorm，题干中的not identified对应定位句中的do not know，题干中的students are required to share the cost对应定位句中的billed to every person，故答案为D）。

【定位及答案】

由题干中的difficult and embarrassing和make inquiries定位到L）段。

定位段③④指出，如果有些事情看起来不对劲，那就要询问。如果还是不妥，那就协商一下。接着表示，如果父母身兼数职，不太了解大学里的官僚制度，英语水平有限，或是没有为孩子的教育提供经济支持，那么自我辩护的重担就落在了学生身上。但这是必要的。

定位段中提及的“自我辩护”即对所收费用是否合理进行询问或协商，题干是对定位段的总结概括，故答案为L）。

【定位及答案】

由题干中的 on student loans定位到A）段第③句。

③句指出，除了由他们自己的银行账户和他们家人的银行账户支付的无数“隐性”自付费用外，他们还将背负巨额的学生贷款债务。题干中的student loans对应定位句中的student loan debt，故答案为A）。

【定位及答案】

由题干中的change the author's future life and that of her family’s定位到J）段⑤句。

⑤句指出，作为一名来自穷困潦倒的铁锈地带社区的低收入学生，这些教育经历有巨大的潜力照亮我的未来——以及我家庭的未来。

题干中的change the author's future life and that of her family's 是对定位句中brighten my future—and my family's future的同义转述，故答案为J）。

【定位及答案】

由题干中的no longer be qualified for financial aid、perform poorly in school和 family income has increased定位到I）段③句。

③句指出，除非成绩很差或家庭收入增加，否则不会取消补助。

题干中的perform poorly in school对应定位句中的low grades，题干中的family income has increased对应定位句中的a raise in family income，故答案为I。

【定位及答案】

由题干中的In addition to tuition和pay extra fees for the courses they take定位到C）段③句。

③句指出，几乎每门课都有一笔不包含在学费里的相关费用，大多数在40 美元到100美元之间。

题干中的In addition to tuition对应定位句中的not included in the cost of tuition，题干中的pay extra fees for the courses they take对应定位句中的Almost every class has an associated fee，故答案为C）。

【定位及答案】

由题干中的charge students a fee和using credit cards to pay bills定位到H）段②句。

②句指出，我的学校对使用信用卡结算未支付费用额外收费，这可能会在你的账单上增加3%以上的费用。

题干中的charge students a fee 对应②句中的charges an additional fee，题干中的 using credit cards to pay bills对应②句中的the use of a credit card to settle outstanding charges，故答案为H）。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 To write his 2010 book, The 5 - Factor World Diet, nutritionist Harley Pasternak traveled to the healthiest countries around the world to learn more about what made their meals extra nourishing.
1 He noted that Japanese people ate a wonderful variety of seaweeds, and that Chinese people tried to include at least five different colors in every meal. 2 Pasternak also came away with some valuable observations about how different the North American way of life was, compared with many other countries.?
1 For starters, Americans eat much bigger portions than people in other countries. 2 “We don't prioritize eating seasonally or locally, and we also add lots of salt, sugar and thickening agents to our foods," explained Pasternak.? 3 Contrast that to the healthy Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets listed in Pasternak 's book. 4 They all seem to stick to the ethos （特质） of regional, seasonal produce.?
1 For example, a traditional Mediterranean diet includes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, nuts and olive oil as the main components of nutritional intake. 2 Fish, chicken and red wine make moderate appearances, while red meat, salt and sugar are used much less often. 3 The benefits of a traditional Mediterranean diet have been studied since the 1970s, and researchers have found that living that olive oil life can help people lose weight, lower their heart disease risk and reverse diabetes.
1 Most other healthy eating cultures also make meals an event — say, multiple courses around the family table, or a glass or two of red wine at a long lunch — as opposed to hastily wolfing down handfuls of cereal above the kitchen sink and calling it dinner.?
1 Each of the healthy eating cultures has its own unique feature. 2 But Pasternak did take note of one unifying factor in all of the healthy societies he observed. 3 "The only overlapping feature in most of these healthy countries is that they all walk way more than the average American," said Pasternak, "So really, regardless of what you're eating, if someone 's walking four miles more than you each day, they're going to be a lot thinner and live a lot longer than you.?

【题目及选项翻译】

What characterizes Japanese and Chinese foods?

日本和中国的饮食有哪些特点？

A. Variety.

多样性

B. Flavor.

口味

C. Color.

颜色

D. Naturalness.

自然


【定位及答案】

由题干中的Japanese and Chinese foods定位到2段①句。

①句指出，他注意到日本人吃很多种类的海藻，而中国人则会在每餐中纳入至少5种颜色的食物。由此可见，不管是日本人还是中国人，在饮食上的特点都是种类丰富，故答案为A）。


【错误选项分析】

根据定位句可知，日本人酷爱食用海藻，可以理解为“天然性”，而中国人则注重食物的颜色丰富，C）和D）只体现了其中一个国家的特点，故排除，而B）项中提及的“口味”在文中并无体现，故排除。

What is typical of Americans in the way of eating?

美国人的饮食习惯是什么？

A) They emphasize nutrition.

 他们强调营养。

B) They tend to eat quite a lot.

他们往往吃得很多。

C) They prioritize convenience.

他们优先考虑方便。

D ) They care about flavors.

他们关心口味。


【定位及答案】

由题干中的 Americans in the way of eating定位到3段①句。

定位句提到，美国人比其他国家的人饭量更大，也就是说，他们吃的更多一些，故答案为B）。


【错误选项分析】

文章3段②句提到，美国人并不会优先吃季节性食物或是本地食物，另外还会加入很多盐、糖和增稠剂到食物中。可见其并非注重营养，故排除A）。

而C）中提及的“便利性”和D）中提及的"口味"在定位段中均无体现，故排除。

【题目及选项翻译】

What features in Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets?

地中海、北欧和冲绳饮食的特点是什么？

A) Fruits and vegetables.

水果和蔬菜。

B) Olive oil and red wine.

橄榄油和红酒。

C) Seasonal local produce.

季节性本地农产品。

D) Unprocessed ingredients.

未加工成分。


【定位及答案】

由题干中的Mediterranean，Nordic and Okinawan diets定位到3段③④两句。

定位句指出，他将此和健康的地中海饮食、北欧饮食和冲绳饮食进行了对比。这些地方的饮食看似都坚持了地方性和季节性农产品的特质，故答案为C）。


【错误选项分析】

文章4段①②句提到，传统的地中海饮食把水果、蔬菜、全麦、坚果、橄榄油作为营养摄入的主要部分。鱼肉、鸡肉和红酒会适度出现，而红肉、盐和糖则更少被使用。A）、B）和D）三项仅涉及地中海饮食，内容片面，故排除。

1 Recognizing when a friend or colleague feels sad, angry or surprised is key to getting along with others. 2 But a new study suggests that being sensitive to people's feelings may sometimes come with an extra dose of stress. 3 This and other research challenge the prevailing view that emotional intelligence is uniformly beneficial to its bearer.?
1 In a study, psychologist Myriam Bechtoldt of the Frankfurt School of Finance and Management in Germany asked 166 male university students a series of questions to measure their emotional intelligence.? 2 For example, they showed the students photographs of people's faces and asked them to what extent feelings such as happiness or disgust were being expressed. 3 The students then had to give job talks in front of judges who displayed serious facial expressions. 4 The scientists measured concentrations of stress hormones in the students ' saliva （唾液） before and after the talk.
1 In students who were rated more emotionally intelligent, the stress measures increased more during the experiment and took longer to go back to baseline. 2 The findings suggest that some people may be too emotionally clever for their own good, says Bechtoldt. 3 “Sometimes you can be so good at something that it causes trouble," she notes.?
1 Indeed, the study adds to previous research hinting at a dark side of emotional intelligence. 2 A study published in 2002 in Personality and Individual Differences suggested that emotionally perceptive people might be particularly influenced by feelings of depression and hopelessness. 3 Furthermore, several studies have implied that emotional intelligence can be used to manipulate others for personal gains.?
1 More research is needed to see how exactly the relation between emotional intelligence and stress would play out in women and in people of different ages and education levels. 2 Nevertheless, emotional intelligence is a useful skill to have, as long as you learn to also properly cope with emotions — both others ' and your own, says Bechtoldt. 3 For example, some sensitive individuals may assume responsibility for other people's sadness or anger, which ultimately stresses them out. 4 Remember, as Bechtoldt says, "you are not responsible for how other people feel."?

The World Pipe Band Championships will take place in Glasgow on Saturday.
Over 120 of the world's best pipe bands will compete at the championships.
Over 4,000 pipers and drummers are expected to descend on the city for the annual event.
It will take place at the St. James Playing Fields in Glasgow on Saturday,18 May from 10:00 am until 7:00 pm.
The event is free.
Also, a free shuttle bus will run between the event car parks and the competition site.
Shuttle buses will run every 15 minutes from 8:00 am until 8:00 pm.
Glasgow City Council says it is estimated to bring $300,000 to the local economy.
The first World Pipe Band Championships were held in Edinburgh in 1947.
The event first took place in Glasgow in 1948.
It has been held regularly in Glasgow since 1986.

Summer doesn't begin for two more days, but scientists are already sounding the alarm about dangerous ice melts going on right now in Greenland.
The vast island usually locks away enough fresh water in its ice sheet, which if melted can raise global sea levels by six meters.
And research shows that in recent years its ice has melted faster than ever before.
This month, as temperatures in northwestern Greenland approach all-time highs, researchers are encountering unusual, surprising levels of melting ice in the region.
The most significant concern here is how early this is all happening.
Greenland experiences annual ice melt and growth cycles.
But this year, the melting season began in early May.
That's a month earlier than normal and something that's happened only once before in the historical record in 2016.
That means that not only is the ice melting very fast, it has more time to melt this summer than it would in a normal climate system.
Longer melt seasons like this one seem to lead to much greater contributions to sea-level rise than in previous decades.
Q3 What is scientists’ warning in the news report?
Q4 What do we learn about this year’s ice melting season in Greenland?
Bundles containing thousands of pounds in cash keep turning up on the streets of Blackhall Colliery in northern England, according to police.
Residents of the village have been coming across bundles of £20 notes — usually worth £2,000 — in the former mining village in County Durham.
The latest discovery was on Monday, meaning four of these cash bundles have been handed in this year and 13 since 2014.
The bundles are usually left in plain sight and have been scattered across the small coastal village.
The owner has two weeks to collect the cash, which is then returned to the finder if not claimed, according to Peterlee Police.
A Durham Police spokesperson said the money has been returned to the lucky finders in all cases except yesterday.
Policeman John Forster said in a statement :" The circumstances remain a mystery so we would welcome any information that will help us get to the bottom of these random incidents ."
He told The Northern Echo :" It isn't an affluent part of the world, so for them to find cash of that amount and instantly think about taking it to the police stations shows the community spirit there is.”
Q5 What happened on the streets of Blackhall Colliery?
Q6 What do the local police do with the money if not claimed in two weeks?
Q7 What did the policeman John Forster say about the villagers?
It's your birthday next week.
What have you got planned?
I'm not sure.
I often feel strange on my birthday.
It's like my brain decides to have a crisis.
It's not entirely unusual to feel anxious or sad around your birthday.
Birthdays can tap into a lot of things people worry about, including their achievements in life in the past decade, or their accomplishments of the past year.
Many begin to search for the meaning of their existence, leading to behaviors such as ending or starting a relationship,or plans, like starting a vigorous diet or fitness program.
I have wonderful friends and I love celebrating their birthdays.
But I don't like being the center of attention, receiving gifts and having a fuss made.
It seems to trigger a type of social anxiety.
I think social media too can intensify things as birthdays now play out more publicly.
Birthday reminders can be helpful, but I kind of worry I won't be able to drum up my own day and show it to look as exciting as it is supposed to be.
Well, to deal with the birthday blues, you should not isolate yourself.
It's best to gradually face your birthday with people you trust.
That would help you learn self-acceptance, or that it's okay to be the focus.
Perhaps. Or I could perceive my birthday as an opportunity to do something for others like asking people to make a donation instead of buying a gift.
Exactly. Or even simply see your birthday as an opportunity to bring people together for them to have fun.
Q8 How does the man often feel on his birthday?
Q9 What does the woman say many people tend to do on their birthday?
Q10 What does the man say about birthday celebrations?
Q11 What does the woman suggest the man do about his birthday celebration at the end of the conversation?
The metro was absolutely terrible this morning.
Oh, was there a delay?
No, but the train was so packed that I could barely move, and it was difficult to breathe too.
At every station, more people squeezed in and I got pushed further and further inside.
When I got to my station, I could hardly get out.
Once I did get out, I was totally exhausted.
That sounds like a nightmare.
Why didn't you take the bus?
The bus takes twice as long and it's just as crowded.
Well, what's the alternative?
Haven't you got a car?
I've got a driver's license, but that's all.
I'm saving up to buy something reasonably small and cute, but it's still a bit expensive for me, and it'll take a while before I have enough money.
Have you thought about getting an electric motorbike?
I consider that for maybe a minute.
But honestly, I've just seen too many horrible accidents involving those dangerous monsters.
What about those popular shared bikes?
You could register to use one.
Yeah, that's a possibility.
There are always several of those bikes out in front of our apartment complex.
Or you could just walk to work.
Well, it's five kilometers from home to the office.
But you've given me a thought.
I could take a change of clothes and jog to work.
But at this time of year, the air pollution is a real problem.
Oh, yeah. I didn't think of that.
You take a taxi if you really have to.
Well, that's an expensive way to get to work.
Not if you use a ride sharing app.
Good idea. I'll download one immediately. Thank you.
Q12 What does the woman say about her subway ride?
Q13 Why hasn’t the woman got her own car?
Q14 What does the woman say about electric motorbikes?

Steve Miller began his career in IT back in the late 1980s.
Being a deaf person in tech required a huge amount of effort in organization.
Because there was no email or text message service, everything had to be done face to face, or by telephone.
Communicating in meetings was very difficult.
He needed a sign language interpreter for every meeting, but it was a huge effort to coordinate.
These days, although challenges still remain, it's a good time to be a deaf person in tech, says Miller.
Big advances in speech recognition technology have enabled communication tools to turn live speech into text in real time on your smartphone or laptop, and sign language into text as well.
New Tech coupled with improvements in hearing aid technology and medical advances means that Miller is able to focus far more on his work.
He has benefited to a great extent from a tiny hearing device in his ear.
It gives him a degree of hearing, and he can use a variety of communication methods depending on the situation.
He can employ lip-reading and have meetings via video instead of on the phone.
These things have made a huge difference.
He no longer has to worry about whether or not he can understand.
He can just concentrate on how interesting the meeting might be and what he needs to get out of it in order to progress.
Q16 What do we learn about Steve Miller?
Q17 What does Miller say is making things better for people like him?
Q18 In what way can Miller benefit from attending meetings via video?
Colour is now spreading through our homes, up staircases, across wood frames and ceilings, filling in neutral spaces.
According to one interior designer,when people return home, they want to see colours that cheer them up and give them a hug.
Pure white walls simply don't do that.
They don't look after you.
Another interior designer commented that certain combinations can key into something on a deeper level, transporting you to a different moment in time.
That's the power of colour.
If you are thinking to try colour on some of your neutral walls, the advice is refreshingly simple: Choose a colour you actually like.
Don't go for a colour because it's in fashion, or you've seen it in a magazine.
If you're weary of full colour, test your tolerance with smaller spaces, such as the inside of a cupboard or a bright window frame.
If it gives you joy every time you open the cupboard, you can start to take it further.
One can also paint the wooden frameworks the same colour as the walls, helping the rooms look bigger.
In the kitchen, painting the overhead cupboards and the walls in the same colour can make it feel more spacious.
While painting the kitchen counters, a bold colour can make everything feel more open and lighter.
Additionally, a painted ceiling is a magical thing without being too obvious and can affect how the space feels as well.

Parents often hear that reading to their children is critical for supporting development, and the message is getting through to them.
In fact, in the United States, a little over half of children between the ages of three and five were read to every day in 2007, and83% of children in that age group in the same country were read to three or more times per week in 2012.
This is good news, because reading to young children helps their language and brain development.
In fact, recent research has found that both the quality and quantity of shared book reading in infancy predicted later childhood vocabulary and reading skills.
In other words, the more time parents spend reading, the greater the developmental benefits in their four-year-old children.
This is an important finding.
But does it matter what books parents read?
A new study has investigated this question.
It followed infants across the second six months of life and found that when parents showed babies books that had faces or objects with specific labels, they learned more.
This is in contrast to books that did not name images, or books that had the same label under each image.
Books that named different characters also promoted greater learning.
So what does this mean for parents?
Not all books are created equal, so parents need to choose the books they share with their children with great care.
Q22 What does the passage say parents increasingly understand?
Q23 What can predict children’s reading skills according to recent research?
Q24 What kind of books are said to help babies learn more?

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 Start of Spring marks the beginning of spring in the Chinese lunar calendar. 2 After the beginning of spring, the days become longer and the weather gets warmer: everything starts to recover and the earth is full of vitality. 3 It is often said that the whole year 's work depends on a good start in spring. 4 Farmers start planting seeds at this time to lay the foundation for a good harvest in this year. 5 The Chinese have been holding celebration activities for Start of Spring since 3,000 years ago. 6 For hundreds of years, welcoming spring has been an important folk custom. 7 During the warm days of spring when flowers blossom, people often travel outside and enjoy the beauty of spring.

questions.stem: ①立春(Start of Spring)在中国农历中表示春天的开始。②立春之后，白天变得更长，天气也愈发温暖：万物开始复苏，大地充满生机。③人们常说“一年之计在于春”。④农民在这个时节开始播种，为全年的丰喷打下基础。⑤中国人在三千年前就已开始在立春这一天举行庆祝活动。⑥数百年来，迎春一直是民间的重要习俗。⑦在春暖花开的日子里,人们常常外出玩，欣赏春天的美景。
questions.answer: 1 Start of Spring marks the beginning of spring in the Chinese lunar calendar. 2 After the beginning of spring, the days become longer and the weather gets warmer: everything starts to recover and the earth is full of vitality. 3 It is often said that the whole year 's work depends on a good start in spring. 4 Farmers start planting seeds at this time to lay the foundation for a good harvest in this year. 5 The Chinese have been holding celebration activities for Start of Spring since 3,000 years ago. 6 For hundreds of years, welcoming spring has been an important folk custom. 7 During the warm days of spring when flowers blossom, people often travel outside and enjoy the beauty of spring.

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Not doing something will always be faster than doing it. 
 2 This philosophy applies in many areas of life.
 3 For example, there is no meeting that goes faster than not having a meeting at all. 
 4 This is not to say you should never attend another meeting, but the truth is that we say "yes" to too many things we don't actually want to do.?
1 How often do people ask you to do something and you just reply," Sure."
 2 Three days later, you're overwhelmed by how much is on your to-do list. 
 3 We become frustrated by our obligations even though we were the ones who said "yes" to them in the first place. 
 4 Even worse, people will occasionally fight to do things that waste time.? 5 You don't have to do something just because it exists. 
 6 It's worth asking if things are necessary. 
 7 Many of them are not, and a simple “no" will be more productive than whatever work the most efficient person can cope with.
 8 But if the benefits of saying "no"are so obvious, then why do we say " yes " so often?
1 We say "yes" to many requests not because we want to do them, but because we don't want to be seen as rude or unhelpful. 2 Often, we have to consider saying “no” to someone we will interact with again in the future — our co-worker, our spouse, our family and friends. 3 Saying "no" to our superiors at work can be particularly difficult. 4 In these situations, I like the approach recommended in Essentialism by Greg McKeown. 5 He writes," Remind your superiors what you would be neglecting if you said 'yes ' and force them to deal with the trade-off. 6 For example, if your manager comes to you and asks you to do X, you can respond with 'Yes, I'm happy to make this the priority. 7 Which of these other projects should I deprioritize to pay attention to this new project?"?
1 Collaborating with others is an important element of life. 2 The thought of straining the relationship outweighs the commitment of our time and energy. 3 For this reason, it can be helpful to be gracious in your response. 4 Do whatever favors you can, and be warm-hearted and direct when you have to say no. 5 But even after we have accounted for these social considerations, many of us still seem to do a poor job of managing the trade-off between yes and no. 6 We find ourselves over-committed to things that don't meaningfully improve or support those around us, and certainly don't improve our own lives.?
1 Perhaps one issue is how we think about the meaning of yes and no. 
 2 The words "yes" and "no" get so often used in comparison with each other that it feels like they carry equal weight in conversation. 
 3 In reality, they're not just opposite in meaning, but of entirely different magnitudes in commitment. 
 4 When you say “no”, you're only saying "no" to one option. 5 When you say "yes", you're saying "no" to every other option. 6 I like how economist Tim Harford put it, “Every time we say 'yes' to a request, we're also saying 'no' to anything else we might accomplish with the time." 7 Once you're committed to something, you've already decided how that future block of time will be spent. 
 8 In other words, saying "no" saves you time in the future.? 9 Saying "yes" costs you time in the future.
 10 “No” is a form of time credit. 
 11 You retain the ability to spend your future time however you want.
 12 “Yes”is a form of time debt. 
 13 You have to pay back your commitment at some point.
1 “No”is a decision.
 2 “Yes”is a responsibility. 
 3 Saying "no" is sometimes seen as a luxury that only those in power can afford. 
 4 And it's true: turning down opportunities is easier when you can fall back on the safety net provided by power, money, and authority.
 5 But it's also true that saying "no" is not merely a privilege reserved for the successful.
 6 It's also a strategy that can help you become successful. 
 7 Saying “no” is an important skill to develop at any stage of your career because it retains the most important asset in life: your time. 
 8 As investor Pedro Sorrentino put it,“ If you don't guard your time, people will steal it from you."
 9 You need to say “no” to whatever isn't leading you toward your goals.?
1 Nobody embodied this idea better than Steve Jobs, who said," People think focus means saying ' yes ' to the thing you've got to focus on. 
 2 But that's not what it means at all. 
 3 It means saying 'no' to the hundred other good ideas that there are. 
 4 You have to pick carefully."
 5 Jobs had another great quote about saying "no": " I'm actually as proud of the things we haven't done as the things I have done.
 6 Innovation is saying 'no' to 1,000 things.”?
1 Over time, as you continue to improve and succeed, your strategy needs to change.
 2 The opportunity cost of your time increases as you become more successful. 
 3 At first, you just eliminate the obvious distractions and explore the rest. 
 4 As your skills improve and you learn to separate what works from what doesn't, you have to continually increase your threshold for saying "yes".
 5 You still need to say "no" to distractions, but you also need to learn to say "no" to opportunities that were previously good uses of time, so you can make space for better uses of time. 
 6 It's a good problem to have, but it can be a tough skill to master.?
1 What is true about health is also true about productivity: an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure. 
 2 More effort is wasted doing things that don't matter than is wasted doing things inefficiently. 
 3 And if that is the case, elimination is a more useful skill than optimization. 
 4 I'm reminded of the famous Peter Drucker quote, “ There is nothing so useless as doing efficiently that which should not be done at all."?

questions.explanation:
【题目翻译】

 People often grant a request just because they want to appear polite and helpful.

人们通常只因为想显得礼貌和乐于助人就答应了请求。


【定位及解析】

由题干中的request、polite和helpful定位到文章C）段①句。

定位句提出，我们答应的许多请求并不是因为我们想去做，而是我们不想被别人觉得自己没礼貌，或者不想帮助他人。

题干中的grant a request对应定位句中的say"yes"to many requests，题干中的polite and helpful对应原文中的don't…rude or unhelpful，故答案为C）。

【题目翻译】

It's no easy job learning to say "no" to opportunities that were once considered worth grasping.

对曾经被认为值得把握的机会说“不”并不是一件容易的事。


【定位及解析】

由题干中的no easy job和once considered worth grasping定位到H段⑤⑥句。

定位段最后两句提到，你仍然需要对分心的事情说“不”，但你也需要学会对以前曾认为是很好地利用时间的那些机会说“不”，这样你就可以腾出空间更好地利用时间。这是一个很好的问题，但它可能是一项很难掌握的技能。

题干中的say“no”to opportunitics that were once considered worth grasping对应原文中的say"no"to opportunities that were previously good uses of time，题干中的no casy job对应定位段最后一句中的tough，题干内容为定位段最后两句的总结归纳，故答案为H）。

【题目翻译】

When you decline a request, you are saving your future time. 

当你拒绝了一个请求，你是在节约未来的时间。


【定位及解析】

由题干中的decline a request和saving your future time定位到E）段⑧句。

定位句提到，说“不”可以节省你将来的时间。

题干中的saving your future time 对应文中的 saves you time in the future，题干中的decline a request对应定位句中的saying “no”，故答案为E）。

【题目翻译】

People sometimes struggle to do things that are simply a waste of time. 

人们有时会努力做一些纯粹是浪费时间的事情。


【定位及解析】

由题干中的struggle、to do things和a waste of time定位到B）段④句。

定位句提到，更糟糕的是人们偶尔会做一些浪费时间的事情。题干中的struggle对应定位句中的fight，题干中的a waste of time对应原文中的waste time。题干是对定位句的同义转述，故答案为B）。

【题目翻译】

Doing efficiently what is not worth doing is the most useless effort.

高效地做不值得做的事是最无用的努力。


【定位及解析】

由题干中的not worth doing和the most uscless effort定位到I）段④句。

定位句提到彼得·德鲁克的名言："没有什么比高效地做根本不应该做的事情更无用了。"题干中的not worth doing对应文中的doing...that which should not be done at all，题干���的the most useless effort对应文中的There is nothing so useless，故答案为I）。

【题目翻译】

It is especially difficult for people to decline to do what their superiors ask them to do.

对于人们来说，拒绝执行上级要求他们做的事情尤其困难。


【定位及解析】

由题干中的cspecially difficult、decline和superiors定位到C）段③句。

定位句提到，在工作中对上司说"不"可能尤其困难。题干中的 cspecially difficult对应原文中的particularly difficult，题干中的 decline to do what their superiors ask them to do对应原文中的Saying“no”to our superiors，故答案为C）。

【题目翻译】

 People agree to do too many things they are in fact unwilling to do.

人们同意做太多他们实际上不愿意做的事情。


【定位及解析】

由题干中的agree、in fact和unwilling定位到A）段最后一句。

定位句指出，事实是，我们对于太多实际上不想做的事情说"是"了。题干中的agree对应定位句中say"yes"，题干中的in fact unwilling to do对应原文中的don't actually want to do，题干为原文内容的归纳概括，故答案为A）。

【题目翻译】

According to one famous entrepreneur, innovation means refusal to do an enormous number of things.

根据一位著名企业家的说法，创新意味着拒绝做大量的事情。


【定位及解析】

由题干中的 innovation、refusal 和enormous定位到G）段⑥句。

定位句指出，创新就是对1000件事说“不”。

题干中的innovation means refusal to do an enormous number of things是对原文中“Innovation is saying‘no’to 1，000 things."的同义转述，故答案为G）。

【题目翻译】

It is an essential aspect of life to cooperate with other people.

与他人合作是生活的一个重要方面。


【定位及解析】

由题干中的essential aspect和cooperate 定位到D）段①句。

定位句指出，与他人合作是生活的重要组成部分。

题干中的essential aspect对应定位句中的important clement，题干中的cooperate对应原文中的Collaborating，故答案为D）。

【题目翻译】

Refusing a request is sometimes seen as a privilege not enjoyed by ordinary people.

拒绝请求有时被视为普通人不享有的特权。


【定位及解析】

由题干中的Refusing a request和privilege定位到F）段②句。

定位句指出，说“不”有时被视为只有当权者才能负担得起的奢侈品。

题干中的privilcge是对原文中luxury的同义转述，题干中not enjoyed by ordinary people是对原文中 only thosc in power can afford的同义转述，故答案为F）。

1 We're eating more fish than ever these days. 2 At around 20 kilograms per person global fish consumption is now more than twice what it was in the 1960s. 
 3 What's really remarkable, though, is where that fish comes from.
1 For the first time in human history, most of our aquatic （水产的） food now comes from farming rather than fishing.?
1 People ate around 73 million tonnes of farmed fish — just more than half of the volume of fish that humans consumed —— in 2014. 
 2 That's out of a total fish supply of 167 million tonnes; the remaining 20 million or so tonnes go into things like animal feed and medical products.
1 To keep eating fish at the current rate, we're definitely going to need to keep aquaculture （水产养殖） developing.?
1 Back in 1974, only 10% of marine fish stocks had been overfished. 
 2 That's because the volume of fish caught in the wild has leveled off since the 1990s.
 3 Now, more than three-tenths are. 
 4 Only a tenth of our oceans ' fish stocks could sustain heavier fishing than current levels.
1 But while catchings at sea have suffered, fish-farming has been growing at a fast rate. 
 2 A lot of that is coming from China, which produces 60% of the world 's farmed fish. 
 3 In fact, some 35 countries, including China, now produce more farmed than wild-caught fish.?
1 This shift toward aquaculture isn't just good for ensuring salmon （三文鱼） on your plate; it's also crucial to ensuring food security and sustainability. 
 2 By 2050, the world will need to feed an estimated 9.7 billion people.
 3 They'll have to get their protein somewhere. 
 4 However, raising cattle, pigs, and other land-based animals requires vast sums of grain and water.
 5 For example, pound for pound, beef requires 15 times more feed to raise than carp, a freshwater fish farmed all over Asia. 
 6 That grain — and the water needed to grow it — could be consumed by people instead.?
1 However, aquaculture is no silver bullet.
 2 In some southeast Asian countries, shrimp farming does disastrous damage to marine ecosystems. 
 3 Despite these problems, however, shrimp continues to be among the most popular sea foods worldwide.?

What does the author say is remarkable about the fish we eat?

作者认为我们吃的鱼有什么了不起的地方？

A) They reproduce quickly.

它们繁殖很快。

B) They are mostly farmed.

它们大多是养殖的。

C) They have become as important as grain.

它们变得和谷物一样重要。

D）They have a longer history than humans.

它们的历史比人类悠久，

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的remarkable about the fish we eat定位到1段最后一句和2段。

第一段最后一句提到，真正值得注意的是这些鱼的来源。第二段接着指出，我们大部分的水产食物来自养殖而非捕捞。由此可知，我们吃的大部分的鱼是养殖的，故答案为B）。


【错误选项分析】

文中没有提到鱼的繁殖速度、鱼的重要性和鱼的历史，故排除A）、C）和D）。

What do we need to do if we keep consuming fish at the current rate?

大幅增加捕捞量。

开发更先进的捕鱼技术。

有效扩大海洋鱼类种群。

不断扩大养鱼规模。

定位句提到，为了保证鱼肉摄入量一直处于现如今的水平，我们肯定需要让水产养殖业不断发展。通过推断可知，让水产养殖业不断发展的举措肯定包括扩大养殖规模，故答案为D）。

【错误选项分析】

7段中只提及了人类生存需要蛋白质，并没有提到动物，故排除B）。

文中没有提到水产养殖对于保持身心健康的影响，故排除C）。

文中也没有提及水产养殖确保了人类���食的平衡健殖的转变对于确保食品安全性和可持续性至关重要。

What does the author imply by saying aquaculture is no silver bullet?

养鱼是不可持续的。

养虾可能会变得相当昂贵。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 In 2020, the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the World Food Programme (WFP).
1 Why a Nobel Prize for the WFP, and why now?
 2 In 2019, the WFP assisted nearly 100 million people in 88 countries. 
 3 It is the safety net for those who fall off the edge of existence. 
 4 It is a response to solving the problem of food instability. 
 5 Its Nobel Prize reminds us all of the moral hazard in imagining that the poor and vulnerable are somebody else 's problem.?
1 The WFP has been around since 1961 and has been the global coordinator of nationally based efforts to avoid disasters with food aid. 
 2 Despite decades of effort to eliminate hunger, the latest estimate is that about 11% of people on the planet (about 820 million people) are suffering daily undernourishment. 
 3 Progress at reducing undernourishment has stopped despite gains through the 1990s and 2000s.?
1 Developed countries sometimes offer food and aid to developing ones, but at a price. 
 2 One American philosopher stated that addressing the needs of the poor and vulnerable is about more than money — it is mostly about creating conditions under which prosperity and opportunity can thrive. 
 3 When aid is offered with heavy conditions attached, like loan repayment or food for resources, it often widens the gap between rich and poor and sustains the old world order. 
 4 This is why the work of the WFP is so vital.?
1 The scientific community, however, can provide a helping hand to the WFP. 
 2 By sharing knowledge of agriculture and climate with peers in countries most vulnerable to poverty and hunger, scientists can help reduce these problems.? 3 By making its voice heard, science can lead by example. 
 4 The ability to overcome food shortages that must be built into some of the poorest countries will not come from loans from wealthy countries, which may have food problems of their own, or world economic institutions. 
 5 This ability will be built upon self-confident people using open and shared scientific knowledge to pull themselves out of their misery.?

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What does the WFP's winning of the Nobel Peace Prize make us realize?

世界粮食计划署获得诺贝尔和平奖使我们认识到什么？

A) More and more people in the world are suffering from starvation.

世界上越来越多的人正在挨饿。

B) All of us can be affected by food instability one way or another.

我们所有人都可能受到粮食不稳定的影响。

C) It is hazardous to leave millions of people poor and vulnerable.

让数百万人贫困和脆弱是危险的。

D) It is morally wrong to think helping the poor is not our business.

认为帮助穷人不是我们的事在道德上是错误的。

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的the WFP's winning of the Nobel Peace Prize定位到2段⑤句。

定位句指出，它的诺贝尔奖提醒我们所有人，把穷人和弱势群体当成别人的问题是一种道德危机。“它”指的是前文提到的世界粮食计划署，D）选项中的morally wrong对应定位句中的moral hazard。由此可知，答案为D）。


【错误选项分析】

3段②句提到，据最新估计，地球上约有11%的人（约82亿人）每天营养不良。并未提及是否有越来越多的人遭受饥饿之苦，故排除A）；

2段④句提到，世界粮食计划署是解决粮食不稳定问题的对策。并未提及粮食不稳定对所有人的影响，故排除B）；

2段⑤句指出，把穷人和弱势群体当成��人的问题是一种道德危机。并没有提及让数百万人处于贫困和弱势是危险的，故排除C）。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What do we learn about the WFP's effort to eliminate hunger?

我们从粮食计划署消除饥饿的努力中学到了什么？

A) It has ensured a sufficient food supply to millions.

它确保了数百万人的充足粮食供应。

B) It is still far from its goal despite the progress made.

尽管取得了进展，但距离其目标仍然很远。

C) It has done a good job in combating natural disasters.

它在抗击自然灾害方面做得很好。

D) It is preventing starvation occurring on a global scale.

它正在防止全球范围内发生饥荒。


【定位及答案】

由题干中的the WFP's effort to eliminate hunger定位到3段。

定位段提到，世界粮食计划署自1961年成立以来，一直是各国通过粮食援助避免灾难的全球协调机构。尽管为消除饥饿付出了几十年的努力，但据最新估计，地球上约有11%的人（约8.2亿人）每天营养不良。尽管在20世纪90年代和21世纪初取得了一些进展，但在减少营养不良方面的进展已经停止。由此推断可知，世界粮食计划署在消除饥饿上取得了一些进展，但距离目标还很远，故答案为B）。


【错误选项分析】

2段②句提到，2019年，世界粮食计划署援助了88个国家的近1亿人。并未提及是否提供了充足的食物，A）的表述太绝对，故排除；

3段①句提到，世界粮食计划署自1961年成立以来，一直是各国通过粮食援助避免灾难的全球协调机构。并未提及抗击自然灾害，也未提及阻止全球范围内饥荒的发生，故排除C）和D）。

【题目及选项概览】

What will happen when food aid is offered at a price?

如果以一定的价格提供粮食援助，会发生什么？

A) The rich will become richer and the poor poorer.

富人会变得更富，穷人会变得更穷。

B) More people will be willing to join in the effort.

将有更多的人愿意加入这项努力。

C) More food will be made available to the needy.

将向有需要的人提供更多的食物。

D) The relief effort will be rendered less sustainable.

救济工作将变得不可持续。

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的food aid is offered at a price定位到4段③句。

定位句指出，如果援助附带沉重的条件，如偿还贷款或以粮食换资源，这往往会扩大贫富差距，维持旧的世界秩序。由此可知，如果以一定代价提供粮食援助，会扩大贫富差距，即可能会导致富人变得更富，穷人变得更穷，故答案为A）。


【错误选项分析】

B）“会有更多的人愿意一起努力”、C）“会有更多的食物提供给有需要的人"和D）"救济工作将变得难以为继"三项在文中均未提及，故排除。

【题目及选项概览】

How can scientists help cope with poverty and hunger?

科学家如何帮助应对贫困和饥饿？

A) By collaborating closely with world economic institutions.

通过与世界经济机构密切合作。

B) By sharing expertise with peers in poverty-stricken nations.

通过与贫困国家的同行分享专业知识。

C) By setting up more food research programs in developing countries.

通过在发展中国家建立更多的食品研究项目。

D) By building self-respect in people suffering from under nutrition.

通过在营养不足的人群中建立自尊。

  

【定位及答案】

由题干中的scientists help cope with poverty and hunger定位到5段②句。

定位句提到，通过与最容易遭受贫困和饥饿的国家的同行分享农业和气候知识，科学家可以帮助减少这些问题。B）选项中的expertise是对定位句中knowledge of agriculture and climate的总结，由此可推断，科学家可以通过与贫困国家的同行分享专业知识来帮助解决贫困和饥饿问题，故答案为B）。


【错误选项分析】

5段④句提到，一些最贫穷的国家必须具备克服粮食短缺的能力，但这种能力不会来自世界经济机构的贷款。而且此处提到与世界经济机构合作的对象是贫穷的国家，并不是科学家，故排除A）；

文中未提及要在发展中国家建立更多的食品研究项目，故排除C）；

文中没有提到要在营养不良的人身上建立自尊，故排除D）。

【题目及选项概览】

What message does the author try to convey at the end of the passage？

作者在文章末尾试图传达什么信息？

A) Wealthy nations should solve their own food problems first.

富裕国家应该首先解决自己的粮食问题。

B) Rich countries should be more generous in providing food aid.

富国应该更慷慨地提供粮食援助。

C) Poor nations should enhance their own ability to solve their food shortages.

贫穷国家应该提高自身解决粮食短缺的能力

D) World economic institutions should play a bigger role in fighting hunger.

世界经济机构应在消除饥饿方面发挥更大作用。

  

【定位及答案】

由题干中的at the end of the passage定位到5段⑤句。

定位句指出，这种能力将建立在自信的人们利用开放和共享的科学知识使自己摆脱痛苦的基础上。结合前文可知，“这种能力"指的是最贫穷的国家必须具备克服粮食短缺的能力。由此推断可知，作者认为贫穷国家应该提高自己解决粮食短缺的能力，故答案为C）。


【错误选项分析】

文章5段倒数④句提到，富裕国家也可能存在粮食问题。但作者没有给出解决建议，故排除A）；

4段①句提到，发达国家有时会向发展中国家提供有偿的食物和援助。并未提及富裕国家应该更慷慨，故排除 B）；

文中并未提及世界经济机构应在对抗饥饿方面发挥作用，故排除D）。

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 The Winter Solstice is the day with the longest nighttime and the shortest daytime, marking the beginning of the coldest season of the year. 2 From this moment on, the temperature is getting lower and lower, and people gradually reduce their outdoor activities. 3 The farmers do not have much work in their fields. 4 They are mainly busy with the maintenance of the irrigation system and the prevention of freezing harm to crops to prepare for the spring sowing in the coming year. 5 The Chinese people have attached great importance to the Winter Solstice over the years. 6 Many places regard the Winter Solstice as a festival and celebrate it in different ways. 7 Northerners have the custom of eating dumplings on the winter solstice, while southerners have the tradition of eating tangyuan on the winter solstice.
