A police officer in the U.S. stopped a large SUV car that was going very slowly and drifting across lanes on a highway.
He expected to find a driver who was either very drunk or having a medical emergency.
Instead, the officer discovered a five year old boy sat on the edge of the driver’s seat.
His feet could barely reach the brake, and his head was only just high enough to see out of the windows.
The child had taken the keys to the family car while his teenage sister was napping.
He then drove three kilometers across town before getting on the highway.
The boy later told confused officers that he was planning to travel to California and buy a Lamborghini sports car.
Although he only had 3 dollar in his wallet, at least he was driving in the right direction.
Why did the police officer stop the SUV car?
What did the boy tell the police officers he was planning to do?
Mobile phones have changed the way we live, how we read, work, communicate, and shop.
But we already know this.
What we have not yet understood is the way the tiny machines in front of us are changing our skeletons, possibly altering not just the way we behave but even the very shape of our bodies.
New scientific research at the University of the Sunshine Coast in Queensland, Australia suggests that young people are developing extra pieces of bone at the backs of their heads.
These pieces of bone are caused by the way people bend their heads when they use the phone.
This shifts weight onto the muscles at the back of the head and causes the bone to grow in a way that is not normal.
This process can be compared to the way the skin hardens in response to constant rubbing or pressure.
The result is a piece of bone like a horn that sticks out from the head by the neck.
What does the report say we have not yet understood about mobile phones?
What happens to the skin when rubbed or pressed constantly?
A village is going to throw a birthday party for an orange cat named Wilbur, who has become famous for making a regular appearance at local shops.
Wilbur has his own internet pages as he approaches his 10th birthday on July 7.
Wilbur is both bold and friendly.
He spends most of his time in shops and businesses around the village.
He'll just take himself into any shop, anywhere.
There was one time when the doctor’s receptionist came back and he was sitting on her chair.
Among his favorite haunts are a local hairdresser, two pubs, and the Nottingham Primary School.
Leslie Harper, who runs one of the pubs, said the cat has been a big hit with their customers.
“He's been a regular visitor for most of this year,”she told the Press Association.
"He's a very relaxed cat, happy for customers and villagers young and old to come in and say hello.”
She also said he is a cat of expensive tastes, who likes his high priced cat food.
Sarah Godfrey, who is organizing Wilbur's party, told the local newspaper,“Wilbur is part of our lives, as he is for everyone who lives in the village.”
What does the report say the village is going to do for the cat Wilbur?
What do we learn from the report about the cat?
What does the pub owner, Leslie Harper, say about the cat?
So, where do you want to go for lunch?
I don't know.
Do you have anything in mind?
What about the sandwich place on Camden Street?
Um, no, sorry.
I don't feel like sandwiches today.
It's a great place, but I think we go there too often.
That's true.
Remember, that's where we saw Bridget Clark, the famous movie star.
Of course. How could l ever forget?
There were crowds of people around her, asking for a photo with her.
What about hamburgers, then?
There's that American style diner on the way to the mall.
I like that place.
Their chips are great, but their service takes a long time, and I need to get back by 2:30 for a conference call.
How about trying something new?
We could try Mario's, the new Italian restaurant on the corner.
It looks alright.
Have you been there?
No, I haven't, but I've noticed that it has great reviews on the internet.
It's supposed to be one of the best Italians in town.
I think Jeremy has been there and said it was amazing.
I'm up for that.
Cool. Have you asked Jeremy if he would like to come with us?
l already have.
He says he can't.
He has brought his own lunch today,so he will stay in.
I think his wife made him soup.
Poor Jeremy.
His wife is a terrible cook.
He should throw that soup in the bin and join us.
What are the speakers talking about in this conversation?
Where did the speakers see Bridget Clarke, the famous movie star?
Why does the woman say she needs to get back by 2:30?
Why does the woman say Jeremy should throw his soup in the bin?
Hi there, how are you today?
Do you have a reservation with us already?
Good afternoon.
Yes, we reserved our rooms yesterday morning on your website for three nights.
The name's Patterson.
Okay, let me have a look.
Yes,we have it here.
You brought the whole family with you, I see.
Yes, the two kids, my wife and l, and her parents too.
Great. So, we have a family room for you and your wife and the kids.
And another double room for your parents in law.
They are right next to each other on the ground floor, since you mentioned in your message that they have trouble with stairs.
That's wonderful.
My father in law has had terrible problems getting up and down stairs since his knee operation last April.
I'm sorry to hear that, and if you need any help to find transportation for the whole family, we can definitely recommend someone for you.
We were thinking of renting a car, but we will explore all the options available for sure.
So yes, that would be very helpful in comparing prices.
We're also wondering what tours and day trips are available.
We have bunches of brochures here.
I would recommend getting out on a boat trip.
The kids will love it, and there are so many islands nearby to explore.
There's also a great night market further into town that has all kinds of food and cool little shops selling souvenirs and local jewelry and clothing made by hand.
That all sounds marvelous.
Now, all I need is to photocopy your passports, and then I can get you all checked in and show you to your rooms.
Who is the man talking to in the conversation?
What do we learn about the man's father in law from the conversation?
Why does the man say they will explore all the options available?
What does the woman suggest the man and his family do close to the end of the conversation?
Artificial intelligence agents play ever more influential roles in our lives.
They do everything from suggesting new friends to recommending purchases.
They're even beginning to drive our cars.
Another role that they are expected to take over is negotiating on our behalf in commercial transactions or legal disputes.
So, it's important to know whether using an artificial intelligence agent might affect how we negotiate.
Research indicates that it does.
In a new study, participants were told to imagine that they were negotiating for something important to them, like a house.
Next, they were told either that they would negotiate for themselves, or they would program an artificial intelligence agent to negotiate for them.
Participants then completed a survey indicating how tough, deceptive, and pleasant or otherwise they wanted to be, or wanted their agent to be, in the negotiations.
For example, participants could choose to be tough by making an opening demand far greater than what they'd be willing to accept.
They could also choose to express sympathy with their opponent, to appear pleasant.
But they could also indicate that they, or their agent, would strategically express anger toward the opponent to gain advantage, or they could opt to convey dissatisfaction with the encounter so that the other party would think they were losing interest.
These are both examples of deceptive strategies.
Participants were more willing to employ deceptive strategies when assigned an agent to negotiate on their behalf.
What does the passage say about artificial intelligence agents?
What does the new study want to find out about using an artificial intelligence agent?
What did participants tend to do when assigned an Al agent to negotiate on their behalf?
New research has studied the effects of a seven-week healthy cooking course.
Academics measured the program’s effect on cooking confidence and self perceived mental health.
Researchers also measured participants' overall satisfaction around cooking and diet-related behaviors.
What were the findings?
Course participants saw significant improvements in general health.
They also reported improved mental health and subjective vitality immediately after the program.
These benefits remained six months after the completion of the course.
What caused these improvements?
Researchers have previously found a link between eating more fruits and vegetables and improved longer term mental health.
This would imply that the participants in the current study may have felt better due to improved diet.
However, the study showed participants’ mental health improved even if their reported diet did not change after completing the program.
Also, the mental health benefits were equal among participants who were overweight or obese and those in a healthy weight range.
This suggests a link between cooking confidence and satisfaction around cooking and mental health benefits.
Who benefits most from learning to cook?
Gender plays a part.
At the start of the program, 77 percent of female participants were confident about cooking, but just 23 percent of males were confident.
At the end of the program, cooking confidence and skills were equal across both counterparts.
This change in confidence could lead to a gender balance in home cooking.
This, in turn, could reduce consumption of unhealthy, high calorie processed meals.
What do we learn about the benefits the participants gained from the healthy cooking course?
What do the new research findings suggest about mental health benefits?
What plays a role in determining who benefits most from learning to cook?
What is personal space?
We often think of it as an invisible bubble of space surrounding us that others can't enter without causing discomfort.
Research shows, however, that we actually have bubbles of different sizes.
Each of these bubbles applies to a different set of people.
The smallest zone, called intimate space, extends outward from our bodies 18 inches in every direction.
Only family, pets and one's closest friends may enter it.
A mere acquaintance entering our intimate space makes us uncomfortable.
Next is the bubble called personal space, extending from 1.5 feet to 4 feet away.
Friends and acquaintances can comfortably occupy this zone, especially during informal conversations, but strangers are forbidden.
Extending from 4 to 12 feet away from us is social space.
Here, people feel comfortable conducting routine social interactions with new acquaintances or total strangers.
Those are the average sizes of Americans',personal bubbles, anyway.
It is important to keep in mind that personal space varies depending on culture and context.
Furthermore, there are significant individual differences.
As we all know, cultural or individual differences in personal bubble diameters are all too often the cause of discomfort.
How did these personal bubbles arise?
According to research, we begin to develop our individual sense of personal space around age 3 or 4.
The sizes of our bubbles are fixed by our teens.
These bubbles are constructed and monitored by the brain region involved in fear.
What does research show about our personal space?
What happens if a mere acquaintance enters our intimate space?
Where do people feel comfortable interacting with new acquaintances or strangers?
When are the sizes of our bubbles fixed?

So yes, that would be very helpful in comparing prices.”“我们曾考虑租一辆车，但我们肯定要研究下所有的选项。所以，是的，这将有助于价格的比较。”选项D中的compare prices与录音内容一致。故选项D为正确答案。

questions.explanation: 【题目】What does the new study want to find out about using an artificial intelligence agent?关于使用人工智能代理，这项新研究想要发现什么?【选项预读】四个选项都以whether it+情态动词开头，意为“它是否……”,可知本题设问方向为对文章中提到的某个对象的某方面情况的验证。【解析】录音中提到“Another role that they are expected to take over is negotiating on our behalf in commercial transactions or legal disputes”和“So, it's important to know whether using an artificial intelligence agent might affect how we negotiate”,它们有望接管的另一个角色是在商业交易或法律纠纷中代表我们进行谈判。因此，了解使用人工智能代理是否会影响我们的谈判方式非常重要。选项A中的have any effect on the way we negotiate与录音中的affect how we negotiate对应，都表示影响我们的谈判方式。故选项A为正确答案。

【题目】What plays a role in determining who benefits most from learning to cook?什么因素决定了谁从学习烹饪中获益最多?【选项预读】四个选项均为名词，可知本题设问对象为文章中的某个关键因素。【解析】录音中提到“This suggests a link between cooking confidence and satisfaction around cooking and mental health benefits. Who benefits most from learning to cook? Gender plays a part”,这表明，对烹饪的信心和满意度与对心理健康的益处之间存在联系。谁从学习烹饪中获益最大?性别有很大影响。虽然选项BC都与录音相同，但是二者在录音中为并列关系，不能作为答案。选项A与录音内容相同，是文中“Who benefits most from learning to cook?”的答案。题干中的plays a role与录音中的plays a part对应，都意为“发挥作用”。故选项A为正确答案。

【题目】What does research show about our personal space?关于我们的个人空间，研究表明了什么?【选项预读】四个选项都以代词it开头，后续成分各不相同，可知本题设问方向为文章中提到的某个概念的具体描述。【解析】录音中提到“Research shows, however, that we actually have bubbles of different sizes”,然而研究表明，我们实际上有不同大小的气泡。选项D中的varies in size与录音中的different sizes对应，都意为“大小不同”。故选项D为正确答案。

sections.title: Section A 选词填空
sections.passage:
1 Exercising for just 10 minutes a week is linked to a longer life, according to a new study published in The British Journal of Sports Medicine.
1 Several recent studies have found that even low-intensity exercise, done for a short amount of time, can have a meaningful 1 on health.? 2 Still, the idea that exercising for just 10 minutes a week may be enough to increase your lifespan is novel. 3 It's also somewhat 2, since the federal physical activity guidelines recommend getting at least 75 minutes of vigorous exercise or 150 minutes of 3 exercise each week.?
1 The study was based on data from more than 88, 000 U. S. adults who 4 in the National Health Interview Survey between 1997 and 2008.?
1 Contrary to some research that has found an 5 limit to the amount of exercise that is healthy, there searchers found that there was 6 no limit to the longevity (长寿) benefits of exercise.? 2 Even the small group of people who got 10 times the amount of exercise recommended by the federal government had a 46% lower 7 of death than the least active group.?
1 Still, observational studies like this one cannot prove cause and effect; they can only find 8.? 2 There searchers also were not able to 9 for certain lifestyle factors that could affect lifespan, including dietary habits and changes in physical activity over time.? 3 Despite these 10, the study's results are yet another indication of the power of physical activity, even in small amounts.?

questions.explanation:
【考点】名词辨析

【解析】空格前是冠词加形容词a meaningful,因此空格处应填名词。该句表示，最近的几项研究发现，即使是短时间的低强度运动，也可以对健康产生重大______。结合选项，表示“影响”的词符合题意。故选项F)impact为正确答案。

【考点】形容词辨析

【解析】���格句为主系表结构，且空格前是副词somewhat,因此空格处应填形容词。前一句意为“尽管如此，每周锻炼10分钟就足以延长寿命的观点还是很新颖的”。空格句句意发生转折，大意为“这也存在一些_____,因为联邦体育活动指南建议每周至少进行75分钟的剧烈运动或150分钟的适度运动”。结合选项，表示“有争议的”的词符合题意。故选项D)controversial为正确答案。

【考点】形容词辨析

【解析】空格后是名词exercise,因此空格处应填形容词或名词。空格句的大意为“这也存在一些争议，因为联邦体育活动指南建议每周至少进行75分钟的剧烈运动或150分钟的___运动”。结合选项，表示“适度的”的词符合题意。故选项H)moderate为正确答案。

【考点】动词辨析

【解析】空格所处的从句缺谓语动词，因此空格处应填动词。空格句的大意为“该研究基于1997年至2008年间_______全国健康访谈调查的88,000多名美国成年人的数据”。结合选项，表示“参加、参与”的词符合题意，也能与in搭配。故选项l)participated为正确答案。

【考点】形容词辨析

【解析】空格后是名词limit,因此空格处应填形容词或名词。空格句的大意为“一些研究发现，健康运动量有_____限；但是，这项研究的工作人员发现，锻炼对长寿的益处似乎是无限的”。结合选项，表示“上边的”的词符合题意。故选项O)upper为正确答案。

【考点】副词辨析

【解析】句子不缺成分，因此空格处应填副词。空格句的大意为“一些研究发现，健康运动量有上限；但是，这项研究的工作人员发现，锻炼对长寿的益处_____是无限的”。结合选项，表示“似乎、看似”的词符合题意。故选项M)seemingly为正确答案。

【考点】名词辨析

【解析】空格前是冠词加形容词a 46% lower,因此空格处应填名词。空格句的大意为“即使是运动量达到联邦政府所建议10倍的一小群人，其死亡_____也比最不活跃的群体低46%”。结合选项，表示“危险、风险”的词符合题意。故选项L)risk为正确答案。

【考点】名词辨析

【解析】空格前是动词find,后缺宾语，因此空格处应填名词。空格句的大意为“然而，像这样的观察研究无法证明因果关系；它们只能找到_____”。结合选项，表示“模式”的词符合题意。故选项J)patterns为正确答案。

【考点】动词辨析

【解析】空格前是be able to,因此空格处应填动词原形。空格句的大意为“研究人员也无法_____某些可能影响寿命的生活方式因素，包括饮食习惯和随时间变化的体育活动”。结合选项，表示“调整、适应”的词符合题意。故选项A)adjust为正确答案。

【考点】名词辨析

【解析】空格前是代词these,因此空格处应填名词。空格句的大意为“尽管存在这些______,该研究的结果还是再次表明了体育活动的力量，即使是少量的体育活动”。结合选项，表示“限制、局限”的词符合题意。故选项G)limitations为正确答案。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Earlier this year, scientists warned that one in six animal species could go extinct (灭绝的) due to climate change. 2 Could the same thing happen to our crops and other foodstuffs too??
1 It's clear that farmers in many parts of the world are going to find things harder in the coming decades. 2 Last week, BBC Future explored one scientist's efforts to help crops cope with the increased probability of droughts. 3 By using the genes from resurrection (复活) plants, Jill Farrant of the University of Cape Town is exploring whether she can design crops to survive for much longer periods without water.?
1 But if we can't find ways to protect other foods, will they survive climate change? 2 Fortunately, there is some good news on this front. 3 Despite alarmist headlines about “foods that are going extinct,” there is no evidence that major food types like beans, chocolate, wine, corn or wheat will cease to exist.
1 But that doesn't mean it's all good news for future food. 2 We will probably have to change where we grow certain crops, as some regions get too hot. 3 The disadvantage, obviously, is that local farmers will suffer under this situation. 4 And some people may struggle to get the same access to certain foods. 5 “Even if overall food production may be unaffected, food security can still be impacted," says Margaret Walsh, a scientist at the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Climate Change Program Office. 6 In other words, even if a certain food is still grown on some corner of the Earth, it doesn't mean that everyone will continue to have the same degree of access as today.?
1 Overall, the yields of many foods, from staples to life-enhancing extras such as coffee and chocolate, will likely be impacted by climate change too. 2 How those decreases will be felt will depend on the degree of warming and the crop in question, but in general, "anything over about 30℃ is very bad for crops," says Wolfram Schlenker, an associate professor of international and public affairs at Columbia University. 3 For example, statistical studies that he and a colleague built of corn and soybean (大豆) production in the U.S. show a steep decline after crossing the 30℃ temperature threshold (临界点).
1 In the U.S. — the world's largest producer of corn and soybeans — farms can move north to some degree, Schlenker says. 2 But eventually, yields will likely suffer because the soil north of lowa declines in quality — a legacy of glacial (冰川的) expansion.? 3 Other studies, including studies of wheat in India and corn in Africa, also found that there is a threshold above which yields sharply decline: crops can adapt and move, but only to a point. 4 “What's common to all studies is the finding that extreme heat is damaging to crop growth, although exact cutoffs vary by crop," Schlenker says. 5 "If predictions for the end of the century are true, though, I think a lot of agricultural areas in the U.S. will see significant hits."
1 Under current conditions, about 4% of the world's croplands experience drought in any given year, but by the end of the century those conditions are forecasted to jump to about 18% per year. 2 Some studies indicate that horticulture crops — generally, everything besides staples — may be impacted most severely, largely because they tend to be confined to a smaller geographic area. 3 Researcher Andrew Jarvis and his colleagues found that 80% of coffee-growing zones in Central America and Brazil could become unsuitable by 2050, for example, while climate change will likely have “great impacts” on cocoa (可可粉) production in West Africa. 4 “High quality chocolate will be less available in the future, and if you want it, you'll have to pay a lot more for it,” Jarvis says.?
1 This means that, for those who can afford it, some foods will simply cost them more in the future. 2 But for poorer people, those same price jumps will likely cause certain foods to go extinct from their diets.? 3 “The more you reduce, the shorter the supply, and the higher the price will jump," Schlenker says.
1 Another potential climate change-induced problem is our dependence on commodity crops — wheat, soybeans, corn and rice — which currently provide humanity with 75% of its calories, either directly or indirectly through the animals we raise on those crops. 2 Jarvis and his colleagues also found that, over the past five decades, the world has seen an increasing standardisation of diets; the foods we eat globally today are 36% more similar than they were in 1961.? 3 While this can be good news for the world's poorest people who now consume more calories, protein and fat than in the past, homogeneity (同一性) and over-dependence on a handful of staples leaves us vulnerable to threats such as drought, disease and pests — all of which are predicted to worsen in many parts of the world as a result of climate change.
1 There are ways we could soften the coming blow to the global food supply, however. 2 Like Farrant's work with resurrection crops, a number of companies, organisations and researchers are aiming to create drought - and temperature-resistant crops through genetic engineering and conventional breeding. 3 For now, the jury is still out as to how successful those endeavours will be.? 4 “The people at Monsanto who I've talked to are much more optimistic that they'll be able to engineer heat-tolerant crops,” Schlenker says. 5 “On the other hand, scientists at the USDA who I've spoken with are much more cautious.”
1 Until genetic engineering comes to fruition, other strategies might also help in some places, including applying more fertiliser, implementing better irrigation, using machinery that gets crops out of the field faster or installing storage facilities to delay spoilage. 2 “Many places could benefit a great deal just by using technologies that already exist," Walsh says. 3 "General farm management can go a long way toward easing changes."?
1 Finally, diversifying our diet away from heat-sensitive wheat, corn, rice and other crops could also help.? 2 “We've seen profound changes in the last decades in what we eat largely as a result of international trade, and I think that trend toward more diversification will continue," Jarvis says. 3 “Depending on a greater number of plant species creates a more vigorous and less risky food system — and one that provides a broader range of nutritional requirements.”

1 One of my bad habits is saying "busy" when people ask me how I'm doing. 2 Sometimes it's because I actually am busy, but other times it's because that's what I think I'm supposed to say. 3 That's what important people say.? 4 That's what people who get promoted say. 5 But working long hours doesn't drive better results. 6 Never taking a vacation won't lead to a promotion. 7 So why are we so proud to talk about how busy we are all the time?
1 In 2016, researchers from Columbia, Harvard, and Georgetown conducted a study to figure it out. 2 They found busy people are perceived to be of high status, and interestingly, these status attributions are heavily influenced by our own beliefs about social mobility.? 3 In other words, the more we believe that one has the opportunity for success based on hard work, the more we tend to think that people who skip leisure and work all the time are of higher standing. 4 That's why we feel like we have to appear busy, and there's a real perception that if someone is knee-deep in meetings, emails and stress, then they're probably a big deal. 5 This culture of busyness is making it hard for employees to find work-life balance.? 6 According to a recent study, one in five highly engaged employees are at risk of burnout (精疲力竭).
1 Personally, I'm going to stop saying “busy” when people ask me how I am. 2 It sounds self-righteous (自以为是的) and sets the wrong tone. 3 Phrases like “ I have limited access to email ” and “ I'll respond as soon as I get back ”sound like you're being held against your will from working as opposed to making the most of your time off.?
1 That's why we recently launched the Out of Office Email Generator, a free tool you can use before your next long weekend or trip. 2 You can share loud and proud that you won't be checking email until you're back.? 3 Managers need to think twice about emailing their teams on the weekend and talking about how busy they are. 4 Leaders should take time off themselves and encourage employees to do the same.

1 Female employees consistently pay lower airfares than men do for the same flights because they tend to book earlier.
1 We compared the airfare paid by employees in the same position within a company for the same class of travel and used a common statistical technique to account for other factors that might affect differences in airfares.? 2 We found that women paid on average $18 less per ticket than their male colleagues. 3 Further investigation allowed us to conclude that this gap is largely explained by the fact that women tended to book earlier than men, 1.8 days on average.
1 We wanted to determine what was causing these gender differences in booking business trips so we tested a variety of possible explanations, such as women choosing to plan ahead or male frequent travelers being inclined to book late.? 2 None of these explained away the gender gap, so we applied data collected from surveys that express consumer preferences that play a central role in economic decisions, such as patience and risk avoidance.
1 We found that only the concept of “negative reciprocity” — in which an employee who feels unfairly treated engages in negative behaviors, such as spending their company ’s money less carefully — explains these differences. 2 The surveys showed men tend to exhibit more of these negative behaviors than women. 3 This isn’t to say that all men engage in these behaviors — or that booking relatively late is a sign of abnormal behavior. 4 It only means that the gender gap disappears when we plug in the negative reciprocity variable.?
1 Prior research on negative reciprocity among workers found that it can result in lower employee motivation, business performance and workplace morale (士气) and culture.?
1 Our results show another way these negative behaviors can manifest themselves, like in airline bookings, and add to evidence that women are less likely to engage in them.
1 Companies spend significant sums of money on business travel. 2 While that $18 difference per ticket may seem small, it adds up. 3 Our analysis suggests early booking by women can translate into savings of $1 million a year for a large multinational company with 20,000 regular travelers.?

Have you noticed how similar you are to your friends?
It may be because your brains operate in harmony with each other.
We know that friends are more likely to be the same age, gender, and ethnic background as each other Now it seems their brains are alike, too.
Researchers at the University of California scanned 42 classmates while they watched videos intended to provoke varying responses.
Some people might find a romantic scene touching, for instance, while others would feel it was embarrassing.
The activity of friends brains was more similar than that of people who didn't know each other, particularly in regions involved in attention, emotion, and language.
This similarity was strong enough that it could be used to predict whether two people were already friends or not .
The relationship probably goes two ways.
We are drawn to people who think like us.
We then influence their thoughts over time, which may push their brain activity into more closely resembling our own.
What may be the reason that friends are similar to each other, according to the recent research?
What does the news report say about the relationship between friends?
Two men who have been best friends for 60 years have just realized they are actually brothers.
It's reported that Alan Robinson and Walter McDonald met in the 6th grade at a school in Hawaii.
They have been best friends ever since.
Alan was given away for adoption soon after he was born, and Walter never knew his father.
So recently, they made separate attempts on DNA matching websites to discover more about their ancestry.
Walter was astonished to find that he matched with website user Robbie737.
He knew immediately that this was his best friend, Alan, whose friends call him Robbie, and flew 737 airplanes when he was a pilot.
The pair were born to the same mother 15 months apart.
What did both Alan Robinson and Walter McDonald attempt to do on DNA matching websites?

It's a really powerful finding, said Patricia Pendry, who led the study.
Universities are doing a lot of great work trying to help students succeed academically, especially those who may be at risk due to a history of mental health issues or academic and learning issues.
This study shows that traditional stress management approaches aren't as effective for this population compare with programs that focus on providing opportunities to interact with therapy dogs.
The researchers measured executive functioning in the students involved in the study.
Executive function is a term for the skills one needs to plan, organize, motivate, concentrate, and memorize.
These are skills students need to succeed in college.
The research has found that students who were most at risk had the most improvements in executive functioning after interacting with therapy dogs.
These results remained when researchers followed up six weeks later.
Many universities provide academic stress management programs and workshops.
These are traditionally very similar to college classes.
They often talk about ways to get more sleep, set goals, or manage stress or anxiety.
Pendry acknowledges that these are really important topics and these workshops help typical students succeed.
But they're less helpful for struggling students.
Pendry believes those students may experience the programs as another lecture and feel even more stressed.
What does the recent study led by Patricia Pendry aim to examine?
What did the new study measure in the participants?
What does Patricia Pendry think traditional management programs may do?
Taking risks in business does not mean going into business blindly and then expecting great results.
On the contrary, taking risks in entrepreneurship involves careful planning and hard work.
Nobody can really be sure if risks will be met with success, no matter how calculated they maybe.
But this should not stop you from taking risks, as risks are necessary if you want your business to succeed.
Some risks may not work out, but an optimistic risk taker will always look at failure as an opportunity to learn.
The willingness to experiment with new ideas is key to business growth.
As the old saying goes, nothing ventured nothing gained.
Failure will teach you how to think and plan strategically.
But just remember that not all risks are good ones, and when you fail, learn from it and move forward.
Since most people tend to avoid risk, businesses that are brave enough to take risks already have a competitive advantage.
They are the ones setting the standard with new ideas, fresh offers and Bold inventions.
Risk takers are best at adapting in difficult times.
Simply put, when most individuals stay away from risk, it means less competition for risk takers.
We don't know if you'll achieve what these risk takers have achieved, but for as long as you want to stay safe, and for as long as you are content with where your business is right now, you will never find out.

choices.text: Learn from our failure and forge ahead.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Distinguish between good and bad risks.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Examine our strategies and find out weaknesses.

questions.explanation: 【题目】What are we advised to do when we fail?当我们失败时，我们应该做什么?【选项预读】四个选项均以动词原形开头，动词及宾语各不相同，可知本题的设问方向为对文章中某个建议的具体描述。【解析】录音中提到“But just remember that not all risks are good ones, and when you fail, learn from it and move forward”,译为“但要记住，并非所有的风险都是好的，当你失败时，要从中吸取教训并继续前进”。选项B中的learn from our failure与录音相同， forge ahead是录音中move forward的同义改写，故选项B为正确答案。

【题目】What does it mean to risk taking businesses when most people tend to avoid risk? 当大多数人都倾向于规避风险时，承担风险的企业意味着什么?【选项预读】四个选项均为名词短语，且定语均为形容词比较级，可知本题设问方向为对某个具体概念的描述，解题时还要结合其定语。【解析】录音中提到“Simply put, when most individuals stay away from risk, it means less competition for risk takers.” “简而言之，大多数人都对风险退避三舍，这意味着冒险者的竞争减少了”。选项D属于录音中的要素，故选项D为正确答案。

1 First of all, Several new parks have been established, providing residents with tranquil spaces to relax. 【改变1：公园建设】 2 In addition, a state-of-the-art library has replaced an old warehouse, becoming a sanctuary for those in pursuit of knowledge. 【改变2：图书馆升级】 3 What's more, the transportation system has also been upgraded, with the introduction of new bus routes that have made commuting smoother for residents. 【改变3：交通系统改善】 4 Local markets are now brimming with a variety of fresh produce, reflecting the agricultural advancements in the surrounding regions. 【改变4：本地市场繁荣】
1 These developments have not only improved the local inhabitants' quality of life but have also drawn numerous tourists, contributing to the economic and communal vibrancy. 【总结：提出这些改变的综合影响】 2 As this vitality continues, my hometown is becoming increasingly attractive as a wonderful place to live and work. 【结尾：故乡的活力发展持续】

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 Since the reform and opening-up, the Chinese people's diet has undergone significant changes. 2 In the past, due to economic backwardness, there were limited types and insufficient quantities of food, and people were only satisfied with being full. 3 Nowadays, with the rapid development of the Chinese economy, food has become more abundant and diverse, and its quality has greatly improved. 4 As the living standards continue to rise, people's demands for diet are increasing, and they pay more attention to eating nutritiously and healthily. 5 Therefore, the low-fat, low-sugar, and organic foods introduced in the market are widely welcomed by people.

questions.stem: ①改革开放以来，中国人的饮食发生了显著变化。②过去由于经济落后，食品种类有限、数量不足，人们仅仅满足于吃得饱。③如今中国经济快速发展，食品不仅更加丰富多样，质量也大幅提高。④随着生活水平不断提升，人们对饮食的要求越来越高，更加注重吃得营养健康。⑤因此，目前市场上推出的低脂、低糖、有机食品受到人们的普遍欢迎。
questions.answer: 1 Since the reform and opening-up, the Chinese people's diet has undergone significant changes. 2 In the past, due to economic backwardness, there were limited types and insufficient quantities of food, and people were only satisfied with being full. 3 Nowadays, with the rapid development of the Chinese economy, food has become more abundant and diverse, and its quality has greatly improved. 4 As the living standards continue to rise, people's demands for diet are increasing, and they pay more attention to eating nutritiously and healthily. 5 Therefore, the low-fat, low-sugar, and organic foods introduced in the market are widely welcomed by people.

sections.title: Section A 选词填空
sections.passage:
1 A number of studies have looked at how family life can affect productivity and satisfaction in the workplace. 2 However, there has been 1 little research on the influence of leisure activities.? 3 So Ciara Kelly and colleagues recruited 129 hobbyists to look at how the time spent on their hobbies 2 their work life.?
1 The researchers found that when participants spent longer than 3 on their leisure activity, their belief in their ability to perform their job was strengthened.? 2 But this was only the 4 when they had a serious hobby that was dissimilar to their job, or when their hobby was similar to their work but they only did it 5.? 3 When their hobby was both serious and similar to their job, then spending more time on it actually decreased their work 6.?
1 Why might that be? 2 To maintain a serious hobby, people need to invest significant psychological resources, say the authors — so if the activity has the same kinds of demands as their work, they may be left 7 and unable to perform well at their job.? 3 But if their hobby is quite different from their career, it may not 8 in the same way but instead help them develop other knowledge and skills that can 9 their confidence at work.? 4 “ Consider a scientist who is a keen rock climber, " says Kelly. 5 Since climbing is so far 10 from their day-to-day work activities, they can still recover from the demands of their job with plenty of resources.?

questions.explanation:
【考点】 副词辨析

【解析】句子不缺成分，且空格后是形容词little,因此空格处应填副词。前一句意为“许多研究都着眼于家庭生活如何影响对工作的生产力和满意度”。空格句和前一句用 However 连接，可见两句意思相反，空格句的大意为“但是__ , 关于休闲活动影响的研究却很少”。由句意可知，此处是想通过转折，形成前后对比，结合选项，表示“惊人地，出人意料地”的词符合题意。故选项 O)surprisingly 为正确答案。

【考点】 动词辨析

【解析】空格前是how 引导的从句的主语 the time spent on their hobbies,空格后是该从句的宾语 their work life,因此空格处应填动词作谓语。空格句的大意为“因此，西娅拉·凯莉和同事招募了129名业余爱好者，研究他们花在业余爱好上的时间如何_____他们的工作”。结合选项，表示“塑造、影响”的词符合题意。故选项 N) shaped 为正确答案。

【考点】 名词辨析

【解析】空格前是形容词的比较级，than 后应为比较对象，因此空格处应填名词。空格句的大意为“研究人员发现，当参与者花比____更长的时间进行休闲活动时，他们对自己完成工作能力的信心就会增强”。结合选项，表示“常态，一般情况”的词符合题意。故选项I)normal 为正确答案。

【考点】 名词辨析

【解析】空格前是定冠词 the, 因此空格处应填名词。空格句的大意为“但只有当他们有一个与工作不同的重度 爱好时……,才会出现这种_____”。结合选项，表示“情况，事实”的词符合题意。故选项 B)case 为正确答案。

【考点】副词辨析

【解析】句子不缺成分，且空格前为动词短语 did it, 因此空格处应填副词。空格句的大意为“但只有当他们有一个与工作不同的重度爱好时，或者当他们的爱好与工作相似，但他们只是____对待这件事情时，才会出现这种_____”。结合选项，表示“随意地，偶然地”的词符合题意。故选项C)casually 为正确答案。
【解析】空格前有代词 their, 其后整体结构应为名词结构，因此空格处应填名词。空格句的大意为“当他们对爱好十分上心而它又与工作相似时，花更多的时间在上面实际上会产生有害的影响，降低他们的工作______”。 结合选项，表示“效率，效能”的词符合题意。故选项 D)efficiency 为正确答案。

【考点】形容词辨析

【解析】空格前是动词left,后面是连词and, 因此空格处应填形容词,并和 and 后面的 unable 并列。空格句的大意为“作者说，为了保持一种重度的爱好，人们需要投入大量的心理资源，因此，如果这项活动与他们的工作具有相同的要求，他们可能会____ ,无法在工作中表现出色”。空格处应填一个具有负面含义的形容词，结合选项，表示“筋疲力尽的”的词符合题意。故选项 F)exhausted 为正确答案。

【考点】动词辨析

【解析】空格前是情态动词 may not, 因此空格处应填动词原形，构成短语____in。 空格句的大意为“但如果他们的爱好与他们的职业有很大不同，爱好可能不会以同样的方式____生活，而是帮助他们发展其他知识和技能……”结合选项，表示“干涉，介入”的词符合题意，这项H词义符合，且能与in 搭配。故选项H) interfere 为正确答案。

【考点】动词辨析

【解析】空格前是情态动词can, 因此空格处应填动词原形。空格句的大意为“但如果他们的爱好与他们的职业有很大不同，爱好可能不会以同样的方式干涉生活，而是帮助他们发展其他知识和技能，从而____他们的工作信心”。结合选项，表示“提高，增加”的词符合题意。故选项A)boost 为正确答案。

【考点】 动词辨析

【解析】空格所处的短语为is_____from, 因此空格处应填动词或形容词。空格句的大意为“由于攀岩与他们的日常工作活动 ,他们仍然可以通过充足的资源从工作的需求中恢复过来”。结合选项，表示“远离的”的词符合题意。故选项L)removed  为正确答案。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Attitudes towards paternity leave (陪产假) have drastically changed in America in the last five years as more fathers feel comfortable taking extended time off, but gender bias persists when it comes to career prospects and the home, according to a new study of working parents.
1 Research by the Boston College Center for Work & Family, which surveyed new parents at four large U.S. companies who were qualified for taking at least six weeks paid parental leave, found that 81% of the 1,240 employees surveyed said the notion of fathers taking leave has become more acceptable.?
1 Of those surveyed, 62% of fathers took the maximum amount of time off compared to 93% of mothers, and around three-quarters of workers said their employer was equally supportive of mothers and fathers taking parental leave and over half said leave policies had made workplace culture better.?
1 The U.S. is one of only three countries in the world not to offer statutory (法定的) paid leave, but increasingly states and companies are starting to take up the issue. 2 So far, eight states and the District of Columbia have their own paid family leave laws.?
1 Brad Harrington, executive director of the center and lead author of the study, estimates only 20% to 30% of companies in the U.S. offer paid parental leave.? 2 He feels the research findings reflect an obvious change in corporate attitudes to new fathers taking time off.
1 “We did a study on paternity leave five years ago. 2 Compared with those findings, these numbers were shocking to me. 3 I did not expect 80% of people to say the organisation finds dads taking this leave acceptable and three-quarters to say it's equally supportive of women and men taking leave," Harrington said.?
1 The previous study found that nearly three-quarters of fathers saw two to four weeks as an appropriate duration for paternity leave and 76% said they would prefer not to take all their time off at once.
1 Since then, there have been a number of legal cases against companies involving paternity leave — including cases against JPMorgan Chase and Estée Lauder — which have helped put pressure on companies to make their parental leave policies gender neutral.?
1 However, the study also shows how traditional gender roles endure both at work, where more women than men reported changes in their perceived career potential, and at home — even among workers who claim to have a strong desire for equality.?
1 The vast majority of men, 97%, said one of the top reasons to take leave was to share caregiving with their partner. 2 But when they were asked about how caregiving and household tasks were divided, their answers painted a different picture. 3 While about 75% of employees said both genders should give the same amount of care, the majority of men and nearly half of women admitted that in reality the female actually did most of it.? 4 A tiny fraction, 2%, of men said they did more of the childcare.
1 Men and women's experiences of the return to work following parental leave were also considerably different. 2 Of the women surveyed, 32% reported a downturn in their job satisfaction, while 14% said it increased. 3 In comparison, 17% of men said their job satisfaction went down and 20% said it went up. 4 Meanwhile, more women reported an increase in their responsibilities and manager expectations after childbirth. 5 Half of the women said they used flexible work arrangements after becoming a parent, while just 27% of men did. 6 Similar percentages of men and women said they enjoyed their careers and that it gave them a sense of achievement, while around half of women and 44% of men said it was a key part of their identity.
1 On the subject of career advancement, 59% of women and 49% of men said leave could be limiting and both genders said they feared it would have an impact on their progress long-term. 2 But on opportunity for promotion, more than double the number of women, 30% compared with 15% of men, believed their chances to be lower after becoming a parent. 3 Despite progress, the struggle for women to reach the highest positions of power is demonstrated in this year's Fortune 500 list, which featured a record 33 female CEOs, but this still represents a tiny fraction of the total.?
1 Harrington said culture change depends on companies putting more focus on men and their responsibilities. 2 “By that I mean companies need to give men paternity leave and encourage men to take time off to be with their kids early on in the kids' life. 3 They also need to recognise that men have to make significant adjustments when they become parents. 4 Companies cannot do all these things to enhance women's advancement and then turn around and say, 'Oh,but we don't expect the men to take over for the women at home.’”
1 In May, the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and Outten&Golden LLP announced a historic class —— action $5m settlement with JPMorgan Chase on behalf of male employees who claim they were illegally denied access to paid parental leave. 2 Derek Rotondo, 35, filed the discrimination charge against his company after he was allegedly told by his HR department that mothers were considered primary caregivers. 3 Thus，they were allowed to take 16 weeks of paid parental leave. 4 Fathers, however, could take just two weeks.
1 The father of two from Columbus, Ohio, who still works at the company as an associate and investigator, said he has witnessed a “domino effect (多米诺效应)” across companies since the settlement, but that there is still substantial progress to be made towards changing attitudes towards paternity leave.
1 “I do think there's still some way to go … there's still going to be sort of the unstated expectation for new dads to essentially come right back to work, but I think the research is showing that's starting to change.” 2 He said equal parental leave is an essential component to creating gender equality in the workplace.? 3 “The old standard of women staying home, having babies and cooking doesn't apply and hasn't applied for a long time." 4 May the totals be large and getting larger.

questions.explanation: 根据题干中的关键词 states in the U.S.和 paid family leave 定位至选项 D。定位句提到，美国不提供法定带薪假期，但越来越多的州已经通过了带薪探亲假的法律。题干是对定位句的概括总结。题干中的 the absence of Federal legislation 在语义上对应选项中的The U.S.is one of only three countries in the world not to offer statutory paid leave; states 对应选项中的 states; have passed laws concerning paid family leave 对应选项 中的 have their own paid family leave laws。故选项 D 为正确答案。

根据题干中的关键词 did less childcare 定位至选项J的第三句。定位句提到，大多数男性都承认，实际上，大多数照顾孩子的事情都是由女性承担的。题干是对定位句的同义替换。题干中的 Most fathers 在语义上对应选项中的 the majority of men; admitted 对应选项中的 admitted; they actually did much less childcare than the mother 在语义上对应选项中的in reality the female actually did most of it。故选项J 为正确答案。

根据题干中的关键词equal parental leave 、indispensable 和 achieving gender equality 定位至选项 P 的第二句。定位句提到，这位父亲认为平等的育儿假是职场中实现性别平等的重要措施之一。题干是对定 位句的同义替换。题干中的equal parental leave 对应选项中的 equal parental leave; indispensable 被改写为选 项中的 essential ; achieving gender equality in the workplace 在语义上对应选项中的creating gender equality in the workplace。故选项 P 为正确答案。

根据题干中的关键词 less objection 和 paternity leave 定位至选项B 的第一句。定位句提到， 波士顿学院工作与家庭中心的一项调查表明，81%的人觉得父亲休陪产假的想法，(比起以前)已较易为人们所接受。题干是对定位句的同义替换。题干中的 survey 对应选项中的 survey; there is now less objection to paternity leave 在语义上对应选项中的the notion of fathers taking leave has become more acceptable。故选项B为正确答案。

根据题干中的关键词five years ago, organisation, same support 和 men and women taking parental  leave 定位至选项F。定位句提到，与五年前相比，现在有四分之三的人表示他们所在的机构对女性和男性休育儿假给予相同的支持。题干是对定位句的概括总结。题干中的five years ago 对应选项中的 five years ago; organisation 对应选项中的 organisation, same support 在语义上对应选项中的 equally supportive ; men and women taking parental leave 对应选项中的 women and men taking leave。故选项 F 为正确答案。

根据题干中的关键词 workers who claim to desire gender equality, stick to 和 traditional gender roles both at work and at home 定位至选项I。定位句提到，研究表明，即便是声称强烈渴望性别平等的员工也在工作及家庭中延续着传统的性别角色。题干是对定位句的概括总结。题干中的 even workers who claim to desire gender equality 对应选项中的 even among workers who claim to have a strong desire for equality ; stick to 被改写为选项中的 endure; traditional gender roles both at work and at home 对应选项中的 traditional gender roles…at work…and  at  home。故选项I为正确答案。

根据题干中的关键词 The majority of workers, parental leave policies, improved 和 workplace culture 定位至选项C。定位句提到，超过一半的员工表示休假政策让职场文化变得更好。题干是对定位句的同义替换。题干中的 The majority of workers 被改写为选项中的 over half; parental leave policies 对应选项中的leave policies; improved 被改写为选项中的 made…better; workplace culture 对应选项中的workplace culture。故选 项C 为正确答案。

根据题干中的关键词In spite of progress, women in top positions 和 small 定位至选项L的3句。定位句提到，尽管女性为获得最高权力职位而进行的斗争取得了进展，今年《财富》杂志500强榜单中已经有33位女性首席执行官，这已创造了纪录，但这仍然只占总数的一小部分。题干是对定位句的概括总结。题干中的 In spite of progress被改写为选项中的 Despite progress; women in top positions 被改写为选项中的 women to reach the highest positions ; small被改写为选项中的 tiny。故选项L为正确答案。

根据题干中的关键词 estimate 和 less than one third of companies in the U.S.定位至选项 E 的第一句。定位句提到，布拉德·哈林顿估计，美国只有20%到30%的公司提供带薪育儿假。题干是对定位句的同义替换。题干中的 estimate 对应选项中的 estimates; less than one third 被改写为选项中的 only 20% to 30%; companies in the U.S.对应选项中的companies in the U.S.; provide 被改写为选项中的 offer; paid parental leave 对应选项中的 paid parental leave。故选项 E 为正确答案。

根据题干中的关键词 A number of lawsuits, pressured 和 formulate gender neutral policies on parental leave 定位至选项 H。 定位句提到，出现的许多针对公司的涉及陪产假的法律案件，这些案件向公司施加压力，要求其制定不带性别色彩的育儿假政策。题干是对定位句的同义替换。题干中的A number of lawsuits 被 改写为选项中的 a number of legal cases; pressured companies 被改写为选项中的 put pressure on companies; formulate gender neutral policies on parental leave 被改写为选项中的 make their parental leave policies gender neutral。故选项H 为正确答案。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 Having a rival can keep you committed to achieving your goals and enhance your overall performance.? 2 But before you go out and find an entrepreneur to outcompete, it's important to understand and avoid the traps that often come with rivalry. 3 After all, competitive rivalry can also hinder effective decision-making and increase your willingness to take risks, behaviors that can ultimately hurt your venture 's success.
1 Finding someone you're committed to outcompeting can be a great way to stay focused on your goals and push your venture to the next level. 2 But when you're intently focused on outperforming your rivals, you may begin to develop a "win-at-all-costs" mentality that causes you to ignore how you achieve success. 3 One group of researchers, for example, examined the link between rivalry and unethical behavior. 4 They found that when people compete against their rivals, they are more willing to behave unethically to win.? 5 But such behavior may stain your reputation and strain relationships important to your success. 6 One way to avoid this trap is to stop and reflect on what's important.? 7 While outperforming your rivals may provide short-term benefits, the loss of your integrity will have long-term consequences.
1 One reason having a rival can enhance your venture 's performance is that it creates a level of excitement that drives you to work harder. 2 But this eagerness to win may also hurt your venture 's success, particularly when it causes you to make impulsive, insensible decisions. 3 But it's possible to avoid such costly mistakes by making a habit of engaging in critical thinking, such as considering opposing viewpoints and conducting cost-benefit analyses, especially for those decisions that are complex and can determine the future of your venture.?
1 The sense of eagerness that comes with having a rival can not only cause you to make poorer decisions, but it can also lead you to take greater risks that put your venture in peril. 2 One way you can overcome the risk- inducing effects of rivalry that stand to endanger your venture 's success is to remain attentive to your emotional state and actively monitor how such feelings are affecting your decision-making.?

choices.label: A
choices.text: By enabling them to out compete other entrepreneurs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: By enabling them to make their venture a success.

choices.label: C
choices.text: By helping them to reach long-term goals.

choices.label: D
choices.text: By helping them to stay goal-oriented.

questions.explanation: 第一段第一句指出，拥有竞争对手可以让你专注于实现目标、提高整体表现。由此可知，竞争可使企业家保持目标导向，keep you committed to achieving your goals 在语义上对应选项 D中的 helping them to stay goal- oriented,故答案为选项 D。

choices.label: A
choices.text: They may adopt strategies that are bound to ruin their venture.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They may resort to unethical means to outperform their rivals.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They may be too eager to succeed while ignoring the huge labor cost.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They may be intently focused on winning at the current market level.

questions.explanation: 由题干中的when competing with rivals定位到第二段第四句。第二段第四句指出，研究人员发现，当人们与对手竞争时，他们更愿意为了获胜而做出不道德的行为。由此可知，人们可能会采取不道德的手段来超越竞争对手，behave unethically to win 在语义上对应选项 B 中的 resort to unethical means to outperform their rivals, 故答案为选项 B.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reflect on what successes are achievable.

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 A multitasker is one who can perform two or more tasks effectively at the same time, which — apart from the obvious differences — is similar to what a computer does. 2 The concept does indeed come from the realms of technology, where it is used to refer to an operating system that can execute multiple tasks at the same time.? 3 However, the question is: can a person really be a multitasker?
1 For most scientists, the answer is no. 2 So much so that, according to experts in neuroscience (神经系统科学), our brains do not handle multitasking situations well.? 3 As soon as two tasks require our attention, productivity suffers. 4 What we call multitasking, therefore, is in reality the ability to move more or less quickly from one task to another. 5 This requires two essential conditions: that one of the tasks needs to be automatic, like walking or eating, and that they both need different mental processes, answering the phone and writing at the same time, for example.
1 However, on the other side of the coin there are people who maintain that it is possible to be, or at least seem to be, multitasking. 2 A recent study concluded that regardless of whether people are actually handling several tasks or not, the mere fact that they perceive this activity as multitasking has a positive effect on their performance.?
1 The business perspective offers a different view: multitasking is understood as the ability to adapt to all types of environment within a company and effectively undertake different activities within a set time frame. 2 Indeed, many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking to improve their productivity. 3 From this different perspective, you can not only be multitasking but this ability can also be taught: something that is easier in fluid organisations, which favour flexibility in their working practices.?
1 The benefits of multitasking are clear. 2 Being quicker and more efficient increases our performance and the number of tasks completed. 3 But having to pay attention to several things at once means that the powers of concentration are reduced and that can lead to more mistakes.?

sections.passage: 1 Since the reform and opening-up, the living standards of the Chinese people have been continuously improving, which is fully reflected in their dietary changes. 2 Nowadays, people are no longer satisfied with simply being full; instead, they pursue safer, more nutritious, and healthier food. 3 The variety of food has become increasingly rich and diverse, no longer limited to local agricultural products. 4 The development of the logistics industry makes it easy for people to taste specialties from all over the country. 5 Undoubtedly, the improvement of food quality and dietary structure provides a strong guarantee for enhancing people's health.

questions.answer: 1 Since the reform and opening-up, the living standards of the Chinese people have been continuously improving, which is fully reflected in their dietary changes. 2 Nowadays, people are no longer satisfied with simply being full; instead, they pursue safer, more nutritious, and healthier food. 3 The variety of food has become increasingly rich and diverse, no longer limited to local agricultural products. 4 The development of the logistics industry makes it easy for people to taste specialties from all over the country. 5 Undoubtedly, the improvement of food quality and dietary structure provides a strong guarantee for enhancing people's health.

sections.title: Section A 选词填空
sections.passage:
1 When people set out to improve their health, they usually take a familiar path: starting a healthy diet, getting better sleep, and doing regular exercise. 2 Each of these behaviors is important, of course, but they all 1 on physical health — and a growing body of research suggests that social health is just as, if not more, important to 2 well-being.?
1 One recent study published in the journal PLOS ONE, for example, found that the strength of a person's social circle was a better 3 of self-reported stress, happiness and well-being levels than fitness tracker data on physical activity, heart rate and sleep.? 2 That finding suggests that the “ 4 self “ represented by endless amounts of health data doesn't tell the whole 5.?
1 There's also a qualified self, which is who I am, what are my activities, my social network, and all of these aspects are not 6 in any of these measurements.?
1 This idea is supported by plenty of 7 research.? 2 Studies have shown that social support — whether it comes from friends, family members or a spouse — is 8 associated with better mental and physical health.? 3 A rich social life, these studies suggest, can lower stress levels, improve mood, encourage positive health behaviors and discourage damaging ones, boost heart health and improve illness 9 rates.?
1 Social isolation, meanwhile, is linked to higher rates of physical diseases and mental health conditions. 2 It's a significant problem, 10 since loneliness is emerging as a widespread public health problem in many Countries.?

questions.explanation:
【考点】动词辨析

【解析】 空格前是���子主语 they,空格后是宾语 physical health, 因此空格处应填谓语动词，构成短语_____on。 空格句的大意为“当然，这些行为都很重要，但它们都____身体健康。”结合选项，表示“关注、聚焦” 的词符合题意。故选项 D)focus 为正确答案。

【考点】 形容词辨析

【解析】空格后是名词well-being, 因此空格处应填形容词或名词。空格句大意为“越来越多的研究表明，社交健康对_____康同样重要，甚至更重要。”结合选项，表示“全面的、整体的”的词符合题意。故选项F) overall 为正确答案。

【考点】名词辨析

【解析】空格前是不定冠词a 加形容词 better, 因此空格处应填名词。空格句的大意为“例如，最近发表在《公共科学图书馆·综合》杂志上的一项研究发现，与健身追踪器上的体力活动、心率和睡眠数据相比， 一个人社交圈的能量是反映个体自述压力、幸福和安乐水平的更好_____ 。”结合选项，表示“标志、迹象”的词符合题意。 故选项 E)indicator 为正确答案。

【考点】 |形容词辨析

【解析】空格后为名词self, 因此空格处应填形容词或名词。空格句的大意为“这一发现表明，无尽的健康数据所代表的‘ ____ 自我’并不能说明全部情况。”结合选项，表示“量化的”的词符合题意。故选项 K) quantified为正确答案。

【考点】 名词辨析

【解析】空格前是定冠词加形容词 the whole, 因此空格处应填名词。空格句的大意为“这一发现表明，无尽的健康数据所代表的‘量化自我’并不能说明全部_____。”结合选项，表示“故事、情况”的词符合题意。故选项 N)story为正确答案。

【考点】 动词辨析

【解析】空格前是 all of these aspects are not,因此空格处应填动词或形容词。空格句的大意为“还有一个‘质化’的自我，包括我是谁、我有什么活动、我的社交网络是怎样的，这些方面都没有_____在这种测量尺度中。” 结合选项，表示“体现、反射”的词符合题意。故选项 M)reflected为正确答案。

【考点】形容词辨析

【解析】空格后是名词 research, 空格处单词起修饰 research 的作用，因此空格处应填形容词或名词。空格句的大意为“这一观点得到了大量_____研究的支持。”结合选项，表示“先前的、优先的”的词符合题意。故选项H)prior为正确答案。

【考点】副词辨析

【解析】空格句不缺成分，且所缺单词起修饰is associated with 的作用，因此空格处应填副词。空格句的大意为“社会支持——无论是来自朋友、家庭成员还是配偶——都与更好的身心健康_____相关。”结合选项，表示“坚定地、强烈地”的词符合题意。故选项 O)strongly 为正确答案。

【考点】 名词辨析

【解析】空格前是名词illness, 空格后也是名词rates,因此空格处应填名词。空格句的大意为“这些研究表明，丰富的社交生活可以降低压力水平，改善情绪，鼓励积极的健康行为，阻止有害的行为，促进心脏健康，提高疾病的_____率。”结合选项，表示“恢复、复苏”的词符合题意。故选项L)recovery 为正确答案。

【考点】副词辨析

【解析】空格句不缺成分，空格处单词起修饰 since引导的从句的作用，因此空格处应填副词。空格句的大意为“这个问题很严重，_____在许多国家，孤独正成为一个普遍的公共卫生问题。”结合选项，表示“尤其、特别”的词符合题意。故选项C)especially  为正确答案。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 As a parent of two boys at primary school, I worry about the issues associated with teenagers and social media. 2 Newspapers are constantly filled with frightening accounts of drug addiction and aggressive behaviour supposedly caused by violent videogames. 3 But even when these accounts touch on real concerns, they do not really reflect the great mass of everyday teenage social behaviour: the online chat, the texting, the surfing, and the emergence of a new teenage sphere that is conducted digitally.?
1 New technologies always provoke generational panic, which usually has more to do with adult fears than with the lives of teenagers.? 2 In the 1930s, parents worried that radio was gaining “an irresistible hold of their children". 3 In the 80s, the great danger was the Sony Walkman (随身听). 4 When you look at today's digital activity, the facts are much more positive than you might expect.
1 Indeed, social scientists who study young people have found that their digital use can be inventive and even beneficial. 2 This is true not just in terms of their social lives, but their education too.? 3 So if you use a ton of social media, do you become unable, or unwilling, to engage in face-to-face contact? 4 The evidence suggests not. 5 Research by Amanda Lenhart of the Pew Research Centre, a U.S. think tank, found that the most passionate texters are also the kids most likely to spend time with friends in person. 6 One form of socialising doesn't replace the other. 7 It expands it.
1 “Kids still spend time face to face,” Lenhart says. 2 Indeed, as they get older and are given more freedom, they often ease up on social networking. 3 Early on, the web is their "third space", but by the late teens, it's replaced in reaction to greater independence. 4 They have to be on Facebook, to know what's going on among friends and family, but they are ambivalent (有矛盾心理的) about it, says Rebecca Eynon, a research fellow at the Oxford Internet Institute, who has interviewed about 200 British teenagers over three years. 5 As they gain experience with living online, they begin to adjust their behaviour, struggling with new communication skills, as they do in the real world.
1 Parents are wrong to worry that kids don't care about privacy. 2 In fact, they spend hours changing Facebook settings or using quick-delete sharing tools, such as Snapchat, to minimise their traces.? 3 Or they post a photograph on Instagram, have a pleasant conversation with friends and then delete it so that no traces remain.
1 This is not to say that kids always use good judgment. 2 Like everyone else, they make mistakes — sometimes serious ones. 3 But working out how to behave online is a new social skill. 4 While there's plenty of drama and messiness online, it is not, for most teens, a cycle of non-stop abuse: a Pew study found only 15% of teens said someone had bullied them online in the last 12 months.
1 But surely all this short-form writing is affecting literacy? 2 Certainly, teachers worry. 3 They say that kids use overly casual language and textspeak in writing, and don't have as much patience for long reading and complex arguments.? 4 Yet studies of first-year college papers suggest these anxieties may be partly based on misguided nostalgia (怀旧). 5 When Stanford University scholar Andrea Lunsford gathered data on the rates of errors in “freshman composition” papers going back to 1917, she found that they were virtually identical to today.
1 But even as error rates stayed stable, student essays have blossomed in size and complexity.? 2 They are now six times longer and, unlike older “what I did this summer” essays, they offer arguments supported by evidence. 3 Why? Computers have vastly increased the ability of students to gather information, sample different points of view and write more fluidly.
1 When linguist Naomi Baron studied students' instant messaging even there she found surprisingly rare usage of short forms such as “u” for “you”, and as students got older, they began to write in more grammatical sentences. 2 That is because they want to appear more adult, and they know how adults are expected to write. 3 Clearly, teaching teens formal writing is still crucial, but texting probably isn't destroying their ability to learn it.?
1 It is probably true that fewer kids are heavy readers compared with two generations ago, when cheap paperbacks boosted rates of reading. 2 But even back then, a minority of people — perhaps 20% — were lifelong heavy readers, and it was cable TV, not the internet, that struck a blow at that culture in the 1980s.? 3 Still, 15% or more of kids are found to be deeply bookish. 4 In fact, the online world offers kids remarkable opportunities to become literate and creative because young people can now publish ideas not just to their friends, but to the world. 5 And it turns out that when they write for strangers, their sense of “authentic audience” makes them work harder, push themselves further, and create powerful new communicative forms.
1 Few would deny that too much time online can be harmful. 2 Some of the dangers are emotional: hurting someone from a distance is not the same as hurting them face to face. 3 If we're lucky, the legal environment will change to make teenagers' online lives less likely to haunt them later on. 4 Just last week, California passed a law allowing minors to demand that internet firms erase their digital past and the EU has considered similar legislation.
1 Distraction is also a serious issue. 2 When kids switch from chat to music to homework, they are indeed likely to have trouble doing each task well. 3 And studies show that pupils don't fact-check information online —— “smart searching” is a skill schools need to teach urgently.? 4 It's also true that too much social networking and game playing can cut into schoolwork and sleep. 5 This is precisely why parents still need to set firm boundaries around it, as with any other distraction.
1 So what's the best way to cope? 2 The same boring old advice that applies to everything in parenting: moderation. 3 Rebecca Eynon argues that it's key to model good behaviour. 4 Parents who stare non-stop at their phones and don't read books are likely to breed kids who will do the same. 5 As ever, we ought to be careful about our own behaviour.?

questions.explanation: 根据题干中的关键词 use of digital technology、benefits、teenagers' social lives 和 studies 定位至选项C 的第一、二句。定位句提到，事实上，研究年轻人的社会科学家发现，年轻人使用数码产品可能会让他们富有创造性，甚至还有益处。这不仅体现在他们的社交生活上，也体现在他们的教育上。题干是对定位句的概括总结。题干中的use of digital technology 对应选项中的their digital use, benefits 对应选项中的 beneficial, teenagers' social lives 对应选项中的 their social lives, studies 在语义上对应选项中的 education。 故选项C 为正确答案。

根据题干中的关键词 urgent、schools teach kids 和 verify online information 定位至选项L的第三句。定位句提到，研究表明，学生不会在网上核实信息——“智能搜索”是学校迫切需要教授的一项技能。题干是对定位句的同义替换。题干中的 urgent 对应选项中的 urgently, schools teach kids 对应选项中的 schools need to teach, verify online information 对应选项中的 fact-check information online。故选项L为正确答案。

根据题干中的关键词write longer and more complex essays 和 error rates remain unchanged 定位至选项H的第一句。定位句提到，但即使错误率保持稳定，学生论文的规模和复杂性却在不断增加。题干是对定位句的同义替换。题干中的write longer and more complex essays在语义上对应选项中的 student essays have blossomed in size and complexity, error rates remain unchanged 对应选项中的error rates stayed stable。故选项H为正确答案。

根据题干中的关键词newspaper reports 和 give a false picture 定位至选项A的末句。定位句提到，但即使这些报道揭露了某些真实问题，它们也没有真正反映青少年日常社会行为的大部分：网上聊天、发短信、 网上冲浪，也没有显示青少年领域里出现的新型数字化方式。题干是对定位句的同义替换。题干中的 newspaper reports 对应选项中的 accounts, give a false picture 在语义上对应选项中的 do not really reflect。故选项A 为正确答案。

根据题干中的关键词 parents、mind their own digital behaviour 和 set a good example定位至选项M的第三、四、五句。定位句提到，丽贝卡·艾农认为，树立良好的行为榜样是关键。不停地盯着手机而不读书的父母很可能会培养出行为相同的孩子。和以往一样，我们应该注意自己的行为。题干是对定位句的概括总结。题干中的 parents 对应选项中的 parents, mind their own digital behaviour 在语义上对应选项中的be careful about our own behaviour, example 对应选项中的 model。 故选项 M 为正确答案。

1 In the history of horse racing, few horses have captured the affection of the British public like Red Rum. 2 Today, three decades after his retirement, he is still one of the best-known and most beloved racehorses of all time.?
1 Red Rum was passed around to several owners before being purchased for Noel Le Mar. 2 The agent who made the purchase was the now-legendary horse trainer Donald “Ginger” McCain.
1 It wasn't apparent at the time, but Red Rum had a serious bone disease in his foot. 2 For many horses (and many trainers) this would mean the end of a racing career before it even began. 3 For Ginger and Red Rum, though, it was just an obstacle to greatness that had to be overcome.?
1 Red Rum 's true talent came out in steeplechases (障碍赛马). 2 His power, speed and jumping ability carried him to his first Grand National title in 1973.? 3 The very next year, Red Rum returned to take his second title. 4 He was the first horse to take successive firsts since Reynoldstown in 1935—1936. 5 Red Rum 's spirit and grace had already begun to charm the leagues of Grand National fans.
1 In the following two years, Red Rum lost out on the title, coming in second both times. 2 When he returned in 1977 to try again, he was largely regarded as past his prime.? 3 He was 12 years old and not expected to place highly. 4 He surprised sporting fans around the world when he came in a remarkable 25 lengths ahead of the nearest horse, taking his third Grand National win. 5 To this day, Red Rum 's third win is known as one of the greatest moments in horse racing history.
1 Red Rum was headed for the Grand National once again in 1978 but suffered an injury in one of his heels shortly before the race. 2 He was retired soon after, but his public life and fame by no means decreased with the end of his career.? 3 Red Rum traveled all over the country for various engagements. 4 He often led pre-race parades at Aintree Racecourse and was a popular guest at charity benefits and public events.

sections.passage:
1 People in business often make decisions based on their own personal feelings or instincts.? 2 It is quite horrifying to see people being guided by some unknown force. 3 But how wise is it, really, to let your instincts drive your decisions?
1 In the decision-making process, relying on instincts only makes sense when you have a vast experience to support you. 2 Simply "feeling" that something is right or should be done is highly subjective and can drown you.
1 On the other hand, there is a more rational approach to making decisions. 2 Data and analysis have long been associated with informed decisions.? 3 These reduce the likelihood of errors and increase the chances of success. 4 Big, systematic data is mostly the foundation of most of our decisions, personal and business alike. 5 But with its extreme usability comes a complication: what do you do if you strongly feel something should not be done, even if the data insists that it should?
1 This seemingly easy question is what drives the need to understand the relationship between instincts and data in the decision-making process. 2 Without making things complicated, the solution to this dilemma is using data and instincts in conjunction to arrive at the best possible decisions.?
1 Instinctive decisions are always backed by previous experiences or information, which acknowledges that instinctive decisions have worked in the past. 2 Decisions are not about making the choice and braving the consequences because you want to blindly trust your instincts. 3 They are about combining your inner wisdom with the knowledge of systematic data to make the best decisions.
1 Sometimes, rational analysis and data are impractical to be employed in certain situations. 2 Absence of definitive criteria, and time and resource constraints, and novel situations are instances which limit the practicality of data. 3 The only feasible option is to rely on what your instincts tell you.? 4 In these situations, instincts can help you make effective and quick decisions.
1 Combining instinctive and rational analysis produces well-rounded decisions.? 2 It reduces the chances of making mistakes, and has increasingly become a favorite approach to decision-making among leaders of today.

African leaders plan to turn the continent into a continent without borders.
They will introduce a single passport policy, allowing free movement between countries.
The idea from the African Union has been modeled on the EU Schengen free movement deal.
Europe has abolished many internal borders.
This enables visa-free movement across the continent.
Currently, 13 African countries have visa-free deals in place with each other.
These allow citizens to visit another country without a visa.
Some countries offer visas on arrival.
In contrast, Americans are able to travel to 20 of the continent's countries without a visa, or secure a visa on arrival.
The African Union, which represents 54 states, wants to abolish the requirement of a visa for Africans visiting other African countries.
It also wants to establish a free trade deal across the continent in the near future, as trade within the African continent costs more than any other region。

Q2 What benefit will a free trade deal bring to African economy?
Researchers in Iceland found a new way of tackling climate change by pumping carbon dioxide underground and turning it into stone.
Other carbon capture and storage methods store carbon dioxide as a gas.
But problems include a high cost and concern about leaks.
This new method of burying carbon dioxide and turning it into stone is cheaper and more secure, the Guardian reports.
To turn carbon dioxide into stone, researchers with the CarbFix project pumped the gas into volcanic rock and sped up the natural process, in which the volcanic rock reacts with gas and forms carbon minerals.
The gas turned into solid in just two years, much faster than the hundreds or thousands of years researchers had predicted.
The research took place at Iceland's Hellisheidi power plant.
Already, the project in Iceland has been increased in scale to bury 10,000 tons of carbon dioxide each year.
One potential difficulty is that for each ton of carbon dioxide buried, the technique requires 25 tons of water.
However, the lead researcher said sea water could be used.
Q3 What new method has been developed to help fight climate change?
Q4 What is a potential difficulty in applying the new technique?
People in France are keeping away from the narrow French stick loaf in favour of healthier, cheaper options, a millers, association has said.
The National Association of French Millers says bread consumption is on the decline, with French people eating nine grams less than in the previous year.
The association is concerned about the effects this trend will have on their trade and suggests three reasons why it is happening.
Firstly, the association cited changing diets, in particular, the switch to those low in calories, as a factor in the reduction of bread consumption.
This could explain why the difference in consumption between genders is so big.
Nowadays, men eat an approximate average of 140 grams of bread daily, whereas women eat 80 to 90 grams.
The second reason they say is lifestyle changes in the country, with people dedicating less time to breakfast when bread would traditionally be eaten with butter and jam.
Finally, the rising cost of bread is considered to be a factor, with the price of a French stick loaf increasing by nearly 25% in the last 10 years.

Love them or hate them, smartphones have become an integral part of our daily lives.
But should they be left outside the classroom?
Nick Gibb, Minister for School Standards in England, believes schools should ban their pupils from bringing in smartphones。
Astrid Natley, a secondary school math teacher, incorporates phones into her classroom.
"My school doesn't have money for tablets, she says.
"When students use their phones for research, they learn they have a powerful tool in their hands.
If we stop children using phones, we're rejecting something they care about.”
Meanwhile, Helen Lockhart, a registered nurse working for community education, supports a complete ban.
" I'm banned from mobile use at work, and my phone must be handed in.
If I'm caught with it in my pocket, I will be subject to disciplinary procedure, which will impact on my career.
We need to teach children how to behave like the professionals they are striving to become.”
Richard Stone, an English teacher, thinks there should be a clear separation between school and home.
"Students should do things differently in the two environments.
Children are getting more than enough screen time in their lives without the need to bring their phone into the classroom.
The internet is too easy and too unreliable a research tool, so let’s leave phones and laptops at home, and show them a different world in their lessons — one of books and pens," he says.

Kate, a six-year-old girl, helped her brother wash windows to get a reward promised by her mother, a purple doll that she wanted.
She watched her mother order the doll online.
The next day Kate asked if she could check the shipping status, so her mom clicked on the web page and then walked out of the room.
Kate saw that her doll would be arriving the next afternoon, but then she noticed something else, suggestions about other dolls and toys she could order.
15 minutes and a few clicks later, with more than $350 worth of dolls in her cart, Kate placed the order and ran off to play.
The next day, while checking on another online order, her mother noticed a long list of dolls on the way.
She was able to cancel two of them, but it was too late to cancel the rest.
She told her daughter that they were going to be returned.
When the packages arrived, Kate wanted to open them, but her parents said no.
Instead of sending back the dolls, her father suggested giving them to the local children's hospital.
So the next week, Kate's family loaded up their car and took all the dolls to the playroom at the children's hospital.
Kate was depressed at first, but then she sat with some girl patients and they opened up all the boxes together, laughing and playing.
She had a lot of fun and learned a really good lesson.

Can the date you were born affect how successful your life is?
According to recent research done in Australia, the answer is yes.
The researchers found that the time when a person starts school has an enduring impact on their lives.
Those who are relatively old, compared to their classmates, have certain advantages over them.
Previous research has found older students achieve better results.
They are also more likely to attend university and become professional athletes, chief executives and even important politicians.
But the Australian researchers wanted to discover what was driving these differences.
They suspected older, more mature students obtained more self-confidence than their peers because they achieved better grades.
To test this out, they conducted two studies.
One was with high school students and the other with more than a thousand Australian adults, age between 24 and 60 years old.
In the first study more than 600 high school students were surveyed about their tendency to take risks and feel confident.
In the second study, those born on both sides of the cutoff date for starting school were asked to complete online math questions and rate their performance.
They were also asked about the risks they took while riding bicycles and managing their finances.
The researchers found that older students displayed greater risk-taking tendencies.
While risk-taking can be considered a negative attribute, it’s also a characteristic of successful people, including athletes, political leaders and entrepreneurs.

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 With the improvement of living standards, more people begin to join the ranks of self-driving tours. 2 Self-driving tourists can either drive their own cars, or borrow or rent a car. 3 The driver may be the owner of the car or the traveling companion. 4 Different from a traditional group tour, a self-driving tour can better meet the personalized needs of tourists and enable them to better enjoy the travel. 5 Self-driving tours are especially popular with young travelers. 6 Young people pursue an independent and free life, and a self-driving tour just meets their needs.

questions.answer: 1 With the improvement of living standards, more people begin to join the ranks of self-driving tours. 2 Self-driving tourists can either drive their own cars, or borrow or rent a car. 3 The driver may be the owner of the car or the traveling companion. 4 Different from a traditional group tour, a self-driving tour can better meet the personalized needs of tourists and enable them to better enjoy the travel. 5 Self-driving tours are especially popular with young travelers. 6 Young people pursue an independent and free life, and a self-driving tour just meets their needs.
