A new study from Oregon State University found that dogs tend to match their behavior with the children in their family.
The findings are important because there is a growing body of evidence that dogs can help children in many ways.
These include helping with social development, increasing physical activity, managing anxiety, or serving as a source of attachment in the face of changing family structures.
Yet, very little research has focused on how dogs perceive and socially engage with children.
The great news is that this study suggests dogs are paying a lot of attention to the kids that they live with, said Monique Udell, the lead author of the study.
"One interesting thing we have observed is that dogs are matching children's behavior, but less frequently than what we have seen between dogs and adults.
This suggests that while dogs may view children as social companions, there are also some differences that we need to understand better."
While research has found dogs can have a lot of positive impacts on a child's life, there are also risks associated with the dog-child relationship.
For example, other studies have found dogs are more likely to bite children versus adults.
"We still have a lot to learn about the dog-child relationship," Udell said.
"But research does show that kids are very capable of training dogs."

questions.explanation: What does the tiny home movement mainly advocate?小户型住宅运动主要倡导什么？【解析】在对话中，男士提到小户型住宅运动主要是关于增加自有住房率以及环境保护的，所以答案是D项。A、B两项对话中没有提到，故排除；C项是利用对话细节设置的干扰项，故也排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: Not a realistic size for families.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only fit for families of four or less.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only suitable for renting to the poor.

questions.explanation: What does the woman say about houses as small as 20 square meters?关于面积小至20平方米的房子，女士说了什么？【解析】女士提到她看过男士的博客，他所写的那些房子面积小到只有20平方米，然后她评价道，对于很多家庭来说，这样的面积并不现实，所以答案是A项。虽然对话中女士提到大多数人想要宽敞的房子，但不能由此推出面积小至20平方米的房子不受大多数美国人欢迎，B项过度推断，故排除；对话中男士提到很多四口之家住在不到30平方米的房子里也过得很开心，但是女士对此并没有作任何评价，故排除C项；D项对话中没有相关信息，故排除。

choices.label: C
choices.text: It will come true sooner or later.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It doesn't appeal to average families.

questions.explanation: What does the man think about the dream of owning a 150-square-meter house?男士对拥有150平方米房子的梦想有什么看法？【解析】在对话中，女士提到150平方米的房子才是人们梦想拥有的房子，男士对此的评价是，考虑到住房成本，这个梦想需要改变了，所以答案是A项。其他三项对话中没有相关信息，故均排除。

questions.explanation: What does the man say about tiny homes?关于小户型住宅，男士说了什么？【解析】在对话中，男士总结道小户型住宅可能并不适合所有人，但对很多人来说是个不错的选择，所以答案是C项。虽然男士提到小户型住宅对环境有益处，即建造时使用更少的土地和资源，但并没有强调其对减少全球浪费至关重要，对此没有相关的明确表述，故排除D项；A、B两项对话中没有相关信息，故均排除。
What do children seem to have a natural desire to do?孩子们似乎天生就渴望做什么？【解析】文章中提到，首先，孩子们似乎天生就有克服挑战、冒险的欲望。B项与文章内容一致，故为答案。其余选项与文章内容不符，故排除。

choices.label: B

questions.explanation: According to the American Psychological Association, what does regular physical activity do to children?根据美国心理协会的说法，规律的体育活动对孩子们有什么作用？【解析】文章中提到，根据美国心理协会的研究，经常进行体育活动（尤其是户外活动）能够减轻孩子们的压力和抑郁情绪。C项与文章内容一致，故为答案。A项文中虽提及，但未提及是美国心理协会的说法，故排除。文中并未提及掩饰情绪和防止儿童感到孤独的内容，故排除B、D。

What does the passage say about cultivating the habit of physical activity?关于培养体育活动的习惯，文章说了什么？【解析】文章中提到，我们都知道体育活动对我们的身心健康十分重要，而培养体育活动的习惯开始得很早。孩子们更有可能从频繁的积极早期体验中养成终身热爱体育活动的习惯。A项与文章内容一致，故为答案。B项文中未提及，故排除。文中并未提及终身努力的内容，故排除C。D项中亲近自然的体验文中虽提及，但这说的是当孩子们不喜欢竞技运动或球类游戏时可以选择的其他活动之一，故排除。

questions.explanation: When are job seekers willing to explore jobs with lower salaries, according to a new study?根据一项新的研究，求职者在什么时候愿意去考虑薪资较低的工作？【解析】文章开头提到，一项新研究发现，当企业更加多元化时，求职者甚至愿意考虑薪资较低的工作。因此，选项C为正确答案。其他选项在文中没有提及，故排除。

questions.explanation: What did participants see in the baseline condition of the study?在这项研究的基准条件组中，参与者看到了什么？【解析】文章中提到，在基准条件组中，参与者看到的是常规格式的邮件，邮件中没有关于多元化的信息。因此，选项A为正确答案。其他选项在文中没有提及，故排除。
What does the passage say participants seem to be paying attention to?文章中提到参与者似乎在关注什么呢？【解析】文章中提到，参与者似乎更关注多元化方面的信息，并以此决定是否点击招聘信息。因此，选项D为正确答案。其他选项在文中没有提及，故排除。
What does the passage say about the findings of a new study from Oregon State University?文章怎么评价俄勒冈州立大学一项新研究的发现？【解析】文章开头提到，俄勒冈州立大学的一项新研究发现，狗往往会使其行为与家中孩子的行为相匹配。这些发现很重要。因此，选项C为正确答案。其他选项在文中没有提及，故排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dogs match their behavior with kids as much as with adults.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Kids and adults alike find in dogs a source of attachment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Kids' attitude to dogs is influenced by adults.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dogs can help kids in many ways.

questions.explanation: What does a growing body of evidence show according to the passage?根据文章内容，越来越多的证据表明了什么？【解析】文章中提到，越来越多的证据表明，狗能在诸多方面帮助孩子，包括助力社交发展、增加身体活动量、缓解焦虑，或是在家庭结构发生变化时成为情感寄托的对象。因此，选项D为正确答案。其他选项在文中没有提及，故排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dogs pay much attention to the kids they live with.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

questions.explanation: What did Monique Udell say their study suggests?莫妮克·乌德尔说他们的研究表明了什么？文章中提到，莫妮克·乌德尔说这项研究表明狗会非常关注和它们一起生活的孩子。A项与文章内容一致，故为正确答案。文中仅提及狗可能将孩子视为社交伙伴，B项的表述超出了原文所给信息，存在过度推断的问题，故排除。C项和D项文章中未提及，故排除。
What does research show kids are very capable of doing?研究显示孩子们非常有能力做什么？【解析】文章最后提到，研究确实表明，孩子非常有能力训练狗。因此，选项B为正确答案。其他选项在文中没有提及，故排除。

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 In recent years, the new energy vehicle (NEV) industry in China has developed rapidly. 2 At present, the annual production of new energy vehicles in China has approached 10 million units, accounting for over 60% of the global market share, and the export volume is also setting new records continuously. 3 The Chinese government, by increasing financial investment and providing policy guidance, encourages new energy vehicle companies to carry out technological innovation, and continuously enhances the competitiveness of their products in the market. 4 The development of China's new energy vehicle industry has not only strongly promoted domestic economic growth but also made a positive contribution to the global use of new energy and environmental protection.

questions.stem: ①近年来，中国新能源汽车（NEV）产业发展迅速。②目前，中国新能源汽车年产量已接近1000万辆，占全球市场份额的60%以上，出口量也在不断创下新高。③中国政府通过增加资金投入和提供政策引导，鼓励新能源汽车企业开展技术创新，不断提升其产品在市场上的竞争力。④中国新能源汽车产业的发展不仅有力地推动了国内经济增长，还为全球新能源利用和环境保护做出了积极贡献。
questions.answer: 1 In recent years, the new energy vehicle (NEV) industry in China has developed rapidly. 2 At present, the annual production of new energy vehicles in China has approached 10 million units, accounting for over 60% of the global market share, and the export volume is also setting new records continuously. 3 The Chinese government, by increasing financial investment and providing policy guidance, encourages new energy vehicle companies to carry out technological innovation, and continuously enhances the competitiveness of their products in the market. 4 The development of China's new energy vehicle industry has not only strongly promoted domestic economic growth but also made a positive contribution to the global use of new energy and environmental protection.

sections.title: Section A 选词填空
sections.passage:
1 When Toni Morrison died in 2019, the world lost one of its most influential authors. 2 But Morrison was not an early success. 3 Her first novel was not published until she was 39, and her last appeared when she was 84. 4 And Morrison was not 1 in this regard.? 5 Numerous writers produce masterpieces well into their 70s and beyond.? 6 Such 2 accomplishments highlight an important point.? 7 Our capacity to speak, write and learn new vocabulary does not seem to 3 with age. 8 Our eyesight may dim and our recall may weaken, but, by comparison, our ability to produce and to 4 language is well preserved into older adulthood.?
1 Indeed, the latest research that has emerged on language and aging shows that language mastery is a 5 that we begin as infants and continue on for the rest of our lives.? 2 Some aspects of our language abilities, such as our knowledge of word meanings, 6 improve during middle and late adulthood.? 3 One study, for example, found that adults over sixty had an average vocabulary size of over 21, 000 words. 4 The researchers also studied a 7 of college students and found that their average vocabulary contained 8 16, 000 words.? 5 In another study, older adults, with an average age of 75, 9 better than participants in their youth or middle years on tasks that required them to determine the meaning of words.? 6 Thus, language seems to be a skill that, contrary to what many might 10, does not weaken with age.?

questions.explanation:
【考点】形容词词义辨析及上下文逻辑理解。

【语法分析】此处需要一个形容词来描述莫里森在相关方面的情况，从前面提到莫里森不是早年成功，39 岁才出第一部小说，84 岁出最后一部，再结合后文“Numerous writers produce masterpieces well into their 70s and beyond.”可知，很多作家都有类似大器晚成的情况，所以莫里森在这方面并非“独特的”，要根据语境判断合适的形容词。

【解析】“unique”意为“独特的，独一无二的”，放在句中表明莫里森这种创作生涯的时间跨度情况在众多作家中并非是独一无二的，体现出与后文众多作家情况的呼应，符合上下文逻辑，强调了她并非个例。

【考点】形容词修饰名词及语境搭配。

【语法分析】空后是“accomplishments”，需要一个形容词来修饰它，前文一直在讲作家们创作作品相关的内容，也就是文学方面的成就，所以要选择一个能体现“文学”属性的形容词来准确描述这些成就。

【解析】“literary”表示“文学的”，“literary accomplishments”意思是“文学成就”，很贴合语境，明确指出了这些成就是属于文学领域的，使表达更准确地围绕文章核心话题 —— 作家与语言创作展开。

【考点】动词词义及句子逻辑关系把握。

【语法分析】空前是“does not seem to”，所以需要填一个动词原形，根据后文“Our eyesight may dim and our recall may weaken, but...”可知，这里是在将语言能力与视力、记忆力进行对比，说明语言能力不像视力、记忆力那样会随着年龄“变差”，要找符合这种逻辑关系且表示能力变差意思的动词。

【解析】“deteriorate”的意思是“恶化，退化，变差”，填入此处正契合语境，表明语言能力并没有随着年龄增长而出现像视力、记忆力那样衰退的情况，准确传达了句子通过对比想要表达的核心意思，完善了句子的逻辑。

【考点】动词形式及与并列结构的搭配

【语法分析】空前的“to”提示这里需要填一个动词原形，与前面的“to produce”构成并列结构，从语言能力的角度来说，与“产生”语言相对应且符合语境的就是“理解”语言，所以要找出能表达“理解”含义的动词，使句子结构和表意都完整合理。

【解析】“comprehend”有“理解，领会”的意思，“to produce and to comprehend language” 表示“产生和理解语言”，这样的表述完整地阐述了我们在语言方面的两种重要能力，既符合语法上的并列要求，又与上下文关于语言能力的描述相契合。

【考点】名词词义与上下文语境的契合度。

【语法分析】空前有“a”，需要填一个可数名词单数，从后文“we begin as infants and continue on for the rest of our lives”的描述来看，是把语言掌握比喻成一个从婴儿时期开始并贯穿一生的过程，所以要选择一个能形象体现这种长期、持续过程的名词。

【解析】“journey”意为“旅程，行程”，用在这里将语言掌握比作一场持续一生的旅程，生动形象地展现了语言学习是一个长期不间断的过程，符合语境对语言掌握特点的描述，使表达更具画面感和感染力。

【考点】副词对句子意思的强调与修饰作用。

【语法分析】此空需要一个副词来修饰动词“improve”，结合语境，是想强调语言能力的某些方面，比如对词义的了解，在中年和晚年时期“实际上”是会提高的，要选择一个能突出这种强调实际情况的副词来准确传达文意。

【解析】“actually”表示“实际上，事实上”，放在此处就是为了着重表明语言能力的部分方面在相应阶段确实会有提高这一真实情况，起到了加强语气、让读者更明确语言能力发展实际状况的作用，使句子表意更精准。

【考点】名词在具体语境中的合理运用。

【语法分析】空前有“a”，所以要填一个可数名词单数，联系上下文，研究人员是在对某类群体进行研究并作对比，提到了大学生群体，这里应该是说研究了大学生的一个“样本”，以此来和前面提到的成年人情况进行对比，进而阐述语言能力相关内容，要根据这种科研描述的逻辑来选择合适的名词。

【解析】“sample”的意思是“样本，样品”，“a sample of college students”即“大学生的一个样本”，符合科研中常见的选取部分对象进行研究的表达方式，清晰地说明了研究对象的范围情况，使整个研究过程在文中的表述更严谨合理。

【考点】副词修饰数量词的准确性把握。

【语法分析】此处需要一个副词来修饰后面的数字“16,000”，从语义角度理解，是在说大学生平均词汇量大概是这个数量，所以要选择一个表示“大约、近似”意思的副词来准确体现对数量的估计情况，使表达符合实际情况和语言习惯。

【解析】“approximately”意为“大约，近似地”，用在此处恰当地修饰了数字，表明所提及的大学生平均词汇量只是一个大致的数值，符合在描述统计数据时常用的表达方式，让读者能清楚知晓这是一个估算的情况，使语言表达更科学准确。

【考点】动词时态及在语境中对行为表现的描述。

【语法分析】空处是句子的谓语动词，根据上下文语境，这里是在比较不同年龄段的人在一些要求确定词义的任务中的表现情况，前面的主语是“older adults”，结合语境需要用一般过去时来体现具体的行为表现，所以要选择一个合适的动词来准确描述这种表现行为。

【解析】“performed”是“perform”的过去式，“perform”有“表现，执行”等含义，“performed better”表示“表现得更好”，该词准确地描述了老年人在相应任务中的行为表现情况，符合整个句子比较不同年龄段人群表现的语境要求，同时也遵循了语法上的时态规则。

【考点】动词词义及与上下文逻辑的连贯性。

【语法分析】空前是“might”，需要填一个动词原形，从全文来看，一直在阐述语言能力并不会像很多人想的那样随年龄减弱，这里就是在说与很多人主观“认为”的情况相反，所以要选择一个表示“认为、假定” 意思的动词来体现这种人们的主观想法与实际情况的对比。

【解析】“assume”意思是“假定，认为”，放在句中表明语言能力与很多人所认为的会随年龄减弱的情况相反，实际上并不如此，使句子完整地表达出了通过对比反驳大众错误认知的逻辑，让文章的结论更具说服力，符合上下文的整体表意逻辑。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 For all the innovation and choice that define the food and drink industries, if you want to make money, you could do a lot worse than fill a bottle with water and sell it. 2 A litre of tap water, the stuff we have cleverly piped into our homes, costs less than half a penny. 3 A litre of bottled water can cost well over a pound, especially for something fancy that has been sucked through a mountain.?
1 Yet the bottled water market is livelier than ever. 2 It defies our increasing awareness of the harm plastics do to the environment and a broader, growing sense that something has to change. 3 Sales in the UK were worth a record £558.4 million this past year, an increase of 7%, according to the latest figures from the market analyst Kantar.? 4 Separate data from other analysts show that last year the British consumed more than 2.2 billion litres of bottled water, including “take-home” and “on-the-go” products. 5 That's an annual rise in volume of 8.5%.
1 Environmental campaigners are struggling to understand why nations blessed with clean tap water grow only fonder of the bottle. 2 “It's very surprising to me,” says Sam Chetan-Walsh, a political adviser at Greenpeace and campaigner against ocean plastic. 3 “Public awareness has never been higher, but the message is not quite reaching all the people it needs to.” 4 Where it is heard, the message is causing concern. 5 Plastic water bottles require oceans of fossil fuels to make and ship. 6 Additionally, single-use plastics of all types are polluting our cities and seas.? 7 Numerous documentaries have shown how plastic is ultimately killing wildlife.
1 Moves against various plastics have gathered pace, from shopping bags to straws and plastic-lined coffee cups. 2 Chetan-Walsh argues that bottled water is different because the alternatives are so obvious. 3 “If a product that is so nakedly unnecessary can exist, then the whole system is failing,” he says.
1 Hope is not entirely out of reach. 2 The rate of growth has begun to ease (sales were up 7% in the year, compared with 8% the previous year).?
1 But even if large numbers of people are quitting bottled water because of care for the environment, others are taking it up. 2 The introduction of the “sugar tax” on juices and soda drinks has pushed more people to bottled water, while health awareness has boosted its desirability.? 3 Tap water consumption is growing at roughly the same pace (UK consumers still drink almost three times as much tap water as bottled water).
1 So the plastic tide only creeps higher. 2 The industry is quick to point out that all its bottles are recyclable. 3 “But collection rates are, at the most generous estimates, 56%, so the actual recycling rate will be lower than that,” Chetan-Walsh says. 4 And while bottles may be recyclable, very few are made of recycled plastic. 5 One water bottle company launched recycled half-litre “eco” bottles alongside its standard bottles. 6 Another has pledged to use only recycled plastic across its range by 2025. 7 Chetan-Walsh believes in a ban on single-use bottles. 8 Bans do exist in some places. 9 Organisers of a famous music festival announced that water bottles will not be sold this summer. 10 San Francisco has banned them from city property and events. 11 Last year, the UK government set out plans to ban single-use plastic from its estate.?
1 Water bottlers, unsurprisingly, don't support bans. 2 But they raise concerns about health rather than profit margins. 3 Last month one chief executive of a water bottling company said that bans would “result in greater consumption of sugary drinks, adding to all the health dangers of obesity, diabetes and tooth decay”.? 4 Kinvara Carey, general manager of an association of the biggest bottled water manufacturers, cites a survey in which people were asked what they would do if bottled water were not available. 5 “Forty-four per cent would buy another drink, which is not great, 14% would go without and 4.5% said they would find a fountain,” she says. 6 “The choice is important.”
1 What if fountains were more numerous, and tap water more clearly available in cafes, restaurants and elsewhere? 2 Dozens of fountains are being installed in London. 3 There are similar initiatives elsewhere. 4 Before plastic and the marketing that made people think they needed bottled water in the first place, fountains were an urban fixture.? 5 Greenpeace, among others, is also pushing for a “deposit return” scheme. 6 This would mean tax on bottled water would be refunded to customers who returned the plastic for recycling.
1 Even if bottled water sales are growing slightly more slowly, the industry is racing to adapt to changing concerns and tastes. 2 Flavoured water is booming: sales of the sparkling variety shot up by 20%, according to the latest analyst data. 3 Meanwhile, international water brands, as well as a range of new companies, are selling high-end reusable bottles. 4 And if you must fill them with tap water, why not add flavouring?
1 As the owner of multiple sugary drink brands and bottled water, PepsiCo is facing challenges on health and environmental fronts. 2 Last year, the company bought SodaStream (a drinks company that sells machines for making tap water bubbly and then consumers add flavours) for $3.2 billion. 3 It also launched a range of fancy bottles that work with tap water and flavour packets.? 4 The bottle is reusable. 5 The packets? 6 Not so much, and, yes, they are made of plastic, although the company invites users to post them back for recycling.
1 As is so often the case, clever marketing can beat reason; awareness is rarely enough. 2 “There is always this kind of slip between concern, intent and changed behaviour,” says Giles Quick, an analyst of bottled water. 3 “The best example is five a day, the recommendation to have at least five portions of fruit and vegetables every day. 4 Almost everyone is aware of this, but something like 15% of us achieve it.” 5 Unless a far-reaching bottle ban does come into force, it will be up to consumers to not only demand change—but to act themselves.?

questions.explanation:
【定位】题目 “Judging from the slowing rate of sales growth（从销售增长速度放缓判断）” 与段落 E 中 “The rate of growth has begun to ease (sales were up 7% in the year, compared with 8% the previous year)（增长速度开始放缓（今年销售额增长 7%，去年增长 8%））” 相匹配。这里 “slowing rate” 对应 “rate of growth has begun to ease”，都体现了销售增长速度的变化。同时，“there is still hope to combat bottled water（仍有希望对抗瓶装水）” 与段落 E 所表达的虽然增长速度放缓，但存在改变的可能性，暗示了对抗瓶装水的希望。

【解析】段落 E 通过描述增长速度的放缓，表明了在这种情况下存在对抗瓶装水的希望，所以答案为 E。

【定位】题目 “Bottled water manufacturers base their arguments against bans of plastic bottles（瓶装水制造商反对塑料瓶禁令的论点）”与段落 H 中“Water bottlers, unsurprisingly, don't support bans（瓶装水商不支持禁令）” 相对应。“base their arguments on health concern rather than on profit（基于健康担忧而非利润）”与段落 H 中 “but they raise concern about health rather than profit margin（但他们提出的是关于健康而非利润率的担忧）” 匹配。这里 “health concern” 对应 “concern about health”，“profit” 对应“profit margin”，清晰表明了制造商反对禁令是基于健康方面的考虑。

【解析】段落 H 明确阐述了瓶装水制造商反对禁令的理由是基于健康担忧，而非利润，符合题目要求，所以答案为 H。

【定位】题目“Sales of bottled water in Britain hit a record high last year（英国去年瓶装水销售额创历史新高）” 与段落 B 中 “Sales in the UK were worth a record £558.4 million this past year（英国去年销售额达到创纪录的 5.584 亿英镑）” 相匹配。“even though people are increasingly aware that plastics are environmentally unfriendly（尽管人们越来越意识到塑料对环境不友好）”与段落 B 中“It defies our increasing awareness of the harm plastics do to the environment（它无视我们对塑料对环境危害日益增长的认识）” 相匹配。这里“increasingly aware”对应 “increasing awareness”，“environmentally unfriendly” 对应“harm plastics do to the environment”，体现了在人们环保意识增强的情况下瓶装水销售额依然增长的情况。

【解析】段落B描述了英国瓶装水市场活跃，尽管人们对塑料危害环境的意识增强，但销售额仍创历史新高，与题目表述一致，所以答案为B。

【定位】题目 “It often happens that people can lack reason when faced with skillful marketing（人们在面对巧妙的市场营销时往往缺乏理性）” 与段落 L 中 “As is so often the case, clever marketing can beat reason; awareness is rarely enough（通常情况下，巧妙的市场营销可以战胜理性；意识往往不足以改变行为）” 相匹配。这里 “lack reason” 对应 “beat reason”，“skillful marketing” 对应 “clever marketing”，都表达了在营销面前人们理性缺失的情况。

【解析】段落 L 通过阐述巧妙营销对人们理性的影响，表明了人们在面对营销时缺乏理性的现象，符合题目要求，所以答案为 L。

【定位】题目 “One city on the west coast of America（美国西海岸的一个城市）” 与段落 G 中 “San Francisco（旧金山）” 相匹配。“has banned single - use bottles from its property and events（已禁止在其财产和活动中使用一次性瓶子）” 与段落 G 中 “San Francisco has banned them from city property and events（旧金山已禁止在城市财产和活动中使用它们）” 相匹配。这里 “single - use bottles” 对应 “them”，“property and events” 对应 “city property and events”，明确指出了旧金山这个城市禁止一次性瓶子的情况。

【解析】段落 G 描述了旧金山禁止一次性瓶子的情况，与题目所描述的美国西海岸城市禁止一次性瓶子的内容相符，所以答案为 G。

【定位】题目 “Manufacturing and shipping of plastic water bottles（塑料水瓶的制造和运输）” 与段落 C 中 “Plastic water bottles require oceans of fossil fuel to make and ship（塑料水瓶需要大量化石燃料来制造和运输）” 相匹配。“consume a tremendous amount of fossil fuels（消耗大量的化石燃料）” 与段落 C 中 “require oceans of fossil fuel（需要大量化石燃料）” 相匹配。这里 “consume” 对应 “require”，“tremendous amount” 对应 “oceans”，体现了塑料水瓶制造和运输对化石燃料的消耗情况。

【解析】段落 C 明确阐述了塑料水瓶制造和运输消耗大量化石燃料这一事实，与题目表述一致，所以答案为 C。

【定位】题目 “One large beverage company（一家大型饮料公司）” 与段落 K 中 “PepsiCo（百事公司）” 相匹配。“has adapted its operations（调整了其运营）” 与段落 K 中 “is facing challenges on health and environmental fronts... It also launched a range of fancy bottles（正面临健康和环境方面的挑战…… 它还推出了一系列高档瓶子）” 相匹配。这里 “adapted its operations” 对应 “launched a range of fancy bottles”，体现了百事公司在面对挑战时做出的运营调整。

【解析】段落 K 以百事公司为例说明了大型饮料公司在面对健康和环保挑战时调整运营的情况，符合题目要求，所以答案为 K。

【定位】题目 “Bottled water is considerably more expensive than tap water（瓶装水比自来水贵得多）” 与段落 A 中 “A litre of tap water, the stuff we have cleverly piped into our homes, costs less than half a penny. A litre of bottled water can cost well over a pound（一升自来水，我们巧妙地用管道输送到家中的那种东西，成本不到半便士。一升瓶装水的价格可能远远超过一英镑）” 相匹配。这里 “considerably more expensive” 对应 “cost well over a pound”，“tap water” 对应 “a litre of tap water”，通过具体价格对比体现出瓶装水比自来水贵得多的情况。

【解析】段落 A 通过对瓶装水和自来水价格的描述，表明了瓶装水比自来水贵得多，与题目表述一致，所以答案为 A。

【定位】题目 “Fountains could be seen in cities before bottled water became popular（在瓶装水流行之前，城市中可以看到喷泉）” 与段落 I 中 “Before plastic and the marketing that made people think they needed bottled water in the first place, fountains were an urban fixture（在塑料以及让人们认为他们首先需要瓶装水的市场营销出现之前，喷泉是城市的一部分）” 相匹配。这里 “before bottled water became popular” 对应 “Before plastic and the marketing that made people think they needed bottled water”，“fountains” 对应 “fountains”，体现了在瓶装水流行之前城市中喷泉存��的情况。

【解析】段落 I 描述了瓶装水流行前城市中喷泉的情况，与题目表述一致，所以答案为 I。

【定位】题目 “More people have taken to bottled water（越来越多的人开始饮用瓶装水）” 与段落 F 中 “the introduction of the “sugar tax” on juices and soda drinks has pushed more people to bottled water（对果汁和汽水饮料征收 “糖税” 促使更多人选择瓶装水）” 相匹配。“because of their health awareness（由于健康意识）” 与段落 F 中 “while health awareness has boosted its desirability（而健康意识也提高了它的吸引力）” 相匹配。这里 “health awareness” 对应 “health awareness”，体现了健康意识对人们选择瓶装水的推动作用。

【解析】段落 F 说明了健康意识是促使人们选择瓶装水的因素之一，符合题目所表达的因果关系，所以答案为 F。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 The weakening of the human connection to nature might be good for economic growth but is bad for people. 2 A tipping point was reached in 2020 when human-made materials — such as steel, concrete and plastic — were found to weigh more than all life on Earth. 3 Continuing to grow concrete forests rather than real ones is shortsighted. 4 Simply being in the nearest wood has such health benefits that the Woodland Trust successfully lobbied for it to be prescribed by doctors.?
1 Yet slipping from popular culture is the wonder and beauty of the natural world. 2 For every three nature-related words in hit songs of the 1950s, researchers found, there was only slightly more than one 50 years later.? 3 It is not a moment too soon that teenagers will be able to take a natural history test, given that for decades children have been able to name more video game characters than wildlife species.
1 Part of remedying this social disease would be for parliament to pass a "right to grow" law, allowing anyone to turn underused public spaces into vegetable and fruit gardens. 2 The idea is for people to get back in touch with the soil — while producing food sustainably.?
1 Vegetable planting has a respectable tradition. 2 In April 1649, locals responded to high prices and food shortages by cultivating vegetables on common land in Southern England. 3 The practice of throwing seed bombs to turn vacant plots of land green took off in 1970s New York, and has been revived (使复活) by green-thumbed (有园艺才能的) social media influencers who defy local US regulations in a war on ugly spots in cities.?
1 Apart from the urgent task of providing more healthy nutrients to those who increasingly can't afford them, publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens connect what we eat to where it comes from — the means of production, if you will. 2 They can make unlovely spaces lovely, and marry use and beauty as well as help promote a sense of community.? 3 Plants are also, of course, our first defence against species loss and climate change. 4 Such planting is a small step for humanity — in the right direction.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The year 2020 was a big turning point in human history.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Economic growth benefits people little in the long run.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature.

questions.explanation:
根据题干可知，本题考察作者在第一段想要强调的内容，根据题干中的定位关键词：in the first paragraph可以定位到文章第一段整体进行分析。
1段1句：该句提出观点——人类与自然联系的减弱对人类有害（The weakening of the human connection to nature .... but is bad for people.)

1段2句：递进，通过举例进一步说明人类与自然联系的减弱是如何对人类有害的，即：这个转折点是人造材料的重量被发现超过了地球上所有生物的重量（...when human-made materials...were found to weigh more than all life on Earth.)

1段3句：作者明确表示对这种现象的看法，即：继续发展混凝土森林而非真实森林是目光短浅的（“Continuing to grow concrete forests rather than real ones is shortsighted.）

1段4句：递进，指出人类与自然联系产生的益处，即：仅仅身处最近的树林中就有诸多健康益处（Simply being in the nearest wood has such health benefits）。
综上可知，本段中，作者重点强调的是人类与自然联系减弱是不明智的这一观点（1段1句），即 “It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature.（减弱人类与自然的联系是不明智的。）”，C 选项与之契合，所以是正确答案。

questions.explanation:
依据题干中的 “researchers”“popular culture” 可定位到文中2段1句：“Yet slipping from popular culture is the wonder and beauty of the natural world.

2段1句：通过转折（Yet）指出，自然世界的奇妙与美丽（the wonder and beauty of the natural world）正在从流行文化中逐渐消失（slipping from popular culture）

2段2句：递进，详细说明研究人员的发现内容：在 20 世纪 50 年代的热门歌曲中（For every three nature-related words in hit songs of the 1950s），每有三个与自然相关的词汇（For every three nature-related words in hit songs of the 1950s），50 年后就只有略多于一个了（there was only slightly more than one 50 years later）。

综上可知，流行文化（popular culture）正日益脱离自然世界，A 选项 “It is increasingly detached from the natural world.（它日益脱离自然世界。）” 准确反映了这一情况，所以是正确答案。

questions.explanation:
题干问作者（author）提议（propose）人们做什么，根据题干所问，结合顺序出题原则，可以定位到3段寻找相关提议信息。
3段1句指出：解决这一社会问题的部分办法（Part of remedying this social disease）是议会通过‘种植权’法律（for parliament to pass a "right to grow" law），允许任何人（allowing anyone）将未充分利用的公共空间变成果蔬园（to turn underused public spaces into vegetable and fruit gardens）。

3段2句：递进指出这样做的目的（The idea is for...），即：让人们重新与土地建立联系（people to get back in touch with the soil），同时可持续地生产食物（while producing food sustainably）
综上可知，作者提议人们通过 “种植权”（a "right to grow"）来重新与自然建立联系（get back in touch with the soil），故B 选项 “Reconnect with nature through the right to grow.（通过‘种植权’与自然重新建立联系。）” 符合文意，为正确答案。

4段1句指出：种植蔬菜（Vegetable planting）有着值得尊敬的传统（a respectable tradition）。

4段2句：递进，具体说明种植蔬菜（cultivating vegetables）在过去的历史功用，即：应对物价高涨和食物短缺（responded to high prices and food shortages）

4段3句：举例，提出纽约让闲置土地变绿的做法（to turn vacant plots of land green），即：投掷种子炸弹（The practice of throwing seed bombs），并且这种做法已经被复兴了（has been revived (使复活) by...）。

综上可知，蔬菜种植长久以来都被用于增加食物供应以及改善城市景观，C 选项 “It has long been used to increase food supply and improve urban landscape.（它长期以来一直被用于增加食物供应和改善城市景观。）” 符合文意，是正确答案。

questions.explanation:
根据题干中的“publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens”，“apart from”定位到文章的5段1句：Apart from（原词复现） the urgent task of providing more healthy nutrients to those who increasingly can't afford them, publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens（原词复现） connect what we eat to where it comes from — the means of production, if you will.

5段1句指出：除了为那些越来越买不起健康营养食品的人提供更多健康营养这一紧迫任务外，公共果蔬园（publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens）将我们所吃的食物与它的来源 —— 也就是生产方式 —— 联系起来（connect what we eat to where it comes from）。但该句提出的是题干中所提及的公共果蔬园的实用功效（practical functions），并非题干所问的apart from，故应继续阅读下句。

5段2句递进，继续指出公共果蔬园的其他好处，即：它们可以让不美观的空间变得美观（make unlovely spaces lovely），将使用价值与美观相结合（marry use and beauty），并且有助于提升社区感（as well as help promote a sense of community）。）”
综上可知，所以公共果蔬园除了实际功能外，还能够增强人们的社区精神，D 选项 “Enhance people's community spirit.（增强人们的社区精神。）” 符合文意，为正确答案。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 Engineering in the U.S. has long been a male-dominated profession. 2 Fifty years ago, it looked like that might change.
1 In 1970, the percentage of women majoring in engineering was less than 1%. 2 In 1979, that number was 9%.? 3 Many hoped women would continue to enter the field at the same rate. 4 But that's not what happened. 5 Today, only 21% of engineering majors are women, a number largely unchanged since 2000.
1 I am a historian who, along with my colleagues, surveyed 251 women engineers who graduated from college in the 1970s. 2 These pioneers reflected on the challenges they faced and had advice for women entering the field today.
1 One survey taker explained, "The greatest challenge for me was continuing to believe in myself, when all the messages I was getting were that I would never be taken seriously or promoted or given raises at the same rate as men, who were clearly less qualified and not as smart as I was."?
1 A chemical engineer who worked in manufacturing agreed, "You have to prove yourself just because you are female. 2 And you have to work twice as hard!"
1 A civil engineer said, "We are women engineers. 2 People don't refer to a man as a 'man engineer' — he's an engineer. 3 We are constantly reminded that we don't truly belong." 4 Another civil engineer stated, "On many levels, you're never quite one of the group."?
1 Women also talked about family caregiving responsibilities. 2 A retired vice president from a major chemical company stated, "Young women engineers are on an equal footing until they have children, then they struggle to balance work and family and compete with men who don't have the same household responsibilities."
1 But over the years things have changed a lot. 2 Young women engineers are more accepted mostly because there are just more of them.?
1 Many women engineers hailed the benefits of their chosen career. 2 A program manager in manufacturing stated that engineering is the best degree. 3 A mechanical engineer said, "It will give you the flexibility to do almost anything. 4 It is also satisfying to see the effects of what you have done."?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It has seen a change in attitude towards women engineers since 1979.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It witnessed a significant increase in women engineers in the 1970s.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It has experienced the gradual weakening of male dominance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It boasted the largest number of engineering majors in 2000.

questions.explanation:
根据题干中的the engineering profession in the United States定位在1段1句的Engineering in the U.S（原词复现） has long been a male-dominated profession部分。

1段1句指出：工程学在美国长期以来一直是一个男性主导的职业（Engineering in the U.S. has long been a male-dominated profession）。1段2句提出，在过去的50年，这种现象似乎发生了变化（it looked like that might change）。

2段1句，承接1段2句，先指���过去的情况：20世纪70年代（In 1970）,主修工程学的女性所占比例不到 1%（the percentage of women majoring in engineering was less than 1%）.

2段2句提出变化结果，即：到了 1979 年，这一数字达到了 9%（In 1979, that number was 9%）。

综上可知，美国工程学专业长期以来一直由男性主导，女性占比很低且变化不大。比对各个选项可知，B选项（它在20世纪70年代见证了女性工程师的大幅增加）与原文的2段1句中的In 1970, the percentage of women majoring in engineering was less than 1%. In 1979, that number was 9%对应，为正确答案。

choices.label: A

根据题干中的one survey taker，her greatest challenge定位在4段1句：One survey taker（原词复现） explained, "The greatest challenge for me（原词复现） was continuing to believe in myself, when all the messages I was getting were that I would never be taken seriously or promoted or given raises at the same rate as men, who were clearly less qualified and not as smart as I was."

4段1句指出：一位调查对象（one survey taker）认为她最大的挑战（The greatest challenge for me）是继续相信自己（continuing to believe in myself），尤其是在她收到的所有信息都是她永远不会被认真对待（when all the messages I was getting were that I would never be taken seriously），或者以与男性相同的速度晋升或加薪时（or promoted or given raises at the same rate as men），而男性显然比她资格差且不如她聪明（who were clearly less qualified and not as smart as I was）。

综上可知，一位调查对象认为她最大的挑战是，在不断收到负面信息的情况下，继续相信自己。比对各个选项可知，D选项（尽管经常受到打击或不公平对待，也不要失去自信）与原文的continuing to believe in myself对应，为正确答案。

根据题干中的定位关键词the two civil engineers定位在6段：A civil engineer（定位词同义替换） said, "We are women engineers. People don't refer to a man as a 'man engineer'—he's an engineer. We are constantly reminded that we don't truly belong." Another civil engineer（定位词同义替换） stated, "On many levels, you're never quite one of the group."

6段1-3句，为题目所问其中一位工程师的观点，其指出：“我们是女性工程师（We are women engineers）。人们不会把男性称作‘男工程师’（People don't refer to a man as a 'man engineer'）。我们总是被提醒着（We are constantly reminded），我们并非真正属于这个群体（that we don't truly belong）。

6段4句指出：另一位土木工程师说，“在很多层面上（On many levels），你从来都不是群体中的一员”（you're never quite one of the group）。

综上可知，女性工程师经常感到自己被排除在群体之外。比对各个选项可知，B选项（被排除在群体之外）与原文的you're never quite one of the group对应，为正确答案。

8段2句进一步指出具体变化是：年轻的女性工程师更容易被接纳了（Young women engineers are more accepted），主要是因为她们的人数增多了（mostly because there are just more of them）。

综上可知，年轻女性工程师现在更被接受的原因是她们的人数增加了。比对各个选项可知，D选项（她们人数的增加）与原文的mostly because there are just more of them对应，为正确答案。

综上可知，许多女性工程师认为她们的职业具有灵活性，并且看到自己工作成果的效果令人满意。比对各个选项可知，A选项（她们对自己的职业感到非常自豪）与原文的It will give you the flexibility to do almost anything. It is also satisfying to see the effects of what you have done对应，为正确答案。

sections.title: 听力

Across the U.S., families are looking to the winter with fear as energy costs soar.
A number of factors are creating a bad situation: Global energy consumption is up, but supplies have been reduced.
The Energy Department projects heating bills will jump 28% this winter for those who rely on natural gas.
Natural gas is used by nearly half of U.S. households for heat.
Heating oil is projected to be 27% higher and electricity 10% higher.
That comes against inflation rates that accelerated last month with consumer prices growing 6.6%.
That's the fastest pace in four decades.
The pain will be especially acute in parts of the country that heavily rely on heating oil to keep homes warm.
It's projected to cost more than $2,300 to heat a typical home with heating oil this winter.
Last month, the federal government added $1 billion in funding to Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, bringing the total to $4.8 billion.
But that represents a reduction from last year's energy assistance package of over $8 billion.
Why are families across the U.S. looking to this winter with fear?
What did the federal government do last month?
Many Americans think they make healthy food choices, but they may be viewing their diet too optimistically.
That's the main finding of a new study by researchers at the U.S. Department of Agriculture in Stoneville, Mississippi.
The study aimed to identify disconnects between how healthily Americans think they eat and how they actually do.
For the study, the researchers asked participants to rate their diet as excellent, very good, good, fair or poor.
Folks also completed 24-hour food questionnaires.
Then, the researchers compared answers to see how well responses to the two exercises matched up.
Of more than 9,700 people, roughly 85 percent were off base when asked to rate the quality of their diet, and almost all overestimated how healthy it was.
Those who rated their diet as poor tended to be far more accurate.
Their rating match that of the researchers more than nine times out of ten.
What is the main finding of a new study about many Americans?
Who tended to rate their diet more accurately in the survey?
It was a heartwarming moment that dozens of Indian rescuers rallied together to use a crane in order to save an elephant trapped at the bottom of a 20-foot well.
The massive rescue effort took place last week close to an army camp.
The elephant wandered out of the jungle and fell into the well.
The army officers had a noise coming from the well and realized an elephant was trapped deep inside.
The officers then threw in some food for the creature and called the local forest department for help.
Video of the rescue operation shows how the team used a crane to lift up the huge animal out of the well and onto the back of a truck.
It was then taken to an examining room for evaluation of any injuries.
The elephant was kept under close supervision for a few days before it was successfully released back into the wild.
What does the report say dozens of Indians did last week?
Why did the army officers call the local forest department?
What does the news report say happened finally?
I need to stop at the bank to withdraw some cash.
Why not just pay with your phone?
Well, actually I've stopped using online payments for the past three months now.
Stopped paying online?
Oh, you must be worried that online payments aren't secure.
No, they are safe.
But paying online is too convenient and I spent too much money on things I didn't need.
Oh, impulse purchases can be an issue for me, too.
I've definitely bought lots of clothes and shoes I didn't need because they were on sale, and paying with my phone was so easy.
But I've found that if I review my spending every night, that keeps me from spending too much.
I tried that strategy, but it just didn't work, because I'd be busy studying all day.
Then when I'm tired and hungry, I'd use my phone to order food, like burgers and other junk, instead of going to the canteen, where I could get a healthier meal for half the price.
Well, what do you do now then?
It seems like you'd have this same problems with cash.
I go to the bank once a week, and the rest of the time I keep my bank card at home, so I can't get more cash out.
And I also have a notebook where I record my expenses.
But what prevents you from just going to the bank and getting more money, if you want to buy something?
The first month I did withdraw extra cash twice, but I felt guilty about it.
And after that I refused to spend more than what I had budgeted, and by now it's just a habit.
Why has the man stopped paying online for the last three months?
What problem does the woman say she may also have?
What does the man say he could do at the canteen?
What is now just a habit for the man?
Please hear me out.
I don't want our son to spend his afternoons doing something he hates, even if it might prepare him for the future.
What about getting him join a sport, like soccer?
From all the running and training, he could become quite athletic.
Not to mention the great physical benefits from exercising outside every day.
Um, I don't think he should be doing something so challenging with all his breathing issues.
What about playing an indoor sport, like badminton?
The environment is easier to control, and he can still get a good workout, in addition to improving his hand-eye coordination.
Besides, I could teach him some of the basics from my time as a badminton player.
Um, I'm thinking team sports should be the way to go.
There's nothing like playing as part of a unit to accomplish a goal like winning a game or even a championship.
He could try basketball since many of the courts are indoors now and it's a sport that could help him understand team spirit while cooperating with others.
May be he could even join the school basketball team when he's ready.
Oh, oh, what about volleyball?
It's a team sport and they often have mixed-gender teams so he could socialize with both girls and boys.
It's not as popular as some sports, which means he has better odds of possibly getting an athletic scholarship in the future.
I also believe you were a beach volleyball athlete yourself not so long ago.
As I've said many times before, beach volleyball and indoor volleyball are completely different.
Why is the woman opposed to their son joining a sport like soccer?
What does the man suggest their son try in order to understand team spirit?
What is one of the woman's considerations in choosing a sport for her son?
What does the man say about beach volleyball?
Lift-off is usually the most environmentally harmful stage of any space mission, with vast quantities of fuel burnt up in a matter of minutes.
For instance, SpaceX's Falcon 9 gets through 112 tonnes of refined fuel, emitting about 336 tonnes of CO2 .
This is the equivalent produced by your average car driving almost 70 times around the world.
This is the equivalent produced by your average car driving almost 70 times around the world.
These issues are growing more pressing with the emergence of commercial spaceflight.
There were 114 space launches in 2020, but there may be up to 1,000 per year in future.
Sustainable fuels are the top priority to enable greener space travel.
Current spacecraft use a variety of fuels, but most are based on fossil fuels.
One potentially greener option is liquid hydrogen and oxygen.
Hydrogen can be obtained sustainably by using solar power to break water down into oxygen and hydrogen.
Reusable rockets can cut down on some of the waste associated with spaceflight.
Traditionally, boosters, fuel tanks and other components are treated as expendable.
But guiding them back to Earth in a controlled manner opens new possibilities — most components from the Falcon 9 can be reused up to 100 times.
Truly environmentally friendly space travel is still some way off.
But we already have many of the technologies needed to start limiting its impact on our planet.
What do we learn from the passage about the lift-off of spacecraft?
What happens traditionally to boosters, fuel tanks and other components in spaceflight?
What does the passage say we already have regarding spaceflight?
Helping to look after a pet can facilitate numerous aspects of a child's emotional development.
Research shows that reading to a loyal and non-judgmental companion, such as a dog or cat, can encourage reluctant readers to read aloud, which will in turn boost their self-confidence.
Having a companion to talk to about their feelings can also help children feel secure and develop communication skills.
A household pet can also cultivate a child's sense of responsibility as their parent explains the necessary processes of keeping their pet happy and healthy.
As a child matures, they can then take on more of the daily responsibilities, boosting their sense of independence.
Pets also provide a fantastic subject for research and learning.
Parents can encourage their child to research their favourite pets at the library or during a supervised internet search.
Taking children along to the pet shop to buy food and supplies will support their cognitive development as their passion for learning flourishes.
A child's physical development can benefit greatly from taking pets for walks in the fresh air.
Even their fine-motor skills can be utilised in taking care of a beloved animal.
When responsibilities are well-paced and communicated, a child can benefit greatly from involvement in bringing up a happy and healthy pet.
And of course, if a child doesn't have a pet in their own household, they can still benefit from all of the above when visiting a friend who does.
What does research show about reading to a loyal and nonjudgmental companion?
How can parents make pets a fantastic subject for their children's research and learning?
How can children still benefit even when their family doesn't have a pet?
A new bill in the Ohio legislature would require state public colleges and universities to send prospective students a packet of information.
This would include costs of college, grants and scholarships.
It would also include expected monthly loan payments and projected salary after college.
State Representative Adam Mathews is one of the two legislators who proposed the bill.
He said it would give prospective students more information about what to expect once they graduate.
"Putting that information in front of them will give them the best opportunity to match their skills and their dreams to what our schools can provide," said Mathews.
He notes that the state can only regulate public institutions in this way, but he hopes private institutions in Ohio follow the lead of the state and post similar information.
He believes giving out this information will help Ohio's colleges and universities to be more competitive.
The information will highlight what a great value they have for their very reasonable cost.
Ohio's schools are already competitive.
The state attracts more undergraduate students than it sends to colleges out of state.
Many colleges and universities currently provide similar information on their websites.
This includes tuition, fees, graduation rates and more.
But students need to search for the information. This bill would require the universities and colleges to send a packet directly to students.
What would the new bill in the Ohio legislature require public colleges and universities to do?
What can the state only do according to Adam Mathews?
What do we learn about Ohio's schools from the passage?
What is the problem with schools providing information on their websites?

questions.explanation: Why are families across the U.S. looking to this winter with fear?为什么美国各地的家庭怀着恐惧迎接这个冬天？【解析】新闻开头提到，随着能源成本的飙升，美国各地的家庭正怀着恐惧迎接这个冬天。接下来的内容具体阐述了今冬取暖费用的上涨情况。新闻提到，能源部预估，对于那些依赖天然气取暖的家庭来说，今年冬天的取暖费将上涨28%。取暖用油的费用预计将高出27%，电费预计将高出10%。这些数据都表明美国家庭担忧的是取暖费用大幅增加，要支付高昂的取暖账单，故选C。选项A表述错误，新闻中提到，依赖天然气取暖的家庭今年冬天的取暖费将上涨28%，而非27%。新闻中虽提到取暖用油的费用预计上涨27%，但依赖取暖用油供暖只是部分美国家庭的情况，故排除B。新闻中只提到消费者价格上涨6.6%，是40年来最快涨幅，并未提及美国家庭将经历40年来最寒冷的冬天，故排除D。

questions.explanation: What did the federal government do last month?联邦政府上个月做了什么？【解析】新闻末尾提到，上个月，联邦政府为低收入家庭能源援助计划增加了10亿美元（added $1 billion）的资金，使该计划的总金额达到48亿美元，故选项A为正确答案。选项中的“additional funding”对应新闻中的“added $1 billion”，同时据此排除选项D。新闻中，联邦政府并未预测今年冬天大多数美国家庭的取暖费上涨幅度，而新闻前半部分提及，能源部对此进行过预估，使用天然气取暖的家庭取暖费涨幅为28%，使用取暖用油供暖的家庭取暖费涨幅为27%，使用电取暖的家庭取暖费涨幅为10%，取暖方式不同，涨幅不同，故排除选项C。选项B新闻并未提及，可排除。

questions.explanation: Who tended to rate their diet more accurately in the survey?在调查中，谁往往能更准确地对自己的饮食进行评级？【解析】新闻末尾提到，这项新研究发现，在调查的9700多人中，大约85%的人在评估自已饮食的品质时是完全错误的，儿乎所有人都高估了自己饮食的健康程度。那些将自己饮食评为“差”的人往往准确得多。由此可知，选项D为正确答案。

questions.explanation: Why is the woman opposed to their son joining a sport like soccer?为什么女士反对他们的儿子参加像足球这样的运动？【解析】在对话开头，男士提议让儿子参加一项运动，比如足球。女士考虑到儿子有呼吸方面的问题，因此她认为他不应该参加像足球这类有挑战性的运动，所以答案是C项。A项张冠李戴，男士提议让儿子踢足球，目的是替换儿子可能讨厌的其他事，由此可知踢足球并非儿子讨厌之事，故排除；B项过度推断，男士只是提及不想让儿子把时间花在可能对未来有帮助但他却讨厌的事上，这一表述并不能合理推断出女士认为儿子必须为将来做准备，故排除；D项曲解信息，女士反对的出发点是儿子的呼吸问题，认为他不适合参与足球这类有挑战性的运动，并非意味着儿子做不了任何有挑战性的事，该项对女士的意思进行了错误解读，故也排除。

What does the man suggest their son try in order to understand team spirit?男士建议他们的儿子尝试什么来理解团队精神？【解析】在对话中，男士指出团队运动对儿子来说是最好的选择，然后他提出了让儿子打篮球的建议，并说明原因，其中一个就是篮球这项运动能够帮助儿子在与他人合作时理解团队精神，所以答案是D项。其他三个选项虽然都在对话中出现了，但不符合本题题意，故均排除。

questions.explanation: What do we learn from the passage about the lift-off of spacecraft?关于航天器的发射，我们从文章中了解到什么？【解析】文章开头提到，发射阶段通常是任何太空任务中对环境危害最大的阶段，大量燃料在几分钟内就会燃烧殆尽。除了温室气体之外，火箭发动机还会排放破坏臭氧层的微粒。由此可知，航天器在发射升空时，既会产生大量温室气体，又会对臭氧层造成损害，选项B与文章内容一致，因此为正确答案。文中提及太空探索技术公司的“猎鹰9号”火箭消耗112吨精炼燃料并排放约336吨二氧化碳这一具体实例，而选项C正是依据此例中的特定数据信息所设置的干扰项，但其不能代表所有航天器发射升空时的普遍情况，且选项中的数据与这一实例也不相符，故排除。根据文章内容，航天器的发射阶段是太空任务中对环境危害最大的阶段，而非最复杂的阶段，故排除选项D。

questions.explanation: How can parents make pets a fantastic subject for their children's research and learning?家长如何能让宠物成为孩子们研究和学习的绝佳主题呢？【解析】文章中提到，宠物也为研究和学习提供了一个绝佳主题。家长可以鼓励孩子去图书馆或在有监管的网络搜索中研究他们最喜欢的宠物。选项A与文章内容一致，因此为正确答案。选项B提到“带孩子们去图书馆借阅有关动物的书籍”，但原文强调的是“鼓励孩子去图书馆”“研究他们最喜欢的宠物”，故排除。选项C表述为“让孩子们自行上网搜索”，而文中明确指出的是“在有监管的网络搜索中…”，该选项忽略了原文中的关键限定条件，故排除。选项D在文章中未提及，也排除。

1 In an era where modernity advances with unprecedented speed, the preservation and promotion of traditional culture are of paramount importance. 【指出现代化下传统文化重要性】 2 To enrich students' knowledge in this area, several strategies can be employed. 【提出丰富学生知识的策略】
1 Firstly, incorporating traditional culture into the school curriculum is essential. 【分论点1-课程融入传统文化】 2 By offering courses in calligraphy, traditional music, and folk arts, students can gain a foundational understanding and appreciation for their cultural heritage. 【说明课程具体内容及作用】 3 Secondly, organizing cultural festivals and events provides students with immersive experiences. 【分论点2-活动提供沉浸式体验】 4 Participating in these activities allows them to connect with traditional practices and fosters a sense of cultural identity. 【阐述活动效果与文化认同】 5 Lastly, utilizing digital platforms to share stories, music, and art from traditional culture can make learning more engaging. 【分论点3-数字平台创新传播】 6 Interactive content can capture students' interest and encourage them to explore further. 【强调互动内容吸引探索】
1 By implementing these methods, we can ensure that traditional culture remains a vibrant part of students' education. 【总结策略保障文化活力】

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 The Mogao Grottoes Digital Exhibition Center in Dunhuang opened in 2014 and is an important part of the Mogao Grottoes conservation and utilization project. 2 The center uses digital technology and multimedia presentation methods to allow visitors to learn about the culture of the Mogao Grottoes and appreciate their artistic masterpieces before entering the caves. 3 This approach limits the number of caves open to the public, reduces the time visitors spend inside the caves, minimizes the impact on the Mogao Grottoes, and ensures that this world cultural heritage is properly protected and utilized for the long term.

questions.stem: ①敦煌莫高窟数字展示中心于2014年开放，是莫高窟保护利用工程的重要组成部分。②展示中心采用数字技术和多媒体展示方式，让游客在进入洞窟参观前了解莫高窟文化。③欣赏其艺术经典，从而限制洞窟的开放数量，缩短游客在洞窟内的停留时间，减少对莫高窟的影响，确保这一世界文化遗产得到妥善保护和长期利用。
questions.answer: 1 The Mogao Grottoes Digital Exhibition Center in Dunhuang opened in 2014 and is an important part of the Mogao Grottoes conservation and utilization project. 2 The center uses digital technology and multimedia presentation methods to allow visitors to learn about the culture of the Mogao Grottoes and appreciate their artistic masterpieces before entering the caves. 3 This approach limits the number of caves open to the public, reduces the time visitors spend inside the caves, minimizes the impact on the Mogao Grottoes, and ensures that this world cultural heritage is properly protected and utilized for the long term.

questions.explanation:
【考点】动词辨析，考查上下文语境中合适动词的选用，需根据句子整体意思及主语与宾语之间的逻辑关系来确定动词形式及含义。

【语法分析】此处句子缺少谓语动词，主语是"New research from biologists at the University of Maryland”（马里兰大学生物学家的新研究），根据上下文语境，需要一个能体现研究得出某种结果或揭示某种情况的动词，且主语为单数，动词应为第三人称单数形式。

【解析】"revealed”意为"揭示，显示”，符合研究揭示新情况的语境，即新研究揭示了视力剥夺也会改变脑细胞相互作用的方式，所以答案是 L。

【考点】动词短语搭配考查，重点在于对"interact with”（与…… 相互作用）这一常用短语的掌握以及在语境中的运用。

【语法分析】"the way brain cells...” 后面是一个定语从句修饰"the way”，在从句中"brain cells” 是主语，缺少谓语动词，结合语境应是表达脑细胞之间相互怎样的意思，"interact with” 是合理的表达相互作用的短语，且符合句子整体结构要求。

【解析】根据句子意思，说的是视力剥夺改变了脑细胞彼此相互作用的方式，"interact” 符合此处表达细胞间互动的语境，答案是 D。

【考点】动词辨析，要根据上下文语义以及句子主语和宾语之间的逻辑关联来选择恰当的动词，且要考虑时态等语法因素。

【语法分析】句子主语"This study”（这项研究）为单数，此处需要一个动词作谓语，根据语境应是表达这项研究对后面提到的内容起到某种作用，结合选项，应选择一个合适的动词原形（因为前面有助动词"does” 构成强调句）。

【解析】"reinforces” 有"加强，强化，印证” 的意思，这里表示这项研究印证了我们正在了解的内容，符合语境，所以答案是 K。

【考点】形容词辨析，考查根据上下文选择合适形容词来修饰名词，以准确表达特定含义。

【语法分析】"a...effect”需要一个形容词来修饰"effect”（影响），根据语境要体现出这种影响是比较重要、显著的意思，来呼应前文关于视力剥夺对听觉产生影响的描述。

【解析】"significant”表示"显著的，重大的”，用在此处能准确表达出操纵视力对动物听觉能力有着显著影响，符合语境要求，答案是 M。

【考点】动词辨析，结合语境判断合适的动词以及其正确的时态形式，要考虑与前面的"have” 构成完成时态的合理搭配。

【语法分析】"have”在这里提示使用完成时态，"window”（窗口期）与所填动词之间应是表达窗口期过去、结束的意思，所以要选择一个符合这种语境且能与"have” 搭配构成现在完成时的动词过去分词形式。

【解析】"closed”作为动词"close”的过去分词，"have closed”表示已经关闭、结束，此处指听觉学习的窗口期被认为已经结束，符合语境，答案是 B。

【考点】形容词辨析，依据上下文理解大脑感官区域的特点描述，选择恰当形容词来符合整体语义逻辑。

【语法分析】"were not...”此处需要一个形容词作表语，根据后文提到儿童时期关键期过后学习语言的情况对比，以及前文关于大脑相关研究的语境，要体现大脑感官区域是否还能改变、调整的特点。

【解析】"adaptable”意为"可适应的，可改变的”，符合此处表达大脑感官区域在儿童关键期后是否还能改变的语境，答案是 A。

【考点】副词辨析，考查根据句子中对儿童和成人学习语言情况对比的描述，选择能准确体现程度差异的副词。

【语法分析】"more...”提示使用副词比较级形式，来修饰动词"learn”（学习），根据语境是要突出儿童学习语言比成人更容易、更轻松的程度差异。

【解析】"readily”表示"容易地，轻松地”，符合儿童学习语言比成人更轻松这一语境，用来体现程度上的对比，答案是 I。

【考点】形容词辨析，根据前文关于大脑听觉皮层根据听到声音进行区域分配的描述，选择合适形容词来修饰"frequencies”（频率）。

【语法分析】"assigning areas of the auditory cortex to...” 中"to” 为介词，后面需要一个形容词修饰"frequencies”，结合语境应是大脑将听觉皮层区域分配给特定的频率，所以要选体现"特定”含义的形容词。

【解析】"specific”意为"特定的，具体的”，符合语境中大脑根据习惯听到的声音把听觉皮层区域分配给特定频率的意思，答案是 N。

【考点】名词辨析，通过对句子整体意思的把握，尤其是关于在成年老鼠身上黑暗环境对不同频率空间情况改变的描述，选择合适的名词。

【语法分析】"the...”提示此处需要一个名词作宾语，根据前文提到的改变等语境，要选择一个能体现空间与不同频率之间某种关系变化的名词。

【解析】"distribution”表示"分布，分配”，这里说在成年老鼠中，在黑暗环境中一周也改变了空间对不同频率的分配情况，符合语境，答案是 C。

【考点】动词辨析，根据前文提到不知道某些模式原因以及后面给出的推测性话语，选择能表达推测含义的动词，且要考虑时态等语法因素。

【语法分析】句子主语"We”，此处缺少谓语动词，结合语境应是表达我们进行推测的意思，要用一般现在时来符合整体描述语境。

【解析】"speculate”意为"推测，猜测”，符合此处我们对看到模式原因进行推测的语境，答案是 O。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Few topics have been so endlessly analyzed as work-life balance. 2 The quest to attain this mysterious state has dominated discussion around careers for years — especially for working parents.? 3 The concept is often presented as something to achieve, or a goal to reach. 4 And once you've reached it, congratulations: you've made it; you're a successful human being of the 21st century.
1 But the problem is that we often tell ourselves:" I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of work, and then I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of 'me time', which will include my family, my hobbies, my workout, my everything," says Anat Lechner, clinical associate professor of management at New York University. 2 "I don't think it's such a simple formula."?
1 And, according to new findings, it may not be. 2 Some researchers are now encouraging us to stop thinking about work-life balance as an achievement that you either hit or don't. 3 Instead, they suggest it may be more of a lifelong process — a continuous, never-ending exercise that requires self-awareness and timely adjustments.? 4 Researchers Ioana Lupu and Mayra Ruiz-Castro argue that work-life balance is"a cycle, not an achievement". 5 In their 2020 study, the researchers interviewed nearly 80 employees at two London-based firms — an equal number of men and women between the ages of 30 and 50, all with at least one dependent child — who worked in middle or senior management roles.
1 Although it sounds like the respondents had a lot in common, here's what separated them: about 30% of the men and 50% of the women reported resisting working long hours. 2 The other respondents, meanwhile, all worked long hours because they thought that's what successful professionals should do.?
1 Lupu and Ruiz-Castro looked at those who rejected the long hours and they found that those workers actually had strikingly similar strategies for maintaining their work-life balance. 2 They had a tendency to reflect and question assumptions in the name of self-awareness and regularly took steps to adjust the things standing in their way to work-life balance.?
1 Lupu and Ruiz-Castro identified five steps that the respondents in the study who had better work-life balance used in their jobs. 2 First, they paused and reconsidered beliefs such as "I'm a professional, so I should work, work, work”, and asked themselves questions like, "What's currently causing me stress?" 3 Second, after identifying the cause, they zeroed in on their resultant emotions. 4 Did they feel angry, sad, energized? 5 Third, they reprioritized, asking "Is working long hours really worth cutting back on family time?”, for example. 6 Fourth, they considered their alternatives: is there anything at work that could be changed to accommodate these new priorities? 7 And finally, they implemented changes, like asking their supervisor for greater flexibility, or deciding not to take on every project that comes their way.
1 This five-step process is something anyone can adopt. 2 Going through the steps, and constantly checking in with yourself, can help you shift and adapt your professional life to something that will better harmonize with your personal one. 3 "Awareness of your emotional state is essential in order to determine the changes you want to make in your work and in your life,” says Lupu.?
1 New York University 's Lechner agrees that finding that balance is an ongoing pursuit. 2 It's not simply about dividing up the hours in your day between work, the gym, kids and chores. 3 If the underlying emotional sources of stress are still there, then the time you actually spend at home may not be enjoyable.? 4 "We come home and even though physically we are there, mentally we may still be processing things that happened at work. 5 We're not present,” she says. 6 What we call "work-life balance” is actually just a substitute to having a sense of fulfillment and contentment.
1 Of course, finding that balance probably shouldn't be something you have to do by yourself. 2 Research by Erin Kelly, professor of work and organization studies at MIT, shows companies and managers can play a key role in creating a better environment for workers. 3 For her book Overload: How Good Jobs Went Bad and What to Do About It, she and co-author Phyllis Moen split more than 1,000 employees at a Fortune 500 company into two groups, one that worked under a management redesign and one that continued working within the existing management structure.
1 Under the management redesign, many steps were taken to ensure better work-life balance and prevent burnout. 2 Managers were regularly reminded to explicitly support their employees. 3 Workers were allowed to make changes, like cancelling 9 am meetings. 4 All of this was done in the name of increasing job satisfaction and giving workers greater flexibility, and to assure workers that it was something management was committed to.? 5 Unsurprisingly, Kelly and Moen found that employees in the redesign group reported less stress and less burnout. 6 They were less likely to quit their jobs; indeed, over the next four years, they were 40% less likely to quit than those who kept working under the old policies.
1 "Work-life balance is understood to be an individual's response, so people think ‘it's up to me to manage the craziness of my work life’,” says Kelly. 2 But organizations need to examine the demands they're placing on employees. 3 "The root problem is not how the two pieces of work and life come together.? 4 It's that we have unrealistic expectations of what we're asked to do on the work side.” 5 If your workplace isn't an environment where work-life balance is possible in the first place, any effort you attempt to make toward it on a personal level will be in vain.
1 That's a conversation that appears to be gathering pace. 2 The new prevalence of remote and flexible working models will likely all play important roles in how we balance our professional and personal lives. 3 And if it seems like finding that perfect balance remains difficult to achieve, the experts say that keeping some perspective can help. 4 For millions of people, work is about being able to put food on the table. 5 Talking about work-life balance"is a very privileged conversation,” says Lechner.? 6 "If we're reflecting, maybe we should also reflect on that.”

questions.explanation:
【定位】题目中"According to a management expert” 与原文中"says Anat Lechner, clinical associate professor of management” 对应，都表明是管理学专家的观点；"work-life balance is not as simple as” 与原文中"I don't think it's such a simple formula” 对应，都表达了工作与生活的平衡并非简单之事；"giving equal amounts of time to work and personal life” 与原文中"I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of work, and then I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of 'me time'” 对应，都是在说给工作和个人生活分配时间。

【解析】段落 B 中 Anat Lechner 教授的观点与题目表述一致，明确指出工作与生活的平衡不是简单地给工作和个人生活分配时间，所以答案是 B。

【定��】"Research found that” 与原文中"Kelly and Moen found that” 对应，都表示研究发现；"those who are given greater flexibility at work” 与"Workers were allowed to make changes...giving workers greater flexibility” 对应，都指工作中被给予更大灵活性的员工；"less stressed and more likely to stay in their jobs” 与"reported less stress...they were 40% less likely to quit than those who kept working under the old policies” 对应，表明压力更小、更不容易离职。

【解析】段落 J 中介绍了 MIT 教授的研究，提到在管理重新设计的情况下，给予员工灵活性，员工压力更小、离职率更低，与题目内容相符，所以答案是 J。

【定位】"Workers who rejected working long hours” 与"those who rejected the long hours” 对应，都指拒绝长时间工作的员工；"tended to make regular adjustments” 与"had a tendency to...regularly took steps to adjust” 对应，都表示有定期做出调整的倾向；"achieve work-life balance” 与"maintaining their work-life balance” 对应，都表明目的是实现或维持工作与生活的平衡。

【解析】段落 E 中提到研究人员发现拒绝长时间工作的员工有相似的维持工作与生活平衡的策略，即会定期做出调整，与题目内容一致，所以答案是 E。

【定位】"Talking about work-life balance” 与"Talking about work-life balance” 对应；"a privilege” 与"a very privileged conversation” 对应；"the better-off” 对应"privileged”，都表示有特权的、富裕的；"those who barely make a living” 与"For millions of people, work is about being able to put food on the table” 对应，指那些工作只是为了糊口的人。

【解析】段落 L 中 Lechner 提到谈论工作与生活的平衡是一种特权，对于很多人来说工作只是为了糊口，与题目意思相符，所以答案是 L。

【定位】"Knowing one's emotional state” 与"Awareness of your emotional state” 对应，都表示对自己情绪状态的了解；"is of utmost importance” 与"is essential” 对��，都表示重要；"deciding what changes to make for a better work-life balance” 与"to determine the changes you want to make in your work and in your life” 对应，都表示为了工作与生活的平衡决定做出什么改变。

【解析】段落 G 中 Lupu 提到了解自己的情绪状态对决定在工作和生活中做出何种改变很重要，与题目内容相符，所以答案是 G。

【定位】"More female professionals” 与"50% of the women” 对应，都指女性专业人员；"reported being reluctant to work overtime” 与"reported resisting working long hours” 对应，都表示不愿意加班；"than their male counterparts” 与"about 30% of the men” 对应，是与男性进行对比。

【解析】段落 D 中提到研究发现约 30% 的男性和 50% 的女性表示拒绝长时间工作，说明更多女性不愿意加班，与题目内容相符，所以答案是 D。

【定位】"Without organizational support” 与"If your workplace isn't an environment where work-life balance is possible in the first place” 对应，都表示没有组织层面的支持或合适的工作环境；"any personal effort...will be unsuccessful” 与"any effort you attempt to make toward it on a personal level will be in vain” 对应，都表示个人的努力将是徒劳的。

【解析】段落 K 中 Kelly 指出如果工作场所本身不支持工作与生活的平衡，个人的努力是没用的，与题目内容相符，所以答案是 K。

【定位】"The question of how to achieve work-life balance” 与"The quest to attain this mysterious state” 对应，都指实现工作与生活平衡的问题或追求；"has long been” 与"has dominated discussion...for years” 对应，都表示时间很长；"the main subject of discussion among workers” 与"discussion around careers...especially for working parents” 对应，都表示是员工们讨论的主要话题。

【解析】段落 A 中提到工作与生活的平衡多年来一直主导着职业相关的讨论，尤其是对有工作的父母来说，与题目说的员工们长期讨论工作与生活平衡的问题相符，所以答案是 A。

【定位】"You may not actually experience emotional wellbeing at home” 与"even though physically we are there, mentally we may still be processing things that happened at work. We're not present” 对应，都表示在家时情感上并不幸福；"remain occupied with what happened at work” 与"mentally we may still be processing things that happened at work” 对应，都表示一直想着工作中的事情。

【解析】段落 H 中 Lechner 提到即使人在家，但如果还在处理工作中的事情，就无法真正享受在家的时光，与题目内容相符，所以答案是 H。

【定位】"Some researchers suggest that” 与"Some researchers are now encouraging us” 及"Researchers Ioana Lupu and Mayra Ruiz-Castro argue that” 对应，都表明是研究人员的观点；"work-life balance is not a goal to achieve” 与"stop thinking about work-life balance as an achievement that you either hit or don't” 及"a cycle, not an achievement” 对应，都表示工作与生活的平衡不是一个要达到的目标；"a process for life to be adjusted promptly” 与"a lifelong process...requires self-awareness and timely adjustments” 对应，都表示是一个需要及时调整的终身过程。

【解析】段落 C 中研究人员提出工作与生活的平衡不是一个成就，而是一个终身的过程，需要自我意识和及时调整，与题目内容相符，所以答案是 C。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 As a university student, I've come to realise just how little I know about money. 2 I've come to the brutal realisation that Australia's youth are being done a great disservice by not receiving any consistent financial education.?
1 Diving headfirst into the crash course of starting university, I've quickly tried to get myself up to speed with the financial terms of the modern era to help manage my personal finances.
1 I've read some financial education books, done some online learning, and have spoken to my nearest and dearest for their pearls of financial wisdom.
1 There are undoubtedly hundreds of great resources out there for those wishing to improve their financial literacy, but while I was researching, I still kept wishing that I didn't have to play catch-up with the money world. 2 I felt that I was sailing the financial seas with no skills and no life jacket!?
1 However, after talking to my friends who felt the same, I quickly realised that it wasn't my ignorance but the lack of financial education in our schooling system that is leaving high schoolers seriously behind in the modern world of money.?
1 Let's compare a theoretical financial education subject to the standard compulsory English class. 2 On average, English may not be the most popular subject, but it's consistently on the schedule throughout high school, with all students graduating fluent in English.
1 A financial education subject should do just the same. 2 It shouldn't be just a one-day event but a course integrated throughout the whole of high school that would allow students to gradually expand their financial literacy, and would prevent the need for a 'catch up' phase once we're out on our own after graduation.?
1 In the same way that learning a language or new skills takes time, building financial skills requires practice and years to gradually accumulate bits and pieces of knowledge.
1 Giving young people the opportunity to become familiar with the world of money would provide them with a great advantage to enter adulthood with confidence and security so that they are able to manage their own money and look after themselves.?

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 Chocolates save us from many things, especially emotional distress. 2 They comfort us in times of trouble, calming down a racing heart by channelling happy calories inside us. 3 We all have faith in chocolates to delight us in an instant!?
1 Recently, chocolate lovers were heartbroken as scientists claimed that they can become extinct by 2050!? 2 But hey, we have some happy news for you. 3 Scientists can still help save chocolates from dying out! 4 If you are not aware as to why scientists made the statement about the death of this wonderful thing, let us tell you the facts. 5 Chocolate trees, whose seeds are used to make chocolate, grow in the tropical plant world and require very specific weather conditions to prosper.
1 Now, fifty percent of the world's cocoa (可可) beans come from two countries in West Africa: Cote d'Ivoire and Ghana. 2 Scientists believe that both of these countries will experience a 3.8°F temperature increase by 2050 due to global warming, endangering the cacao (可可树) farms in the rainforests. 3 These farms will then have to be shifted to cooler mountainous areas, which are the natural habitat of wildlife. 4 This will lead to some tough decisions: whether to grow chocolate or save wildlife.?
1 Unfortunately, the crisis of global warming has already had a serious negative impact on cacao farms' yields, leading to the prices of chocolates skyrocketing.?
1 Scientists, however, are trying to find a long-term and eco-friendly solution to this problem. 2 They are trying to modify the species with a gene-editing technology, which will transform the seedlings into a species that survives even in a drier and warmer climate.
1 According to a report by The Business Insider, in the University of California's new bio-sciences building, tiny green cacao seedlings are lined up in refrigerated greenhouses for a new experiment by using a technology called CRISPR. 2 By manipulating the DNA of plants, this technology is already being used across the world to make plants tougher and cheaper. 3 Similarly, in this unconventional experiment, scientists will make tiny, precise changes to the DNA of the seedlings to make the cocoa crops survive in warmer and drier climates.?

3段3句指出：这些农场（These farms）将不得不转移到较凉爽的山区（have to be shifted to cooler mountainous areas），而这些山区是野生动物的自然栖息地（the natural habitat of wildlife）。但该句为对题干所述现象的描述，并为回答其后将会发生什么，故需要继续阅读下句。

3段4句进一步指出：这将导致一些艰难的决定（lead to some tough decisions）：是种植巧克力还是拯救野生动物（whether to grow chocolate or save wildlife）。

综上可知，如果可可农场转移到较凉爽的山区，那里的野生动物的自然栖息地将被破坏。比对各个选项可知，A选项（那里的野生动物的自然栖息地将被破坏）与原文的which are the natural habitat of wildlife对应，为正确答案。

4段1句指出：不幸的是（Unfortunately），全球变暖的危机（the crisis of global warming）已经对可可农场的产量（on cacao farms' yields）产生了严重的负面影响（has already had a serious negative impact）。

综上可知，可可农场在面临全球变暖的危机时，产量已经大幅下降。比对各个选项可知，C选项（由于产量减少而遭受了很多损失）与原文的a serious negative impact on cacao farms' yields对应，为正确答案。

根据题干中的University of California's new bio-sciences building可以定位至6段1句：According to a report by The Business Insider, in the University of California's new bio-sciences building（原词复现）, tiny green cacao seedlings are lined up in refrigerated greenhouses for a new experiment by using a technology called CRISPR.

6段1句指出：在加州大学的新生物科学大楼里（n the University of California's new bio-sciences building），使用一种名为CRISPR的技术（by using a technology called CRISPR），进行了一项新实验（a new experiment），将细小的绿色可可树苗排列在冷藏温室中（tiny green cacao seedlings are lined up in refrigerated greenhouses）。但该句并未指出科学家们这样做的目的，故需要继续阅读下文。

6段2句进一步指出：通过操纵植物的DNA（By manipulating the DNA of plants），这项技术（this technology）已在全球范围内被用于使植物更顽强且成本更低（is already being used across the world to make plants tougher and cheaper）。

6段3句还指出：科学家们将对幼苗的 DNA 进行微小而精准的改变（scientists will make tiny, precise changes to the DNA of the seedlings），以使可可作物能在更温暖、更干燥的气候中存活下来（ to make the cocoa crops survive in warmer and drier climates）。

综上可知，科学家在加州大学的新生物科学大楼里尝试通过基因编辑技术使可可树苗能够适应更干燥、更温暖的气候。比对各个选项可知，B选项（基因编辑可可树苗，使它们能够适应更干燥、更温暖的气候）与原文的scientists will make tiny, precise changes to the DNA of the seedlings to make the cocoa crops survive in warmer and drier climates对应，为正确答案。

sections.passage:
1 Super realistic masks are made from flexible materials such as silicone and are designed to imitate real human faces — down to every last detail.
