questions.explanation:
【考点】形容词辨析，考查根据上下文语境选择合适的形容词来修饰“face”，以区分真实人脸和面具脸。

【语法分析】此处“which showed a...face”需要一个形容词作定语修饰“face”，与后文“which showed a person wearing a mask”形成对比，所以要选择能体现正常、真实人脸特点的形容词。

【解析】“normal”意为“正常的”，符合此处与戴面具的脸进行对比，让参与者分辨哪张是正常的人脸的语境，答案是 J。

【考点】动词辨析，要根据句子主语和整体语境选择合适的动词形式，此处考查过去分词作后置定语修饰“error rate”的用法。

【语法分析】“The 20% error rate...”为主语，“...in the study”为后置定语修饰“error rate”，这里需要一个动词的过去分词形式，与“in the study”一起构成分词短语作定语，表达在研究中被观察到的错误率的意思，且该动词与“error rate”之间是被动关系。

【解析】“observed”是“observe”的过去分词，有“观察，观测”的意思，“The 20% error rate observed in the study”表示在研究中观察到的 20% 的错误率，符合语境，答案是 K。

【考点】形容词辨析，结合上下文判断能准确描述与真实人脸相对的面具脸特点的形容词，且要符合语法结构中修饰名词的要求。

【语法分析】“tell an...face from the real thing”结构中需要一个形容词修饰“face”，根据前文提到的面具相关内容，应选择表示人造的、非真实的这类含义的形容词来与“real”形成对照。

【解析】“artificial”意为“人造的，人工的”，这里指区分人造的脸（面具脸）和真实的脸，符合语境要求，答案是 C。

【考点】动词辨析，考查根据句子意思及目的状语的表达需求，选择合适的动词原形来构成不定式短语作目的状语。

【语法分析】“to...”此处构成不定式短语，在句中作目的状语，说明收集数据的目的，需要一个动词原形，结合语境应是去确定、查明是否存在种族差异方面的情况。

【解析】“establish”有“确定，查明；建立”等意思，“to establish any differences according to race”表示为了确定根据种族方面的任何差异，符合句子表达收集数据目的的语境，答案是 F。

【考点】形容词辨析，根据前文提到的响应时间变慢以及句子整体逻辑，选择合适形容词来描述选择的准确程度情况，且要符合“less + 形容词”的比较级结构。

【语法分析】“were 5% less...”需要一个形容词构成比较级结构，用来描述在面对不同种族面孔照片时选择的准确程度与其他情况相比更低的意思，根据语境要体现准确性方面的比较。

【解析】“accurate”表示“准确的”，“less accurate”符合此处表示选择的准确性更低的语境，答案是 A。

【考点】动词短语搭配考查，重点在于对“pass...off as...”（把…… 冒充为……）这一固定短语的掌握以及在语境中的运用，同时要考虑时态等语法因素。

【语法分析】“have”在这里提示使用现在完成时态，“have + 过去分词”结构，需要一个动词的过去分词形式与“have”搭配，结合语境表达罪犯把自己冒充成其他人的意思，所以应选“pass”的过去分词形式与“off as”构成短语。

【解析】“passed”是“pass”的过去分词，“passed themselves off as...”表示把他们自己冒充成……，符合语境中罪犯冒充不同年龄、种族或性别的人的意思，答案是 L。

【考点】副词辨析，考查根据句子中对面具逼真程度的强调，选择合适的副词来修饰形容词“realistic”，以加强语气。

【语法分析】“an...realistic mask”需要一个副词修饰形容词“realistic”，根据语境要突出面具极其逼真的意思，所以要选择能体现程度很高的副词。

【解析】“extremely”意为“极其，非常”，“extremely realistic”表示极其逼真的，符合描述面具逼真程度的语境，答案是 G。

【考点】动词辨析，根据句子整体语境以及“cheat sb. out of sth.”（骗取某人某物）这一短语搭配，选择合适的动词形式，此处考查现在分词作伴随状语的用法。

【语法分析】“...posing as a French minister,...”此处逗号后用现在分词短语作伴随状语，对前面冒充行为同时发生的动作进行描述，需要一个动词的现在分词形式，结合语境应是表达骗取钱财的意思，所以选择“cheat”的现在分词形式。

【解析】“cheating”是“cheat”的现在分词，“cheating business executives out of millions of pounds”表示骗取商业高管数百万英镑，符合语境中犯罪团伙利用面具冒充他人进行诈骗的情况，答案是 D。

【考点】动词辨析，根据句子中关于超逼真面具对人外貌关键特征影响的描述，选择合适的动词原形，且要符合“may + 动词原形”表示推测的语法结构。

【语法分析】“may”为情态动词，后面需要接动词原形，结合语境应是表达超逼真面具可能会对外貌关键特征产生某种影响，使它们不容易被识别的意思，所以要选择能体现这种影响作用的动词。

【解析】“allow”有“允许，使得”等意思，“allow the key characteristics of a person's appearance to be...”表示使得某人外貌的关键特征能够……，符合语境中面具对识别外貌特征产生影响的描述，答案是 B。

【考点】副词辨析，根据前文提到的难以检测合成脸以及对安全等方面的影响，选择合适的副词修饰“identified”，以体现识别的难易程度情况。

【语法分析】“be...identified”需要一个副词修饰动词“identified”，根据语境要表达因为面具太逼真，导致外貌关键特征不容易被准确识别的意思，所以要选择体现否定、不易等含义的副词。

【解析】“incorrectly”意为“不正确地，错误地”，在这里可理解为不容易被正确识别，符合语境中面具影响识别准确性的意思，答案是 I。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Most people have a dream in life, a vision of who or what they'd like to be in the future. 2 At a minimum, everyone has interests and values that determine what they want out of their lives. 3 Even so, trying to set achievable goals that you'll work for over the course of many years can be extremely challenging.? 4 It can be hard to know where to even begin, and the things you hope to achieve may seem impossible. 5 But, if you're well prepared you may be able to set goals for your life that are just as fulfilling to work toward as to achieve.
1 We all have goals that we want to achieve in our lives. 2 These goals may include learning a new language, eating healthier and losing weight, becoming a better parent, saving more money, and so on. 3 It can be easy to assume that the gap between where you are now and where you want to be in the future is caused by a lack of knowledge.? 4 This is why we buy courses on how to start a business or how to lose weight fast or how to learn a new language in three months. 5 We assume that if we knew about a better strategy, then we would get better results. 6 We believe that a new result requires new knowledge.
1 What I'm starting to realize, however, is that new knowledge does not necessarily drive new results. 2 In fact, learning something new can actually be a waste of time if your goal is to make progress and not simply gain additional knowledge.?
1 It all comes down to the difference between learning and practicing. 2 Thomas Sterner, in his book The Practicing Mind, explains the key difference between practicing and learning.? 3 He says:“When we practice something, we are involved in the deliberate repetition of a process with the intention of reaching a specific goal.” 4 Here the words“deliberate”and“intention”are key, because they define the difference between actively practicing something and passively learning it.
1 Learning something new and practicing something new may seem very similar, but these two methods can have profoundly different results.? 2 Here are some additional ways to think about the difference. 3 Let's say your goal is to get stronger and more fit. 4 You can research the best instructions on weight lifting technique, but the only way to build strength is to practice lifting weights. 5 Let's say your goal is to grow your startup. 6 You can learn about the best way to make a sales pitch, but the only way to actually land customers is to practice making sales calls. 7 Let's say your goal is to write a book. 8 You can talk to a best-selling author about writing, but the only way to become a better writer is to practice publishing consistently.
1 Passive learning creates knowledge. 2 Active practice creates skill. 3 Let's consider a couple more reasons to prioritize active practice over passive learning.? 4 First, passive learning can be a stick that supports inaction. 5 In many cases, learning is actually a way to avoid taking action on the goals and interests that we say are important to us. 6 For example, let's say you want to learn a foreign language. 7 Reading a book on how to learn a foreign language quickly allows you to feel like you are making progress (“ Hey, I'm figuring out the best way to do this!”). 8 Of course, you're not actually practicing the action that would deliver your desired outcome (speaking the foreign language).
1 In situations like this one, we often claim that we are preparing or researching the best method, but these rationalizations allow us to feel like we are moving forward when we are merely spinning our wheels.? 2 We make the mistake of being in motion rather than taking action. 3 Learning is valuable until it becomes a form of procrastination (拖延).
1 Another point to consider is that practice is learning, but learning is not practice. 2 Passive learning is not a form of practice because although you gain new knowledge, you are not discovering how to apply that knowledge. 3 Active practice, meanwhile, is one of the greatest forms of learning because the mistakes you make while practicing reveal important insights.
1 Even more importantly, practice is the only way to make a meaningful contribution with your knowledge.? 2 You can watch an online course about how to build a business or read an article about a terrible disaster in a developing nation, but that knowledge is unproductive unless you actually launch your business or donate to those in need. 3 Learning by itself can be valuable for you, but if you want to be valuable to others, then you have to express your knowledge in some way.
1 The last important point to consider is that practice focuses your energy on the process. 2 Thomas Sterner once said,“Progress is a natural result of staying focused on the process of doing anything.” 3 The state of your life right now is a result of the habits and beliefs that you have been practicing each day.? 4 When you realize this and begin to direct your focus toward practicing better habits day-in and day-out, continual progress will be the logical outcome. 5 It is not the things we learn nor the dreams we visualize that determine our results, but rather the habits that we practice each day. 6 Fall in love with boredom and focus your energy on the process, not the product.
1 What does this all mean? 2 Is passive learning useless? 3 Of course not. In many cases, learning for the sake of learning can be a beautiful thing.? 4 Not to mention that soaking up new information can help you make more informed decisions when you do decide to take action. 5 That said, the main point of this article is that learning by itself does not lead to progress. 6 We often hide behind information and use learning as an excuse to delay the more difficult and more important choice of actually doing something. 7 Spend less time passively learning and more time actively practicing. 8 Stop thinking and start doing.

questions.explanation:
【定位】题目中“Acquisition of new knowledge”对应原文“learning something new”，都表示新知识的获取；“may not guarantee the progress”与原文“new knowledge does not necessarily drive new results”意思相符，都在强调新知识不一定能带来想要的进步结果，此处“guarantee the progress”与“drive new results”表意相近，都是关于达成某种成果方面的表达。

【解析】段落 C 明确指出新知识不一定能带来新的成果，也就是获取新知识未必能保证达成期望的进步，与题目意思一致，所以答案是 C。

【定位】题目“Your current situation in life”与原文“The state of your life right now”对应，指当下的生活状况；“is built on”和原文“is a result of”表意相近，都表达基于、由…… 造成的意思；“the beliefs and habits you have been practicing daily”与“the habits and beliefs that you have been practicing each day”完全对应，都是说每天践行的信念和习惯。

【解析】段落 J 提到现在的生活状态是由每天践行的习惯和信念所造就的，与题目表达的意思相符，所以答案是 J。

【定位】题目中“Knowing the best way to learn a foreign language”对应原文“Reading a book on how to learn a foreign language quickly”，都是指了解学习外语的相关知识方法；“will not enable you to speak it without actual practice”与原文“you're not actually practicing the action that would deliver your desired outcome (speaking the foreign language)”对应，都表明仅知晓方法而不实际练习，是无法达成会说外语这个结果的。

【解析】段落 F 通过举例说明了解外语学习方法但不实际练习就无法实现说出外语这一目标，与题目意思契合，所以答案是 F。

【定位】题目“find it demanding to create a goal”与原文“trying to set achievable goals... can be extremely challenging”对应，都表达制定目标是有难度的意思；“which will take a long time to achieve”与原文“you'll work for over the course of many years”对应，都涉及目标实现所需的较长时间这一要点。

【解析】段落 A 指出制定需要多年努力去实现的目标极具挑战性，与题目所说制定耗时长久的目标有难度相符，所以答案是 A。

【定位】题目“Learning and practicing seem to be very much alike”与原文“Learning something new and practicing something new may seem very similar”完全对应，都表明学习和实践表面上的相似性；“the two processes can lead to quite different outcomes”与原文“these two methods can have profoundly different results”对应，都强调二者会产生差异很大的结果。

【解析】段落 E 开篇就点明学习新事物和实践新事物看似相似但结果大不同，与题目表述一致，所以答案是 E。

【定位】题目“Absorbing new information”对应原文“soaking up new information”，都表示吸收新信息；“is helpful in making better decisions prior to action”与原文“help you make more informed decisions when you do decide to take action”对应，都体现了新信息对行动前决策的帮助作用。

【解析】段落 K 提到吸收新信息能帮助在决定采取行动时做出更明智的决策，与题目意思相符，所以答案是 K。

【定位】题目“feel like we are making progress by doing some research or making preparations”与原文“we often claim that we are preparing or researching the best method, but these rationalizations allow us to feel like we are moving forward”对应，都表达了通过做准备、研究自认为在进步的意思；“actually we are staying at the starting point”与原文“when we are merely spinning our wheels”对应，都表明实际上并没有实质进展，只是原地打转。

【解析】段落 G 指出我们常以准备、研究为借口觉得自己在前进，实则只是在原地踏步，与题目意思一致，所以答案是 G。

【定位】题目“We are inclined to think”与原文“It can be easy to assume”表意相近，都表示一种容易产生的想法；“a lack of knowledge prevents us from advancing to a better future”与原文“the gap between where you are now and where you want to be in the future is caused by a lack of knowledge”对应，都在说认为是缺乏知识导致无法走向更好的未来，存在现在与期望未来的差距。

【解析】段落 B 提到人们容易认为当下与未来期望状态的差距是由缺乏知识造成的，也就是觉得缺乏知识阻碍迈向更好未来，与题目意思相符，所以答案是 B。

【定位】题目“Learning can benefit you by itself”与原文“Learning by itself can be valuable for you”对应，都表明学习自身能带来益处；“only practice can turn what you learn into meaningful contributions”与原文“practice is the only way to make a meaningful contribution with your knowledge”对应，都强调只有实践才能让所学知识产生有意义的贡献。

【解析】段落 I 阐述了学习本身有价值，但只有通过实践才能利用所学知识做出有意义贡献，与题目表述一致，所以答案是 I。

【定位】题目“Practice involves repeating a process intentionally”与原文“When we practice something, we are involved in the deliberate repetition of a process”对应，这里“intentionally”与“deliberate”表意相近，都表示有意地；“to attain a particular objective”与原文“with the intention of reaching a specific goal”对应，都体现了实践是为了达成特定目标的意思。

【解析】段落 D 中引用的话对实践的定义进行了说明，即有意重复一个过程以达到特定目标，与题目意思相符，所以答案是 D。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 Research in human-vehicle interaction has shown even systems designed to automate driving are far from being error-proof.? 2 Recent evidence points to drivers' limited understanding of what these systems can and cannot do as a contributing factor to system misuse. 3 A recent study tackles the issue of over-trusting drivers and the resulting system misuse from a legal viewpoint. 4 It looks at what the manufacturers of self-driving cars should legally do to ensure that drivers understand how to use the vehicles appropriately.
1 One solution suggested in the study involves requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements (EULAs), similar to the terms and conditions that require agreement when using new software products. 2 But this is far from ideal. 3 The agreement may not provide enough information to the driver, leading to confusion about the nature of the requests for agreement and their implications. 4 Further, most end users don't read EULAs.? 5 A 2017 study shows 91 percent of people agree to them without reading. 6 Among young people, 97 percent agree without reviewing the terms.
1 The issue is that, unlike using a smartphone app, operating a car has serious safety risks, whether the driver is human or software. 2 And human drivers need to consent to take responsibility for the outcomes of the software and hardware.
1 "Warning fatigue" and distracted driving are also causes for concern. 2 For example, a driver, annoyed after receiving continuous warnings, could decide to just ignore the message.? 3 Or, if the message is presented while the vehicle is in motion, it could represent a distraction.? 4 Given these limitations and concerns, even if this mode of obtaining consent is to move forward, it likely won't fully protect automakers from their legal liability should the system malfunction (发生故障) or an accident occur.
1 Driver training for self-driving vehicles can help ensure that drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations.? 2 This needs to occur beyond the vehicle purchase. 3 Recent evidence shows even relying on the information provided by the seller is not going to answer many questions. 4 All of this considered, the road forward for self-driving cars is not going to be a smooth ride after all.

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 Do you ever blend up a protein drink for breakfast, or grab a protein bar following an afternoon workout? 2 If so, you are likely among the millions of people in search of more protein-rich diets.
1 Protein-enriched products are found everywhere. 2 But contrary to all the publicity that everyone needs more protein, most Americans get twice as much as they need.?
1 Many of us living in the most developed countries are buying into a myth of protein deficiency created by food companies and self-identified health experts. 2 Global retail sales of protein supplement products reached an astonishing US$ 18.9 billion in 2020.
1 But are we really in need of more protein? 2 Physicians in the U.S. have never actually examined a patient with protein deficiency because simply by eating an adequate number of daily calories we are also most likely getting enough protein.?
1 In fact, Americans currently consume almost twice the National Academy of Medicine's recommended daily intake of protein although the most desirable protein intake may vary depending on age and activity level.?
1 For example, if you're a dedicated athlete you might need to consume higher quantities of protein. 2 Generally, though, a 140-pound person should not exceed 120 grams of protein per day, particularly because a high protein diet can strain kidney and liver function and increase risks of developing heart disease and cancer.
1 While fats and sugar have taken the beating in turns since over a century ago, protein has managed to remain our red-hot favorite.?
1 In the 1970s through the 1990s, protein products remained visible but moved back somewhat with the dietary spotlight firmly fixed on low-calorie, low-fat, sugar-free snack foods and beverages following the publication of studies linking sugar and saturated (饱和的) fat consumption to heart disease.
1 Later research in 2003, however, suggested high-protein diets could aid in weight loss, and protein quickly regained its former nutrient-superstar status.
1 Now most people living in high-income nations are consuming enough protein. 2 When we replace meals with a protein bar or drink, we also risk missing out on the rich sources of antioxidants (抗氧化剂), vitamins and many other benefits of real food.?

综上可知，美国对蛋白质的宣传是超出人们所需的，实际情况大多数美国人摄入的蛋白质是超额的，故可以理解为，美国对蛋白质的宣传创造了蛋白质缺乏的神话。比对各个选项可知，A选项（它帮助创造了蛋白质缺乏的神话）与原文的contrary to all the publicity对应，为正确答案。

4段2句指出：美国的医生（Physicians in the U.S.）从未诊断过（have never actually examined）蛋白质缺乏的患者（a patient with protein deficiency），因为只要每天摄入足够的热量（because simply by eating an adequate number of daily calories），我们很可能也摄取了足够的蛋白质（we are also most likely getting enough protein）。

综上可知，美国的医生从未真正诊断过患有蛋白质缺乏症的患者，是因为美国人通过日常饮食摄入的蛋白质已经足够。比对各个选项可知，C选项（美国人通过日常饮食摄入的蛋白质已经足够）与原文的simply by eating an adequate number of daily calories we are also most likely getting enough protein对应，为正确答案。

5段1句指出：事实上（In fact），美国人目前摄入的蛋白质几乎是美国医学科学院推荐的每日摄入量的两倍（Americans currently consume almost twice the National Academy of Medicine's recommended daily intake of protein），尽管最理想的蛋白质摄入量可能会根据年龄和活动水平而有所不同（although the most desirable protein intake may vary depending on age and activity level）。

综上可知，人们在决定最理想的蛋白质摄入量时，应该考虑年龄（vary depending on age）和活动水平（activity level）。比对各个选项可知，B选项（年龄和活动水平）与原文的depending on age and activity level对应，为正确答案。

根据题干中的largely out of favor for more than a century定位在7段1句：While fats and sugar have taken the beating（out of favor的同义替换） in turns since over a century ago（同义替换）, protein has managed to remain our red-hot favorite.

7段1句指出：自一个多世纪前以来（since over a century ago），脂肪和糖轮流受到人们的诟病（fats and sugar have taken the beating in turns），而蛋白质却一直深受我们的喜爱（protein has managed to remain our red-hot favorite）.

综上可知，超过一个世纪以来，含脂肪和糖的食物不太受欢迎。比对各个选项可知，D选项（含糖和高脂肪的食物）与原文的fats and sugar对应，为正确答案。

根据题干中的people in developed countries should do to keep healthy定位在10段1句：Now most people living in high-income nations（等于people in developed countries） are consuming enough protein.

10段1句指出：如今，大多数生活在高收入国家的人（Now most people living in high-income nations）摄入的蛋白质已经足够（ are consuming enough protein）。但该句描述的是生活在发达国家的人们的蛋白质摄入状态，并未说明其是否能保持健康，故需要继续阅读下文。

10段2句进一步指出：当我们用蛋白棒或蛋白饮品代替正餐时（When we replace meals with a protein bar or drink），我们也有可能错过（we also risk missing out）真正食物中富含的抗氧化剂（on the rich sources of antioxidants）、维生素（vitamins）以及真正食物中的其他诸多益处（and many other benefits of real food）。该句用从反面回答了题目所问的问题，说明了我们用蛋白质棒或饮料代替正餐时可能产生的问题，也就意味着如果想要保持健康，不应该这么做。而应该重视真正食物有中的益处。

综上可知，作者暗示生活在发达国家的人应该享受天然食物来保持健康。比对各个选项可知，A选项（享受天然食物）与原文的we also risk missing out ... and many other benefits of real food对应，为正确答案。

Six people had to move away from their home to another place after a fire broke out in a building on Main Street Saturday, officials said.
Firefighters responded to the three-story building shortly after 1 p.m. for a reported structure fire, according to Norwalk Deputy Fire Chief Adam Markowitz.
Markowitz said crews encountered heavy smoke coming from the second floor when they arrived.
A team of about 25 firefighters then spent about 25 minutes extinguishing the flames.
Officials described the structure as a mixed-use building that features commercial businesses on the first floor and residential on the second and third floors.
Town records list four apartments in the building.
Due to smoke and heat damage, the four apartments were declared uninhabitable, and the six residents had to move to another place, officials said.
No injuries were reported in connection with the fire.
The Norwalk Fire Marshal is investigating the cause and origin of the fire.
Q1: Why did the six residents have to find another place to stay?
Q2: What does the news report say the Norwalk Fire Marshal is doing?
A new study has cast doubt on historic research suggesting that the season or month of someone's birth is associated with an increased risk of certain mental health conditions.
The study looks at symptoms of anxiety and depression among more than 70,000 older adults in Europe.
A number of past studies have found the link between season of birth and mental health diagnoses.
Researchers have suggested that such links could arise from various things.
These include nutrient intake, sun exposure, climate, and disease exposure varying across the course of the year.
However, evidence has been mixed.
More recent studies have suggested that factors such as social class or economic background have more to do with these diagnoses than month of birth.
Overall, the new study found no significant relationship between participants' month of birth and symptoms of depression or anxiety.
There was some variability in some countries.
In Poland, depressive symptoms fluctuated a little depending on birth month.
In the Czech Republic, the same was true of anxiety symptoms.
But on the whole, there was no systematic pattern.
Q3: What have a number of past studies found about season of birth?
Q4: What did the new study find about the relationship between participants' month of birth and symptoms of depression?
Genetic researchers in China have made a clone of a star police dog.
The clone was born in a laboratory in Beijing in December.
Tests show that the clone and her mother are almost identical genetically.
The mother dog helped solve multiple murders and many other crimes.
The clone has already performed better than traditionally bred dogs on several tests.
If the clone continues to perform as well as expected, it could mean a huge reduction in the training time for police dogs, which usually takes about five years.
The ultimate goal of scientists is to produce clones of talented police dogs that can be trained in months instead of years.
However, this goal is not yet possible due to the current costs of the technology.
This is not the first time a clone has been made of a star police dog.
In South Korea, six clones began working with the police in 2008.
Q5: What do the researchers' tests show about the cloned dog?
Q6: What is the scientists' purpose in cloning police dogs?

Supporters call it “wild camping”; opponents call it “illegal camping”.
What both sides accept is that there has been a boom in the past few months, with increasing numbers of visitors pitching their tents on any bit of land they fancy in the UK.
In part, this reflects the fact that official campsites have been wholly or partially closed, or are overflowing in a summer when fewer people are going abroad.
It is also cheap, at a time when many are worried about what the economic future holds.
But it may also be an expression of a desire for going outdoors — a response to the months of lockdown.
Most of the coverage of the boom in wild camping has been negative.
Camping in public parks has now been banned for August and the early part of September because campers dump litter, human waste, and even their tents on the grassland.
Similar action has been taken even in Scotland, where camping is usually permitted on most of its open land.
Clearly there have to be rules.
It would make sense that wild campers need to ask for permission to camp from landowners, especially outside Scotland, where the law is far more restrictive.
It would be common sense for people to use small tents and leave no trace of their visit.
They have been attracted by a patch of land this close to wilderness, and it is their responsibility to keep it that way.

Imagine boating down the Amazon Rivcr, minding your own business — calmly keeping an eye out for alarmingly large snakes — and a curious pink dolphin appears to swim alongside.
While this may seem like a mythical creature,pink dolphins do exist in the Amazon region.
The Amazon river dolphin is a giant among its species.
It can measure up to 2 meters long and weigh around 204 kilograms.
Size isn't the only thing that sets the Amazon river dolphin apart.
Thriving in South American rivers and temporary lakes caused by seasonal flooding, this freshwater dolphin is sometimes shockingly pink.
Although born gray, males of the species are easily identified as they enter adulthood by a decisive pink shade.
Their unusual coloring is believed to be the result of scar tissue from dolphin fights — whether play fighting or a serious bid for a mate.
The deeper the pink, the more attractive the males are believed to be, and the older the male, the more pink it will have.
There's also a theory that this color helps the dolphins more readily blend in with their surroundings.
During heavy rains, rivers along the Amazon rainforest turn a pink shade, and with it male dolphins are harder to detect.
The Amazon wetland system, fed by the Amazon River, is a crucial place for pink dolphins to breed, and since 2018 has been granted internationally protected status.

In a new Merrill Lynch/Age Wave survey, a full 70%of the early adults said they received financial support from their parents in the past year and 58% said they couldn't afford their current lifestyles without it.
The most common types of financial support include cell phone plans,food,school costs and car expenses.
Parental financial support of early adults, said Ken Dychtwald, CEO of Age Wave, is “the new normal”.
But 64% of the young adults surveyed said parents' financial support to children age 25 to 34 is “a bad thing”, because it makes those kids dependent.
By contrast, only 29% thought supporting men and women age 18 to 24 is bad; the remaining 71% thought that assistance “helps the adult children get ahead”.
Dychtwald believes the young women and men surveyed were saying that by 25, younger adults ought to be financially independent.
In fact, the respondents said, financial independence defines adulthood.
“Financial independence is something they were struggling with and challenged by.
And it scared them a bit,” Dychtwald said.
One big reason they're struggling is attributed to college loans, of which the average amounts to $37,000.
Many of the parents have taken on college loans for the kids, too, sometimes at the expense of their own finances.
In the survey, 60%of early adults define financial success as being debt-free.
Whether that's likely, or even possible, anytime soon, is anyone's guess.

sections.passage:
1 In the current age, there is a significant debate about whether university libraries should be accessible to the public. 【提出问题：大学图书馆是否要对公众开放】 2 Some individuals contend that this would be beneficial for the community, while others hold the view that it could disrupt the university's tranquility and functioning. 【正反观点对比】 3 From my perspective, university officials should be prudent in deciding whether to grant public access to such a vital institution. 【作者观点：学校应该谨慎决定】
1 Firstly, the library is a crucial academic resource and a necessary research hub for students and faculty alike. 【原因1：图书馆是重要学术资源】 2 It should prioritize serving its primary users by maintaining a controlled environment for study and research. 【递进：学校应优先服务学校】 3 If the university opts to open the library to the general public, there is a risk that an influx of visitors could deplete resources and hinder the academic progress of its students and staff. 【反面假设：向公众开放的风险】 4 Additionally, overcrowding could lead to increased noise and potential disturbances, such as conversations and arguments, which would compromise the library's conducive atmosphere for learning. 【原因2：开放图书馆可能带来的风险】
1 In summary, while the idea of opening university libraries to the public has its merits, the potential negative impacts are considerable. 【总结：有利但也有较大弊端】 2 Therefore, it is my belief that such a measure should not be considered as part of the university's plans. 【结论：不应考虑这一措施】

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 The courtyard is a traditional Chinese residential building, with a character of being built around a yard. 2 It is warm in winter and cool in summer, and offers a comfortable environment, which make the courtyard a very suitable place for large families to live in. 3 There are various courtyards around China, but the typical one is the Beijing courtyard. 4 Nowadays, with the development of modern society, the number of courtyards is decreasing. 5 However, the courtyard is still of great significance in passing down Chinese culture and studying Chinese architecture.

questions.stem: ①四合院是中国传统居住建筑，它的特点是房屋建在院子的四周。②冬暖夏凉，环境舒适，很适合大家庭居住。③中国各地有各种四合院，但典型是北京四合院。④如今，随着现代社会的发展，四合院正在减少。⑤但四合院仍然在传承中国文化和研究中国建筑方面有重要意义。
questions.answer: 1 The courtyard is a traditional Chinese residential building, with a character of being built around a yard. 2 It is warm in winter and cool in summer, and offers a comfortable environment, which make the courtyard a very suitable place for large families to live in. 3 There are various courtyards around China, but the typical one is the Beijing courtyard. 4 Nowadays, with the development of modern society, the number of courtyards is decreasing. 5 However, the courtyard is still of great significance in passing down Chinese culture and studying Chinese architecture.

sections.title: Section A 选词填空
sections.passage:
1 It's well known that physical exercise is beneficial not just to physical health but also to mental health. 2 Yet whereas most countries have 1, evidence-backed guidelines on the type and intensity of exercise 2 for various physical health benefits, such guidelines do not yet exist for exercise and mood.? 3 This is 3 due to a lack of necessary evidence.? 4 However, a new systematic review brings us usefully up-to-date on the current findings in this area.
1 Before 4 into some of the key take-aways, an important 5 made in the review is between aerobic exercise and anaerobic.? 2 The former 6 such things as walking, jogging and cycling and means exercising in such a way that your body is able to use oxygen to burn fat for energy.? 3 In contrast, an aerobic exercise — such as lifting heavy weights — is of such 7 intensity that your body does not have time to use oxygen to create energy and so instead it breaks down glucose (葡萄糖) in your blood or muscles.?
1 Beginning first with the influence of exercise intensity on the mood benefits of aerobic exercise the researchers, led by John Chan at Shenzhen University, found 8 results from 19 relevant studies.? 2 Some favoured higher intensity, others low, while seven studies found that intensity made no 9 to mood benefits.?
1 In relation to the intensity of anaerobic exercise, however, the results were far clearer — the optimum (最佳选择) for improving mood is 10 intensity, perhaps because low intensity is too dull while high intensity is too unpleasant.?

questions.explanation:
【语法分析】空格前是从句的谓语have,空格后是逗号和名词短语evidence-backed guidelines，由此可知，空格处应填入一个形容词或分词，与evidence-backed一起充当guidelines的定语。 

【解析】本段综合阐述目前关于运动强度、运动类型和情绪之间关系的研究成果。前后半句表意相反，后半句转折表述目前还没有关于运动与情绪的指导方针，前半句则表述目前存在有益于身体健康的运动类型和强度的指导方针，指导方针详细且有证据支持，故detailed符合语境。

【语法考点】空格前是名词短语the type and intensity of exercise,空格后是介词短语for various physical health benefits, 由此可知，空格处应填入过去分词，充当the typeand intensity of exercise的后置定语。 

【解析】此处阐述大多数国家已存在详细的、有证据支持的关于各种有益于身体健康所需的运动类型和强度的指导方针，故required符合语境。

【语法考点】空格所在句子主系表结构完整，故空格处应填入一个副词，起修饰作用。 

【解析】上文提到“目前还没有关于运动和情绪的指导方针”,此处阐述原因，即“这_______由于缺乏必要的证据”,故partly符合语境。

【语法考点】空格前是介词before,由此可知，空格处应填入一个名词或动名词，充当before的宾语。空格后是介词into,由此可知，空格处应填入动名词，且该词能与into构成合理的搭配。 

【解析】前文提及“一项新的系统综述为我们提供了该领域中有用的最新发现”,本段进一步阐述这一最新发现。该句意为“在_____一些关键要点之前，综述中提出的一个重要______是有氧运动和无氧运动”。dip into意为“把手伸进；浏览”,故dipping符合语境。

【语法考点】空格前是an important,空格后是made in the review,为过去分词短语作后置定语，由此可知，空格处应填入一个名词。 

【解析】下文具体介绍了有氧运动和无氧运动的本质区别，故综述中应该是提到了二者的区别。故distinction符合语境。

【语法考点】空格前是句子的主语the former, 空格后是宾语such things as.…,由此可知，空格处应填入动词的第 三人称单数，充当句子的谓语。 

【解析】空格前面的the former(前者)指代前一句中的aerobic exercise(有氧运动),本句中所列举的散步、慢跑、骑自行车都属于有氧运动的范畴，前后是所属关系，故involves符合语境。

【语法考点】空格前是限定词such,空格后是名词intensity,由此可知，空格处应填入一个形容词或分词，充当intensity的定语。

【解析】与散步、慢跑、骑自行车等低强度的运动相比，举重则是一种高强度的运动，vigorous intensity意为“高强度”,故vigorous符合语境。

【语法考点】空格所在句子主谓宾结构完整，空格前是谓语found,空格后是宾语results,由此可知，空格处要么应填入一个副词，修饰动词found,要么填入一个形容词或分词，修饰名词results。 

【解析】语义判断本段提及运动强度对有氧运动情绪影响的相关研究。首句提到从其益处开始研究，末尾提及研究结果显示无论高强度还是低强度，对情绪益处并无影响，这说明研究结果与一开始的预想相矛盾。因此contradictory符合语境。

【语法考点】空格前是made no,空格后是介词to和名词短语mood benefits,由此可知，空格处应填入一个名词。 

【解析】从运动强度对有氧运动情绪益处的影响开始研究，却得出了相互矛盾的结果，即有氧运动强度的高低对情绪益处并无影响。make no difference意为“没有区别，没有影响”,故difference符合语境。

【语法考点】空格前是be动词is,空格后是名词intensity, 由此可知，空格处要么应填入一个形容词或分词，充当intensity的定语，要么应填入一个副词，修饰be动词。 

【解析】本段阐述无氧运动的强度对情绪益处的影响。由下文“这可能是因为低强度太沉闷，而高强度太令人不快”可知，无氧运动中，中等强度是改善情绪的最佳选择，故moderate符合语境。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 How will we all keep busy when we only have to work 15 hours a week? 2 That was the question that worried the British economist John Maynard Keynes when he wrote his short essay “Economic Possibilities for Our Grandchildren” in 1930. 3 Over the next century, he predicted, the economy would become so productive that people would barely need to work at all. 4 For a while, it looked like Keynes was right. 5 In 1930 the average working week was 47 hours in the United States. 6 But by 1970, the number of hours Americans worked on average had fallen to slightly less than 39.?
1 But then something changed. 2 Instead of continuing to decline, the duration of the working week remained stable. 3 It has stayed at just below 40 hours for nearly five decades.? 4 So what happened? 5 Why are people working just as much today as in 1970?
1 There would be no mystery in this if Keynes had been wrong about the power of technology to increase the economy’s productivity, which he thought would lead to a standard of living "between four and eight times as high as it is today.” 2 But Keynes got that right: Technology has made the economy massively more productive.? 3 According to Benjamin M. Friedman, an economist at Harvard, the U.S. economy is right on track to reach Keynes’s eight-fold (八倍) multiple by 2029. 4 That is a century after the last data Keynes would have had access to.
1 In a new paper, Friedman tries to figure out why that increased productivity has not translated into increased leisure time. 2 Perhaps people just never feel materially satisfied, always wanting more money to buy the next new thing. 3 This is a theory that appeals to many economists.? 4 “This argument is, at best, far from sufficient,” he writes. 5 If that were the case, why did the duration of the working week decline in the first place?
1 Another theory Friedman considers is that, in an era of ever fewer settings that provide effective opportunities for personal connections and relationships, people may place more value on the socializing that happens at work. 2 There is support for this theory.? 3 Many people today consider colleagues as friends. 4 But Friedman argues that the evidence for this theory is far from conclusive. 5 Many workers report that they would like to spend more time with family, rather than at work. 6 Furthermore, this theory cannot explain the change in trend in the U.S. working week in the 1970s.
1 A third possibility proves more convincing for Friedman. 2 That is: American inequality means that the gains of increasing productivity are not widely shared by everyone. 3 In other words, most Americans are too poor to work less.? 4 Unlike the other two explanations Friedman considers, this one fits chronologically (按年代). 5 Inequality declined in America during the period following World War II, along with the duration of the working week. 6 But since the early 1970s it has risen dramatically.
1 Keynes's prediction of a shorter working week rests on the idea that the standard of living would continue rising for everyone.? 2 But Friedman says that this is not what has happened. 3 Although Keynes's eight-fold figure holds up for the economy as a whole, it is not at all the case for the median (中位数的) American worker. 4 For them, output by 2029 is likely to be around 3.5 times what it was when Keynes was writing. 5 This is a bit below his four-to eight-fold predicted range.
1 This can be seen in the median worker's income over this time period, complete with a shift in 1973 that fits in precisely with when the working week stopped shrinking. 2 According to Friedman, between 1947 and 1973 the average hourly wage for normal workers (those who were not in management roles) in private industries other than agriculture nearly doubled in terms of what their money could buy. 3 But by 2013 the average hourly wage for ordinary workers had fallen 5 percent from the 1973 level in terms of actual purchasing power. 4 Thus, though American incomes may have gone up since 1973, the amount that American workers can actually buy with their money has gone down. 5 For most Americans, then, the magic of increasing productivity stopped working around 1973.? 6 Thus, they had to keep working just as much in order to maintain their standard of living.
1 What Keynes predicted was a very optimistic version of what economists call technological unemployment. 2 This is the idea that less labor will be necessary because machines can do so much. 3 In Keynes's vision, the resulting unemployment would be distributed more or less evenly across society in the form of increased leisure. 4 But Friedman says that, for Americans, reality is much darker. 5 Americans now have a labor market in which millions of people — those with fewer skills and less education — are seeking whatever poorly paid work they can get.? 6 This is confirmed by a recent poll that found that, for half of hourly workers, their top concern is not that they work too much but that they work too little. 7 This is most likely not because they like their jobs so much. 8 Rather, we can assume it is because they need the money.
1 This explanation leaves an important question. 2 If the very rich — the workers who have reaped above-average gains from the increased productivity since Keynes's time — can afford to work less, why do they continue to work so much? 3 (Indeed, research has shown that the highest earners in America tend to work the most.) 4 Friedman believes that for many top earners, work is a labor of love.? 5 They are doing work they care about and are interested in, and doing more of it is not necessarily a burden. 6 For them, it may even be a pleasure. 7 These top earners derive meaning from their jobs and work is an important part of how they think of themselves.  8 And, of course, they are compensated for it at a level that makes it worth their while.
1 Friedman concludes that the prosperity (繁荣) Keynes predicted is here. 2 After all, the economy as a whole has grown even more brilliantly than he expected. 3 But for most Americans, that prosperity is nowhere to be seen. 4 And, as a result, neither are those shorter working weeks.

questions.explanation:
【定位】由题干关键信息view..as a chance、socializing at the workplace和develop personal relationships定位到E段。

【解析】E段前两句提到，弗里德曼考虑的另一个理论是，在这个时代，社会环境能够提供的有效的人际关系机会越来越少，人们可能更加珍视在工作中的社交时间。这个理论是有一定依据的，因为很多人现在把同事当作朋友。题干是对这两句的概括，其中socializing at the workplace与原文中的socializing that happens at work同义，view..as a chance对应原文中的place more value on, develop personal relationships对应原文中的consider colleagues as friends,故答案为E。

【定位】由题干关键信息ordinary American workers'、average hourly pay、decreased和work just as many hours as before定位到H段。

【解析】H段提到，从1947年到1973年，美国普通工人的平均时薪的购买力几乎翻了一番。但到了2013年，普通工人的平均时薪的实际购买力与1973年相比下降了5%。提高生产力的魔力在1973年左右就不再起作用了。为了维持生活水平，他们不得不继续努力工作。题干是对这几句的概括，其中ordinary American workers' average hourly pay与原文中的the average hourly wage for normal workers同义，had decreased与原文中的had fallen同义，had to work just as many hours as before与原文中的had to keep working just as much同义，to keep their living standards与原文中的in order to maintain their standard of living同义，故答案为H。

【定位】由题干关键信息average weekly working time、has not changed和nearly half a century定位到B答案解析段。

【解析】B段前两句提到，(美国工人的)每周工作时长不但没有继续下降，反而保持稳定。在近五十年的时间里，它一直保持在略低于40个小时。题干是对这两句的概括，其中American workers' average weekly working time与原文中的the duration of the working week同义，has not changed与原文中的remained stable同义，for nearly half a century与原文中的for nearly five decades同义(decade意为“十年”),故答案为B。

【定位】由题干关键信息inequality in the U.S.、increasing productivity和has not resulted in定位到F段。

【解析】F段前三句提到，对弗里德曼来说，第三种可能性更具有说服力。那就是，美国社会的不平等意味着生产力提高所带来的利益并未被所有人广泛共享。换言之，大多数美国人太贫穷，无法减少工作时间。题干是对这三句的概括，其中inequality in the U.S.与原文中的American inequality同义，increasing productivity has not resulted in reduced working hours对应原文中的the gains of increasing productivity are not widely shared by everyone和most Americans are too poor to workless,故答案为F。

【定位】由题干关键信息Many economists、people's thirst for material things和leisure time定位到D段。

【解析】D段前三句提到，在一篇新论文中，弗里德曼试图了解为什么产值的提升并未转化为更多的休闲时间。可能是人们永远不会在物质上感到满足，总想要更多的钱去买下一样新东西。这种理论也吸引了很多经济学家。题干是对这三句的概括，其中people's thirst for material things对应原文中的people just never feel materially satisfied, assume对应原文中的figure out why, has prevented them from enjoying more leisure time对应原文中的has not translated into increased leisure time, many economists是原词复现，故答案为D。

【定位】由题干关键信息prediction、a shorter average working week、correct和for a time定位到A段。

【解析】A段提到，英国经济学家凯恩斯在1930年预测，在接下来的一个世纪里，经济会变得非常高效(生产率更高),人们几乎不需要工作。有一段时间，看起来凯恩斯是对的。美国人平均每周的工作时间在1930年是47个小时，但到了1970年，已经下降到不足39个小时。题干是对本段内容的概括，其中An economist对应原文中的the British economist John Maynard Keynes, prediction about a shorter average working week对应原文中的he predicted... people would barely need to work at all, correct与原文中的right同义，for a time对应原文中的for a while, in the 20th century对应原文中的in 1930和by 1970(1930是指20世纪30年代，1970同理),故答案为A。

【定位】由题干关键信息labor market、people with less schooling and fewer skills和low-paid定位到I段。

【解析】I 段第五句提到，在美国目前的劳动力市场上，数以百万计的人——那些技能较少、教育程度较低的人——正在寻找他们所能找到的任何工作，不管收入有多低。题于是对这句的同义转述，其中labor market是原词复现，people with less schooling and fewer skills对应原文中的those with fewer skills and less education, to secure any employment对应原文中的seeking...work they can get, even if it is low-paid对应原文中的whatever poorly paid,故答案为I。

【定位】由题干关键信息right、predicting、technology和make the economy much more productive定位到 C段。

【解析】C段第二句提到，但凯恩斯预测得很准：科技确实让经济生产力大幅度提升了。题干是对这句的同义转述，其中Keynes was right与原文中的Keynes got that right同义，原文冒号后面的内容就是凯恩斯预测对了的内容：Technology has made the economy massively more productive,题干中的technology would make the economy much more productive与这句原文同义，故答案为C。

【定位】由题干关键信息the highest earners、keen interest和love定位到J段。

【解析】J段中间提到，弗里德曼认为，对于许多高收入者来说，工作是一种热爱的劳动。他们正在做他们关心和感兴趣的工作，做更多的工作未必是一种负担。题干是对这两句的概括，其中many of the highest earners对应原文中的many top earners, have a keen interest in..what they are doing对应原文中的they are doing work they care about and are interested in, love for what they are doing对应原文中的for many top earners, work is a labor of love,故答案为J。

【定位】由题干关键信息Keynes、a shorter working week、the standard of living和continuing to rise定位到G段。

【解析】G段开头提到，凯恩斯预测每周工作时长将会减少，这种预测是基于每个人的生活水平会持续提高的想法。题干与这句同义，其中According to Keynes对应原文的Keynes's prediction of, a shorter working week为原词复现，with everyone's standard of living continuing to rise与原文中的the standard of living would continue rising for everyone同义，故答案为G。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 LaoZi once said, “Care about what other people think and you will always be their prisoner.”?
1 People-pleasing, or seeking self-worth through others' approval, is unproductive and an exhausting way to go through life.? 2 Why do we allow what others think of us to have so much power over how we feel about ourselves? 3 If it's true that you can't please all people all of the time, wouldn't it make sense to stop trying?
1 Unfortunately, sense often isn't driving our behavior. 2 For social beings who desire love and belonging, wanting to be liked, and caring about the effect we have on others, is healthy and allows us to make connections. 3 However, where we get into trouble is when our self-worth is dependent upon whether we win someone's approval or not.
1 This need to be liked can be traced back to when we were children and were completely dependent on others to take care of us: Small children are not just learning how to walk and communicate, they are also trying to learn how the world works. 2 We learn about who we are and what is expected of us based on interactions with others, so, to a four-year-old, if Mommy or Daddy doesn't like him or her, there is the danger that they will abandon them. 3 We need to understand that when we desperately want someone to approve of us, it's being driven by that little kid part of us that is still terrified of abandonment.?
1 As you become more capable of providing yourself with the approval you seek, your need for external validation will start to vanish, leaving you stronger, more confident, and yes, happier in your life.? 2 Imagine how much time we lose each moment we restrain our authentic selves in an effort to be liked.
1 If we base our worth on the opinions of others, we cheat ourselves of the power to shape our experiences and embrace life not only for others but also for ourselves, because ultimately, there is no difference. 2 So embrace the cliché (老话) and love yourself as it's highly doubtful that you'll regret it.?

choices.label: A
choices.text: We should see through other people's attempt to make a prisoner of us.

choices.label: B
choices.text: We can never really please other people even if we try as hard as we can.

choices.label: C
choices.text: We can never be truly free if taking to heart other's opinion of us.

choices.label: D
choices.text: We should care about other people's view as much as they care about our own.

questions.explanation:
根据题干关键词Lao Zi'squotation可以将答案定位到1段。

1段指出，老子曾经说过：“在意别人怎么想，你将永远是他们的囚徒。”很明显，老子的意思是，让我们不要在意别人的看法，在意他人的看法就禁锢了自己。

综上可知，选项C与原文意思一致，故本题选C。

choices.label: A
choices.text: Our desire to be loved will be fulfilled.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Our life will be unfruitful and exhausting.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Our identity as social beings will be affected.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Our sense of self will be sharpened and enhanced.

questions.explanation:
根据题干关键词base our self-worth on other people's approval可以将答案定位到2段1句。

2段1句：该句指出，取悦他人，或者从他人的认可中寻求自我价值，是徒劳的，是一种令人疲惫的生活方式。

换句话说，把自我价值建立在别人的认可之上，我们的生活将是徒劳和疲惫的，故本题选B。

choices.label: A

choices.label: B

questions.explanation:
根据题干关键词account for our need to be liked or approved of可以将答案定位到4段3句。题干中的account for与原文中的driven by对应。

4段3句：该句指出，我们需要明白，当我们迫切希望有人能够认可我们时，这是由我们内心那个仍然害怕被抛弃的小孩所推动的。

综上可知，我们小时候那种害怕被抛弃的感觉导致我们长大之后，希望能够被别人认可，故本题选D。

根据题干关键词better able to provide ourselves with the desired approval可以将答案定位到5段1句。题干中的better able to provide与原文中的more capable of providing属于同义替换。

5段1句：该句指出，当你变得越来越有能力为自己提供你所寻求的认可时，你对外部认可的需求将开始消失，这会让你更加强大、自信，而且理所当然地，你的生活会更加快乐，故本题选A。本题如果找到了定位句，比较容易答对。

questions.explanation:
根据题干关键词advise us to do in the last paragraph可以将答案定位到6段，6段2句以so开头，是作者的建议。

6段2句：该句指出，欣然接受这句老话并爱自己吧，这样做你不太可能会后悔。该句与全篇表达的意思一致。

综上可知，作者建议大家不要在乎别人的意见，要爱自己，故本题选D。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 Some people have said aging is more a slide into forgetfulness than a journey towards wisdom.? 2 However, a growing body of research suggests that late-in-life learning is possible. 3 In reality, education does an aging brain good.
1 Throughout life, people's brains constantly renovate themselves. 2 In the late 1960s, British brain scientist Geoffrey Raisman spied growth in damaged brain regions of rats through an electron microscope; their brains were forging new connections. 3 This meant brains may change every time a person learns something new.?
1 Of course, that doesn't mean the brain isn't affected by the effects of time. 2 Just as height usually declines over the years, so does brain volume: Humans lose about 4 percent every decade starting in their 40s. 3 But that reduction doesn't necessarily make people think slower; as long as we are alive and functioning, we can alter our brains with new information and experiences.
1 In fact, scientists now suspect accumulating novel experiences, facts, and skills can keep people's minds more flexible. 2 New pathways can strengthen our ever-changing mental structure, even as the brain shrinks.
1 Conventional fixes like word puzzles and brain-training apps can contribute to mental durability. 2 Even something as simple as taking a different route to the grocery store or going somewhere new on vacation can keep the brain healthy.?
1 A desire for new life challenges can further boost brainpower. 2 Research about aging adults who take on new enterprises shows improved function and memory as well as a reduced risk of mental disease.? 3 Openness — a characteristic defined by curiosity and a desire for knowledge — may also help folks pass brain tests. 4 Some folks are born with this take-in-the-world attitude, but those who aren't as genetically gifted aren't necessarily out of luck. 5 While genes can encourage an interest in doing new things, a 2012 study in the journal Psychology and Aging found completing reasoning tasks like puzzles and number games can enhance that desire for novel experiences, which can, in turn, refresh the brain. 6 That's why brain scientist Richard Kennedy says "It's not that old dogs can't learn new tricks.? 7 It's that may be old dogs don't realize why they should.”

根据题干关键词Geoffrey Raisman's finding可以将答案定位到2段2-3句。

2段2句：该句指出，在20世纪60年代后期，英国脑科学家杰弗里·雷斯曼通过电子显微镜在老鼠大脑的受损区域发现了生长的迹象；它们的大脑正在建立新的联系。这句是实验的现象。

2段3句：该句点出了实验的结论：这意味着每当一个人学习新东西时，他的大脑都可能会发生变化。这里虽然没有明确说具体的变化是什么,但是根据实验发现大脑有生长的迹象可知，大脑的变化是正向的。

综上可知，上述内容与选项C表达的意思一致，通过学习大脑可以重新充满活力并改善，故C正确。另外，根据本段首句“在一生当中，人们的大脑不断地进行自我修复”也可以得出此结论。

综上可知，对比四个选项，可知选项D“以新颖的方式处理日常事务”符合原文，为正确答案。

6段1-2句指出，渴望接受新的挑战，比如老年人创办新企业，对大脑功能的改善有所帮助。接下来继续指出，开放性——保持好奇心和对知识的渴望，也可以帮助人们通过大脑测试；最后指出，完成拼图和数字游戏等推理任务可以增强人们对新体验的渴望，这反过来可以使大脑重新充满活力。

总结来看，接受新挑战、保持好奇心和求知欲、渴望新体验，这些都能使大脑重新充满活力，故选项A正确。

综上可知，研究发现，推理任务可以增强人们对新体验的渴望，这种对新体验的渴望又会帮助改善大脑，故选项C正确。选项C中的renovate与原文中的refresh是同义替换。

sections.passage:
A JetBlue Airlines flight from West Palm Beach to New York City was forced to turn around and land Sunday morning after the plane struck a bird.
The flight from Palm Beach International Airport to LaGuardia Airport turned around just minutes after takeoff following the strike.
No injuries were reported on the plane, and the flight took off once again 7.5 hours after the first attempt.
“It was like a split second of panic ... that resulted in this nervous reaction on the plane,” said passenger BrianHealy.
“There was total quiet, and then there was relief when the plane came to a stop.”
An email from JetBlue read, “Our team is working to accommodate customers on later flights.”
Q1: What do we learn about the JetBlue Airlines flight from the news report?
Q2: How did the passengers feel when the plane came to a stop, according to Brian Healy?
A deadly snake, which had finally been tracked down after escaping a zoo, has slipped away for the second time.
The poisonous snake forced the closure of the attraction last week when staff noticed the disappearance.
After six days of desperate searching, he was eventually found and placed in a supposedly secure area.
But it seems the animal is no fan of the zoo, because yet again he is out on the loose.
The snake is a relative newcomer to the zoo but has already been frustrating its staff.
The staff believe he squeezed himself out of a gap located around new energy-saving bubs installed inside the snake house.
He was only found the first time around because staff brought in a special machine to trace him inside a wall opening.
This kind of snake is one of the most deadly and poisonous in the wild, and they can range from 3 to 5 meters in length.
Q3: What do we learn about the deadly snake from the news report?
Q4: How have the zoo staff been feeling about the snake?
Electric bikes have been the craze in downtown Jacksonville since they were first introduced earlier this month as a one-year pilot program.
But they're leading to safety concerns, mainly at night when some riders don't follow the rules of the road.
As the night goes on, groups of riders are often seen traveling in just about every direction in the streets and on pedestrian paths.
That is increasing the probability of dangerous accidents.
Electric bike riders have to follow all the same rules as you would if you were in an automobile.
That means no running red lights or traveling in the opposite direction of traffic on one-way streets.
City Council Member Anna Cumber was instrumental in introducing the electric bikes to Jacksonville as a way to bring new life into downtown.
And she's aware of the concerns.
Cumber said, “People can have fun,but both drivers and riders are responsible for paying attention while on the road.
And never assume the driver is going to stop or see you.”
Q5: What do we learn from the news report about the introduction of electric bikes into Jacksonville?
Q6: What are electric bike riders supposed to do?
Q7: Why did City Council member Anna Cumber advocate the introduction of electric bikes into Jacksonville?
What's the best way to teach children how to save and spend their money?
You should make money a regular topic of discussion.
It's best to start young, so it's instinctive rather than a scary subject.
In our family, we talk openly about things like the budget for holidays, how taxes reduce your income, and how to shop around for the best deals.
Indeed. It's also essential to make money real for children through practical examples.
Working out how much we save using discount pizza coupons, for example, is much more relevant than abstract sums.
We also give our kids pocket money, and the amount they get is linked to chores, such as putting the bins out and emptying the dishwasher.
We do that too, and it's paid according to their age.
Two pounds for each year so they can see some progression.
Teaching them to save is important.
We opened a savings account when they were young.
After birthdays and Christmas, they would go to the branch and deposit their gift money.
Oh, I hadn't considered doing that.
In our house, we have transparent money boxes for them to put small change in, so they can see their savings grow.
When the time is right, I’ll start talking to our children about investing and show them how the money saved for their further education has grown.
I am always talking to my elder daughter about the importance of saving into a pension.
She's just started apart-time job and was thinking of not contributing to her pension.
Luckily, I managed to persuade her otherwise.
Yes, it's such an important lesson to learn.
Q8: What should we do with the topic of money, according to the woman?
Q9: How does the woman say money can be made real for children?
Q10: What is the common practice between the man and the woman?
Q11: What is the woman always talking about to her elder daughter?
Welcome to Books in Review.
Our guest today is John Banks, the author of the best selling new book, Rewarding Success.
Glad to be here, Jane.
Your book has sold 2 million copies, but before we discuss why it's getting so much attention, let's talk about your background.
You're an economist and spent two decades teaching at universities?
I spent 25 years as a professor, actually.
And then, for the last 10 years, I've worked as a political consultant, advising politicians at the national level about problems in our country.
You discuss three of those problems in the book, improving public education, reducing our nation's healthcare burden, and increasing personal savings.
But your ideas about education are the most controversial.
Absolutely. A lot of people think I'm trying to punish students who aren't doing well, when actually my goal is to give all students more incentive to succeed.
I'm not sure I agree with you.
Your proposal to pay cash rewards to students who get good grades is a particular problem.
What about students who don't get good grades?
It seems like you're blaming them for not succeeding, when poor performance in school isn't a child's fault.
But my proposal is not just to reward students with good grades, but also students who show improvements.
Okay, another criticism of the plan is the cash rewards themselves.
Where will the money come from?
If students do better, we'll spend less on schooling.
So, in the end, the rewards will pay for themselves.
What about now?
How will we fund the rewards in the meantime?
Well, by increasing taxes or moving money from other areas of the budget into education.
Q12: What do we learn about the man?
Q13: What does the woman say is the most controversial?
Q14: What does the man say is his real goal?
Q15: What will be one option for funding the proposed rewards according to the man?
I met three different people today, and each time, when I asked, “How are you?”
The reply was exactly the same.
“I'm busy”.
Honestly, I hear the same answer from the vast majority of people I meet.
So I started to think: “Guess what? Everybody's busy!”
I'm busy, you're busy, everybody's busy.
So you being busy doesn't make me sympathetic at all.
Because “busy” is the state of the world.
So I'm launching a campaign to stop people complaining about being "busy.”
It may sound harsh, but the truth is, nobody cares.
In a busy world, “being busy” doesn't stand out, nor does it mean productive, creative, accomplished, or professional.
Steve Maraboli once said, “When someone tells you they are too 'busy', it's not a reflection of their schedule; it's a reflection of YOUR spot on their schedule.”
Donna Lynn Hope has also remarked, "Busy doesn't mean better.
I've never envied a busy person — the one who likes to point out their busy lives to others.”
The reality is, nobody is too busy — it's just about priorities.
So the next time someone asks you how you are, maybe respond differently.
In my experience, the “I'm busy" response is really covering up the fact that they're not actually accomplishing their real purpose.
And “being busy" is the lie they tell themselves about why they can't achieve it.
Q16: Why is the speaker launching a campaign?
Q17: What does the speaker advise us to do next time someone asks how we are?
Q18: Why do many people make the “I'm busy” response according to the speaker?
More and more people are taking up extreme sports, like snowboarding, skateboarding, mountain biking, and many more.
Why are these sports becoming so popular?
One thing that extreme sports do better than perhaps anything else is to help you stop being afraid.
It may sound strange to say that their main function is to reduce fear.
But after a time, your fear response to other things in life will be dramatically reduced.
After all, if you can jump out of a plane or off a bridge, then you can face anything else easily.
When doing extreme sports, you have to become more focused.
You'll be pushed to your limits,and if you aren't focused you'll make dangerous mistakes.
Learning to be this focused when enjoying extreme sports will help you to be focused at work, keeping you more productive and ultimately more successful.
It's great to stay fit and healthy, but standard exercise routines and sports only work the same muscles repeatedly.
With extreme sports, you'll be working entirely different muscles, and that means you get an all-over workout.
Extreme sports also burn a lot more calories than other sports.
Skateboarding, for example, can burn as many as 500 calories per hour.
Basketball burns around 300 in the same time.
When you find that you can overcome the physical or mental challenges involved in extreme sports, you'll feel superhuman and your self-confidence will be at an all-time high.
Q19: What may sound strange to say about extreme sports?
Q20: Why should one be highly focused when doing extreme sports?
Q21: How can extreme sports benefit us more than standard exercise routines and sports?
Most of us have been in teams or organizations where we've had conflict with the people that we're working with around the ideas or decisions that we're discussing.
Conflict is natural.
We all bring different life and work experiences to the table.
We all have different personality preferences and tendencies.
We're not all going to have the same ideas on how to approach policies, programs or problems.
But too often we get caught in this place where conflict is perceived to be negative — something we want to avoid so that we can maintain the harmony of our workplace.
This could be because some people want to avoid conflict at all costs, after all they still have to work together.
But this kind of artificial harmony isn't the answer.
Productive conflict is a vital part of teams and organizations that want to push forward and do more.
Without conflict, we're often stuck in this artificial harmony where people don't express potentially innovative ideas for fear that they may start conflict with others.
But if you're in a place where you have a basis of trust, conflict can be extremely productive.
It can lead to increased innovation and greater trust on teams.
It may be an uncomfortable process, but good leaders and healthy teams recognize that productive and healthy conflict is an important part of how they function.
Q22: What does the passage say about conflict in organizations?
Q23: Why do some people want to avoid conflict at all costs?
Q24: Why is productive conflict important for teams and organizations?
Q25: What does productive conflict need as a basis?

questions.explanation: 【题目】What do we learn about the JetBlue Airlines flight from the news report?从新闻报道中，我们了解到关于捷蓝航空公司航班的什么信息?【解析】新闻开头提到，周日上午，捷蓝航空公司一架从西棕榈滩飞往组约的飞机在撞上一只鸟后被迫掉头降落。由此可知，选项A为正确答案。其余选项新闻中均未提及，故排除。

questions.explanation: 【题目】What do we learn about the deadly snake from the news report?从新闻报道中，我们了解到这条致命的蛇的什么信息?【解析】新闻开头部分提到，一条致命的蛇在逃离动物园后终于被找到，但它又第二次溜走了。新闻接下来详细描述这条蛇两次逃离的细节：第一次逃跑后，这条蛇经过工作人员六天的拼命搜寻后终于被找到，并被安置在一个据说安全的区域，但是它再一次出逃。直到新闻最后都没有提及这条蛇是否再次被找到，所以选项B为正确答案，同时排除选项C。选项A错误，新闻中提到，这条毒蛇第一次逃跑并被找到后，被安置在一个安全的地方，而这并不是当下这条蛇的境况，故排除。选项D错误，新闻中提到，这条毒蛇第一次逃跑后，动物园经过六天的搜寻终于找到了它，而根据新闻所述，这条蛇被安置后又再次出逃，可见D项的说法不准确，故排除。

questions.explanation: 【题目】Why did City Council member Anna Cumber advocate the introduction of electric bikes into Jacksonville?为什么市议员安娜·坎伯提侣将电动自行车引入杰克逊维尔市?【解析】新闻末尾部分提到，市议员安娜·坎伯在将电动自行车引入杰克逊维尔，为市中心带来新的活力方面发挥了重要作用。由此可知，选项B为正确答案。其余选项新闻中均未提及，故排除。

【题目】What should we do with the topic of money, according to the woman?根据女士的观点，我们应该如何对待“钱”这个话题?【解析】对话一开始，男上询问女士教孩子们如何存钱和消费的最佳方法是什么,女士建议男士应该把钱作为一个经常讨论的话题，所以答案是B项。A项在对话中找不到相关信息，故排除；女士说最好从孩子们很小的时候就开始经常讨论这个话题，这样这个话题就不会成为一个可怕的话题，据此可排除C项；男士提到在他们家，他们经常公开讨论一些有关钱的问题，但这不是女士的观点，所以排除D项。

choices.label: A
choices.text: By shopping around for the best deals.

questions.explanation: 【题目】How does the woman say money can be made real for children?女士说如何让孩子们真正了解钱?【解析】在对话中，女士提到，通过实际例子让孩子们真止了解钱也很重要，然后她举了算出使用披萨折扣券能省多少饯的例子，所以答案为C项。男士提到他们家会公开讨论如何货比三家以获得最佳优惠，这不是女士的观点和做法，故排除A项；B项曲解了女士所举的例子，故排除；D项在对话中找不到相关信息，故排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: Paying their kids to help with housework.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Setting kids a good example by sharing chores.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Giving kids pocket money according to their needs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Urging kids to deposit some of their gift money.

questions.explanation: 【题目】What is the common practice between the man and the woman?男士和女士之间的共同做法是什么?【解析】在对话中，男士提到他们也会给孩子们零花钱，而且孩子们得到的零花钱数额与家务劳动挂钩，女士说他们也是这么做的，而且是根据孩子们的年龄支付的。也就是说，女士家也给孩子们零花钱，以让孩子们帮忙做家务，所以答案为A项。B项在对话中找不到相关信息，故排除；C项的“根据孩子们的需求”与对话内容不符，故排除；D项提到的做法是男士家里的做法，女士说自己还没考虑过这么做，故排除D项。

choices.label: A
choices.text: The importance of cutting down family expenses.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The need to learn important lessons from her elders.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The delight in seeing their savings grow.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The necessity of saving into a pension.

questions.explanation: 【题目】What is the woman always talking about to her elder daughter?女士总是和她的大女儿谈论什么?【解析】在对话最后，女士提到她经常跟她的大女儿谈论储蓄养老金的重要性，所以答案是D项。A、B两项在对话中没有相关信息，故排除；C项的“存款增长”在对话中提到了，但这并非女士经常和大女儿谈论的话题，故排除。

choices.label: B

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

questions.explanation: 【题目】What do we learn about the man?关于男士，我们了解到什么?【解析】在对话一开始，女士介绍男士时提到，男士是畅销新书《奖励成功》的作者，所以答案为C项。根据对话中对男士的背景介绍可知，男士并不是一名商人，故排除A项；男士提到自己在过去的10年里，一直在做政治顾问，就国家问题向国家层面的政治家提供建议，据此排除B项；D项是根据男士的名字中的Banks设置的干扰项，故排除。

choices.label: C
choices.text: The man's attempts at drawing public attention.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The man's proposals to solve economic problems.

questions.explanation: 【题目】What does the woman say is the most controversial?女士说什么是最有争议的?【解析】在对话中，女士提到男士在书中讨论的三个问题，即改善公共教育、减轻国家医疗负担和增加个人储蓄，但是他关于教育的观点是最有争议的，所以答案是A项。其他三个选项据此可以直接排除。

choices.label: B
choices.text: To motivate all students to be successful.

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

questions.explanation: 【题目】What does the man say is his real goal?男士说他的真正目标是什么?【解析】在对话中，男士提到很多人认为他在试图惩罚成绩不好的学生，而实际上他的目标是给所有学生更多成功的动力，所以答案是B项。其他三个选项据此直接排除。
【题目】What will be one option for funding the proposed rewards according to the man?根据男士的说法，为提议的奖励提供资金的一种选择是什么?【解析】在对话结尾，女士问男士如何为奖励提供资金，男士提到通过增加税收或将预算中其他方面的资金转人教育，D项的“增加税收”是其中一个方法，故选D。其他选项在对话中均未提及，故排除。

choices.label: D

questions.explanation: 【题目】Why is the speaker launching a campaign?为什么说话者要发起一场运动?【解析】在录音中，说话者提到自己发起了一场运动，让人们停止抱怨“忙碌”。由此可知，选项B与此一致，故为正确答案。说话者提及，大家都很忙，所以忙碌的人并没有让他人产生任何同情心，故排除选项A。说话者最后提到，没有人真的太忙——只是事情的轻重缓急而已，但这并不是说要帮助忙碌的人们理清事情的轻重缓急，故排除选项D。选项C录音中未提及，故排除。

choices.label: D
choices.text: Respond as most busy people do.

questions.explanation: 【题目】What does the speaker advise us to do next time someone asks how we are?下次有人问起我们的近况时，说话者建议我们怎么做?【解析】说话者在开头提到，每当自己问别人“你好吗?”得到的回答都一模一样——“我很忙”,而且大多数人都会这样回答。说话者最后提到，下次有人问你过得怎么样时，也许可以换一种方式回答，即避免说“我很忙”。综合两处信息可知，选项A与说话者讲述的内容一致，因此为正确答案。选项B、C和D均与讲话内容不符，故排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: To show their achievements resulted from great efforts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: To prove they stand out as accomplished. professionals.

choices.label: C
choices.text: To cover up their failure to achieve some purpose.

choices.label: D
choices.text: To tell others a complete lie about their inability.

questions.explanation: 【题目】Why do many people make the “I'm busy” response according to the speaker?根据说话者的看法，为什么很多人会给出“我很忙”的回答?【解析】说话者最后提到，根据自己的经验，“我很忙”这个回答其实是在掩盖一个事实，那就是他们并没有实现白己真正的目标。选项C与此内容一致，因此为正确答案。说话者提到，“忙碌”是他们对白己说的一个谎言，用来解释为什么他们无法实现目标，而不是针对他人的，故排除D项。选项A和B讲话中未提及，故排除。

choices.label: C
choices.text: They will be less challenging after a time.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They should cover so many different types.

questions.explanation: 【题目】What may sound strange to say about extreme sports?谈及极限运动，有什么听起来很奇怪的吗?【解析】文章中提到，极限运动可能优于其他任何运动的一点就是帮助你消除恐惧。说它们的主要功能是减少恐惧，听起来可能有些奇怪。选项A与文章内容一致，因此为正确答案。文章开头就提到，极限运动目前变得很受欢迎，故排除选项B。极限运动的确涵盖许多不同的类型，如滑雪板运动、滑板运动、山地自行车等，这听起来并不奇怪，故排除选项D。选项C文章中并未提及，可排除。

choices.label: D
choices.text: To enjoy the sports to the full.

questions.explanation: 【题目】Why should one be highly focused when doing extreme sports?为什么人们在进行极限运动时注意力要高度集中?【解析】文章中提到，在进行极限运动时，你必须变得更加专注。你会被推到极限，如果你不集中注意力，你就会犯下危险的错误。选项C与文章内容一致，因此为正确答案。选项A、B和D均不是文章中提及的进行极限运动时要高度集中注意力的原因，故排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: By allowing our motivation to be at an all-time high.

choices.label: B
choices.text: By stopping us hurting the same muscles repeatedly.

choices.label: C
