Talking is unique to humans.
An animal might make 10 different sounds, but an adult human knows more than 20,000 words.
Additionally, we’re the only animal that expresses thoughts in full sentences.
[16] Researchers don’t think language was invented; instead, they think it evolved.
How did talking evolve? There are two main theories.
[17] The first theory is that language started with people making different sounds, mostly imitating the things around them, like animal calls, nature sounds, and the sounds of tools.
Perhaps they made the sound of wind to comment on the weather or imitated the sound of a bird to tell a friend that there was a bird nearby.
Then over hundreds of thousands of years, those sounds turned into words that people began to learn as part of their language.
At some point, people started stringing the words together to form sentences.
The other main theory, which is more recent, is that people started off by gesturing — pointing at things with their hands and imitating actions using their bodies.
Eventually these gestures turned into a full sign language.
This theory guesses that after developing sign language people eventually started making sounds along with their gestures.
At some point, they switched to mostly making sounds that became words instead of just using their bodies.
[18] The reason they switched to making sounds, the theory goes, is that talking out loud lets you communicate with someone even when you can’t see them.
Q16: How did language come into being according to researchers?
Q17: How did language start according to the first theory?
Q18: Why did people switch from gesturing to making sounds according to the more recent theory?
Is it a good idea to display luxury brands and other signals of status?
It depends on the situation.
Studies have shown that people who appear to be wealthy tend to be considered more intelligent, disciplined, and competent than those who do not.
[19] But new research found that people believe someone who shows off their social status cares more about benefiting themselves than helping others.
This means people are less willing to collaborate with them.
Modesty may be key when cooperation is essential, but the researchers also found that in some cases, status signaling has advantages.
Experiments showed that participants were less likely to choose someone who signals their wealth or status to join a group seeking cooperative members.
[20] But participants were more likely to choose that person when they’re looking for a competitive team member.
These findings suggest that people should change how they present themselves depending on their social goal.
This is the era of social media.
[21] People can easily share their wealth and status to large audiences, but they need to consider the consequences.
Posting about luxury purchases and expensive vacations online may help you to persuade others and frighten competitors, but it could also signal to potential friends or future employers that you are unlikely to think about the needs of others.
This makes things tricky for people who may want to impress others while also demonstrating that they are a team player.
Q19: How would people describe someone who shows off their social status according to new research?
Q20: When were participants more likely to choose someone who signaled their wealth or status?
Q21: What should people do when sharing their wealth and status online?
Human fascination with animals goes back as far as humans do.
[22] Of the oldest cave paintings discovered, some are up to 40,000 years old, and there are more images of animals than humans.
At some point, humans began to capture and hold animals.
[23] The first-known collections were held by royalty and were not open to the public.
In Egypt, researchers have found buildings from around 3500 B.C., containing the remains of animals, including elephants, which were not native to Egypt.
But life wasn’t easy for these animals.
They probably had short lives, and their remains show evidence of severe injuries.
The first public exhibit of animals may have been created by Egypt’s Queen Hatshepsut around 1480 B.C.
Researchers think the zoo was started with animals brought home from a far-off land known as Punt.
[24] It’s unclear why the Queen built the zoo, but it might have been to show off her wealth and power.
Early zoos are found all over the world.
In China, Emperor Wenwang is said to have built a “Garden of Intelligence” around 1060 B.C.
It included deer, birds, and many fish.
[25] In England, King Henry I set up a collection of animals in about 1110 as part of the royal estate.
His collection included tigers and lions.
This collection eventually moved to the Tower of London in 1235.
The collection stayed at that location for 600 years.

Q23: What do we learn about the first-known collections of animals?
Q24: What might be the reason the Egyptian Queen Hatshepsut built the zoo?
Q25: What do we learn about King Henry I’s collection of animals in England?

sections.title: Part 1 Writing 写作
sections.passage:
1 A well-rounded education is pivotal to students’ growth. 2 To attain this, exploring the integration of humanities into core curricula is essential. 3 From my standpoint, making University Chinese a mandatory course is advantageous, yet its execution demands thoughtful strategies.
1 Firstly, universities should devise practical content, such as academic writing and critical reading. 2 These competencies equip students for real-world communication and research across disciplines. 3 Moreover, professors are supposed to employ interactive teaching methods, like dissecting cultural classics via debates or multimedia. 4 This sparks students’ engagement and deepens their cultural comprehension beyond textbook knowledge. 5 Additionally, the course can provide flexible assessment options, enabling students to showcase learning through creative projects or presentations rather than standardized tests. 6 This caters to diverse talents while upholding academic strictness.
1 In brief, with careful design and student-oriented adjustments, we can effectively foster crucial humanistic literacy. 2 It’s high time we seized this chance to enrich our academic journey.

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 Yuan Longping is honored as the "Father of Hybrid Rice." 2 He led his scientific research team to overcome numerous difficulties and successfully cultivated super hybrid rice. 3 This achievement has gained wide recognition worldwide. 4 The rice cultivated using this technology is not only drought-resistant and disease-resistant but also highly adaptable, capable of withstanding different climate and soil conditions. 5 Its yield can be increased by 20% - 30%. 6 Super hybrid rice not only has higher nutritional value but also tastes better. 7 Currently, this technology has been widely applied in many countries, making significant contributions to global food security.

questions.stem: ①袁隆平被誉为“杂交水稻之父”。②他带领科研团队克服了重重困难，培育出了超级杂交稻。③该成果获得了世界广泛认可。④应用该技术培育的水稻不仅耐旱抗病，而且适应性强，能适应不同气候和土壤条件。⑤产量可提高20%-30%。⑥超级杂交稻不仅营养价值更高，而且口感更好。⑦目前，该技术已在许多国家得到广泛应用，为全球粮食安全作出了重大贡献。
questions.answer: 1 Yuan Longping is honored as the "Father of Hybrid Rice." 2 He led his scientific research team to overcome numerous difficulties and successfully cultivated super hybrid rice. 3 This achievement has gained wide recognition worldwide. 4 The rice cultivated using this technology is not only drought-resistant and disease-resistant but also highly adaptable, capable of withstanding different climate and soil conditions. 5 Its yield can be increased by 20% - 30%. 6 Super hybrid rice not only has higher nutritional value but also tastes better. 7 Currently, this technology has been widely applied in many countries, making significant contributions to global food security.

sections.title: Section A 选词填空
sections.passage:
1 Psychologists have long been interested in how we construct our identities and the sorts of strategies that we use to present ourselves in society. 2 New findings suggest that the kinds of 1 and strategic self-presentation behaviour we see in adults appear at a much younger age than 2 known.?
1 Research shows that a child’s awareness of social standing comes from adults. 2 Like grown-ups, kids want to be 3 by those they admire.? 3 Interactive experiences may provide opportunities for children to learn about what 4 a desirable reputation and the kinds of strategies that are effective for 5 a good reputation in their social environment.?
1 Five-year-olds aren’t just aware of their reputations, they also behave strategically to alter their outward image. 2 They will 6 their behaviour in order to appear moral or socially good in the eyes of key observers.? 3 While we know that adults use a large variety of attributes to manage and create impressions, we don’t yet know whether children 7 and use the fact that different attributes are valuable at different times to different 8.? 4 It’s important for us to further consider where in this process children succeed in controlling their reputation and where they 9.?
1 A question to think about is, “ What happens even earlier than age five? “ 2 Children don’t just show up to the first day of kindergarten and have the idea of reputation pop 10 into existence.? 3 The logical question to ask is, “ What happens even earlier? “

questions.explanation:
【词性判断】空格前是the kinds of，空格后是and strategic self-presentation behaviour。and连接并列成分，strategic为形容词，故空格处需填入形容词，与strategic共同修饰behaviour。

【解析】由定语从句we see in adults可知，这种展示自我的行为是人们在成年人身上看到的，它具有复杂性，因为，一般而言，人越长大行为越复杂，故空格处应填入complex一词，与and后的strategic（策略性的）构成语义上的并列关系，故选D。

【词性判断】该句为比较结构，than引导比较状语从句，从句中省略了主语和be动词，完整形式可能为than [it was] ______ known。known为过去分词，此处需填入副词修饰known。

【解析】New findings（新发现）暗示前后认知的差异，即现在的发现与过去的认知进行对比。代入previously，than previously known明确表达“比先前已知的要早得多”，符合语境，故为答案。

【词性判断】空格前为want to be，空格后是动作执行者by those...，空格处需填入动词的过���分词形式，构成完整的被动语态。

【解析】前句指出“儿童对社会地位的认知源于成年人”，本句通过Like grown-ups类比，说明儿童与成人有相似需求，即希望被自己仰慕的人______ 。admire（仰慕）暗示对象是儿童认可的权威或榜样，而前一句中提及的social standing（社会地位）关系到他人的评价与接纳。成年人渴望被社会认可，儿童同样如此，故空格处需体现“被认可、被接纳”的语义，应填入accepted。

【词性判断】空格前的what在从句中作主语，空格后是宾语，空格处需填入谓语动词。

【解析】前一句提到“互动体验可以为儿童提供机会”，此处的机会指“让他们了解是什么______ 理想的声誉” 。代入选项可知，constitutes（构成，组成）符合此处语境，句意为“让他们了解是什么构成了理想的声誉” 。

【词性判断】空格前为介词for，空格后是名词短语a good reputation，介词后接动词时需用动名词形式，因此空格处需填入动名词，构成目的的状语结构“for+动名词+宾语”。

【解析】前面部分提及“了解是什么构成了理想的声誉”，然后用and连接空格所在的并列部分���进一步说明维护声誉的策略。代入选项可知，building“建立，构建”符合此处语境，句意为“在社交环境中哪些策略能有效树立起良好的声誉” 。前后文形成逻辑链条，即先认知“声誉的要素组成”，再掌握“声誉的树立方法”。

【词性判断】空格前是情态动词will，空格后是名词短语their behaviour，故空格处应填动词原形。

【解析】前一句指出“五岁儿童不仅已具备声誉意识，还会通过策略性行为来改变其外界形象” 。本句承接alter their outward image，说明他们会通过调整行为来达成不同的目的。vary有“改变”之意，符合此处语境，且与alter形成语义复现。

【词性判断】空格前是宾语从句的主语children，空格后是and use... 。and连接并列成分，use为动词原形，故空格处应填入动词原形，与use并列，充当谓语。

【解析】前半句是while引导的让步状语从句，意为“尽管我们知道成年人会运用五花八门的特质进行印象管理”，由此可推测，主句要表达的意思应该是，但不知道儿童是否懂得或运用类似的策略进行印象管理。结合备选项及空格后的and use可知，空格处应填入understand，该词与use（运用）形成认知递进，即先理解规律，再付诸实践。故答案为understand。

【词性判断】空格位于句末，其前面为形容词different，故空格处应填名词。

【解析】此句意为“不同特质在不同情境下对不同______ 具有不同价值” 。代入选项可知，audiences符合此处语境，此处并非特指“观众”，而是引申为“社交场景中的观察方”，如老师、同伴、家长等。

【词性判断】空格位于句末，其前面是宾语从句的主语they，空格处应填谓语动词。where... succeed和where they ______是consider的并列宾语从句，故空格处所填词与succeed并列，需填入动词原形。

【解析】前半句讨论成功控制声誉的环节，后半句应指向失败或难以控制的环节。该词与succeed形成对比，体现研究的客观性，既肯定儿童的策略性能力，也指出其可能存在的认知局限。struggle在此取“艰难应对”之意，符合语境，故为答案。

【词性判断】pop into existence（突然产生）为固定搭配，故空格处需填入副词，修饰动词pop。

【解析】前文提出问题“在五岁之前会发生什么？”，本句用don’t否定了“孩子们在踏入幼儿园的第一天就______ 形成了声誉的观念”的情况，又根据后文提到的问题“更早的时候发生了什么呢？”，可知儿童形成有关声誉的观念并非是一蹴而就的。suddenly“突然地”符合此处语境，故为答案。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Recently, a leading design federation in the UK warned that the UK could face a creative skills shortage, after the latest figures revealed a drop of almost 10 percent in students studying Design and Technology. 2 These figures showed that the number of pupils that sat exams in Design and Technology fell 10 percent from 204,788 to 185,279 last year.?
1 Chief executive John Kampfner of the Creative Industries Federation thinks that this drop in figures has worrying implications for the skills pipeline in Britain’s hugely successful arts and creative industries. 2 He said, “We already have skills shortages in many jobs such as animation (动画制作) and special effects.” 3 He added: “Engineering, which requires a similar mix of creative and technical skills, also has recruitment problems.”?
1 Many other designers and architects have expressed concern over the future supply of home-grown talent for UK firms, and industry bodies have pointed out that there has been a lack of roots-level support. 2 However, if these designers had visited the Design Museum shop in London earlier this year their fears may have been eased. 3 With £10 to spend, they could have bought a fascinating children’s toy called “Dazzle Racer”.? 4 An automotive cylinder (圆柱体), it included a wind-up, elastic-band-powered mechanism, minimal parts, all 100 percent recycled, and lots of stickers. 5 It was good fun, simple, eye-catching and very original.
1 Well, you’d expect the Design Museum to commission and make some interesting items, but this one was different. 2 Designed by a group of six Year 9 and Year 10 boys from Finchley Catholic High School, the toy was the winning entry in the museum’s 2015 Design Ventura competition, which brings the business of design to life for students aged 13 to 16 by challenging them to develop a new creative, sustainable and commercially feasible product for the Design Museum shop and attracts hundreds of entries nationwide.?
1 “We did Design Ventura in my previous school,” says Liam Hourican, Finchley Catholic High School’s design technology curriculum leader. 2 “Then when I changed schools four years ago, I introduced it here because it helps to develop so many skills.”
1 The theme for last year’s competition was “Move”, and Hourican began with three groups working in lunch breaks and after school before selecting the group with the most innovative idea. 2 Each participating school may submit just one proposal. 3 “It’s the taking part and doing the work which is important,” he says. 4 “And I never dreamt we’d win.”
1 Catherine Ritman Smith, head of learning at the Design Museum, is expecting around 10,000 participants aged 13 to 16 to take part this year and says that the project — funded by Deutsche Bank as part of its youth engagement programme Born To Be — is the biggest event in the museum’s calendar. 2 “We started Design Ventura with around 800 young people in 2010 and it has grown steadily since,” she says. 3 “Teachers like it because the skills are all transferable and it helps to validate the value of design as a subject,” she explains, telling me that nearly 600 schools have taken part so far.?
1 So how does the competition work? 2 A single-word theme is announced in the summer. 3 This year it is “Change”. 4 Schools work with groups to produce imaginative design ideas for a product in simple materials that could sell for £10 in the Design Museum shop. 5 Participating schools then register by November and eventually submit their design idea.? 6 Along the way there is training and support for teachers and tutoring for students from designers. 7 An additional bonus is when the winners see their design on sale in the spring of the following year.
1 Hourican and his pupils have happy memories of spending a whole day at the museum, having been selected as one of 10 shortlisted schools to present their idea to a panel of judges, including designer Jasper Conran. 2 Then they worked with the Kin Design Studio in Shoreditch, met designers at their school and attended a lunch with Deutsche Bank employees. 3 The students helped to make decisions and there were plenty of discussions — they changed the product’s name, for example.
1 “One of the really useful things about this competition,” says Hourican, “is that there’s a commercial element because the product is going on sale for real and the boys had to learn about budgeting and marketing, as well as designing their game.”? 2 Profits go to charity. 3 “The winning team chooses where it wants the profits to go,” says Ritman Smith. 4 “The Finchley Catholic High School product raised about £1,000 for Great Ormond Street Hospital.” 5 Winning entries in past years have included a make-your-own cloth kit called Dove Bunting and a threefold, wallet-sized travel game with goals at each end, called Badoiiing.
1 It costs the schools nothing to participate in Design Ventura; the professional designers provide their services for free.? 2 Among them are architect Asif Khan, a Design Museum trustee who has worked as designer-in-residence at the museum, helping emerging architects. 3 He has recently been commissioned to design the new Museum of London building in Smithfield.
1 Another is television presenter and interior designer Naomi Cleaver, who is one of the competition’s judges. 2 “I’m very keen to encourage young people,” she says, observing that design brings together other subjects such as literature, art, history, geography and science. 3 “Now that design education is limited in the curriculum, I’m all in favour of competitions such as Design Ventura, which helps to bring the standard curriculum to life,” says Cleaver.? 4 “And the judging day is terrific fun. 5 Some of these students are very imaginative. 6 One group presented their idea in the form of a puppet show and we see some marvelous demonstration models. 7 I’m always impressed by the levels of confidence and the support the students get from their teachers.”
1 Ritman Smith adds: “Design technology has become a tricky subject to make a case for, and we’ve heard of departments closing in some schools. 2 We find that if pupils take part in Design Ventura in Year Nine it can be the trigger which leads them to opt for it at General Certificate of Secondary Education, so we are helping to keep alive something which is crucial to industry and entrepreneurship.”?

【定位】由题干关键信息During the course、teachers、training and support、students、tutoring from designers定位到H段。

【解析】H段倒数第二句提到，在此过程中，教师会接受培训并获得支持，学生则可以获得设计师的辅导。题干是对该句的同义转述，其中During the course of preparing for Design Ventura对应原文中的Along the way，teachers receive training and support对应原文中的there is training and support for teachers，students get tutoring from designers对应原文中的tutoring for students from designers，故答案为H。

【定位】由题干关键信息visit和the Design Museum shop in London定位到C段。

【解析】C段第二句提到，然而，如果这些设计师在今年早些时候去过伦敦设计博物馆的商店，或许就能减少他们的担忧。题干是对该句的同义转述，其中visit和the Design Museum shop in London是原词复现，题干中的can reduce the designers’ fears对应原文中的their fears may have been eased，而原文中的their fears指的就是C段第一句提到的内容，即许多其他设计师和建筑师也对英国公司未来本土人才的供应表示担忧，故答案为C。

【定位】由题干关键信息One of Design Ventura’s judges和curriculum定位到L段。

【解析】L段第一句提到了竞赛评委之一克利弗。第三句引述了克利弗的原话“鉴于当前设计教育在常规课程中的占比有限，我全力支持像‘设计冒险家’这样的竞赛——它有助于让标准课程变得生动有趣”，题干是对第一句和第三句的概括与转述，其中One of Design Ventura’s judges和competition是原词复现，adds vigour to the standard curriculum in schools对应原文中的helps to bring the standard curriculum to life，故答案为L。

【定位】由题干关键信息Design and Technology、decreased by nearly ten percent和last year定位到A段。

【解析】A段提到，最近，英国一家顶尖的设计联合会警告称，英国可能会面临创意技能短缺的问题，因为最新的数据显示，学习“设计与技术”课程的学生人数下降了近10%。题干是对该句的同义转述，其中Design and Technology和last year是原词复现，decreased by nearly ten percent与原文中的a drop of almost 10 percent同义，Enrollment in Design and Technology与原文中的students studying Design and Technology同义，故答案为A。

【定位】由题干关键信息Participation of ninth graders、Design Ventura、motivate和choose... as their subject定位到M段。

【解析】M段的第二句提到，研究发现，如果学生在九年级时参加了“设计冒险家”竞赛，可能会促使他们在后续普通中等教育阶段选修设计技术这门课程。题干是对该句的同义转述，其中Participation of ninth graders in Design Ventura对应原文中的pupils take part in Design Ventura in Year Nine，motivate对应原文中的trigger，choose design technology as their subject对应原文中的opt for it at General Certificate of Secondary Education，故答案为M。

【定位】由题干关键信息is welcomed by teachers和design as a school subject定位到G段。

【解析】G段最后一句提到，教师们喜欢这个竞赛，因为它培养的技能都是可在学科间迁移的，有助于证实设计学科的价值。题干是对该句的同义转述，其中teachers和as a subject是原词复现，is welcomed by与原文中的like同义，helps to prove the worth of对应原文中的helps to validate the value of，故答案为G。

【定位】由题干关键信息schools、don’t have to pay anything和to take part in the Design Ventura competition定位到K段。

【解析】K段开头提到，学校参加“设计冒险家”竞赛无需花费任何费用。题干是对该句的同义转述，其中schools和Design Ventura是原词复现，don’t have to pay anything对应原文中的costs... nothing，to take part in与原文中的to participate in同义，故答案为K。

【定位】由题干关键信息are challenged to、sustainable和marketable products定位到D段。

【解析】D段第二句中提到，这项竞赛面向13至16岁的学生，通过挑战他们为设��博物馆的商店开发兼具创意性、可持续性与商业可行性的新产品……题干是对该句相关内容的同义转述，其中challenged对应原文中的challenging，create products对应原文中的develop... product，sustainable and marketable对应原文中的sustainable and commercially feasible，故答案为D。

【定位】由题干关键信息learn about budgeting and marketing和game design定位到J段。

【解析】J段开头提到，这项竞赛真正实用的一点在于它具有商业元素——因为获奖作品会真正上市销售，因此几个参赛的男生不仅需要设计游戏，还必须学习预算和营销知识。题干是对该句的同义转述，其中learn about budgeting and marketing与designing their game对应原文，benefit from对应原文中的really useful things，in addition to对应原文中的as well as，game design对应原文中的designing their game，故答案为J。

【定位】由题干关键信息Creative Industries Federation、recruiting和engineers定位到B段。

【解析】B段最后提到，他（即本段开头提到的创意产业联合会首席执行官）认为，同样需要创新和技术能力相结合的工程行业也存在招聘难题。题干是对该句的同义转述，其中Chief executive... of the Creative Industries Federation对应原文中的officer of the Creative Industries Federation，there is difficulty now in recruiting engineers与原文中的Engineering... has recruitment problems同义，故答案为B。

sections.passage:
1 New research suggests that pandas may be at risk of dying out because they are too comfortable.? 2 Experts say too much happiness can stop the bears from searching for new mates.
1 Environmentalists have long believed that building roads or homes near the bears may threaten their survival by “reducing or fragmenting their natural habitats”, The Times reported. 2 But the new research suggests that a “modest degree of discomfort and fragmentation” may actually help preserve panda populations.?
1 The research was conducted by scientists from Michigan State University. 2 It concluded that pandas fail to wander off in search of new mates if they find their habitat too comfortable, resulting in a lack of vital genetic diversity.?
1 For their study — outlined in a paper in the journal Conservation Biology — the team looked at genetic diversity and spread among a Chinese panda population. 2 The ideal level of perfectly livable habitat was found to be only 80% of an area, with the remainder either too harsh or too affected by human activity.
1 The experts concluded that pandas should ideally “be happy enough to thrive, but not so content that they don’t want to move around and find new mates”.
1 Their conclusions about what The Guardian described as this “sweet spot” are in line with the so-called Goldilocks principle: that there can be just the right amount of something.? 2 The concept has been applied to a wide range of disciplines, from developmental psychology to economics and engineering.
1 Claudio Sillero, a professor of conservation biology at Oxford University, told the newspaper that the new findings could have implications beyond panda conservation.
1 “Most large animals that eat meat live in increasingly fragmented landscapes,” said Sillero, who was not involved in the research. 2 “It may well be that the messy nature of their relationship with human efforts induces more animals to scatter or travel further, and might result in greater genetic connectivity and enhanced population persistence.”?
1 The most recent count of pandas found that there were more than 1,800 left in the wild, putting them on the list of vulnerable, but not endangered, species.

sections.title: Section C 阅读理解 Passage 2
sections.instructions: Section C 阅读理解 Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 With those born with natural talents, it feels as if they excel without really trying.? 2 But what about those of us who don’t have a natural talent? 3 We’ve been told all our lives that if you work hard, you too can succeed. 4 But with the release of Angela Duckworth’s Grit, we are given a new key to success.
1 “As much as talent counts, effort counts twice,” says Duckworth in Grit. 2 She introduces a new concept that talent may be overrated, and if you want real success, what you need is grit, the perfect combination of passion and persistence.? 3 Even if you have natural talent, it’s nothing without grit.
1 Duckworth says grit is the difference between success and failure. 2 A person who has grit is more likely to succeed than a person who does not. 3 When we think about attaining success — whether it’s landing that job or learning that new skill — our thoughts are immediately burdened by all the things we must first learn.? 4 If you want that new job, you have to learn the job skills, then the interview skills, then the dress part — and you must be perfect at all of them. 5 Grit is different because it tells us that perfection isn’t the goal.
1 Grit lifts the unreasonable expectations off our shoulders. 2 Grit tells us that the door is open wider than we first thought possible. 3 Grit allows us to redefine our goals.? 4 Think about it: what’s something you’ve always wanted to do, but gave up because you “don’t have the skills for it”? 5 What’s something you love but aren’t good at?
1 The real workings of grit are to have sustainable passion and continue to try. 2 Effort means more than your natural ability. 3 Even if you haven’t mastered a skill, grit tells you that you can still succeed if you can transform your passion into action. 4 In a way, Duckworth is giving new hope to people who have shut the doors on their dreams. 5 She is saying it is possible that you can accomplish anything. 6 If at first you fail, then try one more time with grit.?

[1] A Florida teenager and an Atlanta woman won the overall men’s and women’s divisions Saturday at the annual 7 Mile Bridge Run.
Vaclav Bursa, 15, of Big Pine Key, Florida, finished first overall.
He completed the race in 41 minutes and 1 second and claimed the top spot in the men’s division.
Bursa won third place in the 2022 race.
He is a student at Marathon High School.
Joanna Stephens, 28, of Atlanta, completed the course in 41 minutes and 12 seconds.
She won the women’s division title and placed second overall.
The race drew competitors from 41 US states.
There were also runners from other countries, including Canada, the UK and Switzerland.
The run closed the span between the Middle and Lower Keys to traffic for 3 hours Saturday.
[2] The April contest is one of the most popular running events in the southeastern United States.
The race field filled within minutes after online registration opened in January.
Q1：What does the news report say about Vaclav Bursa and Joanna Stephens?
Q2：What do we learn about the April contest?
British astronaut Tim Peake is stepping down permanently from his role as a European astronaut.
He’s going to take up a full-time position as ambassador for science and space instead — work he’s been doing since 2019.
[3] The former British Army Air Corps helicopter pilot was selected as a European Space Agency astronaut in 2009.
He flew to the space station for a 6-month tour in 2015.
The tour saw him control a robot on earth remotely from orbit.
He also helped dock two spacecraft.
Tim said, “Being an astronaut has been the most extraordinary experience.
I’ve had the privilege of working with an exceptional team of individuals during the past 13 years with the agency.
[4] It has been incredibly exciting and rewarding.
By assuming the role of an ambassador for human flights to space, I’ll continue to support the European and the UK space agencies.”
Q3：What do we learn from the news report about Tim Peake?
Q4：What does Tim Peake say about his work with the European Space Agency?
[5] An Asda store in Wales is now home to five cats after they wandered in and made themselves comfortable.
The supermarket is known for its loyal customers, but now has a different kind of visitor that has appeared over the last year.
Regular shoppers at the supermarket are familiar with the sight of several cats settling down in the shop aisles.
The unusual situation started about 12 months ago, when one cat routinely started visiting the store.
[6] Local newspapers reported that puzzled customers posted on Facebook groups to try to find out if the cat was lost.
But its owner assured the concerned customers it was very much loved and fed at home.
It just enjoyed visiting the shop.
Staff did their best to discourage the pet from hanging around.
But instead of leaving and never coming back, it invited its friends round.
[5] There are now at least five different cats who come almost on a daily basis.
They visit the store so much that [7] staff have been forced to put up signs, asking their customers not to feed them.

W: [8] I’ve been thinking about moving off campus next semester.
M: Hmm... I don’t know if that’s a good idea as your mother and I would worry about you living all by yourself in an apartment so far from home. [9] And then there’s the expense, too. I’m not sure we can afford it.
W: Well, I wouldn’t be alone, actually. Three of my friends from the dormitory would share the place with me. And with four of us, it wouldn’t cost any more than living in the dorm.
M: Are you sure about that? [9] Rents in big cities are high, and then there’s the cost of electricity and gas. Have you factored those in?
W: We’ve budgeted for those, and for Internet and transportation. And if we move far enough from the city center, the rent is low enough for us to afford all of it.
M: What’s about the commute to and from campus? It sounds like you’ll be wasting several hours every day on the road instead of studying.
W: [10] It’s about an hour to campus, but there’s no reason I can’t study on the bus. After all, I did that during high school and my commute was even longer then.
M: That’s true. But I’m not sure why you want to leave campus and go through all that trouble when the cost is the same.
W: For a lot of reasons. We’d have a kitchen, so we could cook ourselves. And we’d each have our own bedroom, where we could study instead of going to the library. We just have more space and privacy.
M: [11] I’m not convinced that the benefits are greater than the disadvantages, but I’ll discuss this with your mother.

M: Hi. Do you have anything in mind?

We assume that if we offer our customers more choices, then they’ll be more likely to buy our products.
[16] But here’s the paradox of choice: if a person is presented with too many choices, they are actually less likely to buy.
[17] In 2012, psychologists published a study about jams.
On a regular day at a local food market, people would find a display table with 24 different kinds of jams.
Then on another day, at that same food market, people were given only 6 different types of jam choices.
Guess which display table led to more sales?
The study found that while the bigger display created more interest, people were almost 10 times less likely to purchase a jar of jam in the case of the smaller display.
Customer satisfaction takes a hit as well.
In the study, the bigger display of jams leads to lower customer satisfaction than the smaller display.
In an extensive study published in 2015, researchers analyzed a total of 99 choice studies and specifically looked at those cases in which reducing choices helped to boost sales.
[18] They found four rules that motivate consumers to buy: when people want to make a quick and easy choice, when the product is complex, when it’s difficult to compare alternatives, and when consumers don’t have clear preferences.
So as you can see, when it comes to choices, less is more.
Q16：What do we learn from the passage about the paradox of choice?
Q17：What did the psychologists want to find out in their 2012 study about jams?
Q18：What is the finding of an extensive study published in 2015?
The New Year has come and gone, and many may have already forgotten what they had resolved to do on January 1st.
But if that resolution was to volunteer more, now is the best time to start.
Volunteering can drop after the holiday season, and by February, some organizations lack the volunteers they had in surplus just a month ago.
[19] According to one survey, only 26% of Americans volunteered, despite reports that many Americans view volunteering as worthwhile.
Why such a disconnect?
[20] Most people cite time and conflicting work schedules as major barriers, but employees and employers would actually benefit if companies made employee volunteering part of the job.
Researchers have found donating our time and talent to others can lower blood pressure, boost happiness and improve mental and physical health.
Studies have also linked employee volunteer programs with more productive employees.
With so much emphasis on employee wellness these days, company volunteer programs could be the perfect 2025 resolution.
But for volunteering to benefit employees and the workplace, the entire organization needs to be involved.
By allowing employees to donate their time during work hours, the workplace becomes an outlet for personal fulfillment without affecting personal time.
[21] In one survey, 89% of employees perceived companies that sponsored volunteer activities as creating a better working environment, and 75% said volunteering was critical to their well-being.
Q19：What do many Americans think of volunteering?
Q20：How could companies ensure both employees and employers benefit from volunteering?
Q21：What did 75% of employees say about volunteering in a survey?
[22] The vast majority of the UK’s 200,000 tonnes of retail sectors annual food waste comes from supermarkets.
But it’s a problem that impacts independent luxury food suppliers too.
The scale is small.
It’s estimated at less than one per cent of the UK’s food waste total.
But the quality from these suppliers is high.
Everything from specialist cheeses to sought-after coffee beans gets thrown away every day in the current food system.
This is where French entrepreneur Sophie André comes in.
[23] In 2016 she moved to London and began by setting up a business delivering luxury hand-made food across the city.
“Food delivery seems to be a big thing here,” She says.
“So I started delivering products by bicycle.
Talking with local producers I learned that a small part of the production is sometimes wasted due to problems with size or shape, but the quality of the products remains unchanged.”
[24] Unlike many food waste projects that have sprung up in recent years, the idea is not simply to redistribute waste food, but to provide a high-quality product.
André’s company Elysia offers breakfasts and snacks specifically aimed at business meetings and events.
Once sourced, Elysia uses waste products to create “simple, natural, straightforward” meals and snacks.
[25] Perhaps unlike other waste food, the supply is regular.
Suppliers will always have a certain amount of surplus.
So the menus remain regular too.
André believes this benefits both her business and her customers.
Q22：What do we learn about the UK’s retail sector food waste?
Q23：What does Sophie André’s business do in London?
Q24：In what way does Sophie André’s business differ from many food waste projects?
Q25：Why will suppliers always have a certain amount of surplus?

questions.explanation: 【解析】新闻后半部分蒂姆评价自己在欧洲宇航局 13 年的工作时说，这是一段极其令人振奋且有意义的经历。由此可知，选项 A 为正确答案。其余三项新闻中均未提及，可排除。

questions.explanation: 【解析】新闻开头就提到，威尔士的一家阿斯达超市如今成了五只猫的家。新闻末尾部分也提到，现在至少有五只不同的猫几乎每天都来超市，非常频繁地光顾超市。由此可知，选项 C 为正确答案。其余三个选项新闻中均未提及，可排除。

choices.label: B

questions.explanation: 【解析】新闻中提到，12 个月前，有一只猫开始定期光顾这家超市，一头雾水的顾客在脸书群组中发帖，试图弄清楚这只猫是否迷路了。由此可知，选项 D 为正确答案。其余三个选项新闻中均未提及，可排除。
【解析】新闻末尾提到，五只猫每天都来超市，如此频繁地光顾超市，以至于员工们不得不张贴告示，要求顾客们不要投喂它们。故选项 A 为正确答案。其余三个选项新闻中均未提及，可排除。

【解析】在对话开头，女士就开门见山地提出自己一直在考虑下学期搬出校园居住，所以答案是 C 项。对话中女士表示搬出校园后她将和宿舍的三个朋友合租公寓，每人均有自己的卧室，而非与朋友合住同一间房，故排除 A 项；对话中女士提到，四个人分摊的话，住在校外的费用不会比住宿舍高，这说明削减生活开支并不是女士的目的，故排除 B 项；对话中女士提到，如果搬到离市中心足够远的地方住，费用将足够便宜，D 项与此完全相反，显然不在女士考虑之中，故也排除。

【解析】对话中，男士听说女士打算搬出校园居住后他提到了费用问题，说不确定自己和女士的妈妈能否负担得起，后面又明确提到大城市的房租很高，还有电费和煤气费，问女士是否把这些因素都考虑在内，他使用了 factor... in 这一固定短语，意为 “把…… 考虑在内”，这与问题中出现的固定短语 take... into consideration（把…… 考虑在内）属于同义转述关系，故答案为 B 项。A 项在对话中没有提到，故排除；虽然女士提到了搬出去住后生活条件的一些变化，但这并非男士建议女士考虑的内容，故排除 C 项；男士担心的是女士上学的通勤距离，而非女士到家的距离，故排除 D 项。
【解析】对话中，当男士提出担心女士每天会浪费好几个小时在通勤路上而无法学习时，女士回应说她到学校大约需要一个小时，但她完全可以在公交车上学习，毕竟高中时她就这样做过，所以答案为 C 项。其他选项女士在描述自己的高中生活时均未提及，故排除。

questions.explanation: 【解析】对话开头女士明确表示她要给侄子劳伦斯挑礼物，然后请男士推荐玩具，并最终选定了一款，所以答案为 C 项。其他三项均与对话内容不符，可直接排除。
【解析】对话中，男士提到，对于十岁左右的男孩来说，今年最畅销的是一款叫做波波侠的动作玩偶，特别受欢迎，所以答案是 B 项。A 项 “很有教育意义” 是女士对她要挑选的玩具的要求，故排除；对话中男士提到波波侠没有电池，C 项与此相悖，故排除；D 项在对话中没有相关内容，故也排除。

questions.explanation: 【解析】对话中，女士提到劳伦斯有个姐姐，年纪比他稍大一点，所以也许一款他们可以一起玩的游戏会很好，因此答案是 B 项。A 项中 “有助于锻炼思维的游戏” 和 D 项中 “可以独自玩或与他人一起玩的游戏” 都是男士对拼图游戏的描述，并不是女士的需求，故均排除；C 项在对话中没有相关内容，故也排除。

questions.explanation: 【解析】对话中，男士向女士推荐海战棋游戏时提到它是一款经典游戏，从上世纪 30 年代就有了，女士回应说他们小时候就有一款，男士接着说每个人都有过这款游戏，而且现在的孩子和他们小时候一样喜欢它。由此可知，海战棋游戏几十年来一直受孩子们的喜爱，答案是 A 项。B 项在对话中没有相关信息，故排除；对话中虽提到，女士说自己有过在外面下雨不得不待在室内时玩海战棋的美好回忆，但并未提及海战棋游戏在室内和室外都可以玩，故排除 C 项；虽然对话中提到海战棋游戏从上世纪 30 年代就有了，但是并没有明确说明它是最古老的游戏之一，故排除 D 项。

questions.explanation: 【解析】文章开头部分明确提到，人们原本认为给顾客提供更多选择，他们就会更愿意购买产品，但 “选择悖论” 表明，当人们面对过多的选择时，他们购买的可能性反而更低。选项 B 与文章表述一致，故为正确答案。虽然文章中提到大展示台吸引了更多关注，但这并非 “选择悖论” 涉及的方面，故排除 A 选项。文章表明更少的果酱种类展示带来的顾客满意度更高，C 选项与原文相悖，故排除。文章中未提及顾客是否会因困惑，属于无中生有，故 D 选项可排除。

choices.label: B

questions.explanation: 【解析】文章最后提到，2015 年发表的大规模研究发现了四条促使消费者购买的规则，D 选项与原文表述相符，故为正确答案。文中未提及顾客什么都不买的情况，A 选项无中生有，故排除。该研究发现的是促使消费者购买的规则，并非提高顾客满意度的技巧和预测顾客偏好，B 和 C 选项可排除。
【解析】文章中提到，一项调查显示，许多美国人认为志愿服务是值得的，选项 C 是原文原词复现，故为答案。文章中没有任何信息表明美国人觉得志愿服务会带来压力，以及将志愿服务视为负担，故可排除 A、B 两项。虽然文中提到志愿服务对健康有益，但未提及它让人充满活力，故排除选项 D。

questions.explanation: 【解析】文章中间提到，2016 年，她（索菲・安德烈）搬到伦敦，创办了一家在全城配送高端手工制作食品的公司，可知索菲・安德烈在伦敦创办的公司是配送高端手工制作食品的，C 选项与原文一致，故为正确答案。文中提到索菲・安德烈最初是用自行车配送食品，而非出租自行车用于配送，A 选项曲解文意。文中提到每天包括备受追捧的咖啡豆在内的食品被丢弃，并未提及索菲・安德烈是否销售咖啡豆，故排除 B 选项。公司虽利用废弃食品制作产品，但核心是配送高端手工制作食品，回收城市废弃食品并非其主要业务，故 D 选项错误。

questions.explanation: 【解析】文章中提到，与近年来涌现出的许多食物浪费处理项目不同，安德烈的想法不只是重新分配废弃食品，而是要提供高品质的产品。也就是说，安德烈的生意与其他食物浪费处理项目的不同之处在于她的生意旨在提供高品质产品，D 选项正确。文中提及伦敦本地与独立生产商将部分因尺寸或形状不符合要求的食品废弃，并未提及安德烈的公司特别关注产品尺寸和形状，故 A 选项错误。文中未提及安德烈的公司试图摆脱当前食品体系的限制，故排除 B 选项。与当地生产商合作是获取废弃食品的方式，而并非是安德烈的公司与其他食物浪费处理项目的区别所在，C 选项错误。

choices.label: C

questions.explanation: 【解析】文章最后提到，或许与其他废弃食品不同，这些食品的供应很稳定，供应商总会有一定数量的盈余食品，所以菜单也能保持稳定。由此可知，供应商总会有一定数量的盈余产品，使得公司的菜单能够保持稳定，从而确保产品供应的稳定性，满足业务需求，A 选项符合文意，故为答案。文章强调的是能够保持 “regular（稳定的）”，而非 “unique（独特的）”，且保持菜单稳定是确保稳定供应带来的结果，并非供应商有盈余产品的原因，B 选项错误。虽然生产过程中存在因尺寸或形状问题导致的浪费，但原文未提及供应商储备盈余产品是为了弥补这些浪费，C 选项属于过度推��。文中未提及客户存在紧急需求，也未表明供应商的盈余产品与满足紧急需求相关，D 选项属于无中生有。

sections.title: Part 1 Writing 写作
sections.passage:
1 In recent years, AI technology has become an increasingly common part of students’ lives. 2 It brings both opportunities and challenges, so learning to use it properly is vital.
1 First, we must uphold academic integrity. 2 This keeps us focused and helps avoid over-relying on AI, even for tough assignments. 3 For instance, AI ought to be used only for brainstorming or grammar checks, as this not only stops plagiarism but also preserves critical-thinking skills. 4 Additionally, schools and teachers are supposed to offer training workshops. 5 With proper guidance on ethical AI use, we can explore its value without misusing it.
1 In short, by adopting the right methods, we can turn AI into a valuable learning partner. 2 It is time to take action and embrace AI - assisted education with wisdom and responsibility.

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 In recent years, the northeastern region of China has been actively developing its ice and snow resources. 2 For example, Harbin has made full use of its rich ice and snow resources to create the unique “Ice and Snow World,” where visitors can enjoy the beauty of ice and snow and also experience the local folk culture. 3 Nowadays, the once-dreaded freezing weather is attracting tourists from all directions, turning into a popular travel destination. 4 The ice and snow tourism industry is making greater contributions to the local economic development.

questions.stem: ①近年来，中国东北地区正在大力开发冰雪资源。②例如，哈尔滨利用丰富的冰雪资源打造了极具地方特色的“冰雪大世界”，让游客在欣赏冰雪之美的同时也能体验当地独特的民俗文化。③如今，曾令人畏惧的冰天雪地正吸引着四面八方的游客，成为深受欢迎的旅游胜地。④冰雪旅游业正为当地的经济发展做出越来越大的贡献。
questions.answer: 1 In recent years, the northeastern region of China has been actively developing its ice and snow resources. 2 For example, Harbin has made full use of its rich ice and snow resources to create the unique “Ice and Snow World,” where visitors can enjoy the beauty of ice and snow and also experience the local folk culture. 3 Nowadays, the once-dreaded freezing weather is attracting tourists from all directions, turning into a popular travel destination. 4 The ice and snow tourism industry is making greater contributions to the local economic development.

sections.title: Section A 选词填空
sections.passage:
1 Sir Alfred Hitchcock was an English movie director and producer. 2 Famously 1 to as ‘The Master of Suspense, ’ Hitchcock is one of the most influential filmmakers in the history of 2.? 3 He was an extraordinary director who entertained his audience with 3 and gripping suspense movies.?
1 His fascination with crime began at an early age when he was 4 by his father who made him spend a few minutes inside a prison for his misconduct.? 2 Hence, his movies are 5 of the guilt and innocence of the wrongdoer and the victim.? 3 He had a gift for creating stories that consisted of deceit, robbery, murder, corruption, and other criminal 6 with incredible plot twists in the storyline.? 4 The principal characters in his movies were often ordinary people 7 in unwanted and unavoidable situations.?
1 He was 8 productive and his amazing body of work is considered fascinating by the critics.? 2 Most of his movies have 9 the test of time and are considered to be masterpieces.? 3 He is also remembered by other filmmakers, for he continues to inspire them to be passionate about their work. 4 He is also 10 by people around the world for his entertaining and exciting stories.?

questions.explanation:
【词性判断】空格位于句子的状语结构中，逻辑主语与主句主语一致，为被动关系。空格前面为副词Famously,后面为to as.…,空格处应填过去分词。

【解析】由Hitchcock is one of the most influential filmmakers可知，他享有盛誉，而下一句提到，他以扣人心弦的悬疑电影为观众带来观影享受，由此可知，此处是说被誉为“悬疑大师”的希区柯克。(be)referred to as为固定搭配，意为“被称为……"”,(be)famously referred to as意为“被誉为”,符合此处语境，故答案为referred。

【词性判断】空格位于句末，前面为in the history of，故空格处应填名词。

【解析】从前文的movie director（电影导演）、filmmakers（电影制作人），以及后文的suspense movies（悬疑电影）可推断，上下文与电影领域有关，此处应填cinema。

【词性判断】空格前面为entertained his audience with，后面为and gripping suspense movies，and连接并列成分，gripping为形容词，故空格处应填形容词，与gripping共同修饰suspense movies。

【解析】空格所填词与gripping（扣人心弦的）共同描述电影的特点，逻辑上需保持情感色彩一致，形成语义递进。engaging意为“引人入胜的”，符合语境，故为答案。

【词性判断】空格前面为he was，后面为动作执行者by his father，空格处需填入动词的过去分词形式，构成完整的被动语态。

【解析】句中提到他行为不端，父亲让他在监狱里待了几分钟，由此可知，父亲为了“惩罚”他才让他在监狱里待了几分钟，punished符合语境，故为答案。

【词性判断】空格前面为系动词are，后面为介词短语of the guilt...，空格处应填形容词。

【解析】前一句提到导演童年时被惩罚的经历，hence（因此）引出结果，即童年经历影响了电影的主题，be symbolic of为固定搭配，意为“象征……”，用symbolic更能体现电影对现实的映射。故为答案。

【词性判断】空格前面为形容词criminal（当然criminal也可以是名词，意为“罪犯”，但它是可数名词，且在此处有other修饰，如果它是名词，应使用其复数形式，故排除其名词词性），后面为介词短语with incredible plot...，故空格处应填名词。

【解析】and other表明空格所填名词应与前面列举的犯罪行为并列，criminal offences表示“刑事犯罪”，能概括前面的具体罪行（deceit、robbery、murder、corruption），符合语境，故为答案。

【词性判断】空格前面为ordinary people，后面为in unwanted and...，空格处应填过去分词，作后置定语，修饰people。

【解析】ordinary people（普通人）与unwanted and unavoidable situations（身不由己之境）二者为人“陷入”身不由己之境的关系。(be) caught in意为“陷入”，符合语境，故答案为caught。

【词性判断】空格所在句子主系表结构完整，前面为系动词was，后面为形容词productive，故空格处应填副词，修饰后面的形容词。

【解析】由空格后的productive（高产的）以及his amazing body of work（其令人惊叹的作品体系）可知，此处是说希区柯克十分高产，代入副词选项可知，highly“非常，极”符合此处语境，故为答案。

【词性判断】空格所在句为现在完成时，前面为助动词have，后面为名词短语the test of time and...，故空格处应填过去分词，构成完成时态。

【解析】由下文与“have  34  the test of time”构成并列关系的and are considered to be masterpiece（被视为杰作）可知，此处是作者高度评价希区柯克的电影，杰作自然能“经受住”时间的考验，而stand the test of time为固定短语，意为“经受时间的考验”，符合此处语境，故答案为stood。

【词性判断】空格前面为He is also，后面为动作执行者by people，空格处需填入动词的过去分词形式，构成完整的被动语态。

【解析】前文提到“其他电影制作人也对他缅怀不已，因为他始终激励着后来者以热忱投身创作”，而空格所在句承接上文，且使用了also一词，可知此处作者仍在正面评价希区柯克，突出其影响力。代入选项可知，worshipped“崇拜；崇敬”符合此处语境，故为答案。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Freshly juiced fruit has become a basic dietary item — especially for busy, health-conscious consumers who can save time on making (and perhaps even chewing) their food without missing out on nutrients. 2 Fruit juice also has been linked to claims that it can help you both lose weight and stay healthy. 3 All of which, of course, has made it highly profitable.? 4 The global fruit and vegetable juices market was valued at $154 billion in 2016 and is expected to grow.
1 But is juicing really as healthy as we think? 2 Most foods containing fructose — a naturally occurring sugar found in all fruits and fruit juices — don’t seem to have harmful effects as long as they’re not contributing to excess daily calories. 3 This is because the fibre found in whole fruits is intact, and the sugar is contained within the fruit’s cells. 4 It takes our digestive system a while to break these cells down and for fructose to enter the bloodstream.?
1 But this is not the case with fruit juice. 2 Unlike whole fruit, fruit juice has most of the fibre removed.? 3 This is why the fructose in fruit juices counts as ‘free sugars’ — which also include honey and the sugars added to foods. 4 It’s recommended by the World Health Organisation that adults have no more than 30g of added sugar, the equivalent of 150ml of fruit juice, per day. 5 The problem is that, with the fibre removed, fruit juice’s fructose is absorbed more quickly. 6 Sudden increases in blood sugar cause the release of insulin (胰岛素) to bring it back down to a stable level. 7 Over time, this mechanism can wear out, increasing the risk of developing type 2 diabetes. 8 In 2013, researchers analysed the health data of 100,000 people collected between 1986 and 2009 and found that fruit juice consumption was linked with increased risk of type 2 diabetes. 9 Another study found a relationship between fruit juice and type 2 diabetes after following the diets and diabetes status of more than 70,000 nurses over 18 years. 10 The researchers explain that the possible reason for this may partly have been the lack of the other components found in whole fruit, like fibre.
1 Juices containing vegetables can provide more nutrients and less sugar than juices made up of just fruit — but they still lack valuable fibre. 2 Diets high in fibre have been linked to a lower risk of developing heart disease, stroke, high blood pressure and diabetes, and it’s recommended adults consume 30g per day.?
1 Aside from the link to type 2 diabetes, many studies agree that fruit juice is harmful if it contributes to an excess in calories.? 2 In an analysis of 155 studies, John Sievenpiper, associate professor at the University of Toronto’s Department of Nutritional Sciences, set out to understand if the associations between sugary soft drinks and health — including risk of diabetes and heart disease — were applicable to the food and drink we generally consume as part of a healthy diet. 3 He compared studies looking into the effects of fructose-containing sugars with control diets free from or lower in these sugars. 4 His aim? 5 To isolate the effects of consuming too many calories from the effects of foods containing different sugars.
1 He found negative effects on blood sugar and insulin levels when food provided excess calories from sugars, including fruit juice. 2 However, when the calories weren’t in excess overall, there were some advantages to consuming whole fruit — and even fruit juice. 3 Sievenpiper concludes that the recommended 150ml of fruit juice per day, which is an average serving, is reasonable. 4 The paper concluded that foods containing fructose may have some small benefits for long-term blood sugar control when they don’t lead to over-consumption of calories.? 5 But when they do lead to too many calories, they risk raising blood sugar and insulin levels.
1 So while we know that fruit juice can cause diabetes if it’s part of a diet that has more calories overall, it’s less clear how juice affects the long-term health of those who aren’t overweight. 2 But we have a higher risk of consuming more than the recommended daily number of calories (around 2,000 for women and 2,500 for men) on the days we drink juice, according to research. 3 Numerous studies have shown that drinking fruit juice doesn’t make us consume any less of other foods throughout the day.?
1 As it is easy to consume large amounts of fruit juice quite quickly, extra calories are taken in. 2 And extra calories can contribute to weight gain. 3 One way we can improve the effects of fruit juice on our health is making sure we select ripe fruit to retain as much of its goodness as possible, according to Roger Clemens, professor of pharmaceutical (药物的) sciences at the University of Southern California.?
1 Another reason for fruit juice’s recent popularity is the argument that it can help to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body.? 2 However, “the whole concept of a juice diet helping to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body is completely false,” says Clemens. 3 “We consume compounds every day that may be poisonous and our bodies do a wonderful job of removing and eliminating anything harmful from our bodies.”
1 And juice isn’t a cure-all for getting your nutrients, either. 2 “There are a lot of nutrients contained in the parts of the fruits, such as in apple skins, that are excluded when you juice them,” says Heather Ferris, a professor of medicine.? 3 “You end up with sugary water with some vitamins.”
1 Plus, she adds, it’s not an ideal way to reach the advised ‘five a day’. 2 “People try to get five servings of fruit and vegetables per day and don’t realise this isn’t just about getting vitamins,” she says. 3 “It’s also about reducing the amount of grain carbs (碳水化合物) and protein and fats in our diet, and increasing fibre.” 4 So while fruit juice is better than no fruit at all, there are limits. 5 It particularly comes with risks when we consume more than 150ml of free sugars per day, or when it puts us over our recommended calorie intake. 6 It provides us with vitamins — but fruit juice is far from a quick fix.

questions.explanation:
【定位】

由题干关键信息fruit juice、different from whole fruit和contains much less fibre定位到C段。


【解析】

C段第二句提到，与整个水果不同，果汁中的大部分纤维已被去除。题干与该句内容同义，其中Fruit juice属于原词重现，different from whole fruit对应原文中的Unlike whole fruit，contains much less fibre与原文中的has most of the fibre removed同义，故答案为C。

【定位】

由题干关键信息a juice diet、rid our body of harmful or poisonous substances定位到I段。


【解析】

I段第一句提到，果汁近来受欢迎的另一个原因是它能帮助清除体内有毒或有害物质的说法。题干与该句同义，其中Some people believe对应原文中的the argument，a juice diet属于第二句中的原词重现，helps to rid our body of harmful or poisonous substances对应原文中的help to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body，故答案为I。

【定位】

由题干关键信息A lot of research、comes to the same conclusion、fruit juice does harm to the human body和surplus calories定位到E段。


【解析】

E段第一句提到，除了与2型糖尿病的关联外，许多研究一致认为，如果果汁导致热量过剩，它就是有害的。题干与这句话同义，其中A lot of research comes to the same conclusion与原文中的many studies agree that同义，fruit juice does harm to the human body对应原文中的fruit juice is harmful，when it leads to surplus calories对应原文中的if it contributes to an excess in calories，故答案为E。

【定位】

由题干关键信息claimed health benefits of fruit and vegetable juices和the industry very profitable定位到A段。


【解析】

A段最后两句提到，当然，所有这一切使其利润十分可观，2016年，全球果蔬汁市场价值为1540亿美元，这一数字预计还将增长。而“所有这一切”指的就是前面几句提到的：鲜榨果汁已经成为一种基本的饮食项目——特别是对于那些忙碌且注重健康的消费者来说；果汁还与一些减肥和保持健康的说法相关联。故题干是对该段内容的概括总结，其中The claimed health benefits是对原文Fruit juice also has been linked to claims that it can help you both lose weight and stay healthy的概括总结，fruit and vegetable juices属于该段最后一句中的原词重现，have rendered the industry very profitable对应原文中的has made it highly profitable，故答案为A。

【定位】

由题干关键信息increase the benefits、fruit juice、our health和choose ripe fruit to make juice定位到H段。


【解析】

H段最后一句提到，南加州大学药物科学教授罗杰·克莱门斯表示，一种办法是，我们可以通过确保选择成熟的水果来榨汁，以保留尽可能多的营养价值，从而改善果汁对健康的影响。题干是对这句话的概括，其中To increase the benefits of fruit juice to our health对应原文中的One way we can improve the effects of fruit juice on our health，we’d better choose ripe fruit to make juice与原文中的making sure we select ripe fruit同义，故答案为H。

【定位】

由题干关键信息Diets containing large amounts of fibre、reduce the risk、heart disease、diabetes和other health hazards定位到D段。


【解析】

D段第二句提到，高纤维饮食与降低患心脏病、中风、高血压和糖尿病的风险存在关联。题干与该句属于同义转述，其中Diets containing large amounts of fibre对应原文中的Diets high in fibre，reduce the risk of heart disease, diabetes and other health hazards是对原文中的have been linked to a lower risk of developing heart disease, stroke, high blood pressure and diabetes的概括，故答案为D。

【定位】

由题干关键信息a research paper、drinking fruit juice、beneficial和consumed in reasonable amounts定位到F段。


【解析】

F段第二至四句提到，如果总热量摄入不超标，食用整个水果，甚至是果汁，还是有一些益处的。西文皮珀得出结论：每天推荐的150毫升果汁（这是平均一份的量）是合理的。该论文得出结论：含有果糖的食物在不导致热量摄入过度的情况下，对长期血糖控制可能有一些小的益处。题干是对这几句内容的概括，其中According to a research paper对应原文中的The paper concluded，fruit juice属于原词重现，beneficial对应原文中的have some small benefits；consumed in reasonable amounts是对原文中when they don’t lead to over - consumption of calories的概括总结，故答案为F。

【定位】

由题干关键信息One expert claims、juicing、wastes a lot of nutrients和contained in fruits定位到J段。


【解析】

J段第二句提到，“水果的某些部分，如苹果皮中，含有很多营养物质，而这些部分在榨汁时会被过滤掉，”医学教授希瑟·费里斯说。题干与这句话同义，其中One expert claims对应原文中的says Heather Ferris, a professor of medicine，juicing与原文中的when you juice them (fruits)同义，wastes对应原文中的are excluded，a lot of nutrients contained in fruits对应原文中的a lot of nutrients contained in the parts of the fruits，故答案为J。

【定位】

由题干关键信息takes some time、fruit’s cells、be digested、fructose和be absorbed定位到B段。


【解析】

B段最后一句提到，我们的消化系统需要一些时间来分解这些细胞，然后果糖才会进入血液中。“这些细胞”指的就是前一句中提到的“水果的细胞”，故题干与该句同义，其中It takes some time对应原文中的It takes... a while，fruit’s cells属于倒数第二句中的原词重现，to be digested对应原文中的our digestive system... to break... down，for fructose to be absorbed与原文中的for fructose to enter the bloodstream同义，故答案为B。

【定位】

由题干关键信息A lot of research、drinking fruit juice和reduce our daily consumption of other foods定位到G段。


【解析】

G段最后一句提到，大量的研究已经表明，喝果汁不会减少全天其他食物的摄入量。题干与该句属于词义转述，其中A lot of research has demonstrated that对应原文中的Numerous studies have shown that，drinking fruit juice does not reduce our daily consumption of other foods与原文中的drinking fruit juice doesn’t make us consume any less of other foods throughout the day同义，故答案为G。

1 We all take a little extra effort to look nice for special occasions. 2 But most of us have conflicting feelings about dressing up and feel guilty about taking the time to focus on clothes. 3 Science now suggests the right dress may give ourselves the extra edge in our professional and personal lives.?
1 We hear sayings like “dress for the job you want; not the job you have”. 2 Most people don’t really believe in them, but research into the impact of clothes on behavior now suggests that there may actually be a grain of truth in these sayings. 3 Science says that the clothes we wear affect our behavior, our mood and even the way we interact with others because of the symbolic meaning that we assign to different types of clothing.?
1 We consider some clothes to be powerful, some to be fun, and so on. 2 We even evaluate people whom we have just met based on their clothes. 3 We also evaluate ourselves based on what we are wearing because of the way they make us feel.? 4 This means that the experience of wearing something affects our attitudes and our choice of behavior.
1 There’s a reason tailored jackets are associated with being ‘dressed for success’. 2 It seems that wearing formal office wear puts us in the right frame of mind to conduct business.? 3 Wearing power clothing makes us feel more confident and even increases hormones needed for displaying dominance. 4 This in turn helps us become better negotiators and abstract thinkers.
1 While a good suit works wonders for our performance in the boardroom, wearing formal wear isn’t a great idea when we want to socialize. 2 Studies have found that people tend to be less open and less able to relax when they wear formal clothes.
1 On the other hand, a casual dress helps us become more friendly and creative. 2 These findings support the idea of wearing business casuals on a Friday; since colleagues are most likely to take out time to socialize on the last work day of the week.? 3 I mean, who wants to hang out with people in their suits?

1 With the rise of pop music, jazz, and electronic music, both opera and classical music started to fade away from the public eye. 2 Some people are beginning to wonder whether opera and classical music are still relevant to the modern world of music. 3 Granted, you will not typically see today’s teenagers lending their ears to Bach anytime soon, but there are some major indicators that both opera and classical music are now still quite alive.?
1 The most major indicator of classical music’s importance in society today is the fact that much of the popular music that is currently being produced uses similar beats, harmonies, and melodies (旋律) as those that were used in some of classical music’s best works.? 2 Even so, it can be difficult for those who do not study music theory to see this as an indicator, since it is subtle and just shows the impact symphonic (交响乐的) orchestras have had on society’s taste in music.
1 A better example for the relevance of opera and classical music can be seen in the invention of the rock opera.? 2 Opera, in its simplest definition, is telling a story using music as its form. 3 The art of telling a story using music has not faded in the least bit. 4 In fact, sometimes actual orchestras are used for major parts of the opera itself. 5 Some of the world’s greatest hits have been parts of rock operas.
1 Fans of classical music can also tell you that there are few types of music that are more expressive. 2 So, it should come as no surprise to anyone that classical music pieces are still used as background music in modern movies.? 3 Symphonic orchestra compositions have also been created solely for the purpose of being included in major motion pictures. 4 These are often very well received amongst mainstream music fans.
1 Classical music and opera are the very foundation of what our modern music is based upon.? 2 Considering the huge impact they have had on our current society, it is without doubt that we can expect them to continue to remain important for centuries to come.

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 In recent years, an increasing number of cities in China have been committed to creating "15-minute convenient living circles." 2 Residents living in these circles can access public services within a 15-minute walking distance. 3 These convenient living circles are equipped with convenience stores, parks, fitness facilities, libraries, schools, community canteens, clinics, and so on. 4 Establishing such living circles helps provide residents with a more convenient, comfortable, friendly, and pleasant living environment, better meet the diverse needs of urban residents, and improve their quality of life and happiness.

questions.stem: ①近年来，中国越来越多的城市致力打造“15分钟便民生活圈”(convenient living circles)。②生活在便民生活圈里的居民可以在15分钟步行范围内获得公共服务。③便民生活圈配备便利店、公园、健身设施、图书馆、学校、社区食堂和诊所等。④建立这样的生活圈有助于为居民提供更便捷、舒适、友好和宜人的生活环境，更好地满足多样化的城市居民需求提高居民生活质量和幸福感。
questions.answer: 1 In recent years, an increasing number of cities in China have been committed to creating "15-minute convenient living circles." 2 Residents living in these circles can access public services within a 15-minute walking distance. 3 These convenient living circles are equipped with convenience stores, parks, fitness facilities, libraries, schools, community canteens, clinics, and so on. 4 Establishing such living circles helps provide residents with a more convenient, comfortable, friendly, and pleasant living environment, better meet the diverse needs of urban residents, and improve their quality of life and happiness.

1 There are many other cases in the medical 5 that document the brain’s amazing ability to 6.? 2 For example, a young boy had a significant portion of his brain removed for medical reasons, which included the part of the brain 7 for sight.? 3 But a few years after his surgery, scientists found that he could 8 see.? 4 They determined that this was because other parts of his brain took over the missing part’s 9 tasks.? 5 Another study involved people who could smell, despite missing the region in the brain that processes information about smells. 6 Though they are not sure how these individuals 10 the ability to smell, scientists believe it is possible that another part of the brain took on that task.?

【词性判断】空格位于形容词critical后，故空格处应填名词。

【解析】前一句提及hemispherectomy（大脑半球切除术），本句指出“尽管缺失这一关键____的一半，参与者仍能正常生活”。代入选项可知，organ符合此处语境。critical organ与hemispherectomy形成手术对象的呼应。

【词性判断】空格前面为定冠词the，后面为名词短语half of...，故空格处应填形容词，修饰后面的名词。

【解析】前文提到“尽管缺失这一关键器官的一半，参与者仍能正常生活”，本句说明原因，即“他们大脑中____一半得到了强化”。____half与missing half形成对比，空格所填词与missing（缺失的）语义相对，故答案为remaining。

【词性判断】空格前面为句子主语This，后面为that引导的宾语从句，空格处应填谓语动词。前文时态为一般现在时，故空格处应填动词的第三人称单数形式。

【解析】前一句提到“研究人员发现，接受过大脑半球切除术的人，其大脑不同网络各部分之间的连接（及由此产生的信息交流），实际上比大脑完整的人更强”，本句结论为“大脑能够弥补某些脑结构的损失”。前后句是研究发现与结论之间的推导关系，故此处应填indicates。

【词性判断】空格前面为形容词medical，后面为that引导的定语从句，故空格处应填名词。

【解析】前文提到了大脑半球切除术的案例，本句指出“医学____存在许多其他案例……”。代入选项可知，medical literature（医学文献）符合此处语境，故答案为literature。

【词性判断】空格位于句末，前面为ability to，故空格处应填动词原形，构成不定式结构，充当ability的后置定语。

【解析】前文提到大脑有形成新网络和新连接的能力，从而能够弥补某些脑结构的损失，这强调了大脑具有神奇的适应能力。本句意为“医学文献中存在许多其他案例，记载了大脑惊人的____能力”，进一步强调大脑的适应能力。故答案为adapt。

【词性判断】空格前面为名词短语the part of the brain，后面为介词短语for sight，空格处应填分词或形容词，作后置定语。

【解析】本句意为“一个小男孩因医疗原因切除了很大一部分大脑，其中包括大脑中____视觉的区域”。responsible for（对……负责）符合此处语境，故答案为responsible。

【词性判断】空格前面为he could，后面为动词原形see，故空格处应填入副词，修饰see。

【解析】前文提到“一个小男孩因医疗原因切除了很大一部分大脑，其中包括大脑中负责视觉的区域”，正常来说，视觉区域的缺失会导致该男孩失明，但本句提到“但在手术数年后，科学家发现他____能够看见东西”。still（仍然）符合此处语境，表明视觉能力一直没有消失，故答案为still。

【词性判断】空格前面为所有格the missing part’s，后面为名词tasks，故空格处应填入形容词或分词，修饰tasks。

【解析】前文提到“……切除了很大一部分大脑，其中包括大脑中负责视觉的区域……仍然能够看见东西”，本句解释原因“其大脑其他区域接管了缺失部分的____任务”。视觉区域当然是负责视觉任务，故答案为visual。

【词性判断】空格前面为从句主语these individuals，后面为宾语the ability to smell，空格处应填谓语动词。

【解析】前一句提到“尽管他们缺失大脑中处理嗅觉信息的区域，却仍能闻到气味”，本句指出“科学家不确定这些人如何____嗅觉能力”。代入选项可知，retained“保留”符合此处语境，故为答案。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Traffic jams are a common problem of most big cities, either in developed or in developing countries, but one kind of traffic jams in particular can be especially frustrating. 2 These are generally known as “phantom” traffic jams, in which dense traffic crawls to a halt for no apparent reason at all.
1 “When caught in such a traffic jam, it is common for drivers to assume that there must be an accident, or construction or something,” said Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) computer science professor Berthold Horn.? 2 “And then you drive and drive and drive... and there isn’t anything there.”
1 The exact cause of these phantom traffic jams has long remained a mystery. 2 But now, new research has found the cause and researchers may have come up with a solution for this frustrating traffic pattern: maintaining equal spacing between cars on the road, rather than driving so closely behind another vehicle that a collision (碰撞) is likely if that vehicle brakes suddenly.?
1 Horn said phantom traffic jams are an emergent property of the flow of vehicles down a highway. 2 A phantom jam begins when a car in dense traffic slows down even slightly, which causes the car behind that vehicle to slow even more — and the slowing action spreads backward through the lane of traffic like a wave, getting worse the farther it spreads.? 3 Eventually, the cars far behind are forced to stop completely or risk hitting the slower vehicles ahead — and so the traffic grinds to a halt over nothing, Horn said.
1 Horn has been working on the problem of phantom traffic jams for years, and he has come up with a solution: By splitting the difference between the cars in front and the cars behind, the spacing of cars in a stream of traffic can act as a damper (抑制) on phantom traffic jams. 2 That is, it can prevent the slow-down effect from being amplified (增强) by the cars that follow behind, he said.? 3 In essence, each driver would constantly make adjustments to keep their car roughly halfway between the car in front and the car behind.
1 Horn calls this method of vehicle spacing bilateral (双边的) control, and he said it could be achieved with relatively simple modifications to the adaptive cruise control that many new cars already have.? 2 Adaptive cruise control is a driver assistance technology that sets a maximum speed for vehicles and automatically slows the speed of the car when traffic is sensed in front of the vehicle. 3 The technology is also known as autonomous cruise control. 4 Such modifications, Horn said, could help fight phantom jams within a few years, maybe decades before an alternative solution, such as networked self-driving cars, becomes a reality on the roads.
1 Traffic jams are caused by a number of factors, such as roads that are poorly designed or over-capacity, localized factors like city traffic-lighting patterns, and events like accidents and construction. 2 But phantom traffic jams can make all those problems worse, Horn said. 3 And the researchers in the new study have calculated that solving phantom jams could save at least some of the estimated $121 billion per year that traffic jams are estimated to cost the U.S. economy, Horn told Live Science.?
1 New research by Horn and MIT postdoctoral associate Liang Wang, published in the journal IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems, shows how bilateral control can fight the problem. 2 The researchers made computer models of real-world traffic conditions, showing how a typical U.S. freeway could benefit from cars using bilateral control. 3 That would be in place when human drivers fail to slow down, thus avoiding tailgating (紧跟) the car in front, Horn said. 4 “Under reasonable conditions today, you might get 1,800 cars per lane per hour throughput (the volume of traffic passing through),” he added. 5 “But with bilateral control, you could almost double that.”?
1 The main alternative to increasing traffic throughput per lane has been to build more lanes and more highways, and putting in new roads is very expensive, he said. 2 “If we can increase the throughput on major highways, even if it’s only by 50 percent, that would be a big deal,” Horn said.
1 With the help of engineering students at high schools in Maine, Horn and Wang have also built a robot simulation (模拟) that shows how bilateral control can suppress phantom traffic jams. 2 Increasing the spacing of vehicles dampens the effect of slowdowns by cars in front of a given car, so that the slowing is not worsened until it becomes a phantom jam, the researchers said.
1 A video from the project shows a train of autonomous robots running along a track without bilateral control; they eventually back up in phantom jams. 2 But when the robots are switched over to bilateral control (by flashing the lights in the room), each autonomous robot tries to keep itself halfway between the robot in front and the one behind; the phantom jams disappear as a result, Horn said.
1 Since starting his research on phantom traffic jams, Horn has learned that schools of fish and flocks of birds and bats use similar spacing strategies to avoid hitting each other while swimming or flying in densely packed groups.? 2 In particular, studies of millions of bats emerging at dusk from caves in Southeast Asia showed that each bat used a form of bilateral control to reduce the likelihood of collisions with other bats in the densely packed swarm (一大群), Horn said.
1 Unlike bats, birds and fish, however, humans have difficulty judging distances behind them. 2 To address that weakness, Horn is now working with the car company Toyota to enable a form of bilateral control via modifications to existing adaptive cruise control systems, which use forward-facing sensors to judge the distance to the vehicle ahead. 3 The bilateral control approach would include adding rear-facing sensors to determine the distance to the vehicle following a car.?
1 But until those systems become standard, human drivers can help reduce phantom traffic jams simply by not following the car in front so closely. 2 As Horn argues, “There’s absolutely no advantage of tailgating the car in front of you.”?

questions.explanation:
【定位】由题干关键信息The age-long mystery和how phantom traffic jams are caused定位到C段。

【解析】C段提到，这种幽灵交通堵塞的确切原因长期以来一直是个谜，但如今，新的研究已经找到了原因，研究人员可能已经想出了应对这种令人沮丧的交通模式的解决方案……题干是对这段内容的概括，其中The age-long mystery对应原文中的has long remained a mystery，has now been resolved与原文中的have come up with a solution同义，how phantom traffic jams are caused对应原文中的The exact cause of these phantom traffic jams，故答案为C。

【定位】由题干关键信息nearly double the hourly throughput per lane和adopting bilateral control定位到H段。

【解析】H段结尾部分提到，他补充道：“在当今合理的条件下，每条车道每小时的通行量（交通流量）可能达到1800辆车。但是在采用双边控制后，这一数字几乎可以翻倍。” 题干是对这一内容的概括，其中It is possible to nearly double对应原文中的you could almost double，the hourly throughput per lane对应原文中的per lane per hour throughput，by adopting bilateral control与原文中的with bilateral control同义，故答案为H。

【定位】由题干关键信息drivers making constant adjustments、equal spacing between cars和help reduce phantom traffic jams定位到E段。

【解析】该段第一句提到，霍恩针对幽灵交通堵塞问题提出了一个解决方案：通过平衡前后车之间的距离（即保持与前车和后车等距），车流中的车辆间距可以起到抑制幽灵交通堵塞的作用。该段最后一句话又提到，每位司机都需要不断调整，让自己的车大致保持在前车和后车的中间位置。由此可知，题干是对这两句话的综合概括，其中drivers making constant adjustments for equal spacing between cars对应最后一句话中的each driver would constantly make adjustments to keep their car roughly halfway between the car in front and the car behind，can help reduce phantom traffic jams与第一句话中的can act as a damper on phantom traffic jams同义，故答案为E。

【定位】由题干关键信息systems for bilateral control、not follow the car in front too closely和reduce phantom traffic jams定位到N段。

【解析】N段第一句提到，但在这些系统成为标准配置之前，人类司机只需不紧跟前车就能帮助减少幽灵交通堵塞。题干与该句同义，其中systems for bilateral control对应原文中的those systems，not follow the car in front too closely与原文中的not following the car in front so closely同义，reduce phantom traffic jams属于原词重现，故答案为N。

【定位】由题干关键信息simple modifications、the existing equipment in new vehicles和spacing bilateral control定位到F段。

【解析】F段第一句提到，霍恩将这种车辆间距控制方法称为双边控制，他说这可以通过对许多新车已经配备的自适应巡航控制系统进行相对简单的改进来实现。题干与该句同义，其中Horn said对应原文中的he said，with some simple modifications to the existing equipment in new vehicles与原文中的with relatively simple modifications to the adaptive cruise control that many new cars already have同义，spacing bilateral control属于原词重现，could be accomplished对应原文中的it could be achieved，故答案为F。

【定位】由题干关键信息Drivers caught up in phantom traffic jams、an accident has happened和some construction is going on定位到B段。

【解析】B段第一句提到，遇到这种交通堵塞时，司机通常会认为一定是前方发生了交通事故、道路有施工或其他情况。题干与该句同义，其中drivers caught up in phantom traffic jams与原文中的caught in such a traffic jam同义，is likely to对应原文中的it is common for，an accident has happened or some construction is going on对应原文中的there must be an accident, or construction or something，故答案为B。

【定位】由题干关键信息Two sets of sensors和determine the distances between cars定位到M段。

【解析】M段第二、三句提到，为了弥补这一弱点（人类难以判断后方的距离），霍恩正在与丰田汽车公司合作，通过改进现有的自适应巡航控制系统来实现一种双边控制，现有的系统使用向前传感器来判断与前方车辆之间的距离。这种双边控制方法将包括添加向后传感器，以确定与后方车辆之间的距离。由此可知，双边控制方法包含两组传感器（向前传感器和向后传感器），用来帮助司机确定车辆之间的距离。题干是对这两句话的概括，其中Two sets of sensors would be used对应原文中的use forward-facing sensors和include adding rear-facing sensors，help drivers determine the distances between cars是对原文中to judge the distance to the vehicle ahead和to determine the distance to the vehicle following a car的概括，故答案为M。

【定位】由题干关键信息Solving the problem of phantom jams和save America billions of dollars every year定位到G段。

【解析】G段最后一句提到，霍恩向《生活科学》杂志透露，这项新研究的研究人员计算出，解决幽灵交通堵塞，每年至少能够为美国节省部分预估因交通拥堵损失的约1210亿美元。题干是对这句话的概括，其中Solving the problem of phantom jams对应原文中的solving phantom jams，save America billions of dollars every year是对原文中save at least some of the estimated $121 billion per year that traffic jams are estimated to cost the U.S. economy的概括，故答案为G。

【定位】由题干关键信息a phantom traffic jam、the cars in the same lane、slow down one after another和creating a wave-like effect定位到D段。

【解析】D段第二句提到，当密集车流中的一辆车稍微减速时，幽灵堵塞便开始了，这会导致后面的车辆减速幅度更大——这种减速行为像波浪一样在车道上向后蔓延，蔓延得越远，情况就越糟糕。换言之，在幽灵交通堵塞中，同一车道的车辆依次减速，会产生波浪效应。题干是对该句的概括，其中a phantom traffic jam对应原文中的A phantom jam，the cars in the same lane slow down one after another是对原文中的a car in dense traffic slows down even slightly, which causes the car behind that vehicle to slow even more的概括总结，creating a wave-like effect与原文中的the slowing action spreads backward through the lane of traffic like a wave同义，故答案为D。

【定位】由题干关键信息certain creatures、strategies similar to bilateral control、avoid hitting each other和moving in dense crowds定位到L段。

【解析】L段第一句提到，自从开始研究幽灵交通堵塞以来，霍恩已经了解到，鱼群、鸟群和蝙蝠群在密集成群地游动或飞行时，会使用类似的间距策略来避免相互碰撞。题干是对这句话的概括，其中Horn has found对应原文中的Horn has learned，certain creatures是对原文中schools of fish and flocks of birds and bats的概括，use strategies similar to bilateral control to avoid hitting each other while moving in dense crowds与原文中的use similar spacing strategies to avoid hitting each other while swimming or flying in densely packed groups同义，故答案为L。

sections.passage:
1 Our society places a high value on physical beauty. 2 Americans spend an average of over $722 each year on their appearance. 3 One in ten Americans has tried to look like a star.?
1 There’s nothing wrong with trying to look our best, but excessive focus on physical appearance misses the soulful aspects of what it means to be beautiful. 2 Trying to look like the magazine pictures can take us on a long ride away from what beauty is really about.
1 Many of us spend far too much time, energy, and money trying to polish an image of what we think will bring attention, love, and connection. 2 In the process, we may fail to attend to ourselves in a way that would move us toward deeper intimacy, fulfillment, and meaning.?
1 It may sound trite (老生常谈的), but beauty is only skin deep; it’s not what brings love toward us. 2 Just read about the latest Hollywood starlets whose seeming love turns into resentment and bitter court battles.
1 Outer beauty can be as much of a curse as a blessing.? 2 We may develop a habit of being so focused on maintaining a perfect appearance that we never cultivate the inner qualities necessary to sustain and deepen intimacy and connection. 3 As I describe in my book, The Authentic Heart, it is the courage to be authentic that connects us in a deeper way.
1 While our initial attraction may be based, in part, on physical chemistry, it is the meeting of our inner worlds that creates the lasting intimacy and spiritual connection for which we long.? 2 If we redirect our attention toward cultivating inner qualities, we might find a magnetic attraction that moves us from something superficial to something that connects us to our depths.
1 The path toward cultivating inner beauty is really simple. 2 But what is simple is not always easy. 3 Not everyone will see us and appreciate us as we take the courageous risk to allow ourselves to be seen as we really are. 4 But if they don’t, it is their loss, not ours.? 5 Eventually we’ll find those compatible souls who appreciate us as we are.

1 Plant-based meats are coming soon to a dinner table near you, but do they deserve a spot on your plate? 2 If you tried a vegetable burger years ago and dismissed it as rubbery and flavorless, it’s a good time to give meatless meat another chance. 3 Newer varieties imitate the look, flavor, and texture of meat. 4 Analysts don’t expect the meat-free movement to slow anytime soon; a 2021 report predicts the market will skyrocket to $74 billion by 2030 — a 957 percent surge.?
1 Plant-based meats are no longer just for vegetarians. 2 Companies such as Impossible Foods and Beyond Meat — the current superstars of the alternative protein sector — are pursuing consumers who enjoy meat but want to reduce their meat consumption for animal rights, health, or environmental reasons. 3 So far, it’s a winning strategy: More than nine out of ten consumers who buy Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products also eat meat.?
1 Many vegetarians don’t actually care for food that resembles meat. 2 When reporter Joan Solsman, a longtime vegetarian, tried a dish from Impossible Foods, she felt so sick that she couldn’t finish it. 3 “Maybe the best sign that Impossible Foods has cracked the code to realistic fake meat is that I couldn’t stand to take another bite, ” she wrote.?
1 Meatless meats are generally a healthier choice than beef because they are cholesterol-free, plus they’re a good source of vitamins, minerals, protein, and fiber.
1 If meatless meat can help you stick to a plant-based diet, that in itself can lead to better health. 2 Not only has red meat been linked to cancer, but studies show that people who ditch meat have lower blood pressure, lower average blood sugar, and lower cholesterol levels.?
1 However, just because it’s plant-based doesn’t mean it’s health food. 2 Most imitation meats are highly processed and contain high amounts of sodium (钠) compared to traditional beef.
1 These new generations of alternate meat get all the attention, but don’t forget about whole grains and vegetables. 2 Beans are an especially excellent protein substitute. 3 They’re nutritious, inexpensive, and far more sustainable than any of the processed meatless substitutes on the market today.?
